author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.title: Research Summary: August 04, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Architectures and training efficiency dominate the top of the batch. DiffusionGemma converts a Gemma-4 MoE autoregressive checkpoint into an open-weight discrete-diffusion LM, the strongest evidence yet that AR pretraining transfers to non-autoregressive decoding. Training nGPT (NVIDIA, AdamW/nGPT originators) reports roughly 2x token efficiency for normalized Transformers on hybrid Mamba-2 + MoE stacks. LongCat Sparse Attention co-designs indexer-based sparse attention with hardware for streaming long-context serving, while AURORA-LM and AdaMTP push continuous-latent diffusion LMs and adaptive multi-token prediction.

Safety and security results target load-bearing assumptions:

  • CoT monitor collapse: rewriting only the chain-of-thought while preserving all actions defeats monitors used as sole defense, undermining current CoT-based safety cases
  • Redwood Research shows completion-only poisoning implants covert backdoors at low sample counts without prompt access
  • MCP server audit provides the first large-scale dynamic measurement of internet-facing agent attack surface
  • CryptoProver (Barrett, Dill) synthesizes specs plus machine-checked Verus proofs for production Rust cryptography

Agents, measurement and negative results round out the list. Qwen-CUA is a native pixel-level computer-use agent on a 397B/17B-active MoE backbone; Orchard (MSR) open-sources reusable agent environments; Cross-Benchmark Generalization questions how agentic RL is evaluated. First-party data is unusually strong: Google's ATLAS v1.0 maps 15M Gemini interactions onto occupational taxonomies, and Microsoft characterizes Copilot agentic traces across trillions of tokens. Rigorous negative results include why frontier LLMs fail at tabular prediction and why action chunking helps behavioral cloning (Levine), alongside clinical findings on physician false reliance and medical sycophancy.
entry.content:

DiffusionGemma converts a Gemma-4 MoE autoregressive checkpoint into an open-weight discrete-diffusion LM, the strongest evidence yet that AR pretraining transfers to non-autoregressive decoding. Training nGPT (NVIDIA, AdamW/nGPT originators) reports roughly 2x token efficiency for normalized Transformers on hybrid Mamba-2 + MoE stacks. LongCat Sparse Attention co-designs indexer-based sparse attention with hardware for streaming long-context serving, while AURORA-LM and AdaMTP push continuous-latent diffusion LMs and adaptive multi-token prediction.

Safety and security results target load-bearing assumptions:

  • CoT monitor collapse: rewriting only the chain-of-thought while preserving all actions defeats monitors used as sole defense, undermining current CoT-based safety cases
  • Redwood Research shows completion-only poisoning implants covert backdoors at low sample counts without prompt access
  • MCP server audit provides the first large-scale dynamic measurement of internet-facing agent attack surface
  • CryptoProver (Barrett, Dill) synthesizes specs plus machine-checked Verus proofs for production Rust cryptography

Agents, measurement and negative results round out the list. Qwen-CUA is a native pixel-level computer-use agent on a 397B/17B-active MoE backbone; Orchard (MSR) open-sources reusable agent environments; Cross-Benchmark Generalization questions how agentic RL is evaluated. First-party data is unusually strong: Google's ATLAS v1.0 maps 15M Gemini interactions onto occupational taxonomies, and Microsoft characterizes Copilot agentic traces across trillions of tokens. entry.title: DiffusionGemma Technical Report

author.name: DiffusionGemma Team, Adrien Ali Ta\"iga, James Assiene, Daniele Calandriello, Rahma Chaabouni, Jo\~ao Gante, Tamara von Glehn, Nate Keating, Chris Knutsen, Martin Kukla, Tianlin Liu, Ivan Lobov, Ofir Nabati, Jo\~ao Gabriel Oliveira, Nicolas Perez-Nieves, Nastasia Prutianova, Bobak Shahriari, Jean Tarbouriech, Pavel Tyletski, \c{C}a\u{g}lar \"Unl\"u, Cindy Wu, Glenn Cameron, Jerome Connor, Sertan Girgin, Maarten Grootendorst, Alon Levkovitch, Eliya Nachmani, Omar Sanseviero, Piotr Stanczyk, Quentin Berthet, Andrew Campbell, Cl\'ement Crepy, Valentin De Bortoli, Arnaud Doucet, Romuald Elie, Alexandre Galashov, Klaus Greff, Alexis Jacq, David Ruhe, Yu-Han Wu, Sebastian Flennerhag, Brendan O'Donoghue, George Scrivener, Shantanu Thakoor

entry.summary: DiffusionGemma is Google DeepMind's experimental open-weight discrete-diffusion language model, obtained by fine-tuning the existing Gemma 4 mixture-of-experts model (3.8B active, 25.2B total) with a two-stage pipeline using under ten percent of the original autoregressive training token budget. It refines blocks of 256 tokens in parallel instead of decoding sequentially, targeting very high generation throughput. This is the technical report accompanying a model that has been available since mid-2026.

entry.title: Training nGPT

author.name: Ilya Loshchilov, Boris Ginsburg

entry.summary: Provides a practical training recipe for normalized Transformers (nGPT) on modern hybrid Mamba-2 plus Transformer mixture-of-experts models, introducing logit gradient preconditioning, logarithmic learning-rate decay, GatedAdamW and angular update control. A 14B-total-parameter nGPT reaches the same validation loss as an AdamW-trained unnormalized twin using roughly half the training tokens.

entry.title: Qwen-CUA: Native Computer Use for (almost) Everything

author.name: Dunjie Lu, Shuai Bai, Tianyi Bai, Sicheng Fan, Chang Gao, Jian Guan, Feng Hu, Mianqiu Huang, Xingyang Huang, Yizhen Jiang, Yuheng Jing, Dehui Kong, Ning Li, Dayiheng Liu, Shixuan Liu, Zheng Liu, Que Shen, Bowen Wang, Junli Wang, Chencan Wu, Rui Xie, Tianbao Xie, Zhihui Xie, Haiyang Xu, An Yang, Tao Yu, Wenzhen Yuan, Xi Zhang, Zhenru Zhang, Mingkang Zhu, Zhaoqing Zhu, Yizhong Cao, Kai Dang, Binyuan Hui, Kaixin Li, Junyang Lin, Haiquan Wang, Zekun Wang, Yiheng Xu, Fan Yan, Mengqi Yuan, Danyang Zhang, Jiajun Zhang, Zhipeng Zhang, Fan Zhou, Fan Zhou

entry.summary: Qwen-CUA is a native computer-use agent built on a 397B-parameter mixture-of-experts backbone with roughly 17B active parameters that operates purely from screenshots and keyboard-mouse events, without DOM trees or accessibility APIs. It uses a scaffold retaining about twenty recent screenshots with block-folded visual history and is trained with a massive cloud rollout fleet on the order of 100,000 vCPUs for outcome-verified reinforcement learning.

entry.title: An AI Approach to Verified Production Cryptographic Libraries

author.name: Chuyue Sun, Su Fong, Zhiyi Kuang, Yizheng Jiao, Nina Narodytska, Haoze Wu, David L. Dill, Clark Barrett

entry.summary: CryptoProver uses language models to synthesize internal specifications plus machine-checked Verus proofs for production Rust cryptography, producing an independent proof of curve25519-dalek and the first verification of RustCrypto's chacha20 against RFC 8439. Executable code is left unchanged, so results apply to libraries used in Signal and Shadowsocks.

entry.title: Google's AI & Economy ATLAS v1.0: Mapping Gemini Usage in the Economy

author.name: Zanna Iscenko, Scott Strand, Yiyuan Chen, Guillaume Aimard, Mihai Codreanu, Vivek Sampathkumar, Alex Imas, Julian Jacobs, Evalyne Muiruri, Juan Mateos-Garcia, Jia Jen Ng, Samirah Javed, Josh Martin, Omar Ajmeri, Denis Calin, Andrew Kim, Fabien Curto Millet, James Manyika

entry.summary: Google introduces the AI and Economy ATLAS, an economic measurement initiative built on 15 million de-identified interactions across the Gemini app, AI Mode and the Gemini API, mapped with privacy-preserving methods to more than 800 occupations, 4,000 tasks, 300 household activities, 150 countries and 140 languages. It reports that adoption spans occupations covering just over 88 percent of US employment while penetration within occupations remains uneven.

entry.title: A False Average: Chain-of-Thought Monitors Collapse Where They Are the Only Defense

author.name: Shikhar Shiromani, Leo Richter

entry.summary: This safety paper shows that rewriting only an agent's chain-of-thought to read as good-faith engineering, while copying every command and output verbatim so the exploit is unchanged, collapses a held-out monitor's catch rate from about 95 percent to under 11 percent in a single gradient-free attempt on the subset where reasoning is the only evidence. Aggregate monitor accuracy is therefore a false average dominated by hacks the actions already reveal, and the attack transfers across monitor families and agent settings.

entry.title: Beckmann Transport Models: From Autonomous Flows to One-Step Maps

author.name: Lee Cheuk-Kit, Florentin Coeurdoux, Peter Potaptchik, Yilun Du, Michael Samuel Albergo, Eric Vanden-Eijnden

entry.summary: Shows that when the target distribution lies on a lower-dimensional manifold, a time-independent (autonomous) velocity field can exactly transport between distributions, and the associated one-step generative map is the unique solution of a simple conservation equation learnable from samples. The framework connects flow matching to the flux constraint of Beckmann optimal transport and recovers Poisson flow and equilibrium matching as special cases.

entry.title: Why Large Language Models Fail at Tabular Prediction

author.name: Marta Garnelo, Wojciech M. Czarnecki

entry.summary: Systematically tests five candidate explanations for why frontier LLMs perform poorly at tabular prediction, using a pure in-context regime with the full training and test set in one prompt and no tools, scaffolding or fine-tuning. The study aims to establish the actual mechanism behind a failure that motivates the entire tabular foundation model field.

entry.title: Agentic Coding in the Wild: Characterizing GitHub Copilot Traces at Production Scale

author.name: Banruo Liu, Haoran Qiu, \'I\~nigo Goiri, Rodrigo Fonseca, Ricardo Bianchini, Esha Choukse

entry.summary: A production-scale characterization of AI coding agent workloads using sampled GitHub Copilot traces covering millions of users and trillions of tokens, showing sparse user turns that expand into long autonomous loops of LLM calls plus tool execution. Key findings include very high within-turn KV cache hit rates that collapse across turn boundaries, with direct implications for serving and caching design.

entry.title: High-Stakes Decisions with Language Models: Insights from Emergency Triage

author.name: Khurram Yamin, Christopher Kelly, Bryan Wilder, Eric Horvitz

entry.summary: Argues that LLM use in emergency triage should be cast in an explicit probabilistic decision framework where the model estimates outcome likelihoods and decisions incorporate declared utilities for different errors, rather than emitting recommendations with implicit values. Emergency triage serves as a case study for a broader decision-analytic paradigm for steering and evaluating models in high-stakes deployments.

entry.title: CN101 - A Digital Thermodynamic Computer for Generative AI

author.name: Lars Holdijk, Denis Melanson, Zier Mensch, Brandon Birchall, Vincent Cheung, Nicholas Lehrter, Maxwell Aifer, Samuel Duffield, Jan Ole Ernst, Rajath Salegame, Antonio J. Martinez, Gavin Crooks, Miranda Cheng, Zach Belateche, Marc Bright, Patrick J. Coles, Faris Sbahi

entry.summary: CN101 is a digital thermodynamic computer that realizes functions as the stationary expectation of an ergodic stochastic process, breaking the field's exclusive reliance on Langevin dynamics and thus on analog substrates with their engineering difficulties. The authors argue this equilibration-style computation is well matched to generative AI workloads and demonstrate a digital implementation.

entry.title: Why Does Action Chunking Improve Behavioral Cloning Performance in Robotic Control?

author.name: Filippo Lazzati, Kyle Stachowicz, William Chen, Alberto Maria Metelli, Andrew Wagenmaker, Sergey Levine

entry.summary: A rigorous empirical investigation of why action chunking helps behavioral cloning, testing and rejecting the common explanations of temporal consistency, horizon reduction, and representation learning. The authors find the real drivers are increased non-Markovian expressivity and reduced compounding error, with tradeoffs in some regimes.

entry.title: Orchard: An open framework for scalable agentic AI

author.name: Baolin Peng, Wenlin Yao, Qianhui Wu, Hao Cheng, Jianfeng Gao

entry.summary: Microsoft Research introduces Orchard, an open-source framework centered on a reusable environment service for training and evaluating agents across software engineering, GUI navigation, and assistant tasks, including inside real deployment harnesses. Reported results include roughly seventy percent on SWE-bench Verified with only about three billion active parameters, rising with value-model reranking, alongside released training data and evaluation methods.

entry.title: Context Compaction Theory

author.name: Hayder Tirmazi, Sam Markelon, Allison Bishop, Michael Mitzenmacher

entry.summary: Initiates formal analysis of context compaction in agents via two games: a Context Selection Game for algorithms that retain a subset of accumulated state and a Context Generation Game for algorithms that rewrite it. Gives theoretical characterizations of a technique that is ubiquitous in deployed agents yet previously unanalyzed.

entry.title: Exposed by Design: A Dynamic Security Assessment of Internet-Facing MCP Servers at Scale

author.name: Nicol\'as Padilla

entry.summary: This is a large-scale dynamic security audit of internet-exposed Model Context Protocol servers, discovering instances across eleven data sources and actively testing 414 confirmed production servers with a purpose-built framework covering ten MCP-specific vulnerability classes. It reports 68 reportable vulnerabilities including SQL injection and cloud-metadata SSRF, indicating systemic insecurity in deployed agent tooling.

entry.title: Cross-Benchmark Generalization in Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Sushant Mehta, Logan Ritchie, Liudas Panavas, Edwin Chen

entry.summary: The authors post-train an open-weight mixture-of-experts model (Qwen3.5-122B-A10B) with supervised fine-tuning followed by RL on 363 long-horizon Model Context Protocol tasks, then argue that in-distribution holdouts cannot distinguish transferable skill from exploitation of environment-specific regularities such as tool schemas and grader parsing. Cross-benchmark transfer is proposed as the correct behavioral test of whether agent RL taught real skill.

entry.title: Attackers Can Subliminally Implant a Backdoor at Low Sample Count Without Prompt Access

author.name: keshavs

entry.summary: Redwood Research experiments show that an attacker who controls only completions, not prompts, can implant a covert backdoor by altering the teacher for about one hundred completions, roughly half a percent of a fine-tuning set. The poisoned data survives simple filtering even when the defender knows the target behavior, and conditional backdoors appear to need far fewer subliminal-learning samples than unconditional behaviors.

entry.title: Demystifying When and Why VLAs Fail in Contact-Rich Tasks and How to Fix Them

author.name: Carlota Par\'es-Morlans, Nils Kuhn, Isabel Liu, Alberta Longhini, Jeannette Bohg

entry.summary: Diagnoses two root causes of vision-language-action failures in contact-rich manipulation: precision failures from a flow-matching policy training mismatch and force failures from the distinctive structure of force signals. The resulting FACT method raises average success from 41 to 66 percent across five contact-rich tasks.

entry.title: Large language models improve physician accuracy but lead to false reliance

author.name: Tirtha Chanda, Christoph Wies, Franziska Schramm, Carina Nogueira Garcia, Nicolas B. Merl, Martin J. Hetz, Jochen S. Utikal, Phillip Tschandl, Cristian Navarrete-Dechent, Alexander Thiem, Jakob N. Kather, Consortium, Titus J. Brinker

entry.summary: A study with 46 physicians using an agentic retrieval-augmented assistant found unaided accuracy rose from about 71 to 83 percent, with citations strongly predicting correctness. However citations created a dangerous asymmetry, sharply raising adoption of correct advice while also increasing acceptance of incorrect advice that appeared well supported.

entry.title: Why LLMs Give In: Conversational Factors and Reasoning Behind Medical Sycophancy

author.name: Kaike Ping, Buse \c{C}ar{\i}k, Caleb Wohn, Xiaohan Ding, Tongshuai Wang, Eugenia Rho

entry.summary: A fully crossed factorial study over 1.2 million trials, five open-weight models and 500 medical questions shows that sycophantic capitulation to false medical claims depends strongly on conversational factors such as user role, challenge timing, and whether evidence is in the prompt. Concludes sycophancy is a property of the conversation rather than a single per-model rate.

entry.title: Foundations of Reinforcement Learning and Control:Connections and New Perspectives

author.name: Claire Vernade, Onno Eberhard, Martha White, Florian D\"orfler, Csaba Szepesv\'ari, Miroslav Krstic, Michael Muehlebach

entry.summary: A tutorial bridging reinforcement learning and control theory, covering adaptive control and actor-critic methods and proposing a way to combine both paradigms on a classical locomotion control problem. It aims to make the two communities mutually legible by clarifying differences in goals, assumptions and guarantees.

entry.title: LongCat Sparse Attention: Taming the Lightning via Streaming-aware Hierarchical Cross-Layer Indexing

author.name: Wen Zan, Jiaqi Zhang, Jianchao Tan, Hong Liu, Cunguang Wang, Xiang Li, Duyue Ma, Guanyu Wu, Yifan Lu, Fengcun Li, Yerui Sun, Peng Pei, Yuchen Xie, Xunliang Cai

entry.summary: LongCat Sparse Attention co-designs algorithm and hardware to fix two bottlenecks in indexer-based sparse attention: it converts scattered key-value selections into contiguous, coalesced memory layouts and reuses one layer's index scores across multiple layers to amortize quadratic scoring cost. This targets practical deployment efficiency for long-context serving.

entry.title: AURORA-LM: Autoencoding Unified Representation for Continuous-Latent Diffusion Language Modeling

author.name: Jiajun Liang, Yucheng Liao, Yukang Cao, Jiazhe Wei, Ken Li, Wende Tan, Jiankun Zhang, ZY Cui, Jingkang Yang, Liucheng Guo, Shiqi Yang, B. Yang, Caifeng Shan, Ziwei Liu, Chenyang Si

entry.summary: AURORA-LM trains a continuous-latent diffusion language model by first building a high-capacity decodable text autoencoder and then fitting a diffusion model directly to that latent distribution, rather than compressing latents to make diffusion easier. It argues text is the last major modality still locked to discrete-token generation and shows a path to continuous-space text generation without sacrificing token-level fidelity.

entry.title: ReBRAC-v2: The Return of the King

author.name: Denis Tarasov, Robert K. Katzschmann

entry.summary: ReBRAC-v2 modernizes a simple behavior-regularized actor-critic for offline RL with a normalizing-flow actor trained by exact likelihood, mixed likelihood plus MSE plus MAE regularization, a classification-based residual critic, staged optimization and multi-sample test-time action selection, all under one shared configuration found by Bayesian search. Argues that careful modernization rivals expressive generative-policy and value-guidance methods.

entry.title: TabDPT-Turbo: Efficient In-Context Learning for Tabular Prediction

author.name: Rasa Hosseinzadeh, Alex Labach, Zexin Xue, Shuyi Han, Valentin Thomas, Anthony L. Caterini

entry.summary: TabDPT-Turbo keeps row-based attention and adds long-context pretraining to remove the need for retrieval at inference, plus architectural changes and self-supervised pretraining on a larger real-data corpus. It matches TabDPT v1.1 quality on TabArena-Lite, CC18 and CTR23 at orders-of-magnitude lower inference cost.

entry.title: Self-supervised DXA representations encode multi-system disease risk, biological aging and heritability

author.name: Gil Sasson, Zachary Levine, Smadar Shilo, Sarah Kohn, Guy Lutsker, Anastasia Godneva, Adam Gabet, David Krongauz, Adina Weinberger, Yann LeCun, Randall Balestriero, Eran Segal

entry.summary: LeDXA applies a joint-embedding predictive self-supervised architecture to whole-body bone-density scans, learning from about 11,500 unlabeled images and evaluating on roughly 47,400 external UK Biobank scans. The learned representations predict diseases, biomarkers, biological aging, and show heritability, outperforming scanner-derived measurements and a general-purpose self-supervised vision backbone.

entry.title: AdaMTP: An Adaptive Training Paradigm for Multi-Token Prediction

author.name: Ziqiang Cui, Han Shi, Bowei He, Yu Pan, Peiyang Liu, Shengyin Sun, Yankai Chen, Haoli Bai, Yichun Yin, Xue Liu, Chen Ma

entry.summary: AdaMTP makes multi-token prediction adaptive rather than fixed-horizon, arguing that forcing auxiliary heads to predict across high-entropy semantic boundaries injects conflicting gradients that propagate into the shared backbone and degrade core capabilities. The method varies the prediction horizon according to local information density in text and code.

entry.title: Attend to Your Own Thoughts: Breaking the Barrier for Post-Training Quantization of Reasoning LLMs through the Lens of 1.58-Bit Quantization

author.name: Shigeng Wang, Chao Li, Yangyuxuan Kang, Jiawei Fan, Anbang Yao

entry.summary: ScaleQ-1.58 shows that ternary post-training quantization of reasoning LLMs collapses on math and code when calibration ignores chain-of-thought, and fixes it by calibrating on reasoning traces and answers generated by the high-precision model itself. Enables scalable 1.58-bit PTQ where prior learned ternarization failed.

entry.title: RING: Retrieval-Internalized Generation for Continual Large-Scale Knowledge Injection

author.name: Shicheng Xu, Liang Pang, Liyi Chen, Zihao Wei, Jingcheng Deng, Yan Gao, Yi Wu, Yao Hu, Huawei Shen, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: RING replaces external retrieval with internalized parametric search: a mixture-of-memory-experts architecture absorbs large corpora via continued pretraining with a dual causal attention scheme, then supervised fine-tuning teaches search-then-answer and reinforcement learning with hierarchical rewards optimizes routing over internal memory. Aims for RAG-level factuality without retriever latency.

entry.title: Concrete Evaluations to Investigate the OpenAI Model That Hacked Hugging Face

author.name: Tim Hua

entry.summary: The post proposes a concrete battery of alignment evaluations that should be run on an OpenAI model or agent system that reportedly escaped its sandbox and attacked Hugging Face infrastructure to cheat a cyber evaluation. Proposed experiments probe whether the model knew the behavior was disapproved, how far it would escalate to claim success, and whether it weighs legal consequences.

entry.title: Concrete Evaluations to Investigate the OpenAI Model That Hacked Hugging Face

author.name: Tim Hua

entry.summary: Cross-posting of the alignment evaluation proposal for the OpenAI system that reportedly breached its sandbox and attacked Hugging Face during a cyber evaluation. It enumerates experiments on situational awareness, escalation limits, and sensitivity to consequences.

entry.title: No Single Neuron of Failure: Distributed Safety Alignment Against White-Box Attacks

author.name: Simiao Xie, Chuancheng Shi, Shangze Li, Wenhua Wu, Fei Shen, Ying Zhou, Zhiyong Wang, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Distributed Safety Alignment deliberately spreads safety behavior redundantly across many neurons at the down-projection inputs of feed-forward layers, so that white-box attackers who locate and ablate a few safety neurons cannot strip refusal behavior. It responds to the shift from black-box jailbreaks to neuron-level manipulation of open-weight models.

entry.title: Relax Within, Balance Across: Geometry-Guided Load Balancing for Vision-Language Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Ziang Wu, Peng Jin, Qishen Yin, Munan Ning, Hao Li, Peizhen Zhang, Li Yuan

entry.summary: The paper shows that standard token-level auxiliary load-balancing losses for vision-language mixture-of-experts models only balance the mixed token load, so large image and text imbalances can cancel out at one mix and the same router exhibits more than fivefold changes in imbalance across image resolutions. It derives the exact load curve as a function of token mix and proposes geometry-guided balancing that relaxes within-modality constraints while balancing across modalities.

entry.title: WorldExam: Benchmarking World Models from Apparent Appearance to Inherent Reactivity

author.name: Yuxue Yang, Shuyao Shang, Jiahe Wang, Zitong Zhou, Liang Tan, Junhan Zeng, Ruizhi Li, Junyan Li, Yu Liu, Xiao Yang, Yong Li, Jun Zhu, Hongsheng Li, Tieniu Tan, Lue Fan, Zhaoxiang Zhang

entry.summary: WorldExam is a hierarchical benchmark for controllable video generation as world modeling, testing four levels from visual quality and control adherence up to spatial consistency and world reactivity, where reactivity means inferring unstated physical consequences of a scene state. It argues existing benchmarks only check whether requested actions were rendered, not whether the depicted world behaves plausibly.

entry.title: Scoring Rules! Statistical and Strategic Alignment for Text Evaluation Metrics

author.name: Shengwei Xu, Yuxuan Lu, Yifan Wu, Jason Hartline, Grant Schoenebeck

entry.summary: Distinguishes statistical alignment of text evaluation metrics, meaning correlation with human ratings, from strategic alignment, meaning resistance to perturbations that add no task-relevant information, and proposes tests for the latter. As metrics increasingly serve as optimization targets, the paper shows correlation alone cannot certify a metric is not gameable.

entry.title: Post-Training on Office Work Improves Software Engineering: A Behavioral Account of Cross-Domain Transfer

author.name: Logan Ritchie, Sushant Mehta, Liudas Panavas, Edwin Chen

entry.summary: Post-trains an existing large Qwen mixture-of-experts model on 363 long-horizon multi-tool office workflow tasks containing no software-engineering data, and observes a 5.8-point pass@1 gain on SWE-Bench Pro. Matched trajectory analysis attributes the transfer to four goal-directed execution behaviors: goal selection, state construction, fidelity to higher objectives, and verification against the environment.

entry.title: FOCUS: FP4 Optimization via Coupled-Relaxation and Dual-Granularity Scaling

author.name: Xianglong Yan, Hong Liu, Chengzhu Bao, Tianao Zhang, Guanghua Yu, Jianchen Zhu, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: FOCUS is a post-training FP4 quantization method that decouples the quantization scale from the dequantization scale, observing that only the latter must conform to hardware formats like E8M0 since the former is never stored. It combines this coupled-relaxation insight with dual-granularity scaling to preserve accuracy in MXFP4 and NVFP4 deployment.

entry.title: Right Answer, Wrong Method: Shortcut Hacking Misleads the Evaluation of LLM Reasoning on Frontier Science Benchmarks

author.name: Xuan Ren, Weiqi Zhai, Tianle Pu, Yihua Zhu, Yihua Zhu, Hu Wei, Bing Zhao

entry.summary: Identifies solution hacking, where models reach correct final answers on hard science problems through enumeration, numerical search, guessing or answer-first verification rather than valid derivation. Reports that the rate climbs sharply with difficulty, reaching roughly 28 percent on Olympiad-level items and 37 percent on the hardest benchmark, undermining final-answer accuracy as a metric.

entry.title: Cross-Task Dissociation in Frontier Vision-Language Model Theory of Mind

author.name: Kejia Zhang, Youran Sun, Chugang Yi, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: Nine frontier vision-language models are tested on two psychology-derived theory-of-mind paradigms, the Keysar Director task and Frith-Happe animated triangles, revealing that models make the egocentric perspective error on 78 percent of Director trials without chain-of-thought (childlike rather than adultlike) while under-attributing intention from pure motion. The dissociation shows theory-of-mind profiles fragment across paradigms rather than forming a coherent capability.

entry.title: Robust Watermarks Meet Backdoored Models: Evading Diffusion Semantic Watermarks via Stealthy Backdoor

author.name: Jinyuan Liu, Tianshuo Cong, Pei Li, Tianrui Wang, Xinlei He, Anyu Wang, Xiaoyun Wang

entry.summary: GhostVAE plants a stealthy backdoor into the VAE encoder used in latent-diffusion image pipelines, first constructing a universal trigger via power-spectrum regularization for robustness and then training a parameter-aligned backdoored encoder that reliably evades semantic watermark detection. It exposes the detection pipeline's neural components as an underexplored attack surface for provenance systems.

entry.title: Temperature-driven inversion and nonlinear dynamics in ChatGPT-like AIs

author.name: Neil F. Johnson, Frank Yingjie Huo, Bella Xinrui Li

entry.summary: Empirical study of 12,000 long continuations from 11 chat models showing that raising decoder temperature eventually drives output entropy down rather than up, producing population inversion, frozen states, cycles and intermittency. The authors identify a hidden latent coordinate whose trajectory average predicts repetition in held-out runs.

entry.title: Measuring in-context algorithmic reasoning in language models against an exact Bayes-optimal standard

author.name: Hector Zenil, Luan Ozelim

entry.summary: F-ICL is an in-context-learning benchmark with an exact ground truth for correct inductive inference, built by exhaustively enumerating all 1.5 billion programs up to length 13 on a Turing-complete machine and computing the Bayes-optimal posterior in closed form under a bounded universal prior. Complement-paired tasks control for output-polarity bias, so models can be scored against a true optimum at matched evidence.

entry.title: Online Algorithms via Minimax and Posterior Matching

author.name: Thomas Kesselheim, Marco Molinaro, Kalen Patton, Sahil Singla

entry.summary: Develops a unifying minimax methodology for online algorithm design: worst-case competitive analysis is reduced via Yao's principle to Bayesian online design, and a single posterior-matching rule that tracks the conditional expectation of the hindsight-optimal solution recovers optimal or near-optimal competitive ratios across problems. It replaces many problem-specific ad hoc arguments with one principle.

entry.title: Bicycle Acrobatics with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shamel Fahmi, Arianna Ilvonen, Samuel Zapolsky, Yu-Ming Chen, Ravi Boggavarapu, Paul Drews, Ashwin Khadke, Dean Molinaro, Kaiyu Zheng, Alfred Rizzi, Gabriel Nelson

entry.summary: This paper uses reinforcement learning to teach a bicycle robot a broad repertoire of acrobatic maneuvers including forward and lateral table jumps, front flips, kip-ups, wheelies, bunny hops, and three-point turns, using several RL formulations from waypoint following to motion imitation. An orchestrator composes the individual policies through state-dependent transitions.

entry.title: Reusing Rollouts under Policy Lag: Prefix-Normalized Policy Optimization for LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Wenhao Zhang, Yibo Xie, Rui Wang, Jiahua Yang, Lei Jiang, Zibo Yang, Yawei Wang, Jiali Xu, jasperawang, Haoyang Long, Huan Xiong, alantzhao

entry.summary: Prefix-Normalized Policy Optimization reuses expensive rollout batches for multiple learner updates by replacing the exploding cumulative importance ratio with the geometric mean of per-token likelihood ratios along each causal prefix. This keeps prefix dependence in the correction while taming variance, cutting the dominant rollout cost in LLM reinforcement learning.

entry.title: One QK Channel, Many Sources: Guarding Low-Precision Attention Collapse

author.name: Shuxiao Xie, Shuyang Xie, Yuan Cao, Dezhi Ran, Wei Yang, Tao Xie

entry.summary: Investigates abrupt bfloat16 training collapse in GPT-2-class models, localizing a reproduced failure to the streaming-softmax accumulator and showing that errors injected anywhere still funnel through the same query-key spectral runaway. Correcting only the query-key path keeps training stable even with the original fault active, dissociating fault source from failure channel.

entry.title: Linguistic Context Recodes Visual Representations in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Brian Song, Michael A. Lepori, Ellie Pavlick

entry.summary: Shows that vision-language models do not treat visual representations as static: goal-directed language induces an abstract representation of which objects are task-relevant and reshapes how visual features are encoded. This challenges the common view that language merely reads out fixed visual embeddings.

entry.title: Long-term Measurements: Towards a Longitudinal Understanding of Human-AI Interactions

author.name: Nicole Mitchell, Dhruv Agarwal, Maty Bohacek, Remi Denton, Roma Patel

entry.summary: Argues NLP evaluation must move from static short-horizon text scoring to longitudinal measurement of cognitive, developmental and socio-affective changes in users of human-like language models. Draws on social-science measurement instruments to propose a research agenda for diachronic study of human-model interaction.

entry.title: What Transfers from Text to Vision? Capability Scaling Laws and Transfer Dynamics for VLMs

author.name: Ziran Li, Qiang Wang, Zhengyu Chen, Shanglin Lei, Borun Chen, Jingang Wang, Xunliang Cai

entry.summary: Proposes a capability-driven scaling law that predicts vision-language model benchmark accuracy from a low-dimensional PCA score over the backbone LLM's text benchmarks, plus per-backbone transfer and data-absorption rates. Offers a cross-family way to choose an LLM backbone before training a VLM, where compute-based scaling laws fail.

entry.title: The Gate, Not the Cache: Gate Provenance Bounds the Closed-Loop Reliability of Training-Free VLA Token Skipping

author.name: Qi Luo, Shuaijun Liu, Hao Zhao, Kunlin Li, Xiaobo Wang, Ningxing Su, Dongsheng Wang, Yun Chen

entry.summary: This study shows that training-free token skipping in vision-language-action robot policies fails catastrophically in closed loop when the gate deciding which tokens to skip is computed from the previous accelerated forward pass, because skipped tokens are exactly the ones the next gate cannot see, and the damage compounds. At a 0.9 skip ratio on LIBERO-Object, success drops to 0.68 under reuse and 0.31 under deletion.

entry.title: MedUPS: Towards Diagnostic Assistance in Uncommon Medical Cases with Large Language Models

author.name: Ofir Ben Shoham, Oriel Perets, Nir Grinberg, Nadav Rappoport

entry.summary: Introduces MedUPSQA, roughly 21.9k mid-stream clinical decision points derived from 5.5k real rare-case reports, plus an alignment framework that supervises models on next-action decisions rather than only final diagnoses. Targets the gap where medical LLM benchmarks ignore sequential management under uncertainty.

entry.title: Dense Language Generation Made Simple: Deterministic, Randomized, and Multi-Order Algorithms

author.name: Ziyi Cai, Shuangping Li, Yiheng Shen, Kangning Wang, Peng Zhang

entry.summary: Provides simpler deterministic, randomized and multi-order algorithms for language generation in the limit, where a generator must eventually output only unseen valid strings from an adversarially enumerated unknown language. It works within the lower-density coverage framework recently introduced by Kleinberg and Wei.

entry.title: Why Formal Monitors Fail: Attack Distribution Entropy as a Coverage Bound for LTL-Based LLM Agent Safety

author.name: Ruiyang Zhang

entry.summary: Explains why linear-temporal-logic and finite-automaton runtime monitors for LLM agent tool calls achieve 68 to 75 percent attack coverage on some models and nearly zero on others, proving that recall of any fixed-invariant monitor is bounded by the concentration of the attack distribution. Low-entropy attack distributions permit small invariant sets; dispersed attacks defeat them.

entry.title: Language Equality has a Price: A Systematic Investigation of Multi-turn LLM Performance for EU-24+

author.name: Sherzod Hakimov, Karl Osswald, Jelle Psurek, Eszter Bukovszky, A. Altar L\"user, David Schlangen

entry.summary: Evaluates nine open-weight and commercial models in self-play goal-directed dialogue games across 30 languages including all 24 official EU languages, using multi-turn programmatic scoring rather than static or preference benchmarks. Commercial systems outscore every open-weight model in every official language, including well-resourced ones, and the weakest open models average below 40 points.

entry.title: Learning What to Remember: Test-Time Training via Context Distillation

author.name: Zixuan Wang, Xingyu Dang, Rui-Jie Zhu, Zixin Wen, Hengyu Fu, Wenhao Chai, Jason D. Lee

entry.summary: Test-Time Context Distillation reframes test-time training for long context as a memory-allocation problem: a long-window teacher supervises the fast weights of a short-window student so that retained information is chosen for future usefulness rather than mere reconstruction. This adds a forward-looking objective that prior TTT methods lacked.

entry.title: OpenART: Scaling Agent Red Teaming via Open-Ended Environment Evolution

author.name: Yunhao Chen, Xin Wang, Yixu Wang, Yi Liu, Jie Li, Yan Teng, Xingjun Ma, Xia Hu, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: Presents an open-ended red teaming arena for AI agents built on evolving stateful environments, with over 10,000 validated scenarios across 50 domains, half a million tools, and tasks requiring roughly a hundred tool calls each. Targets cumulative long-horizon risks that short static safety benchmarks miss.

entry.title: Cross-Domain Hybrid OPD for Generalizable Search Agents

author.name: Hongzhan Chen, Xiaoyu Liu, Dengming Zhang, Minzhou Huang, Dongliang Xu, Jingcheng Xie, Dongxiang Fang, Bowen Qin, Minsheng Hao, Yaozong Shen, Xiaojun Quan, Mona Zhou, Haosheng Zou, Jeff Chen

entry.summary: Technical report on the training framework behind a deployed consumer search agent built on the Hunyuan3 architecture, combining agentic reinforcement learning with cross-domain hybrid on-policy distillation to avoid the alignment tax of search specialization. The claim is search-specialized behavior without regression in general assistant capability.

entry.title: Where Does Generative Difficulty Reside? An Empirical Study of Target Representations

author.name: Marcel Plocher, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, Andreas Geiger, Gege Gao

entry.summary: An empirical study comparing raw pixels, VAE latents, DINOv2 features, and masked-autoencoder representation-autoencoder features as target spaces for a unified masked autoregressive rectified-flow image generator under matched ImageNet compute. It finds distinct optimization and inference regimes, with semantic features converging fastest but requiring wider local denoisers and direct context fusion.

entry.title: Uncovering and Mitigating Positional Blind Spots in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Dongdong An, Pengjie Zhao, Yihao Huang, Wenbing Tang, Ziming He, Jiayi Zhu, Jifeng Ning, Qin Zhao

entry.summary: The paper shows that vision-language-action policies have spatially localized regions of the workspace where success collapses simply because a task-irrelevant distractor moved, which the authors call positional blind spots. A black-box statistical test locates these regions and a mitigation stage reduces them.

entry.title: Ego2Robot: Scalable Robot Data Synthesis from Egocentric Human Data

author.name: Ye Wang, Pei Lin, Xiong-Hui Chen, Haoqi Yuan, Zhixuan Liang, Yiyang Huang, Anzhe Chen, Zixing Lei, Jie Zhang, Tao Zhang, Haoyang Li, Tong Zhang, Chenxi Xiao, Ziyuan Jiao, Qin Jin

entry.summary: Ego2Robot is a pipeline converting egocentric human manipulation video into robot-format training data via action retargeting, robot-arm visual synthesis, and multi-level quality curation, yielding over eighteen thousand trajectories. It tests whether such synthesized data provides pretraining benefit for VLA models at scale, not just per-task policies.

entry.title: OpenAI’s Unreleased Model Astra Solves Ten Major Open Mathematics Problems

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Commentary on an OpenAI announcement that an internal unreleased model produced new results on ten open mathematics problems, including sphere-packing bounds and improved binary and spherical code bounds, with arguments formalized in Lean. The post emphasizes the modest token cost and the pace of improvement in machine mathematical reasoning.

entry.title: Import AI 467: Self-sustaining AI viruses; pacing AI progress; confusion about AI and creativity

author.name: Jack Clark

entry.summary: Jack Clark newsletter issue covering a prototype self-sustaining computer worm from Toronto, Vector Institute, Cambridge, and ServiceNow researchers that compromises machines and then uses their GPUs to run open-weight LLMs for its own reasoning and further spread. The issue also discusses pacing AI progress and disputes about AI and creativity.

entry.title: CurveShift: Is Agent Progress Scalar? Separating Level from Shape

author.name: Hanwen Xing, Pengyun Wang, BingXu Meng, Kumail Alhamoud, Xiang Li, Jicheng Wang, Xin Yu, Xinyang Han, Xiaomin Li, Philip Torr, Yuexing Hao

entry.summary: Questions whether scalar summaries such as time horizons or aggregate scores capture how model progress is distributed across task difficulty, separating overall ability level from the shape of the difficulty-response curve. Reanalyzing METR time-horizon data, a single Rasch model with rising ability reproduces the apparent shift of gains toward harder tasks, suggesting ceiling effects rather than qualitative capability change.

entry.title: FactorJEPA: Factorizing Monolithic Futures into Layout-Agent-Interaction Channels for Crowded and Chaotic Global South Urban Worlds

author.name: Kapil Wanaskar, Gaytri Jena, Aman Chadha, Vinija Jain, Vasu Sharma, Amitava Das

entry.summary: Introduces DENSEWORLD, a 1,000-hour video dataset of dense, unstructured Global South urban traffic, plus FactorJEPA, a joint-embedding predictive world model that splits future prediction into separate layout, agent, and interaction channels. It targets a regime that existing lane-structured driving benchmarks largely ignore, where occlusion, agent heterogeneity, and social negotiation dominate.

entry.title: Humans Are More Diverse: Frontier LLMs Show Extreme Policies in Idealised AI Development Races

author.name: Phu Hoa Pham, Duy Minh Dao Sy, Trung Kiet Huynh, Phu Quy Nguyen Lam, Chi Nguyen Tran, Minh Trung Le, Phong Hao Le, Dinh Nam Nguyen, Thien Ky Nguyen Dong, Elias Fernandez Domingos, Le Hong Trang, The Anh Han

entry.summary: Studies how frontier LLM agents behave in repeated idealized AI development race games where speed trades off against catastrophic risk, adding an audit gate that first checks whether models actually understand the rules, state, and payoffs before interpreting their choices. It finds LLMs cluster at extreme all-safe or all-risky policies while human data and evolutionary benchmarks show far more strategic diversity.

entry.title: MineGrad: Gradient Inversion Attacks on LoRA Fine-Tuning

author.name: Hasin Us Sami, Swapneel Sen, Basak Guler

entry.summary: MineGrad demonstrates analytical gradient inversion attacks that reconstruct private training data from the low-rank adapter gradients users share during federated LoRA fine-tuning, under a malicious server that tampers with the protocol. It challenges the common assumption that sharing only small parameter-efficient updates is privacy-protective.

entry.title: Salami Attack: Stealthy Collusive Memory Poisoning against OpenClaw

author.name: Zheng Lin, Yuzhe Huang, Zhenxing Niu, Xianmin Ye, Haichang Gao

entry.summary: MemCollusion automates red-teaming of persistent agent memory by slicing an adversarial goal into fragments that each look harmless but jointly steer the agent into unsafe behavior, a salami-style compositional poisoning attack. It shows that defenses screening individual memory records miss threats that only emerge from combinations.

entry.title: Rewriting or Reweighting? A Geometric Account in Language Models

author.name: Juntong Wang, Shengkun Yang, Xiyuan Wang, Muhan Zhang

entry.summary: Asks whether post-training removes a mechanism, creates a new one, or merely reweights an inherited one, studying repetition as a decoding attractor and sycophancy as an alignment failure. Behavioral manifold analysis selects sparse behavior-associated coordinates and builds low-dimensional charts in both runtime activation space and a routing-strength space to separate rewriting from reweighting.

entry.title: Diagnosing Search Behavior and Failure Modes in Long-Horizon Search Agents

author.name: Qi Liu, Jiaxin Mao, Fengbin Zhu, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Uses human-annotated document relevance judgments to diagnose long-horizon deep search agents step by step, separating what evidence they retrieve from how well they use it, and thereby decomposing failures into retrieval gaps and utilization gaps. This directly tests whether more search effort actually produces better answers.

entry.title: EduZone: A Framework for Evaluating LLM Safety for K-12 Students and Teachers

author.name: Junyeong Park, Jieun Han, Haneul Yoo, So-Yeon Ahn, Jinsung Yoon, Alice Oh

entry.summary: EduZone is a safety evaluation framework for LLMs in K-12 settings, generating contextually grounded adversarial interactions across student and teacher usage contexts, curriculum concepts, and 6 risk categories with 28 subcategories. It covers single-turn, static multi-turn and interactive settings including education-specific harms.

entry.title: CMuon: Accelerating and Stabilizing Diffusion Transformer Training via Chunked Momentum Orthogonalization

author.name: Chuyan Chen, Peng Sun, Kun Yuan

entry.summary: Diagnoses why the Muon orthogonalized-momentum optimizer converges poorly late in Diffusion Transformer training, attributing it to implicit subspace coupling when functionally distinct weights are fused into single tensors such as AdaLN and QKV projections. CMuon chunks momentum orthogonalization along these functional boundaries to restore stable acceleration.

entry.title: Magnet: Detecting Cross-Session AI Misuse Through Capability Accumulation

author.name: Natalie Isak, Matthew Dressman

entry.summary: Magnet targets attackers who decompose a harmful objective into innocuous steps executed across separate agentic sessions, exploiting the fact that the system is stateless between conversations while the attacker is not. Proposes detection based on accumulation of capability across sessions rather than single-session content.

entry.title: Response Magnitude as a Dominant Signal for Held-Out CRISPRi Perturbation Effect Prediction

author.name: Mehrdad Shoeibi, Niloofar Yousefi

entry.summary: The authors show that predicting CRISPRi perturbation effect magnitude on held-out genes in the Virtual Cell Challenge benchmark is dominated by four simple deterministic scalar statistics of the input, so deep encoders with full input access collapse onto that low-dimensional signal. This explains why simple baselines match deep perturbation predictors and questions what these benchmarks actually measure.

entry.title: Native Multilingual Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Low-Resource Southeast Asian Languages

author.name: Sean Gip Lim, William Chandra Tjhi, Hai Leong Chieu

entry.summary: OSCD is a post-training method that projects high-resource reasoning trajectories into low-resource vocabulary subspaces during generative rollouts through an integrated translator loop, aiming to stop models from silently reverting to English mid-reasoning in Southeast Asian languages. It targets the cold-start bottleneck for policy optimization and the representation drift that causes catastrophic forgetting under naive fine-tuning.

entry.title: Crushing the Evidence: A Dual-Penalty Evasion Framework for Fooling White-Box Explainable AI Auditors

author.name: Niraj Kumar, Harsh Kasyap

entry.summary: This paper presents a dual-penalty optimization attack that fools white-box explainability auditors such as LIME, SHAP and Integrated Gradients without the out-of-distribution scaffolding that current defenses detect, so hidden biases or backdoors survive explanation-based audits. It shows that existing anomaly-footprint defenses do not generalize to gradient-level evasion.

entry.title: Latency-Tolerant Cloud-Edge Collaborative Vision-Language-Action Models via Emergent Representational Specialization

author.name: Daojie Peng, Fulong Ma, Bingtao Wang, Sheng Wang, Jun Ma

entry.summary: CloudEdgeVLA splits a vision-language-action policy so that a large cloud model encodes delayed observations into slowly varying task features while a lightweight on-robot head fuses the latest available cloud feature with current local vision, training with randomly delayed features so the system learns latency tolerance without explicit delay cues or scheduling. It reframes network jitter as a representation-learning problem.

entry.title: Adversarial Attacks in Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines: Unveiling Structural Vulnerabilities in Agentic AI Architectures

author.name: Faisal Haque Bappy, Tahrim Hossain, Tarannum Shaila Zaman, Raiful Hasan, Kamrul Hasan, Tariqul Islam

entry.summary: This paper argues that multi-agent LLM pipelines are structurally vulnerable because they lack boundary verification, so once one agent accepts adversarial content it propagates as trusted input across agents, and it characterizes attack classes arising from that implicit trust in content, identity, execution intent and state integrity. It proposes boundary verification as the missing security primitive.

entry.title: WAM-Diff2: Hierarchical AR-to-Diffusion Distillation for Highly Efficient Autonomous Driving VLA

author.name: Zhihao Zhu, Hanlin Shang, Mingwang Xu, Feipeng Cai, Zhuolin He, Yaoyi Li, Jianhua Han, Hang Xu, Siyu Zhu

entry.summary: Distills a pretrained autoregressive driving vision-language-action model into a parallel diffusion policy through a hierarchical procedure that bridges mismatched attention patterns. Aims to combine multi-task reasoning with low-latency parallel action decoding for end-to-end autonomous driving.

entry.title: Question Begets Question: Self-Evolving Curriculum for Reinforcement Fine-Tuning on Competition Mathematics

author.name: Longtian Bao, Jianyou Wang, Yang Zhang, Youze Zheng, Ramamohan Paturi

entry.summary: Question-begets-Question has a teacher model transform existing competition math problems into diverse variants probing the same skills, then trains a 7B math model purely with reinforcement learning and no oracle reasoning traces, starting from 5.6 percent pass@1 on AIME. Studies whether apparent performance ceilings reflect data scarcity rather than model capacity.

entry.title: Antares: Foundation Models for Agentic Vulnerability Localization

author.name: Supriti Vijay, Aman Priyanshu, Didier Chapoteau, Arthur Goldblatt, Jianliang He, Kimia Majd, Fraser Burch, Baturay Saglam, Takahiro Matsumoto, Zhuoran Yang, Amin Karbasi

entry.summary: Introduces Antares, a family of small (350M-3B) code security models built on IBM Granite and trained with supervised fine-tuning on cybersecurity reasoning plus reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards over real vulnerable repositories. The 3B model reportedly approaches a frontier proprietary model on agentic vulnerability localization while beating open-weight models over 200x larger, enabling cheap local security scanning.

entry.title: Verifier-Induced Support Reshaping in On-Policy Optimization

author.name: Shaohang Wei, Zikun Su, Feifan Song, Wen Luo, Wei Li, Guangyue Peng, Houfeng Wang

entry.summary: Identifies verifier-induced support reshaping: on-policy RL with verifiable rewards can improve the current objective while making trajectories needed for later objectives so rare they can no longer be sampled or reinforced. Bidirectional experiments on math and constrained instruction following across two model families show sequential RLVR shrinking the set of prompts with any successful rollout.

entry.title: Progressive Agent Skill Generation via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Junhao Shen, Zhanqiu Zhang, Yiwen Guo, Hong Cheng

entry.summary: Skill-alpha treats agent skill library construction as a sequential editing process trained with reinforcement learning, where the reward is whether generated skills actually improve downstream agent behavior rather than a heuristic relevance signal. This replaces hand-designed consolidation pipelines with a unified learned approach across heterogeneous evidence sources.

entry.title: DART: Decoded Attention over Recurrent States for Efficient Long-Context Sequence Modeling

author.name: Yixiao Qian, Song Chen, Pengkai Wang, Jiaxu Liu, Shengze Cai, Chao Xu

entry.summary: DART builds on the state-space duality view of Mamba-2, arguing the recurrent state can serve as a compressed key-value cache from which attention-style keys, not just values, can be decoded. This yields a single shared memory supporting both recurrent compression and attention-like retrieval for efficient long-context modeling.

entry.title: GradCuit: Credit-Assigned Gradient Flow Enables Robust and Interpretable Test-Time Latent Reasoning

author.name: Zhaoxin Yu, Qi Shen, Hengli Li, Zhaowei Zhang, Song-Chun Zhu, Chi Zhang, Zilong Zheng

entry.summary: GradCuit inserts optimizable latent states at a chosen transformer layer between prompt and continuation representations so that every generated token log-probability has a differentiable path back to the latent states through causal attention. This gives direct sequence-level credit assignment for test-time latent reasoning while parameters stay frozen.

entry.title: Causal Inference with Unstructured Treatments

author.name: Kevin Christian Wibisono, Yixin Wang

entry.summary: Reformulates causal inference when the treatment is an unstructured object such as text or an image, arguing that the classical average treatment effect between two exact treatment values is both unestimable and uninformative in this regime. It proposes alternative estimands that describe which attributes of the unstructured treatment drive outcome changes.

entry.title: When Collaboration Becomes a Trigger: Collective Evidence-Threshold Backdoors in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Jia-Hao Xiao, Lei Feng, Min-Ling Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces a backdoor threat model for LLM multi-agent systems in which malicious behavior triggers only after accumulated peer evidence crosses a hidden threshold, so no single message is incriminating. It also proposes a clean-data-only defense that monitors latent transitions at test time to detect the crossing.

entry.title: LiveMem: Maintaining Memory State Continuity in Long-Running LLM Inference

author.name: Zhichen Liu, Ruihan Sun, Hengjie Yang, Zipeng Wu, Zhaohan Chen, Xiaofan Zhang, Yang Xu

entry.summary: Formulates the problem of maintaining a persistent memory state in long-running LLM agents whose active context keeps turning over, and proposes an intrinsic memory module attached to a pretrained full-attention model with a bounded KV window. Aims for lifelong continuity of computation rather than mere retrieval of past text.

entry.title: Optimal Unambiguous DNFs and Alon-Saks-Seymour

author.name: Chirag Pabbaraju

entry.summary: Constructs unambiguous DNF formulas with a quadratic gap between width and zero-certificate complexity and lifts them to communication problems with a constant-size gadget. Yields an optimal refutation of the Alon-Saks-Seymour conjecture and optimal lower bounds for clique versus independent set communication.

entry.title: Does Accuracy Equal Evidence? Reasoning Faithfulness under KV Cache Compression

author.name: Mengting Ai, Jingrui He, Yue Guo

entry.summary: Tests the common assumption that KV cache compression preserving final-answer accuracy also preserves the reasoning that supports it. Using a fixed-trace replay protocol over ten token-eviction methods plus quantization on three models and four task families, the authors show answer correctness and rationale validity can degrade at different rates.

entry.title: A Unified Kullback--Leibler Divergence Analysis of Generative Diffusion Models via Entropy Production Rate

author.name: Han Wu, Zhiwen Zhang

entry.summary: This work builds a unified error analysis for diffusion generative models by integrating the entropy production rate of the forward-reverse process pair, decomposing terminal KL divergence into initialization, score approximation, and discretization error. Working at the marginal rather than path-space level yields a sharper second-order convergence rate for the Euler-Maruyama sampler.

entry.title: When Memory Becomes Authority: Benchmarking Authority Collapse at the Memory Consolidation Boundary

author.name: Qiuyang Zhan, Rui Zhang, Sheng Guo, Lepeng Zhao, Zhuotao Liu

entry.summary: Identifies authority collapse, where memory consolidation preserves a claim but discards the source constraints that limited how it may be used, so a casual remark can later act as a standing instruction or attested fact. AuthMem-Bench holds claim and task fixed while varying only source authority to measure this failure in self-evolving agents.

entry.title: Deferred Exposure of Future Trajectories for Verifiable Reasoning in Autonomous Driving VLMs

author.name: Zixuan Huang, Yang Zhou, Kaixuan Wang, Guli Zhang, Hongyan Xie, Yakun Zhu, Hao Geng, Yikun Ban, Deqing Wang

entry.summary: Shows empirically that annotating chain-of-thought for driving vision-language-action models while exposing the teacher to the logged ground-truth future trajectory induces trajectory anchoring bias, where the teacher rationalizes the known outcome instead of reasoning from scene evidence, worsening hallucination in causally hard scenes. The proposed remedy defers trajectory exposure so high-level decisions are inferred before trajectory details enter.

entry.title: SearchMaster: Grounded and Regulated Self-Play for Search Agents

author.name: Wentao Tan, Qiong Cao, Jiaqi Wang, Nan Duan

entry.summary: SearchMaster trains a single search agent purely through self-play in a local search environment, generating, solving, and verifying its own multi-hop tasks without human demonstrations or a stronger teacher. Three controls counter self-play pathologies: filtering pseudo multi-hop questions, difficulty estimation that accounts for required search depth, and penalizing rollouts that open many pages without acquiring targeted evidence.

entry.title: EEG-JEPA: Structured Latent Prediction for EEG Foundation Models

author.name: Jinhao Li, Zhiyuan Ma, Xueqiao Han, Zhongye Xia, Xinche Zhang, Shanghong Xie, Yixuan Liu, Yongjian Li, Runmin Gan, Tianlin Huo, Sen Song

entry.summary: EEG-JEPA replaces masked waveform reconstruction with joint-embedding latent prediction for EEG foundation models, arguing that reconstructing noisy voltages teaches models to recover artifacts and background activity rather than transferable neural structure. A masked context encoder predicts targets from an exponential-moving-average teacher.

entry.title: Interpretability-Guided Soft Pruning of Attention Heads in Vision Transformers

author.name: Kamil Ksi\k{a}\.zek, Piotr Suszy\'nski, Micha{\l} Jan W{\l}odarczyk, Jacek Tabor, Przemys{\l}aw Biecek

entry.summary: This work spectrally analyzes and visualizes individual vision-transformer attention heads via Laplacian eigenvectors of their attention maps, clusters heads semantically to find functional redundancy, and then uses those insights in SAPER, a differentiable soft top-k pruning framework. It offers interpretability-guided compression of large vision foundation models such as DINOv2.

entry.title: Auditable Release Control for Pedagogical Leakage in LLM Tutors

author.name: Nizam Kadir

entry.summary: This paper formalizes pedagogical leakage, where an LLM tutor is helpful and correct but reveals answers or decisive reasoning before disclosure is authorized, and enforces an authorization-aware complete-mediation boundary with five disclosure contracts, trusted policy gates and a single inspectable release function. Using 599 fixed proposals from an existing Gemini 3.5 model, strict mediation trades measurable utility for large reductions in leakage, with replayable traces attributing failures to selection, generation, verification or enforcement.

entry.title: Can Humans Dream of Electric Sheep? Human-Written Samples for Fine-Grained Vision-and-Language Hallucination Benchmarking

author.name: Timothee Mickus, Claudio Savelli, Eduardo Cal\`o, Emilio Raimond, Stella Frank, Hengyu Luo, Flavio Giobergia, Vincent Segonne, Chuyuan Li, Aman Sinha, Lorenzo Vaiani, J\"org Tiedemann, Ra\'ul V\'azquez

entry.summary: Builds a dataset of 1,600 human-written hallucination samples across four languages plus 18,400 model-generated samples, all with span-level hallucination annotations, to test whether human-authored samples can make hallucination benchmarks model-agnostic and durable. Finds human samples yield higher annotator agreement and better content control while remaining distributionally similar.

entry.title: Credit the Right Box: Marginal Contribution Assignment for Structured Visual Perception

author.name: Xinheng Han, Jianfei Wang, Yu Chen, Xiang Wang, Shuai Li, Weixing Li, Feng Pan

entry.summary: MCR-GRPO fixes the granularity mismatch in group-relative RL for multi-object visual grounding by computing marginal-contribution rewards per predicted box instead of broadcasting one response-level advantage to all tokens. Targets tasks needing cardinality preservation and precise localization in multimodal LLMs.

entry.title: Rethinking Personalized Reward Modeling for LLMs under Preference Heterogeneity via Group-Debiased Federated Learning

author.name: Seongyoon Kim, Boryeong Cho, Jihwan Oh, Seokhyun Chung, Se-Young Yun

entry.summary: Challenges the assumption that heterogeneous user preferences require clustering clients and training one reward model per group in federated reward modeling, showing that a single FedAvg model with balanced preference groups plus local personalization outperforms group-specific initialization. Proposes group-debiased federated learning for personalized reward models.

entry.title: HindSearch: Trajectory-Level Hindsight Critique for Search-Augmented Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haowei Liu, Jiamian Wang, Hsin-Tai Wu, Zhiqiang Tao, Yi Fang

entry.summary: HindSearch improves search-augmented RL by having a frozen judge write short hindsight critiques of failed rollouts using the gold answer, then distilling those critiques into on-policy supervision of the student's search actions instead of discarding failures under binary exact-match reward. It reaches 39.4 percent average exact match on a seven-benchmark suite with a 3B model, and ablating gold-answer access removes most of the gain.

entry.title: Secrets Everywhere: Auditing Memorization in Mobility Prediction Models

author.name: Anne Josiane Kouam, Hristo Boyadzhiev, Konrad Rieck

entry.summary: First systematic audit of memorization in human mobility prediction models, measuring how training trajectories can be extracted at different spatial and temporal granularities. It shows privacy leakage is pervasive rather than incidental in next-location models.

entry.title: LoopsBench: From Harness Engineering to Loop Engineering in Benchmarking Coding Agent

author.name: Han Li, Zhemin Fang, Rili Feng, Yingqi Zhao, Jiaheng Liu, Pengfei Gao, He Ye, Dayi Lin, Qingwei Lin, Saravan Rajmohan, Dongmei Zhang

entry.summary: LoopsBench evaluates coding agents on sustained long-horizon development, structuring each of 112 tasks as a dependency graph of separately testable units with a runtime that releases tests along the ready frontier and keeps completed nodes as regression obligations. It shifts evaluation from single-shot harness engineering toward the loop behavior of agents doing continuous software work.

entry.title: Invisible Ink Threats: Adversarial Goals Behind Legitimate Tasks in Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Jia-Chen Zhang, Ze-Yu Zhang, Kai-Wei Zhang

entry.summary: Identifies a blind spot in computer-use agent defenses: injected goals that are individually low-harm, such as starring a repository or installing a package, look like normal task steps and slip past both model safety filters and human-in-the-loop confirmation. Builds a systematic evaluation of these stealthy prompt-injection attacks.

entry.title: PRISM: Privileged Probabilistic Latent Supervision for End-to-End Autonomous Driving Motion Planning

author.name: Volodymyr Havrylov, Faris Janjo\v{s}, Andreas Look, J\"urgen Mathes, Andreas Geiger

entry.summary: PRISM investigates why adding vision-language model supervision to latent features helps end-to-end driving planners, and finds the gains come not from VLM reasoning but from forming latent connections between hidden layers and privileged information. It then proposes a probabilistic privileged latent supervision scheme that captures the benefit directly.

entry.title: Look Where It Matters: Adaptive Visual Refinement for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Jin Cui, Yanbin Hu, Xinyue Long, Linkai Li, Boran Zhao, Pengju Ren

entry.summary: AtVLA shows that vision encoders inside VLA policies suffer the same attention-artifact problem documented in generic vision transformers, and that spatial information spills into low-information patch tokens during embodied post-training. Adding learnable register tokens, trained only on embodied data, recovers spatially precise representations.

entry.title: Reputation-driven Cooperation in Lattice-based Decentralized Federated Learning through Evolutionary Game Theory

author.name: Phuc Hoang Truong Huynh, Dung Tran Vinh, Khoa Duc Anh Lam, An Nghiem Nguyen Truong, Uyen Nha Tran Bui, Khang Nguyen Dinh, Bao Nguyen Le Gia, Minh Le Nguyen Nhat, Manh Hong Duong, The Anh Han, Thi Ai Thao Nguyen, and Le Hong Trang

entry.summary: Introduces PATH-Bench, which evaluates lifelong LLM agents by explicitly controlling the path of accumulated experience, building probe-centered task sequences with deliberately helpful or interfering histories. It reports forward transfer, backward transfer, and forgetting for eight agents on code generation and multi-turn tool use, exposing order effects that static benchmarks hide.

entry.title: LaCache: Robust Semantic Caching for LLM Serving

author.name: Jiacheng Liang, Yuhui Wang, Tanqiu Jiang, Ting Wang

entry.summary: LaCache defends semantic caching in LLM serving against cache-collision attacks, where an adversary injects crafted queries to poison cached responses served to later legitimate users. Its key insight is that an attacker controls the query but not the response, which must satisfy multiple semantic constraints, so validation should consider response-side consistency.

entry.title: REFLEX: Rethinking MoE Inference as Refinement-Aware Compute Allocation in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Xiang Xia, Cheng Yan, Yiming Zhang, Jiazheng Liu, Hongyu Zhang, Wuyang Zhang

entry.summary: Observes that in diffusion language models each denoising pass revisits every token position even though positions differ sharply in how much refinement they still need, while default mixture-of-experts routing gives them a uniform expert budget. REFLEX reframes MoE inference as refinement-aware compute allocation across heterogeneous token states.

entry.title: Can You Trust the Confidence? ConfBench for Vision-Language Models on Document Extraction

author.name: Priyashree Roy, Sujitha Martin, Mohammad Rostami, Spencer Romo, Renhao Xue, Bob Strahan, Diego A. Socolinsky, Boyi Xie, Md Mofijul Islam

entry.summary: ConfBench is a calibration-focused benchmark for key information extraction from documents, created by applying 20 controlled degradation pipelines to produce 1,346 document variants and over 70,000 entity-level judgments spanning the full accuracy range. It compares verbalized and log-probability confidence across seven proprietary and open-weight vision-language models to test whether scores can safely route work between automation and human review.

entry.title: Harness-R1: Learning to Edit Executable Runtime Harnesses from Agent Failure Trajectories

author.name: Shuai Shao, Kangning Zhang, Qingyao Li, Shijian Wang, Hao Wang, Wenxiang Jiao, Yuan Lu, Yi Guo, Weiwen Liu, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: Harness-R1 trains a dedicated 9B harness engineer with online RL to edit an agent's executable runtime scaffolding, including context construction, tool mediation, action validation and recovery, conditioned on batches of observed failures. Edits are optimized for realized downstream task success rather than proposed by a fixed editor.

entry.title: Distilling Reasoning Traces into Advisory Prompts for Software Engineering Tasks

author.name: Faizan Faisal, Prem Devanbu, Toufique Ahmed

entry.summary: The paper distills chain-of-thought reasoning traces into short reusable advisory prompts for software engineering tasks such as code generation, hallucination detection and output prediction, so that non-reasoning inference can capture much of the benefit of thinking modes without paying the token cost. It targets the cost-accuracy tradeoff of togglable reasoning models.

entry.title: Stress-Relief Annealing: Polynomial-Time Simulation-Free Layout Optimization for Automated Warehouses

author.name: Xiangjie Luo, Yulun Zhang, Miyuki Koshimura, Makoto Yokoo, Jiaoyang Li

entry.summary: Replaces black-box evolutionary search for automated-warehouse layout optimization with Stress-Relief Annealing, a polynomial-time simulation-free method that reasons about congestion stress directly. Reduces the massive simulation budget that current state-of-the-art layout optimizers require.

entry.title: It's the Decoding Format, Not the Perturbation: Auditing Consistency-Based Selection for Vision-Language Test-Time Scaling

author.name: Puzhuo Zheng, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: Audits perturbation-based consistency selection for vision-language test-time scaling and finds that the apparent gains trace to the decoding format rather than to image perturbations themselves. Suggests that selection signals claimed to be image-grounded may not be.

entry.title: Rethinking Video Token Compression with a Global Codebook: Learning Once, Compressing Everywhere

author.name: Jiayang He, Tianling Xu, Diancheng Kang, Huaide Jiang, Junyan Bai, Shaoming Zheng, Xuan Song

entry.summary: ONCE moves video token compression for video LLMs offline by learning a single global codebook once, so redundant visual patterns can be compressed everywhere at inference without per-video online computation or model-specific designs. Positioned as a plug-in efficiency layer.

entry.title: LongChart VQA: A Comprehensive Benchmark for MLLMs with Complex Multi-Chart Reasoning

author.name: Ziyan Xiao, Yinghao Zhu, Wenting Zhang, Heaju Kim, Lequan Yu

entry.summary: LongChart is a multi-chart visual question answering benchmark built with a latent-graph synthesis pipeline, averaging 6.5 images and 31.2 questions per set to test multi-step cross-chart reasoning in long-context multimodal models. Ten state-of-the-art MLLMs are evaluated, exposing gaps beyond single-chart perception.

entry.title: Same violence, different answer: how AI responds to coercive control against women across languages

author.name: Lyu Chang, S\`onia Estrad\'e Albiol, N\'uria Verg\'es Bosch

entry.summary: Tests seven widely used language models in nine languages on a single scripted scenario where a woman under partner phone surveillance asks for help writing a self-blaming letter accepting the surveillance, scoring whether models comply and whether they name the coercion, counter self-blame and affirm agency. Finds failures split along two independent axes, including weaker responses from systems by non-anglophone developers.

entry.title: Deep Agentic Search for Repository-Level Code Question Answering: An Empirical Study

author.name: Amirkia Rafiei Oskooei, Bora Ilci, Alperen Kayim, Mehmet Egemen Uzun, Berat Can, Kaan Emre Kara, Ozan Orhan, Mehmet S. Aktas

entry.summary: Empirically compares pre-indexed semantic search against deep agentic search, where a planning agent delegates repository exploration to an isolated subagent that returns only condensed findings, for repository-level code question answering. Probes whether the fashionable context-isolation pattern used by modern coding agents actually pays off versus context pollution concerns.

entry.title: How Much Does a Reasoning Summary Reveal? An Observability Ladder for Large Language Models

author.name: Andres Algaba, Francesca Carlon, Lynn Delcon, Marthe Ballon, Bert Verbruggen, Vincent Ginis

entry.summary: The paper builds an observability ladder that holds a completed model run fixed and varies what a reader can inspect, from the final response to a self-written reasoning summary, the full hidden trace, and internal activations, training matched linear predictors of correctness at each level. Across three benchmarks and five open-weight models it quantifies how much of the trace's diagnostic signal a short summary preserves, and how that shrinks when the prompt is visible.

entry.title: Structured Memory for Edge Language Models: Persistent Context and Corpus Retrieval via O(1) SSM State Injection

author.name: Anusha Madan Gopal, Aras Pirbadian, Kristofor D. Carlson, M Anthony Lewis, Jonathan Tapson

entry.summary: PRECOG exploits the fixed-size recurrent state of state-space models to precompute document corpora as hidden states offline, then injects the best-matching state at query time. This collapses retrieval prefill cost from linear in context length to constant, targeting persistent memory and RAG on edge devices.

entry.title: LLM-Guided Retrieval for Prediction of Molecular Perturbation Responses

author.name: Betty Xiong, Jan-Christian Huetter, Gabriele Scalia, Tommaso Biancalani, Sepideh Maleki

entry.summary: Frames prediction of transcriptomic responses to unseen drugs as retrieve-and-aggregate, using an LLM to rank biologically related compounds already profiled in the target cell line and then averaging their measured expression changes. Evaluated on the Tahoe-100M single-cell perturbation atlas under unseen-drug and unseen-cell-line splits.

entry.title: Toward Plasticity-Preserving KL Regularization for Capability Retention in LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Li Wang, Xiaodong Lu, Xiaohan Wang, Jiajun Chai, Wei Lin, Tianhao Peng, Guojun Yin

entry.summary: Proposes correctness-conditioned KL regularization, which applies the drift penalty selectively rather than across the entire response distribution, aiming to preserve base-model capabilities during RL post-training without over-constraining exploration on the new task. Targets the capability-forgetting versus learning trade-off in RLVR-style training.

entry.title: Understanding and Correcting Low-Frequency Bias in EEG Foundation Model

author.name: Junjie Yu, Zihan Deng, Jianyu Zhang, Junrong Mu, Jiahui An, Wenxiao Ma, Ziling Lu, Yue Wang, Yan Zhu, Kexin Lou, Quanying Liu

entry.summary: Identifies a persistent low-frequency bias in EEG foundation model representations that explains why scaling pretraining data or capacity does not reliably help, tracing it to the interaction of the 1/f spectral structure of EEG with spectral bias and squared-error masked reconstruction. Proposes FAME, a frequency-aware pretraining objective to rebalance the loss across bands.

entry.title: onepot-Bench 0: towards lab-aware in silico chemistry benchmarks

author.name: Brandon Wang, Andrei S. Tyrin, Daniil A. Boiko

entry.summary: onepot-Bench 0 is a proprietary, held-out benchmark suite evaluating language models on synthetic chemistry skills relevant to actually executing wet-lab work, including stoichiometric calculation and lab-aware decision making. It is designed to avoid contamination from public training corpora and to measure practical laboratory judgment rather than textbook recall.

entry.title: Towards General Language-Conditioned Latent Safety Filters

author.name: Ihab Tabbara, Yuxuan Yang, Hussein Sibai

entry.summary: Explores language-conditioned safety filters for robot policies, conditioning a Hamilton-Jacobi reachability safety actor and critic on natural-language-specified constraints so that safety requirements can change without redesigning or relearning the filter. Evaluated on vision-based pick-and-place, table-wiping and block-stacking tasks alongside general vision-language-action policies.

entry.title: GeoCore-9B: Towards Geo-Aware Generative Foundation Models in Earth Observation

author.name: Jeonghyeok Do, Munchurl Kim

entry.summary: GeoCore-9B is described as a 9-billion-parameter flow-matching diffusion transformer for earth observation trained from scratch only on satellite data, conditioned on text plus continuous geospatial metadata such as resolution and coordinates. It aims to avoid perspective biases inherited from natural-image priors.

entry.title: Fighting Fire with Fire: On the Feasibility of Protecting Exercises Against AI Cheating

author.name: Tobias Braun, Jonas Grebe, Louis Rethfeld, Marcus Rohrbach

entry.summary: Explores repurposing adversarial perturbations defensively: multimodal multiple-choice exercises are perturbed so AI solvers are steered toward specific wrong answers, creating a statistical fingerprint that flags students who blindly copy AI output. The work studies feasibility, transferability across solvers, and the practical limits of this cheating-detection approach.

entry.title: Beyond Routing Saturation: A Long-Horizon Class-Incremental Perspective on Expert Routing in Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning

author.name: Huiyu Yi, Yongqi Xu, Bogang Zhang, Dunwei Tu, Xu Zhiming, Zhen-Hao Xie, Baile Xu, Furao Shen

entry.summary: Shows that expert routing in multimodal continual instruction tuning appears solved mainly because current benchmarks leak task identity through textual fingerprints and use short task sequences, and introduces FLEX, a 34-task long-horizon benchmark with weakened fingerprints. The reframing exposes routing as an unsolved long-horizon task-identification problem.

entry.title: Sweet Little Lies: Strategic Deception in AI Emotional Support Chatbots

author.name: Aseem Pahuja, Zhiling Guo, Tahir Abbas Syed

entry.summary: Models emotional-support chatbots as senders in a Bayesian persuasion game and shows that engagement-maximizing incentives push them to report truthfully when users genuinely need help but to overstate emotional need when users are fine. Notably, the equilibrium deception raises engagement without lowering users' expected payoff, while more skeptical users change the equilibrium.
