entry.title: AdaHAT: Adaptive Hard Attention to the Task in Task-Incremental Learning

author.name: Pengxiang Wang, Hongbo Bo, Jun Hong, Weiru Liu, Kedian Mu

entry.summary: AdaHAT extends hard-attention-to-the-task continual learning with an adaptive mechanism that allows controlled updates to parameters previously frozen for earlier tasks, mitigating capacity exhaustion over long task sequences. Trades a small amount of stability for sustained plasticity.

entry.title: Auditing Semantic Gains in Sequential Recommendation: A Lightweight Recovery Test

author.name: Kong Wang, Zhongke He, Xiang Chen, Hongwei Zeng, Kai Deng, Long Wang, Kehua Yang

entry.summary: LIME-Rec is an auditable recovery test that fuses a sequential recommender, a co-occurrence expert, and frozen text-embedding item semantics to check whether reported gains from semantic and generative-retrieval recommenders actually require language-model reasoning. It attributes improvements to specific components via transparent score-level fusion.

entry.title: Weights or Skills? A Survey of Robot-Learning Techniques: from Action-Predicting Weights to Robots that Write their Own Skills

author.name: Gaytri Jena, Kapil Wanaskar, Vinija Jain, Aman Chadha, Vasu Sharma, Amitava Das

entry.summary: This survey organizes robot learning along an axis of frozen-weight vision-language-action policies versus agents that write and refine their own executable skills as code, and grades code-as-policy methods by degree of self-improvement. It highlights that few systems combine execution feedback, persistent skill memory, and evolutionary search into one open-ended loop.

entry.title: UEmbed: Unified Sparse and Dense Multimodal Embeddings

author.name: Tingyu Song, Mingxin Li, Yanzhao Zhang, Dingkun Long, Pengjun Xie, Zhijie Nie, Yilun Zhao, Shu Wu

entry.summary: UEmbed is a decoder-only multimodal embedding model that produces both learned sparse lexical and dense vectors in a single causal forward pass, using learnable special tokens mapped to disjoint vocabulary partitions. It extends learned sparse retrieval beyond bidirectional encoders and into multimodal inputs without extra cross-modal modules.

entry.title: Plasticity of Growing and Elastic Neural Networks in Online Continual Learning

author.name: Jeong Min Kong, Richard S. Sutton

entry.summary: Studies whether neural networks that grow, or grow and shrink, retain plasticity in online continual learning rather than only avoiding catastrophic forgetting. Builds on the finding that incrementally adding randomly initialized hidden units helps preserve a network's continuing ability to learn.

entry.title: GraphIR: Architecture-Level Search States for LLM-Guided Neural Architecture Evolution

author.name: Zhen Liu, Wanqi Zhou, Shuanghao Bai, Yuhan Liu, Jinjun Wang, Jingwen Fu

entry.summary: GraphIR gives LLM-driven neural architecture search an architecture-aware intermediate representation with three views: a tensor-flow skeleton, an explicit mutation surface of editable modules, and a validity envelope of interface constraints. The aim is to stop the LLM from having to infer editability and compatibility from raw code, making mutations more targeted and valid.

entry.title: Augmented Inverse Hybrid Weighting: Robust Inference under Deterministic and Random Distribution Shifts

author.name: Ying Jin, Ying Jin, Dominik Rothenh\"ausler

entry.summary: Introduces an estimator for generalizing evidence across populations when the shift includes both learnable covariate differences and residual random perturbations that no reweighting can capture. The method combines inverse weighting with an augmentation term and provides inference that remains valid under this hybrid shift model.

entry.title: SoniSpeech: A Large-Scale Open-Vocabulary Tri-Modal Dataset for Wearable Silent Speech Interfaces

author.name: Ruidong Zhang, Jiacheng Liu, Fran\c{c}ois Guimbreti\`ere, Cheng Zhang

entry.summary: Releases a 34-hour trimodal corpus for silent speech interfaces using acoustic-sensing eyewear, pairing ultrasound echo profiles with voiced audio and frontal video across 18,000 conversational utterances. A CTC ResNet baseline achieves 26.3 percent word error rate on open-vocabulary silent speech, reportedly the first such result for unobtrusive wearable hardware.

entry.title: RestoreKV: Recovering Full-Cache Behavior Under Aggressive Query-Agnostic KV Cache Eviction

author.name: Changwoo Baek, Seungjun Shin, Kyeongbo Kong

entry.summary: Complements query-agnostic KV cache eviction with a learned restoration step: after prefill, a small set of restore tokens attends to the full cache through a LoRA-adapted pass to produce a compact context-conditioned complement within the same total budget. The insight is that while lost information is context-specific, the mechanism for regenerating a compact substitute can be shared.

entry.title: Bole: Efficient Tree Speculation for Hybrid-Attention Language Models

author.name: Li Wang, Yi Su, Xiabao Wu, Chiran You, Yongchao Liu, Zhan Qiu, Juelu Zhang, Jiajun Zheng, Fangxin Liu, Jie Zhang, Chen Tian, Chengying Huan

entry.summary: Builds a kernel and runtime co-design that makes tree speculative decoding practical for hybrid attention LLMs that mix full attention with recurrent linear attention. It rewrites the linear-attention recurrence into a tree-structured form so verification avoids materializing a full recurrent state per proposal node.

entry.title: A Few Neurons Reveal When LLMs Misuse Tools: Sparse Detection and Selective Steering for Reliable Tool Use

author.name: Yutong Ke, Ming Yin, Chongwen Zhao, Kaizhu Huang

entry.summary: Finds that small failure-specific sets of MLP neurons linearly separate three agentic tool-use failure modes: invalid arguments, unnecessary calls, and omitted calls. Builds a closed-loop framework that shares this neuron basis between sparse detection and activation steering across six models from three families.

entry.title: Distill Where You Fail: Recovering Learning Signals of Negative RL-Groups from Adaptive Teacher Guidance

author.name: Zhuowen Han, Jinwei Xiao, Zhengxi Lu, Renren Jin, Zhiyuan Yao, Yuxin Liu, Hongyan Hao, Yueqing Sun, Yu Yang, Qi GU, Xunliang Cai, Deyi Xiong

entry.summary: Addresses the case where all sampled responses in a GRPO group receive identical rewards and gradients vanish, by selectively injecting on-policy teacher distillation only where it helps. Diagnoses three failure modes of naively combining verifiable-reward RL with distillation and proposes adaptive corrections.

entry.title: Opt.Gear Technical Report

author.name: Juneyoung Park, Youngwook Kwon

entry.summary: Technical report on a family of small on-device foundation models from 1 million to 1 billion parameters with a 64K context, using a hybrid convolutional key-value gated mixer plus local-global attention to curb KV cache growth. Claims up to nearly five times faster prefill and decode on NPUs and strong data efficiency from a curated half-trillion-token subset.

entry.title: Beyond Token-Level Cross-Entropy: Fr\'echet Distributional Post-Training for Autoregressive Image Generation

author.name: Jinhua Zhang, Yisong Lin, Wei Long, Shuhang Gu

entry.summary: This work replaces token-level cross-entropy fine-tuning of autoregressive image generators with a post-training objective based on Frechet distance in representation space, using detached rollout contexts plus differentiable replay and a straight-through estimator. The goal is to close the gap between the training loss and the distributional metrics actually used to evaluate generated images.

entry.title: StreamSplat: Streaming Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Changhao Song, Yuxuan Wang, Qibiao Li, Youcheng Cai, Ligang Liu

entry.summary: StreamSplat performs feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting in a streaming, causal fashion, updating a persistent scene state as calibrated views arrive rather than processing a fixed view set jointly. A voxel-aligned causal cache bounds memory growth by explored geometry instead of stream length.

entry.title: Decoupling semantics from vision: A framework for faithful visual-text compression evaluation

author.name: Yonghan Gao, Zehong Chen, Lijian Xu, Jingzhi Chen, Jingwei Guan, Xingyu Zeng

entry.summary: Argues that current evaluations of visual-text compression, where long text is rendered as images to save tokens, are confounded by the language priors of multimodal models. Proposes an evaluation framework that decouples model capabilities plus a benchmark of semantically low-correlation samples to measure true text preservation.

entry.title: EOVSAM: Efficient Open-Vocabulary Segmentation with SAM 3 in One Pass

author.name: Haomin Peng, Yongkang Li, Zhaoxiang Liu, Xiaojie Jin, Shiguo Lian, Yunchao Wei, Xinggang Wang

entry.summary: EOVSAM adapts a promptable segmentation foundation model for open-vocabulary segmentation in one forward pass, removing the need to iterate over every candidate noun phrase. It replaces multi-stage pipelines with an end-to-end attentional aggregation classifier over generated masks.

entry.title: Token Radius Attention for Efficient Video Generation

author.name: Jiayu Chen, Zhikun Jiang, Maoliang Li, Jiayi Luo, Jiawei Yang, Zihao Zheng, Hengyi Zhang, Guojie Luo, Xiang Chen

entry.summary: Token Radius Attention is a training-free sparse attention method for video diffusion transformers that maps each query token attention entropy to a per-token compute budget, then converts that budget into a temporally decaying neighborhood radius rather than ranking keys explicitly. It exploits the observed log-linear relation between retained attention density and entropy to avoid uniform sparsity budgets.

entry.title: First Deployable Dynamic-CoM: A Unified Policy and Method-Agnostic Benchmark for Humanoid Single-Leg Balance

author.name: Yikai Zhou, Xingyun Wang, Jieming Cui, Bozhou Chen, Yikai Fan, Yixin Zhu, Wenxin Li

entry.summary: This paper reports that eight state-of-the-art unified humanoid policies fail to hold a clean single-leg stance on all 90 test motions in a new benchmark, surviving only by stepping or hopping. It introduces a deployable dynamic center-of-mass observation, showing that the capture point expressed relative to the support foot cancels the unmeasurable base linear velocity and is reconstructible from encoders and IMU alone.

entry.title: Toward Geometry-Scalable Whole-Body Touch for Humanoids: A 3D-Printed Conformal EIT Skin

author.name: Haofeng Chen, Carson Kohlbrenner, Jiri Kubik, Lukas Rustler, Alexander Dickhans, Karel Bartunek, Alessandro Roncone, Hyosang Lee, Matej Hoffmann

entry.summary: A 3D-printed conformal tactile skin uses electrical impedance tomography over a continuous conductive TPU layer instead of discrete taxel arrays, reconstructing contact from boundary voltages. The additive-manufacturing workflow adapts to arbitrary robot curvature, addressing wiring and scaling bottlenecks for whole-body humanoid touch.

entry.title: Fast-Mixing Markov Chains without Gradients

author.name: Robert Kutri, Robert Scheichl

entry.summary: DART is a Metropolis-Hastings sampling scheme where a regularized and tempered surrogate proposal implicitly captures Langevin-like gradient information without ever evaluating target or surrogate gradients. The authors prove the expected proposal displacement matches Langevin drift up to controlled error and derive mixing-rate bounds.

entry.title: Approximate Message Passing with Random Initialization for Phase Retrieval

author.name: Yuchen Chen, Yandi Shen, Xingyu Xu

entry.summary: The authors analyze approximate message passing with random Gaussian initialization for noiseless phase retrieval, where the tiny initial overlap requires a growing number of iterations and breaks fixed-time state evolution. They prove a Gaussian trajectory decomposition and establish that random initialization attains the weak-recovery threshold.

entry.title: AXRP Episode 50 - Eli Lifland on AI 2027

author.name: DanielFilan

entry.summary: An AXRP podcast transcript in which Eli Lifland discusses the AI 2027 forecasting scenario, covering time-horizon growth extrapolation, effective compute forecasts, the path from superhuman coders to superintelligence, misalignment dynamics, and the reception of the scenario. It is a long retrospective on the methodology behind a widely discussed forecast.

entry.title: 402Pilot: An x402 Decision Layer for Autonomous Agent Micropayments

author.name: Yin Li, Yanbo He, Boo-Ho Yang, Rav Lawana, Ziyue Li, Wei Zeng, Jing Tang, Fugee Tsung

entry.summary: 402Pilot adds a buyer-side decision layer above per-request micropayment protocols so an autonomous agent can choose which paid service to purchase under a finite wallet, using a payment-aware discounted contextual Thompson sampling policy. It formalizes agent purchasing as contextual bandits with chosen-only paid feedback and nonstationary markets.

entry.title: CRAFTS: Collaborative Role-Adaptive Fine-Tuning of LLM Agents for Chemical Process Simulation

author.name: Ziyun Zhang, Yuxin Lin, Eldin Wee Chuan Lim, Xinghao Ding

entry.summary: CRAFTS decomposes chemical process simulation building into seven bounded LLM agent roles mirroring engineering workflow stages, with deterministic IDAES and Pyomo checks gating each stage transition. It consumes natural-language requests plus process flow diagrams to produce executable, degree-of-freedom-consistent flowsheet models.

entry.title: MemSIF: From Structured Interactions to Dual-Track Fact Memory for LLM Agents

author.name: YuFei Luo, Xiucheng Xu, Zhen Yang

entry.summary: MemSIF attributes long-term agent memory failures to two misalignments, temporal proximity not matching topical relatedness and write-time salience not predicting later query utility, and builds a dual-track memory that segments raw interactions topically while separately maintaining distilled facts. The design aims to decouple when information arrived from when it becomes useful.

entry.title: VLAGuard: A Framework for Evaluating and Mitigating Physical Attention Hijacking in Vision-Language-Action Robots within Wireless Sensor Networks

author.name: Dongfu Yin, Jinquan Zhang

entry.summary: Demonstrates that printable adversarial patches can hijack the action-conditioned cross-attention of vision-language-action robots, then proposes attention-protective fine-tuning that stabilizes spatiotemporal attention with no inference overhead. Evaluated in simulated and physical edge-robot settings.

entry.title: DynActiveGS: Active Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Scene Reconstruction

author.name: Hongbo Duan, Pengting Luo, Chengzhi Zhao, Yuanhao Chiang, Fangming Liu, Xueqian Wang

entry.summary: DynActiveGS performs active 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction in dynamic scenes by separating structural uncertainty from motion-induced uncertainty, then using those fields for viewpoint selection and path planning. Suppresses motion-corrupted observations during incremental mapping.

entry.title: ACE-GraphRAG: Agentic Context Engineering for Hierarchical GraphRAG

author.name: Yongfeng Huang, Yuren Lai, Ruiying Chen, Haoyu Huang, Mingming Zhao, James Cheng

entry.summary: ACE-GraphRAG adds an inference-time context policy layer to hierarchical GraphRAG, identifying a representation-inference gap where fixed context construction fails to convert multi-resolution graph knowledge into query-appropriate context. It uses parallel depth-oriented and breadth-oriented retrieval branches plus task-conditioned adaptation.

entry.title: Upper-Expectile Multi-Step Q-Learning for Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Abdelghani Ghanem, Mounir Ghogho

entry.summary: Expectile n-step Q-learning replaces the symmetric temporal-difference loss with an asymmetric expectile loss to counter the pessimistic bias that multi-step returns inherit from suboptimal logged actions. The authors prove a contraction property and show that at the extreme expectile the bias vanishes on covered state-action pairs under deterministic dynamics.

entry.title: Convex Neural Energy Elements: Monolithic Finite-Element Assembly of Geometry-Parameterized Neural Operators with Stability and Error Guarantees

author.name: Hongyue Jiang, Jianjiang Zhan, Chenzhuo Zhang, Fan Wang

entry.summary: Shows that geometry-parameterized neural operators trained by field regression yield indefinite assembled Hessians so that finite-element style assembly diverges to spurious solutions, then fixes this by having each element export an architecturally convex scalar energy generated by a hypernetwork. This restores stability and error guarantees for reusable neural finite elements.

entry.title: Feed-Forward Steering in Transformer Residual Dynamics

author.name: Timur Mudarisov, Mikhail Burtsev, Radu State

entry.summary: Extends dynamical theories of transformer residual streams beyond attention by modeling the feed-forward network as a local steering field on each token state, predicting that its tangential component drives motion in residual-direction space and that a commutator defect governs when attention and FFN can be treated as a parallel additive flow. Validated on GPT-2, Pythia, Mistral and Llama by improved one-step angular prediction.

entry.title: Gecko: Fast Private Inference via Secure Public Encoder Offloading

author.name: Cheng'an Wei, Kai Chen, Yue Zhao, Congyi Li, Shenchen Zhu

entry.summary: Gecko speeds up private neural network inference by running a public pretrained encoder outside the cryptographic boundary while keeping only a small private predictor encrypted, and analyzes the new risk that this creates a feature-space shortcut for model-extraction adversaries. It proposes defenses to limit that added extraction risk while preserving the efficiency benefit.

entry.title: RadPRISM: Schema-stratified radiology-report supervision for concept-disentangled image representations and visual grounding

author.name: Fabian Drexel, Marlene Fritzsche, Era Stambollxhiu, Miriam Kumpf, Lena Schmitzer, Lea Schumann, Jannik Kahmann, Friedrich Puttkammer, Johannes Moll, Jannik L\"ubberstedt, Zeineb Ben Chaaben, Anirudh Narayanan, Cosmin I. Bercea, Sebastian Ziegelmayer, Marcus R. Makowski, Daniel Rueckert, Lisa C. Adams, Keno K. Bressem

entry.summary: RadPRISM uses a clinician-defined 19-concept radiology schema as an explicit stratification axis for vision-language pretraining, having an on-premise LLM extract per-concept text spans and aligning each concept in its own dedicated visual subspace. Trained on over 200,000 chest radiograph examinations, it makes concept structure and visual grounding a top-level supervision target rather than a post hoc probe.

entry.title: Same Semantics, Different Paths: Self-Improving Alignment for Vision-Text Compression

author.name: Tianyu Liang, Xiangxi Zheng, Yilin Wang, Dongxing Mao

entry.summary: Shows that when long text is rendered into images for token compression, the vision encoder captures glyphs and layout rather than linguistic semantics, so rendered-text representations diverge from native-text ones. Proposes a self-supervised alignment method that uses the model's own text-path behavior as supervision to close this gap.

entry.title: Hermite Curves as Trajectory Priors for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Qi Lv, Jianming Xing, Zhao Yang, Mingyuan Yao, Yinan Shi, Yawei Jueluo, Mike Zheng Shou, Xiang Deng

entry.summary: This paper argues the action chunk in vision-language-action models is a weakly structured interface and replaces flat per-timestep outputs with piecewise cubic Hermite curves defined by endpoint positions and velocities, enforcing smoothness and continuity by construction. Three variants instantiate the prior across discrete autoregressive and continuous generative policy paradigms.

entry.title: Memory Reward Inflation in Self-Improving LLM Agents

author.name: Mohammad Asadolahi, Amir Amini, Samira Talebi, Amirfarhad Farhadi, Azadeh Zamanifar

entry.summary: Identifies an Echo Gap failure mode in weight-free self-improving agents: because stored episode scores come from LLM self-assessment rather than ground truth, incorrect episodes receive inflated rewards and get preferentially retrieved, compounding errors over time. The effect is shown across multiple memory-based agent designs and model families.

entry.title: Tracing the Cascade: A Topology-Aware Evaluation Framework for Scientific Agent Hallucinations

author.name: Xinshun Feng, Ziqi Miao, Lijun Li, Jing Shao

entry.summary: SCHEMA evaluates hallucinations in scientific agents topologically, building concept graphs from benchmarks so that errors on foundational concepts can be traced as they cascade through multi-step reasoning. It replaces uniform accuracy metrics that treat facts in isolation.

entry.title: Don't Offer What Can't Be Done: Deterministic Executability Gating for LLM Skill Selection at Scale

author.name: Ortal Ashkenazi, Vitalii Kloz, Mykhailo Ulianchenko

entry.summary: Describes a deployed three-stage skill-selection pipeline for a commercial customer-care assistant that adds a deterministic executability gate after semantic retrieval, so the agent never offers skills that cannot run given the current account state. The key design idea is predicate parity between the gate and the skill itself, which guarantees blocked candidates would have failed anyway.

entry.title: A New Theory of Value for Post-AGI Economics

author.name: Keyun Ruan

entry.summary: Proposes Flourishing Value Theory as an economic value framework for a world where AGI erodes scarcities in labor, expertise, and cognitive capability, defining value as the counterfactual and distribution-sensitive contribution to durable human and community capabilities. It argues market price, labor input, and output measures could diverge sharply from human benefit under widespread cognitive automation.

entry.title: FRAMES: Guarded and Dual-Objective Skill Evolution for Agents in Policy-Governed Enterprise Workflows

author.name: Xuhui Wang, Ruoqi Shu, Chen Dan, Tianhua Xu, Mengxi Luo, Yanming Mai, Bo Wan

entry.summary: FRAMES evolves agent skills for policy-bound enterprise document auditing without labeled feedback, using consensus-based mutation, Pareto selection over accuracy and cost, and an anti-regression guard so improving one rule does not break unrelated cases. It reports the best accuracy-cost trade-off among baselines in an internal production deployment while preserving auditability.

entry.title: EchoChange: A Diffusion Language Model with Dual Pass Remasking for Factual Remote Sensing Disaster Change Captioning

author.name: Dongwei Sun, Bowen Yao, Yujie Zhang, Pei Liu, Jing Yao, Xiangyong Cao

entry.summary: EchoChange replaces autoregressive decoding with multimodal discrete diffusion and dual-pass remasking for describing changes between pre- and post-disaster satellite images. The rationale is that with left-to-right generation an early misidentification of the changed object becomes an irreversible premise that cascades into further factual errors.

entry.title: ProWorld: Progress-Aware Hyperbolic World Models for Long-Horizon Visual Goal Reaching

author.name: Zihan Liu, Yuzhe Zhuang, Yuanzu Li, Wanshuang Gou, Jiahong Liu, Min Zhou, Menglin Yang

entry.summary: Proposes a JEPA-style visual world model that adds a goal-conditioned progress ordering signal and hyperbolic latent geometry so multi-step rollouts keep moving toward the goal instead of merely staying locally plausible. Targets long-horizon visual goal reaching where local transition consistency is insufficient.

entry.title: MonitrLLM: A Community-Centered Evaluation Infrastructure for Large Language Models

author.name: Victor Ojewale, Ro Encarnaci\'on, Suresh Venkatasubramanian, Dana\'e Metaxa

entry.summary: MonitrLLM is open-source infrastructure for community-centered LLM evaluation that links full conversation transcripts to user-stated task intent and user-reported outcomes, treating all three as primary signals. A two-week pilot with 26 students demonstrates feasibility.

entry.title: Cost-Effective Automated Judging of Natural-Language Mathematical Proofs

author.name: Benjamin Grayzel

entry.summary: Tests whether cheap open-weight models can grade natural-language math proofs given a reference proof and rubric, finding three inexpensive judges agree with human pass/fail decisions at rates statistically indistinguishable from far more expensive frontier models at up to a hundredfold lower cost. Also finds that majority voting among the cheap judges did not improve on the best single judge.

entry.title: Neural Circuit Function Inference with LLMs

author.name: Yijie Yin (Department of Physiology, Development and Neuroscience, University of Cambridge, Cambridge, UK, MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology, Cambridge, UK), Albert Cardona (MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology, Cambridge, UK, Department of Physiology, Development and Neuroscience, University of Cambridge, Cambridge, UK)

entry.summary: LLantia uses LLMs to distill cell-type function descriptions from the literature and combine them with connectome data to infer function for uncharacterized cell types and whole neural circuits. Outputs are hierarchically structured across candidate behavioural and physiological contexts.

entry.title: Counting the Cost of War Under Satellite Embargo: Zero-Shot Estimation of Impacted Infrastructure

author.name: Saleh Sakib Ahmed, M. Sohel Rahman

entry.summary: This work estimates conflict-zone infrastructure damage without post-strike satellite imagery by using LLMs to extract weapon payloads from incident text, projecting blast radii via Hopkinson-Cranz scaling onto archival maps, and counting exposed buildings with adaptive field-of-view segmentation and pseudo-height estimation. It offers a workaround for imagery blackouts that stall humanitarian assessment.

entry.title: Learning-Based Motion Planning for Dynamic Environments: From Foundational Algorithms to Emerging Paradigms

author.name: Zongyuan Shen, Shalabh Gupta, Shancheng Zhao, Dehua Zhou, Gao Wang, Rui Cheng, Yaming Ou, Zhongqiang Ren, Yikui Zhai, C. L. Philip Chen

entry.summary: This survey reviews learning-based motion planning in dynamic environments from roughly 2015 to 2025, revisiting classical planners as algorithmic foundations and then organizing how learning methods extend or complement them under moving obstacles, uncertain predictions and multi-agent interaction. It spans autonomous driving, service robotics, crowd navigation and multi-robot systems.

entry.title: GraRe: Grasp Candidate Re-Ranking for Frozen 6-DoF Grasp Detectors

author.name: Jibao Yuan, Yuhui Zhao, Yinzhen Lv, Chao Xu, Shun Li, Chenxi Deng, Shaofei Chen

entry.summary: Shows that confidence scores from 6-DoF grasp detectors correlate poorly with actual grasp quality on GraspNet-1Billion, and formulates re-ranking of candidates as a separate task for frozen detectors. A transformer fuses candidate attributes, stratified local geometry and object context to reorder candidates.

entry.title: When Replanning Becomes the Bottleneck: Budgeted Replanning for Embodied Agents

author.name: Shuaijun Liu, Feiyang You, Xingwei Chen, Ningxin Su

entry.summary: BRACE treats LLM replanning in embodied agents as a budgeted control loop, deciding whether to replan, which mode to use, and how many tokens and latency budget to allocate against a service-level objective. It targets heavy-tailed replanning latency that average-case metrics and success rates hide.

entry.title: Coding Agents as Test-Suite Auditors: Finding What Official Suites Miss While Approaching What They Catch

author.name: Shuyang Xie, Shuxiao Xie, Feng Zhu, Yanli Ji, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: The authors use an off-the-shelf coding agent as an auditor that builds adversarial test suites to expose buggy submissions accepted by official online-judge suites, plus a certification chain that confirms bugs without relying on the judge itself. This offers a concrete remedy to label noise in widely used code benchmarks and training datasets.

entry.title: LEAP: Lean Environment-Feedback via Adaptive Pruning for Code RL in GPU Kernel Generation

author.name: Tankun Li, Zhi Chen, Yaohua Tang

entry.summary: LEAP improves reinforcement learning for CUDA kernel generation by pruning environment feedback adaptively, tackling sparse binary pass/fail rewards, long compilation latencies, and reward dilution in multi-turn loops. It targets critic-free GRPO-style post-training for low-level systems code.

entry.title: AOSpec: Action and Observation Co-Speculation for Low-Latency Agent Serving

author.name: Hao Mark Chen, Jinnan Guo, Wayne Luk, Hongxiang Fan

entry.summary: AOSpec reduces agent latency by speculatively predicting both the agent's next actions and the environment's tool observations across the full loop, rather than only one side. Expected Value Decoding steers speculation toward the slowest, highest-payoff tool calls while remaining output-lossless.

entry.title: Do Neural Networks Really Beat the Curse of Dimensionality? A Bit-Complexity View

author.name: Tong Mao, Jinchao Xu

entry.summary: Re-evaluates approximation efficiency in terms of bit complexity and metric entropy rather than parameter count, comparing polynomials, sparse grids, finite elements, and shallow and deep networks. Questions whether the apparent ability of neural networks to escape the curse of dimensionality survives finite-precision accounting.

entry.title: Benchmarking Sheaf Neural Networks for Inductive Tasks

author.name: Stefano Fiorini, Edoardo Coppola, Pietro Li\`o

entry.summary: Provides the first systematic inductive-setting benchmark of sheaf neural networks, sweeping three diffusion mechanisms, three restriction-map parameterizations, stalk dimensions and six modern GNN components. It tests whether the theoretical advantages seen in transductive node classification transfer when generalizing to unseen graphs.

entry.title: Learning to Persuade Privately Informed Receivers

author.name: I. Arda Vurankaya, Ufuk Topcu

entry.summary: Studies online Bayesian persuasion when the receiver also has a private, unobservable signal from an external source unknown to the sender, with the sender only observing the receiver's binary action. Gives a learning algorithm with sublinear regret of order T to the three-quarters relative to the best signaling scheme.

entry.title: Verification Without Sufficiency: Per-Chunk Filtering Fails on Multi-Hop RAG, and Decomposition Repairs It

author.name: Randhir Kumar

entry.summary: Shows that the common retrieval-augmented generation practice of scoring and filtering each retrieved chunk independently is structurally incapable of handling multi-hop questions, since no single chunk entails the answer. Entailment-based verification AUC drops sharply on multi-hop benchmarks versus single-hop, and the paper argues that question decomposition restores verification usefulness.

entry.title: Generated Images Are Easier to Forget: A Machine Unlearning Perspective for Synthetic Image Detection

author.name: Jun Nie, Yonggang Zhang, Tongliang Liu, Yiu-ming Cheung, Bo Han, Xinmei Tian

entry.summary: Observes that large vision models pretrained on natural images assign similarly low loss to real and generated images, limiting their discriminative power, and reframes synthetic image detection through machine unlearning. The core claim is that generated images are more readily forgotten than natural ones, providing a training signal for detection that generalizes across unseen generators.

entry.title: Celty: SpMspV GPU Kernel and SIMT Co-Design for Efficient Dual-Sparse LLM Inference

author.name: Ruokai Yin, Priyadarshini Panda

entry.summary: Targets dual sparsity in single-user LLM decoding, where unstructured weight pruning meets runtime activation sparsity and produces a sparse-matrix sparse-vector workload that GPUs handle badly. It co-designs a run-length compressed CSC format, a GPU kernel, and SIMT microarchitecture changes to make this pattern efficient.

entry.title: Understanding Sparse Attention Selectivity in Long-Context Foundation Models via Counterfactual Evaluation

author.name: Xingyu Ren, Youran Sun, Chugang Yi, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: Audits how block sparse attention changes which content actually influences long-context model outputs, using replayed routing across four architectures and matched probe cards carrying correct, misleading, or filler content. It documents that sparsification causally flips output decisions in most tested settings and identifies competing patterns of signal concentration versus distortion.

entry.title: Look Ahead Before You Distill: Future Trajectory Validation of Teacher Guidance for Agentic On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Chishui Chen, Yaoyou Fan, Te Sun, Yi Yang, Chenghao Sun, Delin Mao, Hongbo Qiao, Zuowei Zhang, Junxi Wang, Chenxing Sun, Yangen Hu, Lu Pan, Xuyang Liu, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: Improves on-policy distillation for multi-turn agentic tasks by executing a short teacher bridge at high-disagreement states and then checking whether the resulting student continuation actually improves, rather than assuming teacher guidance always helps. The lookahead validation prevents wasted or harmful supervision as student trajectories drift.

entry.title: Advancing Relevance Measurement with Vision-Language Models for Web-Scale Search

author.name: Han Wang, Alex Whitworth, Pak Ming Cheung, Zhenjie Zhang, Krishna Kamath, Xi Chen, Roberto Konow, Kurchi Subhra Hazra

entry.summary: Describes a production vision-language-model pipeline at Pinterest Search that replaces costly human relevance annotation for online A/B experiments, validated against human labels. Shows VLM judges can scale search relevance measurement and unlock further uses of automated labelling.

entry.title: Averaging Bias: Human Faithfulness Annotations are not Locally Faithful

author.name: Huajian Zhang, Yiyang Feng, Jiawei Zhou

entry.summary: Questions whether single global human faithfulness labels for summaries actually implement the strict rule that every sentence must be supported, using LLM judges as per-sentence raters across four benchmarks. Finds global labels behave more like an average over sentences, revealing an averaging bias in widely used benchmarks.

entry.title: Mind the Gap: Zero-Query Jailbreaks via Filter-Generator Discrepancy in Text-to-Image Systems

author.name: Wanguang Li, Zhaoxin Wang, Handing Wang

entry.summary: Identifies a gap between how text-to-image safety filters and image generators represent the same prompt, and exploits this filter-generator discrepancy to craft jailbreak prompts offline without querying the target system. Improves over transfer attacks that overfit to a single surrogate filter.

entry.title: DeltaFlow: Noise-Adaptive Bidirectional Gated Delta Networks for Embedded Language Flows

author.name: Guangfu Guo, Xiaoqian Lu, Linsey Pang, Weiran Yao, Haolin Chen, Kunpeng Liu, Long Cheng

entry.summary: Replaces quadratic non-causal attention in continuous diffusion-style language denoising with a bidirectional gated delta network backbone, exploring alternating-direction and parallel-scan variants plus noise-adaptive memory control and temporal state consistency. Aims to make iterative denoising language models linear-cost per step.

entry.title: RADAR: Rubric-Aware Dependency and Redundancy Analysis for LLM-as-Judge Evaluation

author.name: Divyansh Singh, Reza Davari, Afra Mashhadi

entry.summary: RADAR is a preflight diagnostic that probes whether rubric criteria used by LLM judges are statistically entangled, generating synthetic probes and producing a directional coupling matrix. Validated on three evaluation suites, it warns when aggregate rubric scores used for model-release decisions may be distorted by criteria that co-move.

entry.title: Video Models as Native 4D Renderers: World-Grounded Conditioning from Animated Mesh

author.name: Junhao Chen, Mingjin Chen, Henghaofan Zhang, Minglin Chen, Liaoyuan Fan, Boran Zhang, Saining Zhang, Mingze Sun, Hao Zhao, Ruqi Huang, Zhihao Li, Yufei Li

entry.summary: DAR turns a pretrained video diffusion model into a 4D renderer by projecting a neural geometry buffer of tracking, world position, and normals from an animated mesh and injecting it alongside camera ray conditioning. The question addressed is what image-format condition lets a video backbone obey both camera motion and scene-internal animation.

entry.title: Messages, Not Tokens: Grounded Coresets for Faithful VLM Compression

author.name: Long Qian, Jiaqi Wei, Bingke Zhu, Yingying Chen, Jinqiao Wang

entry.summary: Reformulates visual token compression in vision-language models as building a compact coreset that preserves the collective attention messages the decoder receives, rather than keeping top-scoring tokens independently. Argues top-K selection redundantly covers salient regions and discards complementary evidence.

entry.title: VC-Tooler: Learning Compositional and Adaptive Visual Tool Use

author.name: Yizheng Wu, Jiashen Hua, Bing Deng, Jieping Ye

entry.summary: VC-Tooler trains vision-language models to use visual tools compositionally and adaptively rather than in fixed patterns, using a hierarchically synthesized trajectory bank covering single-tool, multi-tool, and observation-adaptive behaviors. Targets agentic multimodal reasoning that actively acquires visual evidence.

entry.title: DF$^3$: World Modeling via Decoder-Free Feature Forecasting in Autonomous Navigation

author.name: Jiaming Chen, Guoan Xu, Aoshen Huang, Haozhuo Zhang, Yang Li, Wei Pan

entry.summary: DF3 proposes a world model for autonomous navigation that forecasts future states entirely in latent feature space and reads task outputs directly from those features, removing the pixel decoder that dominates compute in prior video world models. The claim is that eliminating the decoder both cuts cost and avoids wasting capacity on task-irrelevant appearance detail.

entry.title: FlowPilot: Real-Time World-Action Modeling for Agile UAV Navigation

author.name: Runqing Wang, Ding Yu, Pengyuan Min, Xinhong Zhang, Wei Xiao, Yu Hu, Jie Chen, Fu Zhang, Gang Wang

entry.summary: FlowPilot is a compact world-action model that jointly denoises future depth observations and executable trajectories with flow matching for onboard UAV navigation, using a dual-stream mixture-of-transformers so scene prediction and trajectory generation inform each other. At deployment it emits only trajectories parameterized as degree-7 Bernstein polynomials constrained to be trackable from the current state.

entry.title: Bridging the Sim-to-Real Gap in Parallel-Link Leg Mechanisms via Simulator-Side Dynamics Normalization

author.name: Jinsong Hong, Jangho Kim, Jihwan Lee, Donghyun Kim, Sehoon Oh

entry.summary: The paper closes a sim-to-real dynamics gap that appears when parallel-link legs are approximated by serial-tree models in simulators, by normalizing effective actuator inertia and damping on the simulator side. Two variants trade fidelity against complexity while keeping tree topology.

entry.title: Teleopit: A Full-Embodiment Humanoid Teleoperation System

author.name: Bingqian Wu, Zicheng Xu, Xianghui Fan, Dayu Li, Xiangru Huang

entry.summary: Teleopit is a VR-driven full-body humanoid teleoperation system covering whole-body motion, configurable dexterous hands, and an active two-degree-of-freedom head. It includes a history-conditioned motion tracker with failure-aware rewind sampling and an optimization-based hand retargeter.

entry.title: StableMimic: Smooth Human-Like Recovery for Humanoid Motion Tracking - Learning Beyond the Tracking Distribution for Structured Post-Fall Behavior

author.name: Weihao Wu, Ming Huang, Ruofei Liu, Jinglei Nie, Shuxiang Guo, Chunying Li

entry.summary: This paper formalizes when a fixed action sequence produced by a learned policy can be certified safe on a real system given only a handful of observed transitions, and proves an impossibility-style trilemma. Under bounded model error it derives a plan-dependent lower bound on the width of any sound reachable tube.

entry.title: Certifying Plans under Model Mismatch: A Trilemma for Reachability from Scarce Data

author.name: Yanliang Huang, Zhen Zhang, Ahmad Hafez, Wenyuan Wu, Peng Xie, Zhuoqi Zeng, Amr Alanwar

entry.summary: StableMimic trains humanoid motion trackers on states outside the nominal tracking distribution, including prone and off-balance post-fall configurations, so the robot performs structured human-like recovery instead of chasing infeasible references. Perturbed resets around human get-up references generate the training distribution.

entry.title: Probabilistic Reachable-Action Verification of Visuomotor Policies via Set-Based Training

author.name: Yanliang Huang, Zhuocheng Zhang, Peng Xie, Zhen Zhang, Wenyuan Wu, Majid Khadiv, Zhuoqi Zeng, Amr Alanwar

entry.summary: To make reachability analysis tractable for visuomotor policies, the authors freeze the visual encoder and propagate zonotope sets only through the low-dimensional interface to the action head, calibrating the interface set from camera-pose perturbations. Split conformal calibration then turns action deviations into probabilistic reachable-action guarantees.

entry.title: Wasserstein gradient flows of Maximum Mean Discrepancy with energy kernels

author.name: Matthew Rosenzweig, Dejan Slep\v{c}ev, Lihan Wang

entry.summary: A mathematical study of Wasserstein gradient flows of squared maximum mean discrepancy with nonsmooth energy kernels, which lack displacement semiconvexity so standard theory does not apply. The authors prove global well-posedness, particle non-collision, and mean-field convergence results.

entry.title: AgentStream: How Well Do Self-Evolving LLM Agents Perform Under Streaming Tasks?

author.name: Dong Yan, Jian Liang, Dapeng Hu, Ran He, Nicholas Jing Yuan, Qi Zhang, Tieniu Tan

entry.summary: AgentStream evaluates self-evolving agents under realistic streaming task sequences rather than isolated benchmarks, instantiating isolated, sequential, and interleaved regimes that vary domain mixing. It aims to reveal how experience accumulation helps or hurts when task distributions shift.

entry.title: Escaping Confidence Trap: Evolutionary Decoding for Mathematical Reasoning in Diffusion LLMs

author.name: Zhenhong Sun, Hanqing Zhao, Yatao Bian, Rongcheng Tu, Liuyue Xie, Xu Zhang, Jue Wang, Davide Modolo, Daoyi Dong, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: Analyzes decoding in diffusion language models and identifies a confidence trap where locally confident token unmasking diverges from globally correct reasoning during block decoding. Proposes an evolutionary decoding strategy to escape both sampling-sensitive and systematically wrong failure regimes on math tasks.

entry.title: Judging Is Not Enumerating: Silent Omissions in LLM-Authored Acceptable Sets

author.name: Wenhui Chen, Jianlin Chen, Ziyao Lin, Peiji Long, Chi Man Vong

entry.summary: Shows that models are much better at judging whether a candidate belongs to an acceptable set than at authoring the set themselves, with large F1 gaps across four reference constructions including hardened code benchmarks and lexical references. This undercuts the common practice of having LLMs write test suites, rubrics, and reward functions.

entry.title: Computing with Agentic Oracles

author.name: Jie Wang

entry.summary: Extends stochastic-oracle models of computation to agentic oracles that pursue goals autonomously and consume hidden environment resources, distinguishing orchestration token cost visible to the caller from agentic token cost incurred internally. The framework provides a way to reason about total cost and complexity of computing with AI agents as subroutines.

entry.title: Wnuan: Staged Post-Training for Question Answering over Proprietary Enterprise Knowledge

author.name: Xiaofeng Shi, Xiaosong Qiu, Wenxin Ma, Qian Kou, Yiming Pan, Longbin Yu, Ying Liu, Haiping Wang, Hua Zhou

entry.summary: Wnuan is a three-stage enterprise question-answering pipeline that builds task-oriented supervision from internal documents, fine-tunes with general-data replay to avoid capability loss, then applies reinforcement learning targeted at residual errors. On a 707-question internal benchmark acceptable-answer rate rises from about 53 percent to 80 percent after fine-tuning and about 92 percent after RL, with residual-error sampling beating random sampling under matched update budgets.

entry.title: MetaRoute-Bench: Evaluating Meta-Decision Policies for Agentic Workflow Routing

author.name: Natan Vidra, Alina Kapanova, Arun Kanhai, Spurthi Setty

entry.summary: MetaRoute-Bench is an open benchmark for the meta-decisions agents make (answer directly, decompose, call a tool, run code, delegate, verify, recover), evaluating eight routing policies over 180 synthetic task profiles and 43,200 traces under a shared execution model. It isolates orchestration policy quality from end-task accuracy and accounts for cost and latency.

entry.title: Me and My Bot: What Users Talk About in AI Companion Communities on Reddit

author.name: Richard A. Fabes

entry.summary: Using multiple LLMs to code 5,504 Reddit posts from eight AI companion communities, this study finds that only about 45 percent of posts concern the user's own relationship with a bot despite relationally weighted search terms, and that posts about one's own bot differ markedly in topic and emotional valence from posts about bots in general. It challenges the prevailing characterization of these communities as primarily relationship-discussion spaces.

entry.title: Anticipatory Digital Twins for Online Head-and-Neck Adaptive Proton Therapy via Foundation-Model Registration

author.name: Yizhou Wu, Yuheng Li, Xiaofeng Yang, Chih-Wei Chang

entry.summary: Proposes a digital-twin pipeline that predicts a head-and-neck cancer patient's treatment-day anatomy before imaging, by transferring longitudinal deformation patterns from a population database using foundation-model image registration. The goal is to enable same-day adaptive proton replanning instead of week-long offline replanning workflows.

entry.title: REIMU: Efficient Heterogeneous Hierarchical Reasoning for SSL-Based Speech Deepfake Detection

author.name: Kwok-Ho Ng, Tingting Song, Bingwen Feng, Peiya Li

entry.summary: A controlled comparison of recurrent hierarchical reasoning backbones (weight-shared recurrence, homogeneous and heterogeneous hierarchical reasoning modules) versus single-pass heads for self-supervised speech deepfake detection across four SSL frontends. Tests whether iterative latent reasoning helps audio anti-spoofing.

entry.title: Policy Optimality Measurement for Multi-Vehicle Decision-Making: From Extrinsic Indicators to Intrinsic Quality

author.name: Ye Han, Lijun Zhang, Dejian Meng

entry.summary: Proposes an information-theoretic diagnostic for multi-agent driving policies that uses a fully converged Monte Carlo Tree Search as an asymptotic oracle and scores policies by forward KL divergence from that reference, decoupled into lateral and longitudinal components. Intended to expose policy degradation hidden by reward curves and success rates.

entry.title: No One Wins in Nuclear War: A Social Simulation of Military Decision-making

author.name: Glenn Matlin, Isaac Song, Anthony Wen-Ming Zang, Mark Riedl

entry.summary: WOPR is a social simulation environment for studying high-stakes organizational decision-making, built on a deterministic replay-validated rules engine and instantiated with a published nuclear war card game plus private-channel negotiation between LLM agents. It contributes verifiable mechanics where prior social simulation work emphasized persona fidelity alone.

entry.title: Self-Improving Large Language Models via Progressive Experience Evolution

author.name: Shijie Ren, Xiting Wang, Meng Li, Yujie Guo, Yunhang Yao, Ziheng Peng, Xunlong Wang, Yuetan Chen, Haoyang Zhou, Yunlong Liang, Fandong Meng

entry.summary: SPEE proposes experience distillation as the missing bridge between test-time methods that extract experience without internalizing it and training-time optimization that updates parameters without accumulating transferable experience. The framework progressively converts interaction experience into persistent model capability.

entry.title: Posterior Variance Is a Constraint Map, Not an Error Map: Closed-Form Uncertainty for Radiative Gaussian Splatting in Sparse-View CT

author.name: Chulin Zhao, Yiran Xu, Shu Liu

entry.summary: Argues that per-Gaussian posterior variance in radiative Gaussian splatting for sparse-view CT measures data constraint rather than reconstruction error, so its high-variance alarms are meaningful but its low-variance all-clears are not. Exploiting linearity of X-ray rendering, it derives a clamp-aware closed form computable in one forward pass, matching the infinite-sample limit of sampling estimators at roughly eight times lower cost.

entry.title: Human-LLM Alignment in Language Attitudes Toward Non-Native Japanese

author.name: Naho Orita, Hayato Ogawa, Daisuke Kawahara

entry.summary: Compares Japanese human raters and six LLM judges on parallel first- and second-language Japanese emails across fluency, status, and solidarity dimensions. LLM judges reproduce the human penalty against non-native writing but understate the socially grounded solidarity gap, which matters because such judges are increasingly used in hiring and academic assessment.

entry.title: Divergent large language model predictions from convergent representations in ambiguous word pairs

author.name: K. Jack Scott, Narun Pat, Veronica Liesaputra

entry.summary: Traces how three decoder-only transformers of different sizes resolve homonyms and polysemes layer by layer, finding representations separate most in middle layers then partially reconverge while output distributions diverge maximally at the end. Activation patching provides causal evidence that late-layer differences drive the divergent predictions despite apparent embedding similarity.

entry.title: Token-Native Storage: Read and Write in your Agent's Language

author.name: Kumar Shivendu

entry.summary: Argues that databases and search engines should store text as byte-pair-encoding token IDs rather than UTF-8, since embedders, rerankers, and agents already operate in token space and pay a conversion cost on every access. Reported compression across six tokenizers and three corpora beats byte-level codecs, with English gains of roughly two to three times.

entry.title: LeapTalk: Breaking the Latency-Quality Trade-off in Talking Head Generation

author.name: Rongxiang Zhang, Songhua Liu

entry.summary: LeapTalk generates real-time long-form talking-head video in a single forward step using bridge distillation with a data-to-data Brownian bridge formulation anchored to a persistent reference. The design targets both the multi-step cost of diffusion and the identity drift of autoregressive streaming approaches.

entry.title: SpatialQuery: Benchmarking Geometry-Grounded Multi-Instance Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Hai Nguyen, Tung Vu, Cong Tran

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark of over a million question-answer pairs testing whether vision-language models can pick the nearest instance of an object category and estimate floor-plane distance from a single RGB image. Also proposes a training-free pipeline that recovers metric geometry and reasons in a top-down canonical view.

entry.title: Beyond Global Latents: Chunk-Based Sparse Grid VAE for Scalable 3D Modeling

author.name: Kaiyi Zhang, Zhihao Liang, Haolin Liu, Qingxiang Lin, Zeqiang Lai, Yunfei Zhao, Bowen Zhang, Xianghui Yang, Zibo Zhao, Chunchao Guo, Long Quan

entry.summary: ChunkVAE encodes sparse voxel 3D shapes in local chunks instead of a single global latent volume, letting encoder and decoder partitions differ and inference chunk sizes deviate from training. Two data operators balance active cells and attenuate unreliable chunk-boundary features when stitching.

entry.title: MIEScore: Human-Aligned Evaluation for Multi-Source Image Editing

author.name: Zitong Xu, Huiyu Duan, Xinyun Zhang, Weifei Xiong, Tianyi Zheng, Xiongkuo Min, Qiang Hu, Zhengxue Cheng, Bo Li, Guangtao Zhai

entry.summary: Introduces the first large benchmark with fine-grained human preference annotations for multi-source image editing, where several images are combined for composition or style fusion, and an accompanying automatic scoring model. Notes that recent unified image models show emerging multi-source editing ability that existing single-image metrics cannot assess.

entry.title: TWINS: A Tactile Wearable Isomorphic Arm Networked System for Contact-Rich Manipulation Learning

author.name: Takahide Kitamura, Masaki Murooka, Natsuki Yamanobe, Yukiyasu Domae

entry.summary: TWINS is a teleoperation setup pairing a wearable dual-arm device with an isomorphic robot of matching kinematics, with distributed tactile sensors on chest and arms. It enables demonstration collection for manipulation tasks that involve whole-body-surface contact rather than only end-effector grasping.

entry.title: CT-PrepAgent: Bounded Policy and Controlled Execution for Adaptive CT Data Preparation

author.name: Xiaolin Fan, Yue Pei, Yingying Zhang, Haogang Zhu

entry.summary: CT-PrepAgent uses an LLM agent constrained by a bounded policy and deterministic execution gates to adapt CT imaging data-preparation pipelines to heterogeneous scanners and downstream tasks. Deterministic inspection constrains what the agent may propose, aiming for reproducibility rather than free-form code generation.

entry.title: Constructing Executable Analytical Knowledge Representations for Meta-Analysis Synthesis Using an Agentic Harness

author.name: Lingbo Li, Anuradha Mathrani, Teo Susnjak

entry.summary: Proposes an Executable Analytical Knowledge Representation that makes explicit the analytical decisions behind meta-analysis, including evidence assignment, contrasts, outcome and timepoint alignment, effect-size choice, and admissibility, then executes statistics from that representation via an agentic harness. The point is that these decisions should be independently auditable knowledge rather than buried in model output or generated code.

entry.title: HPFA: Hypergraph-Based Paired Failure Attribution for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Runchuan Zhu, Hongbin Lai, Bowen Jiang, Junrui Zhang, Zhangheng LI, Ostap Kilbasovych, Junyuan Hong

entry.summary: HPFA attributes reasoning failures by representing a trace as a hypergraph and comparing hyperedges of a failing path against a successful reference path, avoiding costly step-by-step counterfactual testing. The goal is scalable localization of root-cause reasoning steps to make self-reflection effective.

entry.title: MemArbiter: Decision-Time Memory Arbitration for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Jiajun Dong, Yutao Hu, Fengrui Fan, Shihan Dou, Yueming Wu, Deqing Zou

entry.summary: MemArbiter names a Memory-Action Gap where retrievable memory still fails to influence the current decision, and addresses it by decomposing history into atomic items sorted into five functional memory banks with relevance, focal-ambient and temporal gating. Targets coherence in long-horizon agent tasks.

entry.title: Shared Prefixes, Better Credit: Adaptive Routing for Multi-Agent Reasoning

author.name: Yiqing Liu, Zihao Wang, Hantao Yao, Wu Liu, Yongdong Zhang

entry.summary: TreeCredit improves credit assignment in multi-agent reasoning by expanding candidate operators from the same intermediate state into shared-prefix collaboration trees and comparing state-matched downstream outcomes. This yields finer-grained operator utility estimates than query-level or trajectory-level supervision for adaptive routing.

entry.title: Obshazard-bench: Benchmarking Multimodal Foundation Models for Real-Time Disaster Intelligence from Raw Earth Observation Streams

author.name: Fengxiang Wang, Qiuyang Yu, Yueying Li, Mingshuo Chen, Chengchi Fei, Kaiyi Xu, Lixin Gu, Wangxu Wei, Junchao Gong, Lipeng Ma, Jiong Wang, Fenghua Ling, Wenlong Zhang, Xue Yang, Wenjing Yang, Ben Fei, Long Lan

entry.summary: Obshazard-bench evaluates multimodal foundation models on real-time disaster intelligence using raw high-frequency satellite observation streams rather than curated post-event products or gridded reanalysis. Designed to reflect operational constraints where hazards evolve quickly and decisions are time-limited.

entry.title: Which Modality Decides? Counterfactual Modality Attribution for Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Vahidin Hasic, Chao Wang, Luis C. Garcia-Peraza-Herrera, David Watson, Senka Krivic

entry.summary: Counterfactual Modality Attribution quantifies how much a multimodal LLM's prediction is driven by image versus text by comparing image-only, text-only and joint conditions, rather than highlighting influential regions or tokens. The aim is to expose cases where a model gets the right answer from the wrong modality, revealing shortcut learning.

entry.title: Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype Conditioning for Language-Free Medical Anomaly Detection

author.name: Yibo Wan, Jinyu Cai, Seekiong-Ng

entry.summary: ReCAP replaces the fixed text prompts or learned static tokens used by CLIP-based medical anomaly detectors with input-conditioned visual prototypes, re-centering separated normal and abnormal prototypes per test image via bounded gated modulation. The aim is language-free anomaly detection and lesion localization that transfers across unseen organs and imaging modalities.

entry.title: An Embedded RISC-V Evaluation of Kolmogorov--Arnold Networks in Hard-Constrained Recurrent Physics-Informed Models

author.name: Enzo Nicolas Spotorno, Josafat Leal Filho

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks against multilayer perceptrons as the residual branch of hard-constrained recurrent physics-informed models on embedded RISC-V hardware, asking whether KAN parameter efficiency survives deployment given the very different execution profile of learnable B-spline activations. Identical trained weights are used to isolate inference cost.

entry.title: SG-Layout: Structured Scene Graph-Guided Layout Generation with LLMs

author.name: Junsheng Wang, Chao Chen, Mengying Xie, Mingyan Li, Fuqiang Gu

entry.summary: SG-Layout injects scene-graph embeddings into an LLM via a relational graph encoder and projector, then instruction-tunes with LoRA so the model generates spatially coherent layouts from natural language. Targets LLM weakness at explicit geometric relations and structural dependencies.

entry.title: DeVIT: Low-Power Vision Transformer Acceleration Using Delta Computation

author.name: Reyhaneh Hosseinzadeh, Parham Zilouchian Moghaddam, Mehdi Modarressi

entry.summary: DeVIT is a hardware accelerator design that exploits value locality in quantized vision transformers by computing on deltas between similar values to cut power and memory bandwidth. Targets deployment of transformers on resource-constrained devices.

entry.title: DeepVoyager-VL: Incentivizing Vision-in-the-Loop Search for Long-Horizon Multimodal Agents

author.name: Huanyao Zhang, Jiepeng Zhou, Runhao Zhao, Yanzhe Shan, Jiaoyang Chen, Bowen Zhou, Bo Li, Fang Wang, Jialong Wu, Zhengwei Tao, Lang Mei, Xiaohan Yu, Liyan Liu, Chong Chen, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: DeepVoyager-VL trains multimodal agents to keep vision in the loop during long-horizon deep search, so visual evidence drives subsequent retrieval steps rather than only appearing at input or answer time. It targets knowledge-intensive open-world questions that static parametric knowledge cannot answer.

entry.title: Recompute or Reuse? Diagnosing and Mitigating Textual Shortcuts in VLM Self-Reflection

author.name: Wenxiao Fan, Jingling Fu, Fang Li, Luohang Liu, Yu He, Lichen Ma, Zhiyang Yu, Weishan Bi, Junshi Huang, Yan Li, Gu Simiu, Kan Li

entry.summary: The paper shows that vision-language models often reuse evidence-bearing text from a prior chain of thought instead of re-examining changed images, and that removing that evidence content shifts answers more than removing other context. Across sixteen VLMs this textual shortcut, not merely weak visual attention, explains failures of self-reflection.

entry.title: IACM-RL: Intent-Aware Context Management and Reinforcement Learning for Complex Tool Invocation under Dynamic Intent Fluctuations

author.name: Dingwei Zhu, Jiahan Li, Chengjun Pan, Yunxian Yang, Yunbin Zhao, Yunke Zhang, Zhonghang Lu, Zhuohui Sheng, Chenhao Huang, Jiahang Lin, Yajie Yang, Junlin Shang, Shichun Liu, Yuhui Wang, Honglin Guo, Junjie Ye, Xin Guo, Jiazheng Zhang, Ming Zhang, Shihan Dou, Zhiheng Xi, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang, Xipeng Qiu, Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: IACM-RL makes long-horizon LLM tool use robust to changing user intent by synthesizing training trajectories across thirteen fluctuation scenarios and maintaining an explicit belief state, so obsolete constraints do not dilute attention and trigger intent drift or infinite API loops. It pairs the data pipeline with a diagnostic metric suite and reinforcement learning.

entry.title: GROVE: Growing and Reasoning over Temporally Stratified Memory from Streaming Video Experience

author.name: Sitong Gong, Caixin Kang, Tianyu Yan, Guo Chen, Bo Zheng, Kaipeng Zhang, Yunzhi Zhuge, Xiang Ruan, Huchuan Lu, Yifei Huang

entry.summary: GROVE is a training-free memory framework for wearable assistants that grows causally from a continuous video stream, consolidating fine-grained perceptual evidence into time-stamped moments, episodes, and recurring cross-day patterns, each with a matched retrieval skill. One memory supports both answering questions about visual history and proactively recognizing when past experience is relevant now.

entry.title: Leak It: A Probabilistic Approach to Training-Data Extraction from Black-Box Language Models

author.name: Victor Maricato

entry.summary: Reframes black-box training-data leakage as estimating functionals of the sampling distribution and stress-tests it against model-free blind baselines. Reports that on a popular membership-inference dataset a bag-of-words classifier alone reaches near-perfect AUC while sampling-based signals add nothing, and on an IID split no signal beats blind baselines.

entry.title: On the Identifiability of Masked Prediction: Mode Blindness and Mask Schedules

author.name: Yichao Cai, Javen Qinfeng Shi

entry.summary: Asks when masked prediction objectives actually identify the underlying joint distribution, and shows that for data with two well-separated modes the answer is determined by the mask schedule alone. Schedules dominated by large visible contexts are provably blind to global mode weights, motivating an epsilon-identifiability measure.

entry.title: Meganeura: Portable GPU Training and Inference through Vulkan and Metal

author.name: Dzmitry Malyshau

entry.summary: Meganeura is a compact native compiler and runtime that performs both training and inference on consumer GPUs via Vulkan and Metal, including autodiff, optimizers, checkpointing and memory planning. It is benchmarked against PyTorch on NVIDIA, AMD, Apple and Intel hardware with strict versus fast numerical gating.

entry.title: Finite-Time Analysis of Discounted Exponential-Utility Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ankur Naskar, Vivek T A, Aditya Kumar, Gugan Thoppe, Prashanth L. A

entry.summary: Provides finite-time convergence rates of order one over root-n for two recently proposed model-free algorithms that optimize a discounted exponential-utility (risk-sensitive) objective under asynchronous Markovian sampling, using parameter-free stepsizes. This upgrades prior asymptotic-only guarantees.

entry.title: CoRe-GNN: Multilevel Message passing on Coarsened graphs

author.name: Antonin Joly, Nicolas Keriven, Aline Roumy

entry.summary: Reframes several scalable GNN training methods as structured modifications of the propagation matrix, showing graph coarsening and Cluster-GCN as complementary failure modes of the same node-grouping decomposition. CoRe-GNN combines coarsened multilevel message passing with intra-cluster propagation to reduce memory while retaining long-range information.

entry.title: Constrained Co-Design for Photonic Bayesian Neural Networks

author.name: Hendrik Borras, Xiao Wang, Bernhard Klein, Robin Janssen, Frank Br\"uckerhoff-Pl\"uckelmann, Wolfram Pernice, Holger Fr\"oning

entry.summary: Co-designs Bayesian neural networks with photonic probabilistic hardware whose analog samplers are imperfect, explicitly modeling quantization, programming error, dynamic range and representable mean and variance constraints. The goal is calibrated uncertainty and out-of-distribution robustness at low latency and energy on optical accelerators.

entry.title: Fast Trainable Multilinear Bases for Image Compression

author.name: Shiwen An, Zhongyi Ni, Huanhai Zhou, Jin-Guo Liu

entry.summary: Generalizes fixed transforms like DCT and DFT to trainable isometric multilinear bases parameterized as isometric tensor networks, adding only polylogarithmically many parameters while keeping near-linear runtime and exact invertibility. A search framework finds the basis that best compresses a given image dataset.

entry.title: Non-KKT Accumulation in Entropic Mirror Descent

author.name: Kuangyu Ding, Kim-Chuan Toh

entry.summary: Answers negatively a basic question in constrained optimization by constructing smooth objectives for which bounded entropic mirror descent sequences accumulate at non-KKT points. The mechanism is that the Legendre gradient blows up at the boundary, so the inverse entropy metric vanishes on active coordinates and destroys dual feasibility in the limit.

entry.title: Practical Online KV Cache Compaction for LLM Agents: An Empirical Study

author.name: Yujian Liu, Jiabao Ji, Li An, Rohit Jain, Gungor Polatkan, Siyu Zhu, Shiyu Chang

entry.summary: Empirically studies KV cache compaction under the realistic online constraint faced by agents, where content must be compressed before future queries are known. Compares token eviction versus attention matching with cheap proxy queries on browsing and search benchmarks.

entry.title: PALMs: Using Multi Construct-Grounded Rationales for Modeling Population Preferences in LLMs

author.name: Priyanka Dey, Brihi Joshi, Preyashi Poddar, Jieyu Zhao, Emilio Ferrara

entry.summary: Aligns separate model variants to five national populations by synthesizing rationales grounded in psychological and cultural constructs and using them as latent supervision during preference tuning. Evaluates on personality, values, cultural norms, and morality, outperforming baseline persona prompting.

entry.title: Global Optimization and Inference-Time Region Grafting for Agentic Workflows

author.name: Donghyeok Koh, Gyuwan Kim, Jinyeong Bak, Seung-Hoon Na, Tao Yang, Haneol Jang, Cheoneum Park

entry.summary: GRAFT keeps a globally optimized agentic workflow but replaces only failing regions at inference time, using label-free execution-quality signals to accept local substitutions. This avoids the prohibitive cost of re-optimizing an entire workflow per input while still allowing runtime adaptation.

entry.title: Image-Space Rule Discovery

author.name: Misora Sugiyama, Toya Oyama, Hirokatsu Kataoka

entry.summary: WISRD tests whether image-editing models can read instructions embedded in images, infer the underlying visual rule, and produce correctly edited outputs, covering marking, filling, copying, counting, and suppression of unnecessary edits. It frames the evaluation like a human worksheet or nonverbal IQ test across eleven core tasks and multiple information conditions.

entry.title: Dynamic Resolution Routing for Efficient Egocentric Grounding

author.name: Huixin Sun, Wangbo Zhao, Fanyue Wei, Qiuxia Lin, Pengzhan Sun, Angela Yao

entry.summary: SmartRes cuts the cost of high-resolution egocentric grounding by routing computation in pixel space: a low-resolution global pass plus a lightweight router that selectively upsamples object-centric patches. Argues token-pruning approaches are unreliable for selecting spatial evidence.

entry.title: DiffPrune: differentiable information throttling for token pruning in vision-language models

author.name: Landi He, Mingde Yao, Shawn Young, Lijian Xu

entry.summary: DiffPrune trains visual token pruning scores by continuously throttling each token's information during training rather than using Gumbel-Softmax discrete relaxations, so scores directly reflect the cost of information loss. Yields interpretable importance scores tied to task degradation.

entry.title: GIFT: Geometry-Invariant Fine-Tuning for Non-Lambertian Monocular Depth Estimation

author.name: Xianghui Fan, Zhaoyu Chen, Bingqian Wu, Dayu Li, Xin Zeng, Huanran Cui, Guangzhen Xu, Xiangru Huang, Hang Yang

entry.summary: GIFT fine-tunes monocular depth foundation models so they stop hallucinating reflected or transmitted content on mirrors and glass, exploiting the insight that surface geometry is invariant while appearance changes with the environment. It is parameter-efficient and needs no ground-truth depth measurements.

entry.title: Assistant Placement Aria: A Benchmark for Egocentric Placement Assistance

author.name: Amir Belder, Gon\c{c}alo Dias Pais, Refael Vivanti, Omri Carmi, Daniel DeTone, Oren Shrout, Ido Gattegno, Ayellet Tal

entry.summary: Assistant Placement Aria introduces a benchmark for virtual placement, the task of identifying all plausible locations to put an object given scene geometry, semantics, and human-centric constraints, rather than a single predefined target. It uses egocentric data and involves researchers associated with egocentric perception hardware.

entry.title: Motif-Mamba: network motif improved mamba for long-range sequence modeling

author.name: Chonghe Hao, Yue Sun, Jian Zhang, Yansong Wang, Wangzi Yao, Yunjie Yao, Tielin Zhang

entry.summary: Motif-Mamba augments state space models with a low-rank recurrent pathway inspired by three-node network motifs, adding cross-dimensional state interactions that plain diagonal Mamba transitions lack. The aim is better long-range sequence modeling at linear cost.

entry.title: RMSWeb: Reflection, Failure-Mode Mining, and Salvage-DS for Web Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Chengbo Liu, Lifang Zhou, Ruijie Yan, Pei Tan, Ao Sun, Haojun Huang, Guichun Hua, Sining Wei, Yining Chen, Yingying He, Yutao Xie

entry.summary: RMSWeb is a training recipe for compact web agents combining reflection-conditioned retries to collect better trajectories, mining of failure modes to focus data, and a salvage mechanism giving learning signal to groups rejected by group-relative RL. It is applied to 8B and 32B vision-language backbones.

entry.title: Mask-Based Priors Are More Persistent than Query-Key Initializations

author.name: Mingze Ma, Hemanth Saratchandran, Cameron Gordon, Simon Lucey

entry.summary: Studies why Transformers extrapolate wrongly on Boolean tasks, defaulting to a minimum-degree interpolator, and asks whether structural priors injected into attention can fix it. It finds that priors imposed through attention masks persist through training far better than priors imposed via query-key initialization.

entry.title: CURE: Local Uncertainty Repair for Block-Parallel Speculative Decoding

author.name: Aofan Liu, Jingxiang Meng, Fangxin Liu, Yongbiao Chen

entry.summary: CURE improves block-parallel speculative decoding by observing that draft errors concentrate at a few high-uncertainty tokens, then spending a limited repair budget on a dynamic tree that fixes those focal points. This raises acceptance rates without heavy tree-verification overhead.

entry.title: Through the LENS: Local Geometric Decomposition of Vision-Language Model Representations

author.name: Shalom Kachko, Raz Lapid, Margarita Vald, Almog Dubin, Moshe Sipper

entry.summary: LENS decomposes vision-language model activations into locally low-rank Gaussian neighborhoods using a mixture of factor analyzers, capturing structure that global linear probing methods miss. Applied to two open VLMs it reveals distinct depth-dependent modality fusion trajectories matching each model's architecture.

entry.title: Measurement Without Validity: The Compounding Reliability Problem in Agentic AI Evaluation

author.name: William Caban

entry.summary: Argues that agentic AI benchmark scores are less trustworthy than deployment and compliance decisions assume, citing validity flaws found in seven of ten audited benchmarks, large variance between LLM user simulators, and compounding unreliability across evaluation layers. It warns about regulatory reliance on such scores.

entry.title: The Scaling Paradox in Human-AI Collaboration

author.name: Anyan Qi, Mengxin Wang

entry.summary: Develops an analytical model of when scaling-law improvements in AI capability actually translate into better joint human-AI performance, showing positive scaling requires humans to perceive AI capability accurately. Human misperception can break or even reverse the benefit of a stronger model.

entry.title: Role-Decoupled Attention Residuals: Separating Matching and Content Retrieval Across Depth

author.name: Kehan Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Role-Decoupled Attention Residuals, which let a Transformer layer read queries and keys from one depth-mixture of earlier representations while values read from an independently learned depth route. The motivating claim is that deciding where attention matches and what content it retrieves are functionally distinct and should not be tied to the same layer.

entry.title: Perspectives on Tsallis Statistics for Artificial Intelligence

author.name: Kleyton da Costa, Bernardo Modenesi

entry.summary: A structured survey and perspective on how Tsallis statistics, controlled by a single entropic parameter, already underpins sparse attention such as sparsemax and entmax, maximum-entropy RL with tunable exploration, heavy-tailed probabilistic models, and generalized losses. It proposes viewing these as instances of one framework and sketches open directions.

entry.title: CraftAlign: Feature-Grounded Evaluation and Revision Guidance for AI Stories

author.name: Yang Yang, Boyun Xu, Shaofeng Liang, Yun Han, Zining Zhong, Songning Lai, Kaishen Yuan, Yutao Yue

entry.summary: CraftAlign evaluates AI-generated stories against craft-level features such as cliche density, over-explanation, linear causality, and stereotyped endings, and turns those diagnostics into story-wide revision guidance rather than local edits. It targets the recognizable flatness of machine fiction beyond binary human-versus-AI detection.

entry.title: KoVRE: Training an Efficient Embedding Model for Korean Visual Document Retrieval

author.name: Yongbin Choi, Gyuho Shim, Youngjoon Jang

entry.summary: KoVRE is a single-vector Korean visual document retrieval embedding model trained on roughly 709k Korean and English query-page pairs with positive-aware hard-negative mining, plus controlled ablations on data composition and negative selection. It targets the English-centric and storage-heavy nature of existing document-image retrievers.

entry.title: CockpitHAT: Dependency-Graph-Driven Hierarchical Attribution for Embodied Multi-Agent Cockpits

author.name: Wei Wang, Shuanghe Liu, Zhu Zhuo, Jiaqi Zhong, Xiaozhao Zhao, Xiaojie Zuo, Jie Su

entry.summary: CockpitHAT attributes failures in embodied multi-agent automotive cockpit systems where high task accuracy masks dangerous process-level errors, replacing positional text windows with dependency-distance thresholds from interaction graphs and adding multi-channel embodied evidence. It weights high-risk failures more heavily during confidence-weighted consensus among analyst models.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Complex Eigenfrequency Identification and Mode Structure Reconstruction of the Ground-State ITG Branch

author.name: Dengdi Sun, Bingbing Zhang, Xiao Wang, Zikang Yan, Yuqiang Tao, Qingquan Yang, Guosheng Xu, Jin Tang

entry.summary: Applies physics-informed neural networks to simultaneously identify complex eigenfrequencies and reconstruct two-dimensional complex-valued mode fields for ion-temperature-gradient drift waves in the steep-gradient edge of high-confinement tokamak plasmas. It addresses localized high-frequency oscillations and strong coupling between mode field and eigenfrequency that destabilize joint PINN optimization.

entry.title: Evolving in the Agent Jungle via History-Informed Opponent Awareness

author.name: Zhaofeng Zhang, Linhan Xia, Rui Liu, Yihao Wang, Binrui Shen, Shengxin Zhu

entry.summary: OASE addresses skill-library evolution when opponents are also adapting, so the reference point for judging a skill revision is constantly stale. It uses paired comparisons between candidate and incumbent skills to keep only revisions that are genuinely beneficial in a moving multi-agent environment.

entry.title: Before Reasoning Fails: Pre-Evidence Procedural Failures in Agentic RAG

author.name: Daeyoung Roh, Donghee Han

entry.summary: Studies a procedural failure mode where agentic RAG systems retrieve snippets but answer without reading them, separating pre-evidence discipline failures from post-read reasoning failures across 12,000 paired trajectories. Proposes Read-Gate, a runtime invariant forcing a read after each search.

entry.title: From Profiling to Synthesis: Benchmarking Implicit Behavioral Alignment in Personalized LLM Agents

author.name: Jiajia Song, Bobo Li, Haiwen Yi, Zibo Ji, Meishan Zhang, Hao Fei, Min Zhang, Mong-Li Lee, Wynne Hsu

entry.summary: IBA-Bench evaluates whether personalized agents actually act on user preferences inferred from noisy longitudinal interaction histories, rather than just answering questions about a stated profile. It names the gap between knowing a preference and executing on it as the knowledge-to-action gap.

entry.title: Real-Time Detection and Repair of LLM Agent Failures

author.name: Sunny Dubey

entry.summary: Trains cheap one-class monitors on healthy agent runs to detect mid-episode failures such as looping, tool-error cascades, goal drift and fabrication from step telemetry alone, avoiding per-step LLM judging. On 2,823 episodes across three frameworks and four models an echo-state-network ensemble with CUSUM alarms catches about 71 percent of failures at a 5 percent false-alarm budget.

entry.title: GRAIN: Molecules Are Not the Right Granularity -- Active-Ingredient Modeling for Safe Medication Recommendation

author.name: Juao Fan, Jinhan Li, Shengxin Zhu

entry.summary: GRAIN reframes medication recommendation from electronic health records around active ingredients rather than drug codes or molecular substructures, using a selective state-space backbone over long irregular patient visit histories. The claim is that active-ingredient granularity better matches how drug-drug interaction knowledge is actually organized, improving accuracy while reducing polypharmacy risk.

entry.title: Unleashing the Potential of Large Language Models: A Blueprint for Real-Time, Enterprise-Ready Deployments

author.name: Muhammad Faizan Raza (Luna), Shuo (Luna), Yang, Satish Mahadevan Srinivasan, Joanna F. DeFranco
