entry.summary: This paper corrects Q-value estimation in offline reinforcement learning using the behavior policy's own Q-function, aiming to reduce both excessive pessimism and overestimation bias, with theoretical convergence analysis and an error bound. Diffusion models are used to express the policy and mitigate distribution shift.

entry.title: Agentic Graph Token Reasoning

author.name: Zhuoyi Peng, Yi Yang

entry.summary: Argues that current graph-token methods feed LLMs a single static compressed graph view chosen before the model sees the query, and instead lets the model iteratively request and revise graph encodings during reasoning. Turns graph tokenization into an agentic, query-conditioned retrieval loop.

entry.title: UpliftBench: Revealing Outcome-Regime and Objective Mismatch in Uplift Evaluation

author.name: Binshuang Li

entry.summary: UpliftBench evaluates twelve treatment-effect estimators under an isolated multi-objective protocol across seven dataset families and argues that disagreement in the uplift literature stems mostly from metric choice. Reports that a widely used ranking metric shows essentially no correlation with true effect-estimation accuracy.

entry.title: CARE: A Cascaded Framework for Efficient and Reliable Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Zemin Chao, Qianhui Xu, Jianhe Cen, Guangzhi Ge, Xiao Chen, Hoangzhi Wang

entry.summary: CARE is a model-agnostic cascade for time-series anomaly detection where a lightweight residual MLP autoencoder with a normality-conditioned gate filters out easy normal points, and only uncertain points reach the heavy detector. This exploits the rarity of anomalies to cut average inference cost while retaining accuracy.

entry.title: CRIP: Channel Level Representation Injection for Personalized One-Shot Federated Learning

author.name: Zijian Jiang, Chaoli Sun, Handing Wang, Xilu Wang

entry.summary: CRIP performs one-shot federated learning under strong domain heterogeneity by aligning and injecting channel-level feature representations rather than aggregating parameters or distilling through an auxiliary public dataset. This targets the feature-shift problem that single-round federated methods usually ignore.

entry.title: Recursive Gaussian Processes and the Bayesian Brain

author.name: Moumita Das, Dipanjan Ray, Sourabh Bhattacharya

entry.summary: Draws a formal correspondence between predictive coding in cortex and recursive Gaussian processes, arguing that a single GP indexed by layer avoids the representational collapse of deep GPs while retaining exact Bayesian hierarchical inference. Components of the model are mapped onto putative neurobiological mechanisms such as precision-weighted error signaling.

entry.title: CascadeLUT: Information-Ordered Streaming Inference for Bandwidth-Constrained FPGAs

author.name: Oliver Cassidy, Marta Andronic, George A. Constantinides

entry.summary: Presents an FPGA inference framework for lookup-table neural networks that reorders input features into information-ranked subsets so predictions can be refined progressively as data streams in, rather than waiting for the full sample. This targets bandwidth-limited deployments where data movement, not compute, is the bottleneck.

entry.title: Pruned BPE: Post-training Visibility Pruning and Token Reallocation for Byte Pair Encoding

author.name: Kenny Shao

entry.summary: Notes that standard byte pair encoding exposes intermediate merge tokens to the model even when they rarely survive in the final encoding, and proposes separating merge construction from the model-visible vocabulary. Low-exposure tokens become internal-only nodes and their vocabulary slots are reallocated to better-used candidates learned through resumed training.

entry.title: Rethinking PPG-based Sleep Staging: Datasets, Metrics, and Benchmarks

author.name: Shuntian Zheng, Jiawei Wang, Cong Fu, Huan Yu, Chen Chen, Yu Guan, Sai Gu

entry.summary: Argues that the persistent gap between photoplethysmography-based and EEG-based sleep staging reflects a mismatch between what the signal carries and the 30-second clinical labeling standard rather than only modeling weakness. The paper reassesses datasets, metrics, and benchmarks for wearable sleep staging accordingly.

entry.title: Using Lower-Bound Representations for Trajectory Similarity Learning

author.name: Liwei Deng, Haotian Meng, Yupu Zhang, Yan Zhao, Torben Bach Pedersen, Kai Zheng, Christian S. Jensen

entry.summary: Replaces learned trajectory embeddings with representations assembled from analytic lower-bound components, yielding single-vector encodings that provide admissible and interpretable lower bounds for multiple trajectory distance measures. This targets fast retrieval with guarantees that neural embeddings cannot provide.

entry.title: Learning-Based Stochastic Optimal Control with Infinite-Horizon Probabilistic Constraints

author.name: Francesco Cordiano, Kanghui He, Bart De Schutter

entry.summary: Reformulates infinite-horizon stochastic control with joint chance constraints as a constrained Markov decision process via state augmentation, proves strong duality, and gives a dual ascent algorithm converging to an optimal feasible deterministic Markov policy. Function approximation extends the approach to continuous state and input spaces.

entry.title: How Benchmarks and Evaluation Protocols Shape Conclusions in Provenance-Based Intrusion Detection

author.name: Lorenzo Guerra, Thomas Chapuis, Guillaume Duc, Pavlo Mozharovskyi, Van-Tam Nguyen

entry.summary: Re-evaluates representative provenance-based intrusion detection systems under a unified protocol with temporally separated test periods and validation-only threshold calibration, asking which architectural claims actually hold. It finds that raising alerts and enabling investigation diverge sharply, with several systems flagging attacks without supplying process-level detail.

entry.title: Adaptive Reconstruction of Bosonic Quantum States

author.name: Vasilisa Usova, Phila Rembold, Ian Yang, Marco Rossignolo, Simone Montangero, Samuele Tosatto, Gerhard Kirchmair

entry.summary: Introduces an adaptive measurement strategy that estimates fidelity to a family of bosonic states related by phase-space transformations, rather than a single fixed target, while reconstructing the Wigner function from few measurements. It couples a physics-informed parametric model with Bayesian inference to cut tomography cost.

entry.title: A Spectral Filtering Approach to Regret Analysis of Distributed Online Control for Linear Dynamical Systems

author.name: Ting-Jui Chang

entry.summary: Extends online spectral control from centralized to distributed multi-agent linear systems with adversarial disturbances, giving regret bounds against the best centralized linear policy using only local observation and neighbor communication. Bridges online convex optimization and networked control.

entry.title: Network Information Enhances Unreliable News Domain Detection

author.name: Raphaela Ke{\ss}ler, Roman David Ventzke, Viola Priesemann, Giordano De Marzo

entry.summary: Builds a validated domain co-sharing network from Telegram URL sharing and shows that unreliable news domains cluster together, then uses graph neural networks over this structure to classify source reliability. Network signals help even without any text content features.

entry.title: Intention Inference Under Execution Noise: Separating Aleatoric and Epistemic Uncertainty in Social Dilemmas

author.name: Kival Mahadew, Jonathan Shock

entry.summary: Reformulates noisy repeated social dilemmas as a POMDP where opponent intentions are latent and executed actions are noisy observations, solved with active inference that separates epistemic from aleatoric uncertainty. Shows standard MDP formulations structurally cause over-retaliation in the noisy iterated prisoner's dilemma.

entry.title: A Heuristic Perspective on Debiasing Language Models

author.name: Tian Lan, Yemin Wang, Chuancheng Shi, Xiangyu Wu, Zesheng Shi, Yuan Wang, Jiang Li, Guanglai Gao, Xiangdong Su

entry.summary: Presents an automatic debiasing framework that uses simple heuristic templates to first elicit a model's biases and then fine-tunes on the elicited material, avoiding counterfactual data augmentation and manual annotation. Aims for lower cost and broader cultural coverage than projection-based methods.

entry.title: TreeProbe : A Tibetan Medicine Benchmark for Cultural Bias in LLMs

author.name: Jin Zhang, Linyu Li, Weili Jiang, Yuqing Cai, Yutong Liu, Guanquecairang, Yongbin Yu, Jingye Cai, Nyima Tashi, Gadeng Luosang

entry.summary: Introduces the first cultural-bias benchmark organized around the theoretical structure of Tibetan medicine, testing whether LLMs reason within that knowledge system or fall back on dominant biomedical framings. Provides quantitative tools where none previously existed.

entry.title: Select-And-Extract: A Lightweight Plugin for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Chenming Tang, Jiawei Han

entry.summary: Adds a lightweight plugin to retrieval-augmented generation that first retrieves a wide candidate set, then selects and extracts the relevant spans, targeting both retrieval failure and reading failure without heavy structured indexing or many LLM calls. Positions itself as simple and generalizable.

entry.title: Disentangled Contrastive Learning for Zero-Shot Multilingual Dense Retrieval

author.name: Chao Huang, Yufeng Chen, Changhao Guan, Guang Yang, Dongze Chen, Kaiyu Huang

entry.summary: Proposes disentangling semantic from language-specific features in contrastive training for multilingual dense retrieval, arguing that entangled shared representations interfere with optimizing relevance. The goal is better zero-shot transfer to low-resource languages lacking annotated retrieval data.

entry.title: Manifold-GS: Certified Hybrid Assets via Varifold-Conservative Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Boyang Li

entry.summary: Manifold-GS separates appearance opacity from geometric quadrature mass in Gaussian splatting and represents surface-like Gaussians as a discrete unoriented varifold, exporting only confidence-certified open surface patches. The aim is to make splatting outputs usable as structured assets without hallucinating collision surfaces in unobserved regions.

entry.title: Learning How Much, Not Just What: Cross-Patient Burden Order for CT Vision-Language Pretraining

author.name: Guoliang You, Haifan Gong, Xiaomeng Chu

entry.summary: Spectrum adds severity ordering to CT vision-language pretraining, arguing that existing objectives only establish what is present and collapse graded burden language into presence-absence signals. It uses cross-sectional cohorts to supply cross-patient burden ordering where longitudinal paired scans are scarce.

entry.title: GuideGround: VLM-guided Semantic Understanding and Viewpoint-aware Reasoning for 3D Visual Grounding

author.name: Yiwen Wang, Yuyang Deng, Yihao Long, Xi Zhao

entry.summary: GuideGround uses a general vision-language model to supply open-vocabulary semantics and global scene perception as guidance for a task-specific 3D grounding model, instead of treating semantic understanding as closed-set classification. The design also preserves viewpoint-specific evidence rather than averaging across views.

entry.title: InstancePin: Instance-Addressable Layout-to-Image Diffusion via Coordinate Pinning

author.name: Chaoyue Wu, Yunfei Zhang, Si Wu

entry.summary: InstancePin adds instance-level addressability to layout-conditioned diffusion by pinning each object to coordinates, so crowded same-category objects such as pedestrians and vehicles are not blended into one semantic blob. It targets urban scene synthesis where fine instance separation matters.

entry.title: Pixel Ignores, Superpixel Sees: Adverse Weather Image Restoration via Semantic-Center SSM

author.name: Dayu Li, Shihao Zhou, Leizhi Shu, Jin Wu, Chi Man Vong, Jufeng Yang

entry.summary: SSR restores images degraded by adverse weather using a state-space model that scans along superpixel-based semantic regions instead of pixel-serial order, arguing degradations are spatially non-uniform. Intended to avoid learning features from semantically conflicting regions.

entry.title: Global-Scale Self-Supervised Spatiotemporal Learning for NDVI Time-Series Reconstruction

author.name: Ang Li, Menghui Jiang, Xiaobin Guan, Dong Chu, Huanfeng Shen

entry.summary: GloSSR reconstructs cloud-corrupted vegetation index time series globally using self-supervision, creating training pairs by artificially degrading relatively clean observations with realistic cloud patterns. Sidesteps the impossibility of collecting paired clear and degraded data for the same place and time.

entry.title: VR3D: View-Robust 3D Representation Learning for Aerial-Ground Person Re-Identification

author.name: Chao Ji, Shiyu Xuan, Zechao Li

entry.summary: VR3D tackles aerial-to-ground person re-identification by lifting 2D image features into a canonical 3D coordinate space using single-view 3D priors, so that matching happens in a view-independent representation. This targets the severe geometric deformation and occlusion caused by drone versus ground camera viewpoints.

entry.title: FRA-NBV: A Fast and Reflectivity-Aware Next-Best-View Strategy

author.name: G. F. Preziosa, E. Setti, M. Faroni, A. M. Zanchettin, P. Rocco

entry.summary: FRA-NBV is a next-best-view planner that explicitly reasons about reflection-induced depth dropout when reconstructing shiny industrial parts with low-cost depth sensors. It infers reflective regions from spatial measurement patterns without prior object or material models.

entry.title: Residual-Based Adaptive Kalman Filtering for Legged Robot State Estimation

author.name: Mihaela Popescu, Dennis Mronga, Shivesh Kumar, Frank Kirchner

entry.summary: An online adaptation scheme for the process and measurement noise covariances in Kalman filtering for legged robot state estimation, driven by filter residuals and innovations. It removes the need for expert hand-tuning across gaits and terrains.

entry.title: Backward Bayesian Outcome Weighted Learning

author.name: Emmanuel M. Rockwell, Michael R. Kosorok, Nikki L. B. Freeman

entry.summary: BBOWL extends Bayesian outcome weighted learning to multi-stage dynamic treatment regimes via backward induction, propagating uncertainty backward through decision stages. This gives individual-level uncertainty quantification for precision-medicine treatment recommendations that classification-based methods lack.

entry.title: TrAC: Trace-Conditioned Answer Consistency for Efficient Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs

author.name: Dahai Yu, Lin Jiang, Rongchao Xu, Guang Wang

entry.summary: TrAC estimates answer reliability by re-eliciting an answer conditioned on the model's completed reasoning trace and measuring whether the trace actually supports the original answer. This fills a gap between single-trace confidence signals and expensive multi-sample consistency methods.

entry.title: QWRF-Net: A Quantum-Wavelet Framework with Rectified Flow for Short-Term Precipitation Nowcasting

author.name: Zhuo Wang, Chaorong Li, Wenjie Luo, Chuanhu Deng

entry.summary: QWRF-Net combines wavelet decomposition, quantum-inspired components and rectified flow generative modeling for short-term radar precipitation nowcasting, focusing on preserving intense convective cores across longer lead times. Motivated by flood and flash-flood early warning.

entry.title: FairForensics: Seeing Expressions and Parsing Demographics via Vision-Language Modeling for Generalizable Fair Deepfake Detection

author.name: Yaning Zhang, Jiao Wu, Zan Gao, Linlin Shen

entry.summary: Builds a demographically balanced benchmark for fair deepfake detection and proposes a vision-language detector that reasons over facial expressions and demographic attributes. Targets joint improvement of cross-manipulation generalization and demographic fairness.

entry.title: StyleForge: Indoor Furniture Styling by Counterfactual Reasoning in a Hypergraph Field

author.name: Lingwei Dang, Shishuo Shang, Pan Liu, Jiajia Cheng, Ziyan Qiu, Zhenhao Zhang, Yufei Zhu, Shenghui Huang, Qingxin Xiao, Yun Hao, Juntong Li, Qingyao Wu

entry.summary: StyleForge selects furniture assets for a fixed room layout so the whole scene is stylistically coherent, using a dynamic hypergraph style field and counterfactual reasoning over candidate distributions with priors from a frozen multimodal model. Targets shape, material, and color conflicts that arise from independent per-slot retrieval.

entry.title: Loop-Mamba: A Loop Mamba with Degradation-Aware and Shared Memory for Old Photo Restoration

author.name: Runci Bai, Yucheng Xin, Pu Wang, Yongcong Wang, Chen Wu, Dianjie Lu, Guijuan Zhang, Pengwen Dai, Guangwei Gao, Siyuan Yao, Zhuoran Zheng

entry.summary: Loop-Mamba restores old photographs suffering from coupled scratches, fading, blur, and missing regions by iteratively propagating a persistent restoration state through a lightweight state-space model. A degradation estimator predicts local maps and global scores to guide each refinement pass.

entry.title: ReMiX-MAE: Learning Missing-Channel Cross-Modal Representations from RGB-Only Clinical Facial Videos for Sympathetic-Mediated Pain Assessment

author.name: Nan Bi, Taoyue Wang, Lijun Yin, Vandana Sharma

entry.summary: ReMiX-MAE pretrains a masked autoencoder on synchronized RGB, thermal, and depth clinical facial video, explicitly training robustness to missing modalities so that only RGB is needed at deployment for pain assessment. It also contributes clinically grounded video data with sequence-level self-report labels.

entry.title: Protocol generalisation for brain tissue microstructure estimation via hypernetwork-controlled geometric deep learning

author.name: Andrea Brigliadori, Leevi Kerkela, Hui Zhang

entry.summary: This paper uses a hypernetwork to condition a rotationally equivariant spherical convolutional network on the diffusion MRI acquisition protocol, so brain microstructure estimation generalizes across b-vectors and b-values without retraining. It combines protocol generalization with the rotational equivariance that prior generalizing methods lacked.

entry.title: FreqNav: Stage-Wise Frequency Routing for Object-Oriented Aerial Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Yin Tang, Jiawei Ma, Jiahao Li, Hao Zhang, Zhemin Sun, Jianqiao Sun, Deyu Zhang

entry.summary: FreqNav routes visual features by spatial frequency depending on the navigation stage, giving low-frequency layout information priority during early exploration and high-frequency target detail during final approach and landing for aerial vision-language navigation. It argues that using identical visual tokens throughout causes interference from clutter.

entry.title: Complete Motion Planning using Workspace-Fibered Decomposition for nR-Planar Manipulator

author.name: Aayush Rath, Antony Thomas

entry.summary: This paper decomposes motion planning for redundant planar manipulators by first constructing obstacle-constrained reachable workspaces for lower-dimensional non-redundant sub-chains and then recursively lifting them through redundant orientation fibers. This yields reduced planning manifolds with completeness properties while avoiding explicit construction of full configuration-space obstacles.

entry.title: Deep Learning CNN and Recurrence Analysis for Alpha Gamma EEG Biomarkers in Fragile X Syndrome

author.name: Zag ElSayed, Payton Siekierski, Jack Yanchen Liu, Ernest Pedapati

entry.summary: Builds a multi-representation deep learning pipeline (CNN plus LSTM plus recurrence-plot analysis) to classify EEG alpha and gamma oscillation phenotypes in Fragile X Syndrome. Aimed at automated biomarker characterization of a neurodevelopmental disorder.

entry.title: Asking Questions the Right Way: A Multi-Agent Conversational System for Prompt Formulation in Complex Task Resolution

author.name: B. Sankar, Pawni Yadav, Srinidhi Ranjini Girish, Amogh A. S

entry.summary: PAWNI is an eight-agent conversational front-end that turns vague user queries into structured prompts through guided clarification dialogue backed by a self-evolving knowledge base, plus a taxonomy of 18 prompt elements in three tiers. It optimizes the question rather than the model response.

entry.title: Retrieval Augmented Biomedical Question Answering with Weak Question Recovery and Neural Reranking for BioASQ Task 14b

author.name: Xueying Zhao, Lee Mai, Balaji Anandganesh

entry.summary: A shared-task system description for biomedical question answering combining PubMed retrieval, multi-source query expansion, fine-tuned MiniLM reranking, reciprocal rank fusion, conditional recovery for weakly retrieved queries and biomedical LLM answer generation. Includes post-retrieval pruning to remove low-relevance snippets.

entry.title: EntailLLM: Verifying LLM-Generated Vulnerability Discovery Paths with Domain Knowledge via Logic Programming

author.name: Kaustuv Mukherji, Jaikrishna Manojkumar Patil, Colton Payne, Paulo Shakarian, Dana Warmsley, Nigel Stepp, Evelyn Kim

entry.summary: EntailLLM checks whether LLM-proposed vulnerability discovery paths through a binary's call graph are logically consistent with an independent domain-knowledge graph, using temporal annotated logic for entailment verification. It targets silent domain-knowledge violations in safety-critical software analysis such as medical devices.

entry.title: TextNCA: Neural Cellular Automata for Language Modeling via Hierarchical Local Attention

author.name: Avni Mittal, Avinash Anand, Ashutosh Kumar, Dikshant Kukreja, Kritarth Prasad, Sushane Dulloo, Erik Cambria, Timothy Liu, Zhengkui Wang, Rajiv Ratn Shah

entry.summary: TextNCA implements a neural cellular automaton as a hierarchical, weight-shared, strictly local causal windowed attention model for language, cascading stages with windows of 8, 32, and 128 tokens. At roughly 30M parameters it underperforms parameter-matched Transformers, and the authors present it as an analytical probe of which properties, locality, iteration, or weight sharing, drive behavior.

entry.title: DeGS: A Scalable 3DGS Architecture via Decoupled Workload Parsing and Reorganization

author.name: Minnan Pei, Gang Li, Zeyu Zhu, Siting Wang, Junwen Si, Zhuoran Song, Yu Feng, Fangxin Liu, Xiaoyao Liang, Jian Cheng

entry.summary: DeGS is a hardware architecture for 3D Gaussian splatting inference that decouples the tightly coupled checking-while-blending dataflow, reorganizing workloads to eliminate spatial redundancy from irregular Gaussian coverage and temporal redundancy from asynchronous pixel termination. The goal is accelerator scalability as processing elements increase.

entry.title: HarMoE: Multi-Source Chest Radiograph Pretraining with Dataset-Disentangled Experts

author.name: Haozhe Luo, Ziyu Zhou, Shelley Zixin Shu, Mauricio Reyes

entry.summary: HarMoE pretrains chest radiograph models on multiple heterogeneous multi-label classification datasets rather than relying on report-image alignment with a single dominant corpus, using dataset-disentangled mixture-of-experts to prevent entangling clinical semantics with dataset identity. This aims for broader pathology coverage and better transfer.

entry.title: Can Foundation Models Hear What Made That Sound? A Tiered Benchmark of Audio-Language Models and Traditional Classifiers for Closed-Set Sound Source Identification

author.name: Sajjad Abdoli, Ghassan Al-Sumaidaee, Ahmad ElShiekh, Ahmed Rashad

entry.summary: This benchmark compares eleven approaches to closed-set sound-source identification across 2,242 clips and 23 fine-grained classes, spanning task-aware LLMs including several Gemini variants and Kimi-Audio, fixed-vocabulary taggers, a zero-shot audio-text model, and an audio-grounded LLM. Because the methods receive tasks and are scored differently, results are reported in four tiers rather than a single leaderboard, with the strongest model reaching roughly 86 percent category-level F1 but far lower fine-grained accuracy.

entry.title: GeoArbiter: Verifiability-Guided Grounding for Remote-Sensing Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Xuechen Li

entry.summary: Shows that coordinate-keyed geographic retrieval substantially boosts remote-sensing multimodal LLM land-use accuracy, but that models often follow retrieved records even when imagery contradicts them. GeoArbiter is a training-free pipeline that gates trust in external records by whether the attribute in question is visually verifiable.

entry.title: Logit-Origin Centering for Singleton Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Mayank Sharma, Rohit Kumar Mourya, Pratik Mazumder

entry.summary: Shows that leading fully test-time adaptation methods for tabular models, which inherit batch-dependent designs from vision, degrade sharply when examples must be classified one at a time in strict streaming. Proposes a logit-origin centering fix for the singleton regime.

entry.title: EulerLoRA: Rank-Driven Jump Dynamics for Calibrated Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning

author.name: Srinivas Anumasa, Dianbo Liu

entry.summary: EulerLoRA makes low-rank adaptation stochastic by sampling structured variations along rank-one adapter components, yielding multiple predictive trajectories while matching deterministic LoRA in expectation. Reported to match or beat LoRA ensembles on image classification and OOD detection with far fewer parameters.

entry.title: Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Radio Resource Management under Coupled Finite-Horizon Constraints

author.name: Yeonseo Jeong, Wonhyeok Ko, Sungweon Hong, Songnam Hong

entry.summary: HeLyMARL is a Lyapunov-embedded heterogeneous multi-agent RL framework for dense wireless networks that jointly handles user association, scheduling, base-station activation and handover under hard finite-horizon energy and handover budgets. Lyapunov drift terms convert horizon-level budgets and the non-decomposable proportional-fairness objective into per-slot signals.

entry.title: A Spatial Persistence Gradient in European Warming Consistent with North Atlantic Cold-Blob Influence

author.name: Mauricio Herrera-Mar\'in, Alex Godoy-Fa\'undez, Diego Rivera

entry.summary: Uses long-memory (DFA Hurst) analysis of ERA5 temperature residuals across European sub-regions to show a strong negative association between interannual persistence and recent warming rate, with Atlantic-proximal high-persistence regions warming more slowly. The relationship survives multiple residualization schemes, memory estimators, leave-one-region-out checks and several null models.

entry.title: Beyond Random Partitioning: Unsupervised Spatio-Temporal Stratification for Cohort Balancing in Longitudinal Medical Imaging

author.name: Qinghui Liu, Jon Andr\'e Ottesen, Atle Bj{\o}rnerud, Kyrre Eeg Emblem

entry.summary: Argues that naive random splitting of small longitudinal clinical imaging cohorts silently creates covariate shift and temporal imbalance, turning validation and test evaluation into out-of-distribution testing. Presents an auditable framework characterizing grid integrity, intensity fingerprints and temporal trajectories, then uses unsupervised spatio-temporal stratification to balance splits.

entry.title: PhenoStitch: Training-Free Panoptic Crop Mapping from Satellite Image Time Series

author.name: Xuechen Li

entry.summary: Proposes a panoptic crop mapping pipeline that needs no task-specific gradient training: a frozen segmentation foundation model oversegments satellite patches, analytic harmonic phenological signatures summarize the time series, and a graph energy minimization merges regions into parcels. This targets transfer to new regions and seasons where parcel-level labels are unavailable.

entry.title: Model-Agnostic FDR Control via Group Gaussian Mirror and Permutation SHAP

author.name: Jiaan Han, Junxiao Chen, Yanzhe Fu

entry.summary: Extends false discovery rate controlled feature selection from single-coordinate hypotheses to grouped features such as lags, recurrent states, or attention blocks. It uses matrix-valued mirror statistics for grouped linear models and permutation SHAP derivatives with kernel dependence measures for neural sequence models.

entry.title: 3DZip: Spatial-Aware Feature Diversity-Guided Token Compression for 3D Question Answering

author.name: Changwoo Baek, Kyeongbo Kong

entry.summary: Reduces the thousands of geometry-aware tokens produced by 3D vision-language models using a three-stage compression that accounts for spatial structure and object-level token imbalance, rather than relying on attention or semantic relevance alone. The aim is cheaper 3D question answering with preserved spatial reasoning.

entry.title: Dominant Arm Identification with Mixing and Recycling Observed Samples

author.name: Jonghyun Sim, Wonyoung Kim

entry.summary: Studies bandit identification of the arm most likely to produce the highest realized reward rather than the highest mean, arguing that mean-based and pairwise-comparison methods can select the wrong arm under this criterion. It introduces a dominance score with a doubly robust estimator plus a sample mixing and recycling scheme with convergence guarantees.

entry.title: Generative Brownian Bridge Diffusion In Motion Space For Enhanced Myocardial Strain Analysis

author.name: Rishov Paul, Frederick H. Epstein, Miaomiao Zhang

entry.summary: Learns a Brownian bridge diffusion model in motion space that maps standard registration-derived cardiac motion from routine MR sequences to the high-accuracy motion obtained from specialized strain imaging. The intent is accurate regional myocardial strain without costly acquisitions or manual post-processing.

entry.title: Probabilistic Deep Learning for Drought Forecasting: Role of Internal Climate Variability

author.name: Henri Funk, Cornelia Gruber, G\"oran Kauermann, Helmut K\"uchenhoff, Magdalena Mittermeier

entry.summary: Presents a probabilistic deep learning framework for European drought forecasting that treats internal climate variability as structured signal rather than noise, deriving an uncertainty-aware drought bound from a large climate model ensemble. The bound is intended to represent a physically grounded range of plausible outcomes for adaptation planning.

entry.title: TELLER: Non-intrusive Cross-Layer Root-Cause Analysis for LLM Inference

author.name: Ruilin Xu, Junyi Li, Pengfei Chen, Zongxuan Xie

entry.summary: Provides a non-intrusive root-cause analysis framework for production LLM inference that stitches together GPU tracing, CUDA API events, and service logs into per-request call-chain trees without modifying model binaries. The goal is diagnosing failures that span the serving engine, backend, kernels, and distributed communication.

entry.title: D\'ej\`a Cue: Localizing States in Object Histories via Vocabulary-Relative Coordinates

author.name: Haofan Cao, Zhichao You, Yunkai Yang, Liang Guo, Jie Wang, Chongshou Li

entry.summary: Defines identity-conditioned state-moment retrieval, where the task is to localize the interval in a tracked object history during which a described state such as empty or cut holds. Because absolute image-text similarity is dominated by shared object identity, the method scores each candidate state relative to the alternatives, in a training-free framework.

entry.title: Can Language Models Identify Shadow Trading Targets? An NLP Evaluation of SEC Enforcement Theory

author.name: Sarah Wilson, Michael MacKay, Anthony Marello, Trinav Bhattacharyya

entry.summary: Tests whether an LLM pipeline over the management discussion sections of annual filings can identify economically linked peer firms in advance, the premise underlying the SEC's contested shadow trading enforcement theory. Scores semantic similarity across 30 merger events to assess ex ante identifiability.

entry.title: UniHEAR: Unified Heterogeneous-Source Attentive Retrieval for Knowledge-Based Visual Question Answering

author.name: Ganzhong Luo, Yang Ren, Hanyong Wang, Shuyu Zheng, Menglong Yang

entry.summary: UniHEAR unifies retrieval across heterogeneous knowledge sources for knowledge-based visual question answering and makes the reranker aware of which source each candidate came from. It targets two named failure modes: single-source retrieval bottlenecks and source-blind pointwise reranking.

entry.title: Semantically Calibrated Evidence Composition for CT Vision-Language Learning

author.name: Guoliang You, Haifan Gong, Xiaomeng Chu

entry.summary: SCOPE addresses how independently grounded anatomy-level findings should be composed into a study-level CT representation, rather than choosing between global report alignment and fine-grained anatomical correspondence. It calibrates the semantic contribution of each piece of local evidence during composition.

entry.title: Reconstruction-Shift Discrimination via Mask-Guided Latent Diffusion for Medical Anomaly Detection

author.name: Yibo Wan, Jinyu Cai, Yunhe Zhang, Yi Bin, See-kiong Ng

entry.summary: DMD supplements ambiguous reconstruction residuals in unsupervised medical anomaly detection with a discriminative signal based on how latent representations shift under mask-guided diffusion reconstruction. This targets cases where expressive models faithfully reproduce pathology or where benign variation produces large residuals.

entry.title: Practical Noise Modeling for SPAD Intensity Imaging

author.name: Wendi Liu, Yujie Lu, Zengxi Zhang, Haiyang Jiang, Weihang Ran, Yinqiang Zheng

entry.summary: Develops a calibrated forward noise model for single-photon avalanche diode intensity imaging, modelling binary-frame accumulation as a binomial process with separate exposure-dependent dark count and exposure-independent bias terms. This enables realistic training data for denoising sensors that record only detection occurrence without photon timestamps.

entry.title: IDraw: Artist Verification from Digital Drawing Images

author.name: Nayoung Kim, Nan Jiang, Bangjie Sun, Jaewon Shin, Sojeong Kim, Jun Han

entry.summary: IDraw verifies whether a disputed digital drawing was made by a claimed artist, using tablet-pen sensor signals available only during training to learn behavior-related cues, then applying the model to images alone. Also tries to separate artist style from depicted content similarity.

entry.title: UniMoCa: Unifying Motion and Camera Controls as Visual Proxies for Faithful Human Video Generation

author.name: Liming Tan, Ye Chen, Hao Zhang, Lirong Qian, Feifei Li, Bingbing Ni

entry.summary: CHOW-SLAM is a dense RGB-D SLAM system that pairs a compact parametric-hash hybrid scene representation for spatial constraints with overlapping-window optimization for temporal constraints from past observations. Designed for online operation under limited compute.

entry.title: T$^2$exture: Sparsely Perturbed Thermal-to-Texture Imaging

author.name: Jiashuo Chen, Cheng Dai, Yanan Hu, Fanglin Bao

entry.summary: Reconstructs temporally dense thermal texture sequences from mostly passive infrared frames plus a few actively illuminated keyframes, defining thermal texture as the residual between illuminated and passive states. Avoids the data cost of spectral sensing or reliance on registered auxiliary modalities.

entry.title: Belief-Space Perception Routing under Coupled Sensor Faults and Compute Contention

author.name: Sparsh Roy, Vihan Aggarwal, Davin Yin

entry.summary: This paper builds a perception router that jointly tracks probabilistic beliefs about sensor degradation and onboard compute contention, couples them with a noisy-OR model, and uses the joint belief to pick among four detector configurations so each frame meets its deadline. Reported deadline-miss reductions are largest exactly when both stressors co-occur.

entry.title: ORCESTRA: VLM-driven Visual Robot programming in Mixed Reality

author.name: Ivan Snegirev, Elizaveta Semenyakina, Mikhail Konenkov, Artem Lykov, Miguel Altamirano Cabrera, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: ORCESTRA is a mixed-reality system for programming robot digital twins either by no-code waypoint teaching on real surfaces or by spoken commands that a vision-language model converts into structured plans, with a shared backend for metric grounding and embodiment-aware validation. It supports manipulators, a mobile base, and a humanoid, positioning MR preview as a safety layer before physical execution.

entry.title: Towards Autonomous Formulaic Alpha Discovery: An Evolutionary Computation Perspective

author.name: Xinwei Yu, Yiyang Fu, Mingcheng Fan, Enqi Li, Yilin Gao, Shugong Xu

entry.summary: This article surveys automated formulaic alpha discovery in quantitative finance under a single evolutionary computation framing, unifying genetic programming, reinforcement learning, GFlowNets, Monte Carlo tree search, LLM-based, and agentic approaches that are normally treated as separate families. It highlights shared obstacles such as noisy fitness estimates, nonstationarity, and semantic redundancy.

entry.title: Motion Planning for Mobile Manipulators Navigating Doorways via Model Predictive Control

author.name: Kasra Sinaei, Kasun Weerakoon, Christopher Bradley, Seyed Abolfazl Fakoorian, Donald Ebeigbe

entry.summary: This work formulates a mobile manipulator and a door as one coupled dynamical system inside a nonlinear model predictive control problem, generating collision-free base and arm trajectories for opening and traversing push and pull doors. Manipulation feasibility is enforced through a penalty instead of explicit arm kinematics in the planner.

entry.title: AutoFOAM: The Self-Refining Autonomous OpenFOAM Agent

author.name: Arun Govind Neelan, A Seshaditya

entry.summary: AutoFOAM is a self-evolving agent built on a 14B Qwen coder model that writes, runs, evaluates, and iteratively improves OpenFOAM computational fluid dynamics simulations from natural-language prompts. It fine-tunes on a small curated prompt set and uses a seven-stage evolution loop with degeneration safeguards.

entry.title: Nova: An End-to-End MLIR Compiler for Deep Learning

author.name: Adwaid Suresh, Aparna A, Harshini V M, Jona Delcy C A, Killi Uma Maheswara Rao, Ram Charan Golla, Surendra Vendra

entry.summary: Nova is an end-to-end just-in-time MLIR-based compiler that captures eager tensor execution and lowers it with cross-operation fusion, memory hierarchy optimization, and register-level tuning. It targets the gap between flexible eager frameworks and hardware-efficient execution.

entry.title: Shared Organizational Memory for Enterprise Coding Agents: System Design and Deployment Snapshot

author.name: Harsh Rao Dhanyamraju, Leonidas Raghav

entry.summary: Describes a deployed enterprise system that automatically captures task-adjacent developer experience during coding work, curates it into approved question-answer memories, and serves it back to coding agents. It targets internal knowledge such as proprietary DSLs and local conventions absent from public training data.

entry.title: TRACE-TS: Attribution-Grounded and Traceable Sensor-Language Reasoning for Human Activity Understanding

author.name: Sparsh Rastogi, Tanmay Kumar, Baiyu Chen, Jatin Bedi, Zechen Li, Flora D. Salim

entry.summary: TRACE-TS grounds language-model explanations of wearable sensor data in attributions from an expert classifier, building directed-acyclic-graph reasoning traces with explicit evidence provenance and distilling them into a compact model. The goal is verifiable rather than merely fluent activity explanations.

entry.title: Geometric Self-Supervised Pre-training for Neural Combinatorial Optimization

author.name: David Aguado, Daniel Fuertes, Carlos R. del-Blanco, Fernando Jaureguizar

entry.summary: Proposes a geometric self-supervised pre-training scheme for neural combinatorial optimization on routing problems, addressing the poor scaling of reinforcement-learning solvers to large instances. It adapts the pretraining paradigm to graphs whose only features are 2D coordinates.

entry.title: Behavioral Grammar: Detecting Adaptive Malware via Tiny Language Model Priors and Second-Order Temporal Analysis

author.name: Zihan Luo

entry.summary: Treats host runtime behavior as a language and trains a 0.88M-parameter causal Transformer on eight-token discretized system events to learn normal behavior self-supervised, deriving anomaly scores for malware detection. It targets the tradeoff between evadable signatures and unauditable heavy deep models.

entry.title: Trustworthy AI in Digital Health: A Comprehensive Review of Robustness and Explainability

author.name: Abdullah Mamun, Shovito Barua Soumma, Hassan Ghasemzadeh

entry.summary: A review organizing recent work on robustness and explainability for AI in digital health across the model lifecycle, from data collection through deployment and human interaction. Intended as a practical synthesis for healthcare practitioners.

entry.title: ELECTRIC: Evidential Learning-Enhanced CT Reconstruction via Iterative Correction

author.name: Ge Wang

entry.summary: ELECTRIC is a physics-guided Bayesian CT reconstruction loop in which an evidential network proposes an image plus an epistemic uncertainty estimate that is converted into an adaptive precision field for a Poisson-weighted maximum a posteriori update. Treats learned prior confidence as an explicit state variable of iterative reconstruction, with two simulation studies on low-dose CT data.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence and Modeling & Simulation: An Overview

author.name: Niclas Feldkamp, Philippe J. Giabbanelli, Istvan David

entry.summary: A structured overview report maps the bidirectional intersections of AI and modeling and simulation, organized along the stages of simulation studies from specification and input modeling through execution, verification and output analysis, and noting that simulations serve as data generators, training environments and evaluation platforms for AI. It functions as a community roadmap rather than new research.

entry.title: An Information Theoretic Treatment of Yager's Probability Distribution Negation

author.name: Roberto Bruno, Ugo Vaccaro

entry.summary: The authors give a comprehensive information-theoretic analysis of Yager's negation of a probability distribution using entropy and majorization theory, unifying and strengthening previously scattered properties and generalizations. They argue these results justify Yager's definition as the most principled notion of distribution negation.

entry.title: SPECTRA: Band-Routed Embedding and Stage-Wise LoRA for Cross-Sensor Fine-Tuning of Geospatial Foundation Models

author.name: Xingyan Li, Jordan A. Caraballo-Vega, Jie Gong, Mark L. Carroll, Jianwu Wang

entry.summary: SPECTRA adapts Earth-observation foundation models to downstream sensors with mismatched spectral bands using band-routed patch embeddings plus stage-wise LoRA to keep fine-tuning cheap. It jointly targets spectral mismatch and adaptation cost, which prior work handled separately.

entry.title: Human-Centered Reflections on Care Robots: A Comparative Study of Caregiver Perspectives

author.name: Laura Londo\~no, Klaus Baumann, Abhinav Valada, Markus Langer

entry.summary: A mixed-methods acceptance study of four care-robot categories with 298 caregivers across the US, Mexico, and Chile, combining established technology-acceptance constructs with qualitative reflections. It maps how task type and cultural context shape willingness to adopt robots in healthcare settings.

entry.title: Learning Compositional Meta-Routing for Agentic Workflows: An Executable Benchmark

author.name: Natan Vidra, Alina Kapanova, Arun Kanhai, Spurthi Setty

entry.summary: Introduces an executable benchmark plus a budget-aware meta-router that chooses compositions of agentic operations (answer directly, decompose, retrieve, run code, delegate, verify) from raw task text. Outcomes are machine-checked after execution across data analysis, research, and document tasks, including a lexical-shift generalization split.

entry.title: AutoCause: A Python framework that automates expert decisions in environmental time-series causal discovery

author.name: Marco Ruiz, Miguel Arana-Catania, David R. Ardila, Rodrigo Ventura

entry.summary: AutoCause is an open-source workflow that records and defaults the many expert choices in environmental time-series causal discovery (test choice, lags, sample adequacy, multiple-testing control) so that resulting graphs are comparable and auditable. It wraps four established methods plus non-causal references and grades links by cross-method support across 145 datasets.

entry.title: CoSynFlow: Conformal Symplectic Neural Flows for Cross-System Prediction of Dissipative Hamiltonian Dynamics

author.name: Baige Xu, Takaharu Yaguchi

entry.summary: CoSynFlow learns continuous-time solution maps for dissipative Hamiltonian systems by composing symplectic shear layers with a conformal factor that tracks dissipation, preserving conformal symplectic geometry. Aims at cross-system generalization for structure-preserving dynamics prediction.

entry.title: Relative Parameter Importance in Task-Agnostic Replay-Free Continual Learning

author.name: Malavika Suresh, Ikechukwu Nkisi-Orji, Nirmalie Wiratunga

entry.summary: Introduces relative parameter importance, which weighs each parameter's importance for the current task against past tasks, to regularize continual learning without stored data or task identity at inference. Parameters important mainly for past tasks are frozen while others remain plastic, allowing forward transfer.

entry.title: Nonlinear Laplacians Improve Signed-Directed Graph Learning

author.name: Ali Parviz, Yuichi Yoshida

entry.summary: Introduces a nonlinear Laplacian operator for signed and directed graphs that only propagates messages along edges where node potential differences agree with edge direction. Extends signed and directed Laplacian theory into a nonlinear message-passing operator for GNNs.

entry.title: FedChronos: Federated Fine-Tuning of Time-Series Foundation Models for Privacy-Preserving Commodity Price Forecasting

author.name: Amit Sharma, Nitin Auluck, Akramul Azim

entry.summary: FedChronos federates parameter-efficient fine-tuning of a pretrained time-series foundation model across institutions that cannot pool data, using low-rank adapters transmitted with standard federated averaging algorithms. Applied to commodity price forecasting under regulatory and competitive data constraints.

entry.title: Gram-Space: Structure-Preserving Codebook Compression for Memory-Efficient Neuro-Symbolic AI

author.name: Weilun Wang, Wantong Li

entry.summary: Proposes Gram-Space, a compression scheme for vector symbolic architecture codebooks that uses Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization to store high-dimensional hypervectors in a compact orthonormal coordinate system while exactly preserving inner products. This reduces the memory bottleneck of neuro-symbolic reasoning systems without changing their numerical behavior.

entry.title: Do Static Embeddings Add Value to Hybrid Dutch Retrieval?

author.name: Ant\'onio Pereira Barata

entry.summary: A controlled study of whether cheap static embedding models add complementary signal to Dutch hybrid retrieval once BM25 and a transformer embedder are already fused via weighted reciprocal rank fusion, using five MTEB-NL datasets with exhaustive scoring and cross-validated weights. It tests marginal value rather than standalone benchmark quality.

entry.title: Fruit-HSNet: A Machine Learning Approach for Hyperspectral Image-Based Fruit Ripeness Prediction

author.name: Ahmed Baha Ben Jmaa, Faten Chaieb, Anna Fabija\'nska

entry.summary: Surveys hybrid quantum neural networks that couple classical layers with quantum processing units, organizing theory, implementations, and applications across heterogeneous architectures and hardware assumptions. It acknowledges recent benchmark evidence that practical quantum advantage has not yet been demonstrated at scale.

entry.title: Pretraining on Call Graphs: When Binary Analysis Tasks Profit From Context

author.name: Samuel Valenzuela, Johannes Kinder

entry.summary: Dissects whether adding call-graph (inter-procedural) context helps binary function embedding models across reverse-engineering tasks. Finds gains on code similarity do not transfer uniformly to other downstream tasks, questioning how context refinements are evaluated.

entry.title: The Push-Forward Transform for Continuous and Robust Comparison of Dynamic Shapes

author.name: Roua Rouatbi, Juan-Esteban Suarez Cardona, Ivo F. Sbalzarini

entry.summary: Introduces a push-forward transform that maps shapes into a shared reference domain so that shapes and their temporal evolution can be compared invariantly to translation, rotation, scaling, and reparametrization. Avoids reliance on landmarks or learned embeddings.

entry.title: A Simple Approximation to the Distribution of the Ridge Regression Estimator

author.name: Jos\'e Luis Montiel Olea, Ryan Strong, Amilcar Velez, Zhuoheng Xu, Haomin Yu

entry.summary: Derives a simple Gaussian approximation to the finite-sample distribution of ridge regression under nonstandard asymptotics where regularization grows with sample size and coefficients are local to the shrinkage target. Allows heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation, capturing the bias-variance tradeoff explicitly.

entry.title: The methodology of Constructing the Large-Scale Dataset for Detecting Presuicidal and Anti-Suicidal Signals in Social Media Texts in Russian

author.name: Igor Buyanov, Darya Yaskova, Danil Serenko, Danil Shkereda, Andrey Yaskov, Ilya Sochenkov

entry.summary: Documents a methodology for building a large Russian-language dataset annotating presuicidal and anti-suicidal signals in social media text, including annotation instructions, class taxonomy, and verification procedures. Intended to support risk triage tools in a high-prevalence setting.

entry.title: Gaokerena: A Small Persian Medical Language Model Family

author.name: Mehrdad Ghassabi, Hamidreza Baradaran Kashani, Pedram Rostami, Sadra Hakim, Zahra Kazemi, Audrina Ebrahimi

entry.summary: Releases a family of compact Persian medical language models trained on a newly curated 90-million-token medical corpus plus expert-vetted physician question-answer pairs, aimed at consumer hardware deployment. Reports moderate gains on a translated medical MMLU benchmark.

entry.title: Morphology Aware Reversible Semantic Tokenization and Hierarchical Word Composition for Tamil Language Models

author.name: Anand Murugan

entry.summary: Builds a morphology-aware, byte-exact reversible tokenizer for Tamil using finite-state transducers plus a learned hierarchical word composer, and compares it against existing Indic subword tokenizers. Targets the mismatch between statistical subwords and Tamil's rich agglutinative morphology.

entry.title: PlainMedScale: A Corpus of Multi-Level Simplified Medical Texts in German and English

author.name: Bruno Brocai, Ilaria Papagno, Mayumi Ohta

entry.summary: Introduces a topic-aligned German and English medical corpus with four graded levels of comprehensibility, moving beyond binary expert-versus-lay contrasts. Pilot studies show common readability metrics fail to generalize across the full gradient and that a leading open-weight LLM prompted for plain language still retains input difficulty.

entry.title: When Words Divide: Diachronic Ideological Polarization in Political Discourse on Social Media

author.name: Roy Yitzchak, Noa Lavie, Ella Rabinovich

entry.summary: Measures ideological polarization longitudinally by training temporally aligned community-specific word embeddings for opposing political subreddits and tracking semantic divergence of political concepts. Finds substantial increases in polarization at both concept and topic level over time.

entry.title: Entity-Faithful Repair of Synthetic Supervision for Zero-Shot Image Captioning

author.name: Zhiyue Liu, Wenkai Zhou, Jian Qin, Qipeng Jiang

entry.summary: ReCap repairs fine-grained entity-level misalignment in synthetic image-text pairs used for zero-shot captioning, rather than filtering or regenerating pairs by global similarity. The premise is that synthetic pairs often look globally plausible while missing entities or misgrounding attributes.

entry.title: SafeBuild-Bench: A Temporal-Robust Construction Safety Benchmark with Graph-Enhanced Data Mining

author.name: Yi Cui, Zilin Wang, Yijie Xu, Qianyi Cai, Huizai Yao, Shuai Jiang, Bingzhuo Zhong, Hui Xiong

entry.summary: SafeBuild-Bench mines over 100,000 industrial image-text inspection records into around 3,300 expert-verified tasks testing whether multimodal models identify concrete construction hazards under realistic site and temporal variation. A graph-enhanced mining pipeline makes expert verification scalable against redundant, long-tailed archives.

entry.title: Representation Transfer of Foundation Models for Ultra-Widefield Retinal Imaging

author.name: Mingya Alexa Gong, Da Ma, Lovre Antonio Budimir, Ivana Matovinovic, Sven Loncaric, Myeong Jin Ju, Yukun Zhou, Siegfried K. Wagner, Pearse A. Keane, Marinko V. Sarunic

entry.summary: A controlled study of how pretraining objective choice (supervised, masked autoencoding, self-distillation) affects transferability of vision transformer features to weakly supervised ultra-widefield retinal disease classification within a fixed multiple-instance-learning pipeline. It isolates encoder pretraining as the variable while holding aggregation constant.

entry.title: SecondOpinion: Anatomy-Aware Gated Reasoning for Efficient Medical Image Analysis

author.name: Siam Tahsin Bhuiyan, Rashedur Rahman, Sefatul Wasi, Riyadul Islam, Syoji Kobashi, Ashraful Islam, Saadia Binte Alam

entry.summary: SecondOpinion spends extra compute only on hard medical imaging cases by gating an anatomy-guided second stream behind a learned correctness classifier. It mimics a clinician seeking a second opinion, aiming for accuracy at lower average cost.

entry.title: AdaForensics: Learning A Characteristic-aware Adaptive Deepfake Detector

author.name: Xiaoke Yang, Haixu Song, Xiangyu Lu, Shao-Lun Huang, Yueqi Duan

entry.summary: AdaForensics uses a hypernetwork to adapt a deepfake detector on the fly to each face's characteristics, learning both shared and characteristic-specific embeddings. Argues that one fixed detector for all identities misses person-specific forgery cues.

entry.title: ISRS-DETR: Detection-Guided Click Propagation for Remote Sensing Interactive Segmentation

author.name: Thanh Duc Pham, Anh Nguyen, Duong Duc Hieu, Minh-Tan Pham

entry.summary: ISRS-DETR improves interactive segmentation of remote sensing imagery by propagating a user click across same-class objects using detection guidance, rather than treating every instance as an isolated target. This cuts the very high per-image click budgets that make interactive annotation of satellite imagery impractical.

entry.title: TravKAN: Fast and Interpretable Nonlinear Traversability Analysis with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks

author.name: Daniel Fusaro, Simone Mosco, Wanmeng Li, Alberto Pretto

entry.summary: TravKAN applies Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks to terrain traversability estimation for mobile robots, representing decisions as compositions of learnable univariate functions so that compact analytic expressions can be extracted after training. The motivation is interpretability of terrain-robot interaction alongside speed.

entry.title: Spike-HTR: Spiking Neural Transformer for Handwritten Text Recognition

author.name: Xiubo Liang, Jinxing Han, Yuke Li, Haoqi Zhu, Yu Zhao, Hongzhi Wang

entry.summary: Spike-HTR is a hybrid spiking recognizer for handwritten text that converts a static image into a coarse-to-fine input stream so short spiking horizons suffice, and reduces the number of width positions processed by the sequence mixer. It exploits the fact that most pixels are background and most sequence positions are blank.

entry.title: Localization in Spatiotemporal Fields via Environmental PDEs

author.name: Jose Fuentes, Abdullah Al Redwan Newaz, Ana Cavalcanti, Leonardo Bobadilla

entry.summary: This paper localizes vehicles by using spatiotemporal physical fields governed by PDEs such as shallow water equations and advection-diffusion as location signatures, fusing multiple predicted field channels as multimodal measurements. A Rao-Blackwellized particle filter splits the state into sampled nonlinear and analytically tracked components.

entry.title: Push-Wiper: Toward General-Purpose Robotic Cleaning across Varied Stains and Surfaces with Segmented Pushing Trajectories

author.name: Renhao Lu, Mingxin Wang, Chenyang Cao, Yang Yang, Guoping Pan, Kangkang Dong, Yi Cheng, Houde Liu

entry.summary: Push-Wiper reframes cleaning viscous stains as an aggregation problem, using a sponge to progressively gather material with segmented pushing trajectories generated by a diffusion policy, then detaching the collected residue and self-cleaning the sponge. This avoids the smearing of conventional wiping and the surface damage risk of scrubbing.

entry.title: Sampling-Based Visibility Task Planning

author.name: Stav Ashur, Avishai Sintov

entry.summary: This paper develops sampling-based task and motion planning algorithms specialized for visibility-based instruments such as cameras, flashlights, and directional antennas, whose field-of-view constraints break common heuristics and distance metrics. Two new samplers are introduced for this class of tools.

entry.title: Dynamic UAV-based search operations using probabilistic diffusion modeling of Man Overboard incident victims

author.name: Dimosthenis Angelis, Evangelos Boukas

entry.summary: A UAV search strategy for man-overboard incidents predicts the drifting search area with an extended Kalman filter driven by an oceanographic leeway drift model, then compares five coverage patterns. The work is motivated by very high fatality rates in such incidents.

entry.title: Emergence Invariance: From Symbolized Thought to Interface Refinement

author.name: Yi Liu

entry.summary: A philosophical position paper arguing language is a formalized subset of situated cognition, so language-first probabilistic models inherit structural incompletenesses even as scale produces compensatory emergent abilities. It formalizes a symbolization premise and asks whether emergence can ever recover every missing distinction.

entry.title: DeBERTa-Sentinel: Toward Transparent and Trustworthy Detection of AI-Generated Text

author.name: Muhammad Yousaf Rehman, Muhammad Islam

entry.summary: Fine-tunes DeBERTa-v3 for AI-generated text detection with token-level explanations, positioning transparency against black-box commercial detectors and claiming better robustness to paraphrasing than prior transformer detectors. Framed as responsible detection infrastructure for the web.

entry.title: PartMat: Material-Aware 3D Part Decomposition with a Single Global Latent

author.name: Guangming Fu, Jin Song, Yiyun Fei, Guoqiu Li, Ruigao Yang, Jianan Jiang

entry.summary: PartMat decomposes a 3D object into material-consistent parts, such as fabric, wood, and metal, from a reference image and whole-object geometry, representing all parts with a single global latent instead of generating them independently. This keeps cost from scaling linearly with part count while producing edit-ready assets.

entry.title: UniqueSplat: View-conditioned 3D Gaussian Splatting for Generalizable 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Haixu Song, Xiaoke Yang, Shengjun Zhang, Jiwen Lu, Yueqi Duan

entry.summary: UniqueSplat makes feed-forward 3D Gaussian splatting view-conditioned, predicting Gaussians tailored to each target viewpoint rather than a single fixed set per scene as in pixelSplat and MVSplat. The view prior is baked into network parameters so Gaussians adapt dynamically at query time.

entry.title: Open-Set Visual Text Forensics via Sparse-Constraint Rectified Flow

author.name: Jiangling Zhang, Shuxuan Gao, Zeyu Chen, Yichao Liu, Yu Zhou

entry.summary: This paper detects and localizes AI-generated manipulation of visual text by estimating the local restoration cost needed to bring a query image back to authentic visual-text statistics, using a sparse-constraint adaptation of rectified flow rather than learning forgery-specific boundaries. Self-supervised artifact injection mitigates training data scarcity.

entry.title: Amortizing the Calibration Triple: A Projection-Consistent Neural Operator for Local-Stochastic Volatility

author.name: Xiaozhen Wang, Ana\"is Despr\'es, Martin Dureau, Francois Buet-Golfouse

entry.summary: Learns a neural operator that amortizes the slow iterative calibration of local-stochastic volatility models, jointly outputting an arbitrage-constrained implied volatility surface, the corresponding local volatility, the leverage function, and the conditional moment required for projection consistency. Both DeepONet and Fourier neural operator backbones are evaluated.

entry.title: Semantic Alignment of AI Models: Concept Collapse, Checkpoint Dynamics, and Cross-Lingual Transfer

author.name: Tyler Ashoff, Jordan Rodu

entry.summary: Uses topological methods to compare high-dimensional language model embedding spaces against interpretable low-dimensional baselines such as ontologies and curated knowledge graphs. The stated goal is to characterize semantic structure and track model adaptation and cross-lingual transfer beyond saturated outcome benchmarks.

entry.title: Characterizing Treatment-Context Medication Evidence Across Clinic Notes and Structured EHR Medication History

author.name: Mingyang Jiang, Congning Ni, Weixin Liu, Zhijun Yin

entry.summary: Presents a note-grounded pipeline that uses LLM-assisted reference building, human review, and deterministic normalization to reconcile medication mentions in clinic notes with structured EHR medication history. Held-out evaluation on over 5,000 mention rows shows improved canonical agreement, quantifying how much same-visit disagreement is genuine versus an artifact of extraction and normalization.

entry.title: PhysAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Reliable Remote Heart Rate Estimation

author.name: Yehui Yang, Bo Zhao, Junzhe Cao, Hui Ma, Yue Sun, Wenjin Wang, Zitong Yu

entry.summary: PhysAgent is an inference-time multi-agent framework that arbitrates among conflicting heart-rate candidates produced by different remote photoplethysmography estimators, rather than training a new base model or asking a multimodal LLM to output heart rate directly. Verification agents check physiological plausibility of each candidate.

entry.title: RSC-GestureNet: Reliability-Aware Selective Causal Recognition of Chinese Traffic Police Gestures

author.name: Cheng Li, Renjun Gao, Boyi Fu

entry.summary: RSC-GestureNet recognizes traffic police hand signals causally from continuous video while down-weighting unreliable pose joints and selectively emitting only calibrated predictions. Also releases a corruption benchmark with several pose and image perturbations.

entry.title: SDDMO-Bench: A Benchmark Suite for Streaming Data-Driven Dynamic Multi-Objective Optimization

author.name: Wenjie Xiao, Hui Bai, Junhao Chen

entry.summary: SDDMO-Bench converts classical dynamic multi-objective test problems into streaming environments with controllable distributional drift and sequential data revelation, giving ground-truth optima and drift annotations that real problems lack. It crosses five time-dependent base functions with six drift patterns to standardize comparison.

entry.title: RAG-TESTER: Automated End-to-End Testing of Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models

author.name: Ange Maiztegi, Jon Ayerdi, Miren Illarramendi, Aitor Arrieta

entry.summary: RagTester automatically generates documents, test inputs, and expected outputs for retrieval-augmented systems, executes them, and grades answers with an LLM judge, targeting hard passages, unanswerable queries, and coverage gaps. It is evaluated across 24 generator-embedder combinations.

entry.title: WM-Cov: Test Adequacy for Interactive World-Model-Style Autonomous Driving Simulation

author.name: Jianxun Cui, Ping Wu, Stanisa Peric, Marko Milojkovic, Vladan Devedzic

entry.summary: WM-Cov defines test adequacy for autonomous-driving evaluation using interactive world-model simulators, where the scenario evolves in response to the planner under test rather than replaying a fixed trajectory. It provides a provider-agnostic layer for deciding when closed-loop evidence is sufficient to stop testing.

entry.title: Diagnose Before You Compress: Prediction-Independent Bottleneck Witness Refinement for LLM Serving Traces

author.name: Liming Liu, Chao Hu, Mingfei Lu, Cong Tan, Yiwei Ge, Chijin Zhou, Yongjun Xie, Runzhe Wang, Xiaohai Shi, Heyuan Shi

entry.summary: Proposes bottleneck-preserving witnessing for compressing production LLM serving traces, arguing that rare non-representative requests are precisely the ones that reveal component bottlenecks. It avoids circular evaluation that arises when predicted bottlenecks are used as ground truth.

entry.title: DASH: Decoupled Adaptive Surrogate - Acquisition Harness for Automated Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Changquan Zhao, Yuxiang Sun, Ruihao Zhu, Cheng Hua, Yulian He

entry.summary: DASH decouples surrogate model selection from acquisition function adaptation in automated Bayesian optimization, arguing surrogates should be chosen on predictive reliability while acquisitions respond to campaign context. It uses an LLM to help drive the adaptive selection.

entry.title: HetGPS: Scalable Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Physics-Anchored Adaptive Safety for EV Charging

author.name: Xiangwei Wang, Nanduni Nimalsiri, Yu Xia, Peng Wang, Saman Halgamuge

entry.summary: HetGPS combines a learned graph risk model that sets intervention strength with a physics model that sets the correction direction, applied to safe multi-agent electric vehicle charging coordination. Parameter sharing keeps model size independent of fleet size across five nested distribution networks.

entry.title: PosterMELD: Multi-Agent Paper-to-Poster Generation for Controllable Design Diversity with Editable Print-Ready Outputs

author.name: Haojie Hu, Chenhao Dang, Yaojia Liu, Hengrui Kang, Conghui He, Weijia Li

entry.summary: PosterMELD generates scientific posters with a template-conditioned multi-agent pipeline that plans capacity-aware slots before rendering, uses deterministic gates plus VLM review, and exports editable PowerPoint and image artifacts. Reports a print-ready rate metric over 621 papers instead of only scoring completed outputs.

entry.title: Not All EEG Moments Are Equal: Position-Adaptive Time Scheduling for EEG Generation

author.name: Boheng Liu, Ziyu Li, Chenghua Duan, Qing Li, Xia Wu

entry.summary: Argues that flow-matching EEG generators wrongly assume a single global time progression for all channels and segments, and introduces position-adaptive time scheduling driven by per-position reconstruction error plus factorized spatio-temporal attention. Targets data scarcity in brain-computer interface modeling.

entry.title: Automated ECG Interval Measurement and Wave Delineation Using Fast Fourier Convolution ResNet

author.name: Farhan Adam Mukadam, Harshit Mishra, Nachiket Makwana, Pradyot Tiwari, Subramani Kandasamy, KVS Hari

entry.summary: Evaluates an end-to-end ECG delineation pipeline based on a Fast Fourier Convolution ResNet on 10,646 clinical 12-lead recordings, reporting clinical interval accuracy with bias, Bland-Altman limits of agreement, bootstrap intervals and rhythm-stratified errors. Shifts evaluation from fiducial-point timing on small curated sets to clinically meaningful interval measurement at scale.

entry.title: Evidence-Unit Fairness and the Limits of Query-Adaptive Sparse-Dense Fusion in Financial Document Retrieval

author.name: Chenyu Wu, You Lin

entry.summary: TrustAgentNet proposes a dual-tier blockchain design for agent networks: a global chain tracking skillset metadata lifecycles with off-chain auditing, plus transient task-specific chains for trustless multi-agent collaboration. It targets the mismatch between what third-party agent skills claim and what they actually do under trust-by-declaration assumptions.

entry.title: Hybrid Attention Estimation Pipeline for Adaptive HRI Using an Expressive Robotic Head

author.name: Pablo Moraes, Monica Rodriguez, Christopher Peters, Hiago Sodre, Tobias Doernbach, Bruna Guterres, Ricardo Grando

entry.summary: An applied HRI case study builds an attention-estimation pipeline for an expressive robotic head that fuses a fast geometric face and head-pose layer with a slower vision-language model producing contextual labels (attending to robot, using phone, attending elsewhere), integrated by a finite state machine. It demonstrates practical multi-rate fusion of classical perception with semantic VLM judgments.

entry.title: When Extreme Darkness Meets Motion Blur: MeanFlow for Unified RAW Restoration

author.name: Zepu Wang, Jingze Liang, Weijie Xiao, Kexin Chen

entry.summary: This work tackles extremely low-light RAW image restoration when motion blur is also present, releasing the SIDED dataset with controlled motion degradation on real low-light RAW pairs and proposing a unified RAW tokenizer plus a MeanFlow-based restoration model. It targets a realistic degradation combination that prior low-light methods ignore.

entry.title: PICopilot: An LLM-based Agentic Framework for Assisting Photonic Integrated Circuit Design via Script Generation

author.name: Xiaohan Jiang, Zeyu Li, Wei Zhang, Jiang Xu

entry.summary: PICopilot is an LLM-based agentic assistant that generates design scripts for photonic integrated circuits, addressing the productivity gap created by the shift from GUI design tools to script-based flows requiring API expertise. It claims to be the first such framework for PIC design automation.

entry.title: CoWAM: Coordination Contracts for Selective Policy Intervention with WAMs

author.name: Shuaijun Liu, Qifu Wen, Shuyang Hao, Qi Luo, Chenglong Zhang, Feiyang You, Chengyu Wu, Ningxin Su

entry.summary: CoWAM adds a selective intervention layer over world-action-model-based bimanual robot policies, encoding synchronization, role compatibility, and collision constraints as typed coordination contracts with calibrated gates. The nominal action is only overridden when an alternative provably satisfies all obligations, with abstention as a fallback.

entry.title: Progressive$^2$: A Teacher-Student Progressive Co-Evolving Knowledge Distillation Method for Substantial Model Compression

author.name: Tiancong Cheng, Ying Zhang, Zhiwen Yu, Yifang Yin, Bin Guo

entry.summary: Proposes a distillation scheme where a progressively strengthened teacher and a progressively shrunken student co-evolve, aimed at cases where the server model and client capacity gap is very large. Targets substantial compression without the usual collapse in transfer quality.

entry.title: A Physics-Chemistry-Informed Neural Network (PCINN) for Real-Time Spatial-ALD Coverage Prediction and Reliable Kinetics Inversion

author.name: Ning Hu, Chang Liu, Yunlei Jiang, Yuan Dong

entry.summary: Builds a hybrid physics-and-chemistry-informed surrogate for spatial atomic layer deposition coverage prediction that reaches CFD-level accuracy from only 30 training simulations while answering queries in milliseconds. The network learns a constrained correction rather than acting as a full black box, and also supports kinetics inversion.

entry.title: Modeling Unknown Nonlocal PDE Systems via Flow Map Learning

author.name: Zhongshu Xu, Ying Li, Yanzhi Zhang, Dongbin Xiu

entry.summary: Learns the finite-time evolution operator (flow map) of unknown nonlocal PDEs directly from solution data instead of approximating the nonlocal operators themselves, with modal and nodal formulations. Demonstrates stable long-horizon prediction of fractional diffusion and wave equations from short observation windows.

entry.title: From field-scale to large-scale spectral libraries: Tabular foundation models in soil spectroscopy

author.name: Viacheslav Barkov, Jonas Schmidinger, Robin Gebbers, Martin Atzmueller

entry.summary: Benchmarks a tabular in-context foundation model against CNNs, rule-based regression, random forests, and PLS across 85 soil spectroscopy regression tasks spanning field scale to a global spectral library. Provides guidance on regression and dimensionality-reduction choices for high-dimensional collinear spectra.

entry.title: AdvPlan-Bench: Adversarial Evaluation of Structured Plan-Generation Agents

author.name: Alina Kapanova, Arun Kanhai, Natan Vidra, Spurthi Setty

entry.summary: AdvPlan-Bench evaluates structured plan-generation agents adversarially, representing plans as typed action chains and scoring them against an opposing agent's best responses using game-theoretic diagnostics such as advantage and Nash gap. Offline and synthetic-score based, it targets the gap between judging plans in isolation and under opposition.

entry.title: SparseKAN: Compressing Kolmogorov--Arnold Networks Across Basis Functions, Neurons, and Bits

author.name: Kazi Ahmed Asif Fuad, Lizhong Chen

entry.summary: SparseKAN compresses Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks along three axes at once - basis functions, neurons, and numerical precision - using hierarchical learnable gates trained with a differentiable cost objective. Learned structure is then hardened to explicit budgets and physically compacted for real savings.

entry.title: Breaking Diversity Collapse in Spiking Pseudo-Ensembles for Efficient OOD Detection in Remote Sensing

author.name: Srinivas Anumasa, Rushi Shah, Qiran Zou, Dianbo Liu

entry.summary: Attaches multiple lightweight classification heads to a frozen spiking network backbone to approximate a deep ensemble for out-of-distribution detection at low compute cost. An agree-disagree training objective prevents the heads from collapsing into correlated predictions while preserving in-distribution accuracy.

entry.title: BiKAN: Restoring Collapsed Basis of Binary Kolmogorov--Arnold Networks

author.name: Kazi Ahmed Asif Fuad, Lizhong Chen

entry.summary: Identifies that binarizing polynomial Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks collapses the elementwise basis because all even powers become one and odd powers become the input, destroying expressivity. BiKAN restores pairwise structure by adding selected degree-two Walsh characters generated via circular channel rolls and learned binary projections using the same XNOR and popcount primitives.

entry.title: Pseudorandom Streams within Diffusion Models Act as Learnable Inputs That Affect Generation Quality

author.name: Shengzhi Deng, Chenqi Ye, Yanze Guo

entry.summary: Argues that the pseudorandom number streams consumed by diffusion training and sampling are deterministic orbits whose structure can be partially predicted and even exploited, affecting loss, gradients and generation quality. Uses a small MLP orbit predictor plus a diffusion probe trained on random tensors to test exploitability.

entry.title: Enriched text-guided variational multimodal knowledge distillation network (VMD) for automated diagnosis of plaque vulnerability in 3D carotid artery MRI

author.name: Bo Cao, Fan Yu, Mengmeng Feng, SenHao Zhang, Xin Meng, Yue Zhang, Zhen Qian, Jie Lu

entry.summary: Builds a variational multimodal knowledge distillation network that injects radiologist domain knowledge as enriched text supervision to diagnose carotid plaque vulnerability from 3D MRI. The approach distills multimodal clinical reasoning into a model that operates on imaging at inference.

entry.title: Domain-Generalized Adaptive Semantic Communication for Collaborative Perception

author.name: Fan Gao, Youzheng Wang, Ning Ge

entry.summary: RSTA is a semantic communication framework for vehicle-to-everything collaborative perception that handles simultaneous observation-domain shift and unseen wireless channel corruption. It combines cross-domain prototype alignment and cross-channel gradient consistency during pretraining with a reliability-gated entropy-minimization adapter at deployment.

entry.title: Rethinking Total Absorption Gamma Spectroscopy Deconvolution: Supervised Machine Learning vs Response-Matrix Methods

author.name: J. Balibrea-Correa, E. N{\'a}cher, C. Fonseca-Vargas, J. L. Tain

entry.summary: Systematically compares supervised machine learning estimators against classical response-matrix deconvolution for extracting beta-feeding distributions in total absorption gamma spectroscopy, using realistic Monte Carlo simulations of a real spectrometer. The comparison clarifies when non-parametric learned estimators help on this ill-posed inverse problem.

entry.title: Generative Models for Modeling and Synthesizing MIMO Channels in Adverse Weather Conditions

author.name: Vignesh Nandakumar, Faraz Barati, Brian L. Evans

entry.summary: Synthesizes MIMO channel state information for adverse weather conditions by training a weather-conditioned diffusion model on channels measured or simulated in mild conditions, covering three weather types at three intensities. This provides data for evaluating 5G and 6G coverage where real measurements are scarce.

entry.title: CARNet: Channel-Adaptive Receiver Network for Robust NextG Communications

author.name: Chao Jiang, Zhuo Xu, Yongli Yan

entry.summary: Proposes a mixture-of-experts neural receiver where routing selects ResNet-based experts specialized for different wireless channel conditions, aiming to fix the poor generalization of static neural receivers. Targets next-generation communication physical-layer detection.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Representations for Binary Program Clustering: From Empirical Study to Retrieval-Augmented Learning

author.name: Martin Mocko, Daniela Chud\'a

entry.summary: First systematic study of self-supervised and tabular representation learning methods for clustering binary programs and malware families, adapting vision SSL objectives to tabular malware features and then adding retrieval-augmented learning. Establishes performance ceilings on public malware datasets.

entry.title: DE-NER : Zero-shot Named Entity Recognition via Dialogue Elicitation of Large Language Models

author.name: Xuankang Zhang, Jiangming Liu

entry.summary: Proposes a dialogue-elicitation framework for zero-shot named entity recognition that uses conversational turns to draw out entity knowledge from LLMs instead of relying on hand-tuned prompts and demonstrations. Reports roughly four F1 points average gain over competitive zero-shot baselines.

entry.title: Observatorio Lazaro: A self-populating database of anglicism usage in the Spanish press

author.name: Elena Alvarez-Mellado

entry.summary: Documents a continuously running system that has monitored English lexical borrowings in the Spanish digital press since 2020 using a neural sequence labeller, now covering over two million borrowings across nearly two million articles. Provides a public interface and API for diachronic lexical research.

entry.title: RH-RAG: Trustworthy Long-Form Generation for Privacy-Constrained Settings

author.name: Raj Shekhar Singh
