Aims to close the gap between content-semantic pretraining and behavior-driven ranking.

entry.title: Data Turnstile: A Scalable Open Framework for Function-Calling Data Generation

author.name: Goutham Ramakrishnan and Megha Sharma

entry.summary: Releases an open framework that turns user-supplied API specifications into high-quality synthetic function-calling training data through constrained stepwise generation with validation and error-feedback loops. Motivated by small language models being unable to compensate for noisy tool-use supervision through capacity.

entry.title: SAGP: Semantic Affordance-Guided Grasp Planning via Coarse-Zone VLM Reasoning

author.name: Muhayy Ud Din and Irfan Hussain

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free grasp planner where a vision-language model reasons only about coarse semantic zones, such as handle versus blade, and those zones then constrain a geometric grasp planner. Avoids both fine-grained part segmentation and direct pose prediction, which is prone to spatial hallucination.

entry.title: The Greedy Advantage in Finite-Horizon Bandits

author.name: Kai Zhou, Michael Lingzhi Li, Kai Wang

entry.summary: Develops regularized greedy algorithms for Bernoulli multi-armed bandits and derives the first finite-horizon regret envelopes for them, decomposing regret into transient exploration cost and a term that decays exponentially with regularization strength. Yields principled rules for calibrating regularization when the experiment horizon is externally fixed.

entry.title: Dense Temporal Contrast Synthesis via Conditioned Latent Transport

author.name: Smriti Joshi, Apostolia Tsirikoglou, Daniel M. Lang, Richard Osuala, Noah M\'arquez Varaa, Alejandro Guzman, Grzegorz Skorupko, Sebastian Ibarra Arregui, Lidia Garrucho, Akane Ohashi, Dimitra Ntoula, Eugen Divjak, O\u{g}uz Lafc{\i}, Jan C. Peeken, Julia A. Schnabel, Fredrik Strand, Oliver Diaz and Karim Lekadir

entry.summary: Proposes a conditioned latent transport model that predicts contrast-enhanced breast MRI in a single forward pass, anchoring the latent trajectory to pre-contrast anatomy and using continuous time conditioning for temporal continuity. Aims to reduce reliance on gadolinium contrast agents that are contraindicated for some patients and environmentally problematic.

entry.title: ModelEquivBench: Certifying Multi-Relational Evaluation of LLM-Generated Optimization Models

author.name: Penglin Zhu, Jungang Xu

entry.summary: ModelEquivBench replaces binary equivalence judgments for LLM-generated optimization models with a seven-level semantic profile spanning representation alignment, feasible-set relations, objective ordering, optimal value, and optimizer sets. Each verdict carries an independently checkable certificate.

entry.title: MolGVR: A Chemistry-Grounded Framework for Text-to-Molecule Generation

author.name: Qian Tan, Xuanyu Zhu, Lei Jiang, Zhonghang Yuan, Chen Zhang, Yuqiang Li

entry.summary: MolGVR reframes text-to-molecule generation as a generator-verifier-refiner loop, converting natural-language descriptions into explicit chemical constraints that candidate molecules are checked against and revised toward. This targets the failure mode where generated molecules silently violate structural constraints implied by the prompt.

entry.title: MOT-SR: Multi-Objective Tool-Augmented Scientific Equation Discovery with Large Language Models

author.name: Boxiao Wang, Runxiang Wang, Kai Li, Chongming Li, Zhiwei Chen, Yifan Zhang, Jian Cheng

entry.summary: MOT-SR augments LLM-driven symbolic regression with external analytical tools that extract variable dependency structure as priors, and replaces single-objective fitting-error selection with multi-objective evaluation including structural complexity and generalization. The aim is to avoid premature convergence to local optima in equation discovery.

entry.title: The Parts Are Greater Than the Sum: Automated Task Sequencing for Efficient Training of Multi-Policy LLMs

author.name: Jiajia Tang and Sizhe Yuen and Francisco Gomez Medina and Yali Du and Adam Sobey

entry.summary: Proposes an automatic multi-policy PEFT framework that groups and sequences heterogeneous tasks into compatible adaptation paths instead of forcing all tasks through one shared LoRA optimization space. The aim is to reduce interference and catastrophic forgetting under a fixed parameter budget.

entry.title: CodeShrink: Adaptive Visual Compression for Efficient Multimodal Code Understanding

author.name: Wenxin Tang, Jingyu Xiao, Zhenyu Liu, Zipeng Xie, Junliang Liu, Wang Luo, Yuan Jiang, Yintong Huo, Michael Lyu

entry.summary: CodeShrink reduces multimodal LLM input cost when code is rendered as images by removing whitespace-induced tokens through blank-free rendering with explicit structural markers, and adaptively choosing compression settings per input with a lightweight agent. It addresses the fact that optimal compression varies across inputs, tasks, and models.

entry.title: The Asymmetric Effects of Knowledge Distillation on Bias in Small Language Models

author.name: Plawan Kumar Rath

entry.summary: Shows that distilling a larger teacher into small instruction-tuned students improves context-following on unambiguous bias benchmarks but degrades appropriate abstention on ambiguous ones, converting prior refusals into stereotyped answers. The asymmetry replicates across two student families and 28 configurations.

entry.title: LAWFUL: Law-Aligned Witness for Faithful Use of Latents

author.name: Kevin Chen, Kenneth W. Parker, Anish Arora

entry.summary: LAWFUL asks not only whether a network predicts physics accurately but whether its internal circuit actually implements the governing law across the law domain of validity, identifying four interpretability gaps. It contributes a coverage-aware causal-consistency measure over continuous counterfactuals and a domain-of-validity test for identified circuits.

entry.title: SciToolAgent-Evo: An Ontology-Aware Self-Evolving Agent for Open-World Scientific Tool Acquisition

author.name: Yuqi Tang, Chenyi Zhou, Libin Wang, Keyan Ding, Qiang Zhang, Huajun Chen

entry.summary: SciToolAgent-Evo lets a scientific agent expand its own tool repertoire in open-world settings by maintaining an ontologized tool graph and memory of skills and experiences, distilling knowledge from contrastive successful and failed trajectories. At inference a bandit gate balances exploring new tools against exploiting known ones.

entry.title: Is It Time for the Renaissance of Salient Object Detection in the Era of MLLMs?

author.name: Wenzhuo Zhao, Xiuzhi Li, Zhongkuan Mao, Ronghao Xian, Yao Jiang, Zhao Gao, Keren Fu, Qijun Zhao, Jian Cheng

entry.summary: Builds a diagnostic benchmark that decomposes salient object detection into localization and segmentation with phrase, box, and attribute annotations, revealing that multimodal LLMs beat specialized systems at localizing salient objects but lag badly at mask quality. Traces the gap to mismatches in foreground cardinality, granularity, and extent, then recasts zero-shot saliency to align with the annotation protocol.

entry.title: Weight-Space Mixture-of-Experts for Implicit Neural Representation Classification

author.name: Stanislaw Janik, Michal Byra

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical mixture-of-experts Transformer that classifies signals directly in the weight space of implicit neural representations, with conditional computation aligned to the implicit network structure. Combined with meta-learning that shapes INR parameters for downstream use, it reports state-of-the-art weight-space classification accuracy.

entry.title: FibVLA: An Efficient Temporal Vision-Language-Action Model with Fibonacci Sampling

author.name: Li Lin, Wujun Xu, Weiwei Meng, Kaiwen Xia, Kang Hao Cheong, Shuai Wang

entry.summary: FibVLA uses Fibonacci-spaced logarithmic hindsight sampling of proprioceptive states and visual frames so a vision-language-action model can access long-horizon history at sub-linear token cost. This targets the tension between temporal context and inference efficiency in embodied policies.

entry.title: Evolving language compositionality in a frequency-structured meaning space

author.name: Fabio De Ponte, Eloise Gaines-White, Conor Houghton, and Seth Bullock

entry.summary: Extends the iterated learning model of language evolution by making some meanings far more frequent than others, testing how frequency structure interacts with the transmission bottleneck that normally produces compositionality. Finds that high-frequency meanings can escape the grammar governing rarer meanings, mirroring irregularity patterns in natural languages.

entry.title: Automatically Differentiable Model Updating (ADiMU): conventional, hybrid, and neural network material model discovery including history-dependency

author.name: Bernardo P. Ferreira, Miguel A. Bessa

entry.summary: ADiMU is a fully differentiable framework that calibrates or discovers history-dependent material constitutive models from either full-field displacement plus force data or direct strain-stress data. It works uniformly across physics-based, neural network, and hybrid models spanning tens to millions of parameters without hyperparameter tuning.

entry.title: Do Medical Foundation Models Generalize on the African Brain?

author.name: Kaouther Mouheb and Gonzalo Esteban Mosquera Rojas and Juancito van Leeuwen and Stefan Klein and Esther E. Bron

entry.summary: Benchmarks generalist and segmentation-specific medical foundation models on African brain MRI, using a Nigerian dementia dataset and BraTS-Africa, against a from-scratch baseline. Foundation models help substantially for segmentation but only modestly for classification, and the paper quantifies performance gaps between African and non-African cohorts.

entry.title: Representations from Pretrained Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials as Coarse Coordinates for Material Generation and Evaluation

author.name: Paul Hagemann, Katharina Ueltzen, Simon M\"uller, Janine George, Philipp Benner

entry.summary: Shows that atom-averaged representations from pretrained machine-learning interatomic potentials such as MACE work well as coarse coordinates for evaluating and guiding inorganic crystal structure generation. Introduces a Coarse-Fine Transport Distance that scores both quality and novelty of generated structures in one distributional metric.

entry.title: Benchmarks Are Not Monolithic: Sample-Level Auditing and Orchestration for LLM Evaluation

author.name: Philipp D. Siedler, Jordan Sassoon

entry.summary: Argues that benchmarks are internally heterogeneous and introduces a framework annotating individual samples along five dimensions including cognitive demand, content quality, task properties, context, and safety or fairness. Applying it to MMLU, ARC, WinoGrande, HellaSwag, and TruthfulQA reveals variation that aggregate accuracy hides, enabling criterion-driven construction of composite evaluation subsets.

entry.title: Hypergradient-based Bilevel Reinforcement Learning with Improved Sample Complexity

author.name: Naman Saxena, Mudit Gaur, Vaneet Aggarwal

entry.summary: Proposes a Hessian-free hypergradient algorithm for bilevel reinforcement learning that exploits the optimality of the Boltzmann policy under entropy regularization, covering meta-learning, hierarchical decomposition, and RLHF as instances. Reports improved iteration and state-of-the-art sample complexity bounds relative to penalty-based approximations.

entry.title: TORUS: A Test of Rendering-Understanding Self-Coherence for Unified Audio Models

author.name: Aryan Vijay Bhosale, Harshit Rajgarhia, Abhishek Mukherji, Dinesh Manocha

entry.summary: Proposes TORUS, the first self-coherence test asking whether a unified audio model's understanding head agrees with what its own generation head produced, across speech, sound, and music in five task families. Five open unified models are evaluated against a cascaded pipeline of specialized state-of-the-art components.

entry.title: FairFund-Bench: Evaluating Distributive Bias in LLM Resource Allocation

author.name: Martin Lukk (University of Toronto)

entry.summary: Shows that contradictory findings in LLM discrimination audits can be explained by audit design choices, then introduces a benchmark that systematically varies evaluation task, comparison context, and whether the audit is transparent or disguised. It uses 600 requests for financial assistance built from human-authored text to measure distributive bias.

entry.title: Overcoming the Weakest-Link Effect in LLM-Driven Program Optimization via Heterogeneous Edit Recombination

author.name: Jingwen Fu, Zhen Liu, Yuhan Liu, He Zhang, Nanning Zheng

entry.summary: Argues that LLM-driven program search suffers a weakest-link effect because textual gradient style update directions become unreliable as the program-to-score mapping grows complex. Proposes recombining heterogeneous edits from different sources instead of relying on a single first-order textual update direction.

entry.title: SERUM: State Extraction and Refinement for User Modeling

author.name: Andy J. Phu, James Mooney, Karin de Langis, Khanh Chi Le, Dongyeop Kang

entry.summary: Extracts finite-state models of user behavior directly from unstructured screen-recording video using multi-pass hierarchical vision-language-model annotation that alternates activity recognition and intent inference. Synonymous states are merged by sentence embeddings to yield compact taxonomies for personalized agentic assistants.

entry.title: MROPE: A Multi-Robot Safe Cooperative Strategy via combined Predictive Safety Filters and Ellipse-based Constraint Compression

author.name: Alice Rosetti, Lorenzo Pichierri, Domenico Cappello, Fabrizio Schiano, Giuseppe Notarstefano

entry.summary: Presents a hierarchical control strategy for drone swarms tracking a moving target in cluttered space, compressing complex obstacle geometry into a single safe bounding ellipse per drone to cut computation. It combines distributed aggregative optimization, decentralized consensus for safe-region agreement, and local predictive safety filters, validated in simulation and hardware.

entry.title: Frugal Bayesian Optimization: Scalable Surrogates for Data- and Resource-Limited Discovery

author.name: Panagiotis Krokidas, Christoforos Rekatsinas, Vassilis Sioros, Grigorios M. Chatziathanasiou, Efi-Maria Papia, George Giannakopoulos

entry.summary: Runs a compute-aware comparison of Bayesian optimization surrogates across eight synthetic functions and nine real datasets, finding Gaussian processes incur the largest time and memory cost without better sample efficiency than scalable tree- or spline-based alternatives. Argues for reporting computational frugality alongside optimization quality.

entry.title: Event-Based Upper-Body Humanoid Teleoperation Under Challenging Illumination

author.name: Haoyu Fu, Zhou Ge, Chengze Li, Chenzhao Sun, Ze Cui, Wenjing Zhou, Xulei Qin

entry.summary: Builds a real-time upper-body humanoid teleoperation system driven by neuromorphic event cameras, exploiting microsecond temporal resolution and over 120 dB dynamic range to track human motion under severe backlighting and sub-5-lux lighting. Combines optimized event accumulation with gravity-aligned inertial fusion and a causal motion module.

entry.title: CBCT-IQ: A Publicly Available Annotated Cone-Beam CT Dataset for Image Quality Assessment and Benchmarking

author.name: Sepideh Hatamikia, Anna Breger, Clemens Karner, Birgit Pohn, Poorya MohammadiNasab, Martin Buschmann, Stephanie Nougaret, Laura Haddad, Ali Abbasian Ardakani, Afshin Mohammadi, Paul Apfaltrer, Wolfgang Birkfellner, Alfred Pohl, Ander Biguri, Gernot Kronreif, Carola-Bibiane Sch\"onlieb, Tess Reynolds

entry.summary: Releases the first open-access cone-beam CT image-quality dataset with 1,764 expert-annotated slices acquired under systematic variations in acquisition settings, enabling development and validation of quantitative image-quality metrics. Addresses the dose-versus-quality tradeoff where subjective expert review is currently the clinical standard.

entry.title: TRACT: Temporally Routed Action Chunks with Chronological Phase Authority for Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Jiahao Liu, Kento Kawaharazuka, Tasuku Makabe, and Kei Okada

entry.summary: Addresses the mismatch when an action chunk predicted by an imitation policy crosses a procedural phase boundary but is conditioned on only the current phase, by factorizing the horizon into an accepted current phase plus one current-to-next boundary. Uses a task-local graph to constrain chronological phase ordering and routes future queries through phase-specific paths for contact-rich manipulation.

entry.title: Studying quantization trade-offs for efficient inference deployment in machine translation

author.name: Jim Zhao, Sohir Maskey, Koen Oostermeijer, Douglas Orr, Teryn Jones

entry.summary: Studies quantization trade-offs for two translation model families spanning 1.7B to 22B parameters under controlled server-orchestration workloads on single A100 and H100 GPUs. Finds that combining document chunking with 4-bit or 8-bit weight and 8-bit activation quantization improves the latency-throughput Pareto frontier.

entry.title: Bridging the Question-Answer Gap in Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Hypothetical Prompt Embeddings

author.name: Domen Vake, Jernej Vi\v{c}i\v{c}, Aleksandar To\v{s}i\'c

entry.summary: HyPE moves hypothetical-content generation in RAG from query time to indexing time by precomputing hypothetical questions per chunk and embedding those instead of the chunk text. This removes the runtime overhead of HyDE-style methods while narrowing the stylistic gap between queries and documents.

entry.title: DreamQAS: Learning a Decision-Useful World Model for VQE-Efficient Quantum Architecture Search

author.name: Jiayang Niu, Yan Wang, Jie Li, Ke Deng, Azadeh Alavi, Muhammad Usman, and Yongli Ren

entry.summary: DreamQAS applies model-based RL to quantum architecture search by keeping the known deterministic circuit dynamics exact and learning only the expensive post-VQE energy feedback with a recurrent randomized-prior ensemble. Uncertainty-aware pessimism and selective real-VQE verification control the reliability of imagined rollouts.

entry.title: A Neurosymbolic Approach for Explainable Early Diagnosis of Alzheimer's Disease

author.name: Ranveer Singh, Pranuthi Tenali, Saurabh Mathur, Ameet Soni, Vaishali Phatak, Karla Lynch, Daniel Murman, Matthew Rizzo, Sriraam Natarajan

entry.summary: An automated pipeline extracts clinically relevant linguistic variables from raw audio of verbal fluency tests using pretrained speech foundation models, then builds a Bayesian network to reason about Alzheimer's progression markers. The system recovers known clinical relationships and surfaces some novel ones.

entry.title: Neuron Statistics: Notes on the Tensor Programs Master Theorem

author.name: Rongyi Zhu

entry.summary: An expository note on the tensor programs master theorem, explaining how neuron-level averages in very wide networks converge to expectations in a simpler scalar random process and how this underpins Gaussian process and neural tangent kernel limits. The main technical content walks through the proof when a random weight matrix and its transpose are reused, as in backpropagation or weight sharing, by conditioning on earlier uses and isolating a fresh Gaussian component.

entry.title: Graph Neural Network Surrogates for Contacting Deformable Bodies with Necessary and Sufficient Contact Detection

author.name: Vijay K. Dubey (1), Collin E. Haese (1), Osman G\"ultekin (1), David Dalton (2), Manuel K. Rausch (1), Jan N. Fuhg (1) ((1) The University of Texas at Austin, (2) University of Glasgow)

entry.summary: Presents a graph neural network surrogate for contact mechanics between deformable bodies that embeds continuous collision detection and, unusually, sufficient (not merely necessary) contact conditions. This lets fast surrogates handle soft-soft contact with varying geometries, which prior surrogates could not.

entry.title: ViSAGE: Constructing Self-Correcting Memories for Long-Form Video Understanding

author.name: Xinkui Zhao, Enbo Chen, Yifan Zhang, Chang Liu, Guanjie Cheng, Naibo Wang, Yueshen Xu

entry.summary: ViSAGE builds entity-centric, self-correcting memories for long-form video understanding by binding identity cues across long time ranges and applying bidirectional refinement to propagate delayed identity resolution backward through memory. It targets entity confusion and hallucination caused by compression and pure vector-similarity retrieval.

entry.title: FillGS: Filling Observation Gaps in 4D Gaussian Splatting via Viewpoint-Time Selection and Generative Refinement

author.name: Takashi Otonari, Toshihiko Yamasaki

entry.summary: Improves dynamic-scene 4D Gaussian Splatting by actively selecting spatiotemporal virtual viewpoints based on rendering sensitivity and motion-aware observation density, rather than heuristic virtual-view placement, then refining those views with a generative model. Targets artifacts in sparsely observed regions of scenes with large motion.

entry.title: MoPET: Parameter-Efficient Mixture-of-Experts for Unified Medical Image Classification

author.name: Sebastian Doerrich, Daniel W\"urtinger, Francesco Di Salvo, Shyam Nandan Rai, Christian Ledig

entry.summary: MoPET injects a sparse mixture of low-rank PEFT experts into a frozen vision foundation model with a learned router, letting one generalist network serve many medical imaging tasks without per-task adapters. The routing is intended to share capacity while limiting negative transfer between conflicting domains.

entry.title: Homotopy-Aware Corridor Generation without Predefined Reference Paths

author.name: Haoze Dong, Minghan Li, Meng Guo, Zhongkui Li

entry.summary: Generates safe navigation corridors as sequences of convex sets on graphs of convex sets without requiring a predefined reference path, so corridor geometry is not biased by a guiding trajectory. Extends visibility-based deformation from paths to convex-set sequences to fuse topologically redundant corridors while keeping genuinely distinct homotopy classes.

entry.title: OASIS: Occlusion-aware Single-image Hand Avatar Reconstruction via 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Zhisheng Han, Shiyao Wu, Jiayan Qiu, Yakun Ju, Lu Liu, Le Zhang, Pengfei Feng, Huiyu Zhou, Zheheng Jiang

entry.summary: OASIS reconstructs animatable 3D hand avatars from a single image using 3D Gaussian Splatting instead of implicit NeRF representations, aligning image observations with 3D hand geometry to form geometry-grounded visual evidence tokens. It specifically targets severe self-occlusion and pose-dependent deformation of articulated hands.

entry.title: Single Forward Pass Evals on Fable, Opus 5, and GPT-5.6-Sol

author.name: Christine Corry

entry.summary: A fellowship research update replicates earlier single-forward-pass evaluations on an existing baseline model and then extends them to Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6-Sol, all released weeks to months before the coverage date. The newer models show large gains in reasoning without visible chain of thought, with one reaching roughly 88 percent on generated arithmetic using problem repeats versus prior best around 60 percent, and one gaining substantially from filler tokens.

entry.title: Efficient Logic Gate Networks for Video Copy Detection

author.name: Katarzyna Fojcik

entry.summary: Replaces floating-point video descriptors with differentiable logic gate networks that compile into pure Boolean circuits for video copy detection, combining aggressive frame downscaling and binary preprocessing. The result is very compact descriptors and fast inference for large-scale near-duplicate search.

entry.title: Optical Flow Sensor: A Direction-Selective Bionic Retina Design

author.name: Juchen Zhou, Bonan Yan, Yuchao Yang

entry.summary: Presents a pixel-level integrated circuit that computes optical flow on-chip by combining event-based ON/OFF comparisons with time-difference measurement, plus a specialized address-event readout interface. The bionic retina design targets low-latency, low-power motion sensing versus dense frame-based flow computation.

entry.title: Learning Optimal Dynamic Matching via Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Genta Okada, Shunya Noda, Junpei Komiyama, Akira Matsushita

entry.summary: Develops a value-based reinforcement learning framework with graph neural networks for dynamic matching markets in continuous time with stochastic arrivals, type transitions, and exits. Proves an event-time reduction so the planner need only act right after each event, and shows the optimal edge-wise Q-function reduces to a single continuation-value function on post-decision residual graphs.

entry.title: BLADE: Boundary-Expanded and Layer-Adaptive Dynamic Exit for Efficient LLM Reasoning

author.name: Keshu Fu, Keqin Peng, Jun Bai, Shuhan Qin, Chen Li, Junzhu Liang, Yefei Chen, Jiaqi Li, Yuanxin Ouyang

entry.summary: Presents BLADE, which terminates LLM reasoning early by probing many ordinary reasoning boundaries rather than only explicit self-doubt phrases, and adapts which hidden layer is inspected because predictive signal for different intermediate states lives at different depths. It estimates whether the generated prefix already suffices for a correct answer.

entry.title: UltraSAM3: A Concept-Driven Foundation Model for Universal Ultrasound Image Segmentation

author.name: Bo Xu, Quanhao Zhu, Rui Lin, Boling Zhu, Chenyuan Wang, Hongfei Lin, Feng Xia, Chenhua Ji

entry.summary: Builds a concept-driven foundation model for universal ultrasound segmentation that avoids requiring expert-drawn visual prompts, instead conditioning on clinical concepts to handle speckle noise, low contrast, and ambiguous boundaries. Targets flexible clinical deployment across many ultrasound tasks.

entry.title: UniPolymer: A Unified Framework for Property Prediction, Structure Recommendation, and Evaluation in Polyimide Design

author.name: Junquan Hu and Zhihui Wang and Peng Xu and Xinru Guo and Xintong Li and Kun Lu and Ben Fei

entry.summary: Unifies property prediction, target-conditioned generation, candidate evaluation, and structure recommendation for polyimide design, and releases a curated dataset of about 10,000 repeating units labeled with glass transition temperature. Adds explicit consistency checking so candidates far from the design target are filtered before costly experiments.

entry.title: End-to-End Fairness Optimization with Fair Decision-Focused Learning

author.name: Yu Wang, Violet (Xinying) Chen

entry.summary: Proposes end-to-end fairness optimization that treats fairness jointly in the prediction stage (accuracy disparity across groups) and the decision stage (alpha-fair resource allocation). Fair decision-focused learning trains predictors against decision regret in fairness rather than accuracy alone.

entry.title: QR-Structured Thermal Triggers for Targeted Semantic Attacks on Infrared Vision-Language Models

author.name: Xiang Chen, Yingying Zhao, Chao Li, Jiaju Han, Ben Zhang, Ang Li, Jiahuan Long, Yiwei Wei, Jiujiang Guo, Chengyin Hu

entry.summary: QR-STT is a black-box, training-free physical attack on infrared vision-language models that embeds thermal QR-like patterns whose modules are set to cold, neutral, or hot states to steer model outputs toward a target semantic. A gradient-free search tunes module topology and rendering parameters.

entry.title: The K-Space Signature: Frequency-Domain Representation Learning for Medical Deepfake Detection

author.name: Riccardo Raciti, Francesco Guarnera, Francesco Rundo, Luca Guarnera, Sebastiano Battiato

entry.summary: Proposes a forensic framework for detecting synthetic medical images by working in the frequency domain and subtracting an empirical global anatomical prior from the log power spectral density to isolate hardware and generative traces. Targets the risk that generative medical imaging models are repurposed for fraud or harm.

entry.title: TransGraspNet: Physically and Geometrically Consistent Manipulation of Transparent Labware

author.name: Hailing Hu, Mingyi Zhu, Yiquan An, Yifei Tian, Tianyou Zuo, and Lifeng Zhou

entry.summary: TransGraspNet enforces consistency from perception through execution for grasping transparent, liquid-filled laboratory glassware, coupling boundary-consistent detection, depth reconstruction, normal estimation, and task-aware grasp scoring. The motivation is that independently optimized stages compound errors into unstable grasps and spills.

entry.title: CoDe-SSM: Context-Detail Decoupled State Space Model for Efficient UHD Image Restoration

author.name: Jiaxu Su, Zhijian Wu, Jun Li, Bo Zhang, Yefeng Zheng

entry.summary: CoDe-SSM restores ultra-high-definition images by routing aggregated global context and clustering residuals through separate pathways in a state space model, so that fine edges and textures poorly captured by shared aggregation are preserved. A global cluster scan module handles recurring degradation cues efficiently.

entry.title: Bootstrapping Self-Supervised Learning of Binary Classification Using Error Bounds: A Case Study on a Robotic Insertion Task

author.name: Zebin Duan, Norbert Kr\"uger, Juan Heredia, Thorbj{\o}rn Mosekj{\ae}r Iversen, Frederik Hagelskj{\ae}r

entry.summary: Presents a self-supervised data engine for robotic insertion that pairs a fast learned classifier with an expensive verification step, invoking verification only when prediction confidence is low. Error bounds let the system control failure rates while gathering data and improving during task execution, cutting deployment setup time.

entry.title: Pause, at least after unipolarity

author.name: David Matolcsi

entry.summary: A strategy essay arguing that the world is likely to reach military unipolarity within a lifetime, that this outcome is dangerous, but that once it occurs the standard competitive justification for racing toward superintelligence disappears. The author urges that advocacy be shaped now so that a long halt to frontier AI development becomes the default at that point.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Planning with Spatio-Temporal and Topological Constraints using STL-GO

author.name: Sheryl Paul, Vidisha Kudalkar, Anand Balakrishnan, Lars Lindemann, Alberto Speranzon, Jyotirmoy V. Deshmukh

entry.summary: Addresses multi-agent path planning under specifications written in spatio-temporal logic with graph operators, which can express both when and where agents act and how they must interact over sensing, communication, and task topologies. The work provides planning methods that satisfy these combined constraints.

entry.title: OSAGEN: Object-Aware Mask Priors and Multistage Decoupled Diffusion for Industrial Anomaly Generation

author.name: Jinyi Xu, Peng Chen, Yunkang Cao, Chengliang Liu, Xinghui Dong, Chao Huang

entry.summary: OSAGEN generates synthetic industrial defect images with matching masks using object-aware mask priors and a three-stage decoupled diffusion adaptation that learns normal appearance, coarse defect appearance, then fine mask calibration. It aims to fix over-adherence to mask geometry and object-incompatible condition masks in few-shot anomaly generation.

entry.title: CENDRe: Concept Extraction with Natural Domain Representations

author.name: Antonia Holzapfel and Andres Felipe Posada Moreno and Sebastian Trimpe

entry.summary: CENDRe extracts human-interpretable concepts from CNNs trained on time series by clustering per-timestep latent representations in two stages, covering frequency as well as time features and automatically selecting the number of concepts. It also aims to align concept localizations with the regions the model actually uses.

entry.title: Single- to multi-fidelity history-dependent learning with uncertainty quantification and disentanglement: application to data-driven constitutive modeling

author.name: Jiaxiang Yi, Bernardo P. Ferreira, Miguel A. Bessa

entry.summary: Generalizes data-driven constitutive modeling to multi-fidelity, history-dependent data using Bayesian recurrent networks that separate epistemic model uncertainty from aleatoric data noise. The hierarchy spans simple deterministic networks up to multi-fidelity variance-estimating Bayesian RNNs.

entry.title: Evidence-Ledger Adjudication for Claim-Evidence Traceability

author.name: Gengyu Chen, Yongjie Yu, Weiling Wang

entry.summary: Studies an agentic workflow that pairs each generated claim with an evidence packet, adjudicates the support relation, and routes unsupported or contradicted claims back for revision, benchmarked blind on 2,335 rows drawn from AVeriTeC, CLIMATE-FEVER, and SciFact. The agentic ledger nearly doubles macro-F1 over the strongest non-agent baseline.

entry.title: TAPR: Enhancing LLM Performance with a Task-Aware Prompt Rewriter

author.name: Oliver Savolainen, Emanuele Bastianelli, Hosein Azarbonyad

entry.summary: TAPR trains a small model with GRPO to rewrite user prompts into task-optimized prompts, using LLM-as-judge rewards on both the rewritten prompt and the resulting downstream output. Fine-tuning a small Phi model yields consistent gains across question answering, summarization, and arithmetic reasoning.

entry.title: Evaluating Federated Pre-Training: On the Reliability of Downstream Fine-Tuning and Intrinsic Evaluation

author.name: Claudia Grosser, Maike Heuer, Denis Krompass, Thomas A. Runkler

entry.summary: Asks which evaluation protocol best reflects federated pre-training quality, comparing pre-training perplexity against downstream fine-tuning benchmarks using controlled centralized and federated 16M-parameter transformers trained on identical client data. It examines whether task adaptation obscures true pre-training quality differences.

entry.title: ReLoop-UME: Recurrent Depth with Learnable Retrieval Registers for Universal Multimodal Embedding

author.name: Shijie Wang, Xiangzhao Hao, Yueti Li, Guangyu Cao, Xinyu Tang, Haiyun Guo

entry.summary: Studies where retrieval-relevant structure emerges across layers of universal multimodal embedding models and proposes recurrent depth reuse with learnable retrieval registers instead of generating extra rationale or latent tokens. The goal is added computation without extra token generation, keeping retrieval latency low.

entry.title: TextCloak: Thwarting Unauthorized LLM Exploitation via RL-Driven Unlearnable Text

author.name: Chengshuai Zhao, Pingchuan Ma, Dawei Li, Bohan Jiang, Zhiyuan Yu, Zhen Tan, Huan Liu

entry.summary: Proposes TextCloak, a reinforcement-learning framework that perturbs text so that models trained on it lose utility, targeting unauthorized generative training rather than the discriminative classification setting most prior unlearnable-example methods assume. Avoids the class-specific linguistic cues that fail in open-ended generation.

entry.title: NeSyFS: A Neuro-symbolic Fast-Slow Thinking Framework for LLM Agent under Partial Observability

author.name: Duo Xu, Faramarz Fekri

entry.summary: Proposes a neuro-symbolic fast-slow framework for LLM agents acting under partial observability, addressing belief-state inference, objective misalignment, and planning under uncertainty rather than conditioning on raw or summarized histories. Symbolic components maintain structured beliefs while the LLM handles flexible reasoning.

entry.title: Mining Verdict Boundaries for Neural Network Verification

author.name: Jiawei Ren, Guanqin Zhang, Zhenya Zhang, and Yulei Sui

entry.summary: Improves branch-and-bound neural network verification by exploiting monotonicity along search tree paths to locate the boundary between verified and unverified subproblems, rather than solving every subproblem sequentially with costly bound propagation. This reduces the number of expensive verification calls needed for completeness.

entry.title: Retrieval-Driven Training-Free AI-Generated Video Attribution

author.name: Renxi Cheng, Chaolei Han, Jie Gui, Hongsong Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free approach to attributing AI-generated videos to their source generator by casting attribution as instance retrieval over generative fingerprints, avoiding reliance on access to the generation model. Motivated by forensic and regulatory needs as synthetic video becomes indistinguishable from real footage.

entry.title: Extrapolating the emergence of Hamiltonian chaos with random-feature Hamiltonian neural networks

author.name: Jaesung Choi

entry.summary: Tests whether parameter-aware Hamiltonian neural networks trained only in regular, torus-dominated regimes can extrapolate to unseen parameter values where chaos emerges. A random-feature Hamiltonian network reportedly predicts the onset and growth of chaotic regions without any training data from those regimes.

entry.title: Beyond Feature and Structure Alignment: Learning Transferable Propagation Knowledge for Graph Foundation Models

author.name: Yi Wang, Jitao Zhao, Di Jin, Dongxiao He

entry.summary: Argues that graph foundation models fail partly because graphs lack a natural transferable unit like tokens or patches, and that existing work only aligns features and structures. The paper instead proposes treating message-propagation behavior as the transferable knowledge unit across graph domains.

entry.title: Progressive Decision-Making for Localizing Open-Ended AI-Generated Image Forgeries

author.name: Jingyi Hou, Xiaoxia Chen, Leyu Zhou, Zhichuang Wang, Zhijie Liu

entry.summary: Reframes localization of AI-generated image manipulations as a sequential decision-updating process rather than a single-shot segmentation prediction, so the detector can progressively refine judgments from weak and unevenly distributed forensic traces. Targets open-ended forgeries whose appearance cannot be exhaustively covered by training data.

entry.title: MDIR: A Task-Manifold Impedance Retargeting Method for Contact-Rich Teleoperation

author.name: Liu Jiahao, Kento Kawaharazuka, Tasuku Makabe, Kei Okada

entry.summary: Reparameterizes a single fixed-impedance teleoperation demonstration into an executable variable-impedance command by decomposing the recorded response into work, exertion, and support channels on a task manifold. Preserves projected task-channel behavior near the demonstrated trajectory while reducing impact and force variability in contact-rich tasks.

entry.title: Training-Free Entity-Level Few-Shot Segmentation of Remote Sensing Images with Advection Refinement

author.name: Xueting Bai, Huan Ni

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free few-shot segmentation pipeline for remote sensing that uses a segmentation foundation model to produce category-agnostic entity primitives, then reasons at entity rather than pixel level with prototype and text-based semantic fields. An advection-equation refinement step propagates semantics to reduce fragmented predictions.

entry.title: Cross-Resolution Semantic Learning for Graph Domain Adaptation

author.name: Yingxu Wang, Haoze Huang, Zhongkai Zheng, Shangsong Liang

entry.summary: Defines semantic resolution shift in graph domain adaptation, meaning the neighborhood range at which class-discriminative evidence is strongest differs between source and target graphs, making fixed same-resolution alignment suboptimal. Proposes routing knowledge across propagation resolutions to reduce negative transfer.

entry.title: Simulation Code Generation for Fluid Systems using Large Language Models: Benchmarking Models and Prompting Strategies

author.name: Jan Marius St\"urmer and Jascha Knack and Tobias Koch and Andreas Weinmann

entry.summary: Benchmarks ten LLMs and six prompting strategies on translating neutral graph descriptions of fluid systems into executable simulation code for a water-network Python library and Modelica. Assesses both software-quality metrics and whether the generated models reproduce benchmark physical scenarios.

entry.title: OSEF: One-Step Evidence Fusion for Cross-Video Scene Procedure Planning

author.name: Zhentong Ye, Lei Zhang, Sijia Zhou, Yingda Yu, Yuehan Shi, Jiaqi Xuan, Shuaiwu Dong, Guanchao Tong, Meimei Zhang, Bin Li

entry.summary: Introduces Cross-Video Scene Procedure Planning, a harder variant of video procedure planning where the model must first retrieve the right video and localize the window before predicting actions. Ships an eleven-source benchmark with typed negative distractors and an answer-leakage gate, evaluating nine planner families.

entry.title: STAGE: STyle-controllable Action GEneration for personalized autonomous driving

author.name: Zihao Liu, Xing Liu, Yizhai Zhang, Panfeng Huang

entry.summary: STAGE learns style-controllable driving action generation via imitation learning with style and latent action modality encodings, then uses preference learning to map a user onto a continuous monotonic aggressiveness value. The goal is autonomous driving behavior that matches an individual user's habits with low human annotation cost.

entry.title: DynoDINO: Harnessing Dynamic Latent Information from DINO Features for Multi-Phase Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Yu-Pu Hsu, Jen-Jee Chen, Yu-Chee Tseng

entry.summary: DynoDINO uses DINO features with dynamic latent modeling to segment lesions across multi-phase contrast-enhanced CT, where diagnostic contrast kinetics span phases that are often misaligned or incomplete. It replaces per-phase independent processing or naive fusion with explicit temporal reasoning.

entry.title: A Human-Centered Validation of the Explainability-Performance Coefficient

author.name: Christian Oliva and Luis F. Lago-Fern\'andez

entry.summary: Extends the Explainability-Performance Coefficient into a model-agnostic score quantifying explanation quality by trading off feature-selection sparsity against retained model performance, validated across tabular, text, and image data. Adds a human-centered validation of whether the metric tracks human understanding.

entry.title: Balancing of Humanoid with Object Mass: Trade-off Analyses and Lifting Control

author.name: Hyunjong Song, William Z. Peng, and Joo H. Kim

entry.summary: Analyzes how carrying an object changes humanoid balance stability by formulating object mass in whole-body dynamics with distributed contact wrenches and centers of pressure, then quantifying its nonlinear effects on momenta and constraints. Uses the resulting balanced state basin to design lifting control rather than relying on heuristics or learned policies.

entry.title: Freeze, Then Select: Structured Field Adapters and Stability-Validated Weak Selection for PDE Discovery from Sparse Observations

author.name: Juncheng Zhong, Chenghuang Shen, Jianfeng Liu, Zhengdong Xiao, Longjiu Luo, Qianrong Wang, Wenjun Xu, Wenlian Lu

entry.summary: The authors analyze why neural PDE discovery from sparse data often loses the correct set of differential terms during joint optimization, then propose a two-stage remedy: fit a structured spline-based field surrogate first, freeze it, and then select equation terms using stability across independent weak-form systems. The decoupling makes term selection more reliable than end-to-end residual training.

entry.title: The Debiased Score Test: Hunt-and-test for Semiparametric Hypotheses

author.name: Aditya Dhawan, F.Richard Guo, Rajen D. Shah

entry.summary: This paper generalizes the parametric score test to semiparametric settings where the target is a regression function defined as a risk minimizer, testing whether it lies in a given linear function class. A sample-splitting hunt-and-test procedure uses machine learning on one half to find a promising score direction and tests it on the other half, giving goodness-of-fit tests and detection of effect modifiers.

entry.title: Longitudinal Adaptive Experimental Design for Learning Multiple Target Estimands with Semiparametric Efficient Inference

author.name: Wenxin Zhang, Mark van der Laan

entry.summary: The paper develops a semiparametric efficiency framework for adaptive experimental design in longitudinal settings with multi-stage, time-varying treatments, and proposes design criteria that can target a single estimand or jointly optimize several. A key finding is that optimal randomization at earlier stages depends on later-stage decisions, and the authors provide inference that remains valid under adaptive data collection.

entry.title: The Art of Shipping Slopware

author.name: lsusr

entry.summary: A practitioner essay arguing that internal AI-usage leaderboards at large tech companies create perverse incentives to burn tokens, and that firms have mostly bought coding assistants without changing engineering practice. The author sketches top-down workflows tailored to current assistant models, noting that best practices shift with each model generation.

entry.title: LLM Framework for Discovering Major Mathematical Conjectures: AI's Quest for the Next Riemann Hypothesis

author.name: Alizer Wong, Zixin Zeng, Yi Tan, Wenyuan Li, Xuhang Chen, Xingru Lai, Yang Shi, Liangsi Lu and Yanhui Chen

entry.summary: COSI-Lab releases a multi-sensor dataset of 32 academics in ecologically valid conference mingling sessions, annotated for apparent intent by multiple external observers. The framing treats annotator disagreement as meaningful perspective diversity to be modeled rather than noise to be averaged away.

entry.title: Why It Hurts: Identifying the Drivers of Negative Thoughts in Emotional Support Conversations

author.name: Hainiu Xu, Zhaoyue Sun, Hanqi Yan, Jinhua Du, Caroline Catmur, Yulan He

entry.summary: Introduces AppraiSal, a benchmark of 996 emotional support conversations annotated for which cognitive appraisal dimensions are actually salient, and tests whether LLMs can identify salient dimensions instead of exhaustively scoring all of them. The motivation is that current reframing frameworks ignore context-dependent saliency.

entry.title: The Checking Problem: What must be true before AI ships in a regulated firm

author.name: Prerit Ahuja

entry.summary: Runs six document-heavy financial workflows across four model families and three tool setups, scoring 5,093 output elements against both a demonstration bar (one correct run) and a stricter production bar demanding reproducibility, attribution, and calibrated confidence. Only about 56 percent of configurations clear the production bar, and the paper quantifies the resulting human review burden.

entry.title: Guarantees on Dynamical System Distinguishability for LLM Token Generation

author.name: Mohamed Akrout, Dan Wilson

entry.summary: Provides theory for the practice of classifying LLM outputs by treating token embedding trajectories as black-box dynamical systems, formalizing it as a hypothesis test between two stochastic linear systems. It shows total variation distance between stationary distributions can be tiny even when dynamics differ, implying an accuracy floor, and analyzes scaling with sequence length and transfer across embedding models.

entry.title: SynCoTrain: A Dual Classifier PU-learning Framework for Synthesizability Prediction

author.name: Sasan Amariamir, Janine George, Philipp Benner

entry.summary: SynCoTrain tackles prediction of whether a hypothetical crystal can actually be synthesized, framing it as positive-unlabeled learning because failed syntheses are rarely published. It co-trains two different graph neural network classifiers so each supplies pseudo-labels to the other, reducing model bias in a data-scarce regime.

entry.title: To Facilitate or not to Facilitate: Human and LLM Facilitator Tendencies in Online Discussions

author.name: Dimitris Tsirmpas, Katerina Korre, John Pavlopoulos

entry.summary: Investigates when, rather than how, to intervene in online discussions by building a unified corpus of facilitation datasets, surveying expert facilitators on timing, and comparing those judgments with LLM decisions. It finds systematic differences between human and model intervention tendencies.

entry.title: Fracture Risk Prediction in Adults Over 50 Years Old Using DXA and EHR: Comparison of Traditional and Machine Learning Models in Two Large Cohorts

author.name: Jiahe Qian, Hao Dai, Kunyu Yu, Hexin Dong, Xing He, Erik A. Imel, Jiang Bian, Yifan Peng, Yi Liu

entry.summary: Develops and externally validates time-to-event fracture risk models for adults over 50 using electronic health record features and DXA-derived T-scores from two large US health systems, comparing traditional clinical tools with machine learning. External validation across separate networks strengthens the generalizability claim.

entry.title: MPP-GNN: Subject-Adaptive Community Detection for fMRI-Based Alzheimer's Disease Classification

author.name: Yang Zhang, Xiao Zhou, Jonathan Warrell, Avram Holmes, Xuan Zhang, and Mark Gerstein

entry.summary: MPP-GNN classifies Alzheimer's disease from functional MRI connectivity by learning subject-specific brain module partitions through a bilevel probabilistic pooling formulation rather than assuming a fixed number of modules for all subjects. The discovered modules then guide the learned connectivity representation.

entry.title: Library Reachability in LSR-Synth: How Anti-Memorization Design Changes the Measurement of Symbolic Discovery

author.name: Zhan'ao Yao, Liang Yin, Zhihao Gao, Boxuan Zhang, Xiaoyu Wu, Linjing Li, Rongyan Wang, Tingwei Chen, Youwei Wang, Xiaolin Zhao, Jiahui Shi, Jianjun Liu

entry.summary: Interrogates whether the anti-memorization design of the LSR-Synth equation discovery benchmark actually separates LLM scientific priors from plain symbolic search, by constructing a semantics-free baseline with a fixed, publicly documented operator vocabulary. The result is a measurement critique of how symbolic discovery progress is claimed.

entry.title: RAID: Towards Robust AI-Generated Image Detection with Bit-Reversed Images

author.name: Renxi Cheng, Jie Gui, Hongsong Wang

entry.summary: Detects AI-generated images by transforming inputs into bit-reversed representations that amplify low-order bit-plane statistics differing between real and synthetic images, then applies gradient-based patch selection and a small classifier. A theoretical argument is offered for why bit-plane structure separates the two classes.

entry.title: Few-shot Deep Learning for Phase-Amplitude Aberration Correction in Transcranial Focused Ultrasound

author.name: Minju Seol, Minjee Seo, Seonaeng Cho, and Kyungho Yoon

entry.summary: Proposes a few-shot deep surrogate that predicts per-element phase and amplitude corrections for a 96-element transcranial ultrasound array directly from patient CT scans, replacing expensive full-wave time-reversal simulation. Aims to make patient-specific aberration correction fast enough for real-time treatment planning.

entry.title: Small Is Enough: Per-User Style Rewriting of AI-Edited Text via LoRA Adapters

author.name: Antorweep Chakravorty

entry.summary: Builds a privacy-first single-user system that fine-tunes LoRA adapters on locally generated paired data so small models can rewrite AI-edited text back into the user's own style without inference-time prompting. Finds the composite quality score plateaus around 0.69 across model sizes from 0.5B to 7B, suggesting small models suffice for this task.

entry.title: Assessing the Generalization of Graph Neural Networks for Fault Location Across Increasing Distributed Energy Resource Penetration Levels

author.name: Burak Karabulut, Olayiwola Arowolo, Carlo Manna, Chris Develder, Jochen L. Cremer

entry.summary: Benchmarks spatio-temporal graph attention networks against purely temporal, purely spatial, and classical baselines for fault location in power distribution networks, and tests generalization as distributed energy resource penetration rises to 50 percent. Shows how changing fault signatures from bidirectional flows affect learned models.

entry.title: TFGformer: Multivariate Time Series Forecasting via Time-Frequency Graph Learning and Covariate Fusion

author.name: Yu Sun and Yuan Chang and Xiaohou Shi and Yan Sun

entry.summary: Presents a retrieval-augmented multivariate time-series forecasting framework combining shape-aware memory with RevIN normalization for magnitude-robust retrieval plus a future-consistency contrastive objective. Targets heterogeneous IoT sensor data where foundation models lack dynamic access to external historical patterns.

entry.title: Ordered-to-disordered transfer learning with graph neural networks for formation-energy and HOMO-LUMO gap prediction in high-entropy perovskite oxides

author.name: Panupol Untarabut, Narjes Jomaa, Sylvian Cadars, Olivier Masson, Samuel Bernard, Assil Bouzid and Santanu Saha

entry.summary: Evaluates ordered-to-disordered transfer learning with four graph neural network families (CGCNN, GATGNN, ALIGNN, M3GNet) for predicting formation energy and HOMO-LUMO gaps in high-entropy perovskite oxides. Tests how two-body versus three-body structural representations affect transfer from ordered training data to disordered targets.

entry.title: Concept Extraction for Time Series with ECLAD-ts

author.name: Antonia Holzapfel, Andres Felipe Posada-Moreno, Sebastian Trimpe

entry.summary: Extends concept-extraction explainability, previously developed for images, to convolutional time-series classifiers, producing human-inspectable concepts plus localization of where in the series they fire. The goal is to expose shortcut learning and spurious features in models used for medical and industrial monitoring.

entry.title: Miles: Metric Learning with Expandable Subspace for Pre-Trained Model-Based Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Kai Jiang, Zisong Lin, Hongyuan Zhang, Xueru Bai and Xuelong Li

entry.summary: Miles addresses class-incremental learning on top of pre-trained backbones by expanding a metric-learning subspace in a guided way, seeking a middle ground between shared-parameter methods that forget and per-task branches that inflate compute. It decouples representation adaptation from classifier growth.

entry.title: Empowering Cross-Domain Sequential Recommendation with Hybrid Tokenization and Serial-Parallel Decoding

author.name: Yuxuan Hu, Yuhao Wang, Tianbo Huang, Chao Zhang, Ziwei Liu, Lihua Zhang and Xiangyu Zhao

entry.summary: GenCDSR improves generative cross-domain sequential recommendation with a hybrid tokenization scheme that injects cross-domain collaborative signals into semantic identifiers and a serial-parallel decoder that avoids slow beam search. The focus is both accuracy and real-time serving feasibility.

entry.title: Mitigating Class-Tail Undercoverage in Medical Vision-Language Models under Clinical Shift

author.name: Mushir Akhtar, M. Tanveer

entry.summary: Proposes CALCoDe, a post-hoc conformal prediction layer for frozen medical vision-language models that detects which disease classes are at risk of coverage failure after distribution shift and sets class-conditional thresholds with deferral. The point is that overall coverage can look fine while a single clinically important class is badly under-covered.

entry.title: TAGTorch: A PyTorch Library for Geometry, Topology, and Symmetry-Aware Machine Learning

author.name: Brendan Kennedy, Tegan Emerson, Gregory Roek, Emilie Purvine, Henry Kvinge

entry.summary: Introduces a PyTorch library unifying topology-, algebra-, and geometry-inspired machine learning tools, including preprocessing, architectures, training methods, and analysis utilities that previously existed only as scattered research prototypes. Aims to reduce fragmentation in the geometric and topological deep learning ecosystem.

entry.title: Rolling With Resistance: Preference-Optimized LLM Counselors Can Trade Goal Persistence for Relational Attunement in Motivational Interviewing

author.name: Weiying Chen, Junlong Shen, Zhexuan Tang

entry.summary: Studies whether preference optimization can teach LLM counselors to roll with client resistance in motivational interviewing, using a two-axis framework of goal persistence and relational attunement derived from a clinical integrity code. Finds that penalizing one failure mode through DPO on the AnnoMI corpus tends to push models toward the opposite failure rather than the desired balanced behavior.

entry.title: When Unlearning Fails: Reliable Data Deletion under Post-Training in Agent Networks

author.name: Zihao Ding, Jun Huang, Liang Dong

entry.summary: Shows that in self-improving federated agent networks, deleting requested data is insufficient because the data has already shaped later self-collected trajectories, producing an influence echo that survives retraining and grows with the amount of affected retained data. Proposes MUTE, which uses deployment, collection, and aggregation records to mute those echoes for reliable deletion.

entry.title: Conditioning Tree-Based Diffusions and Flows for Probabilistic Tabular Regression

author.name: Silas Koemen

entry.summary: Argues that tree-based diffusion models for tabular regression inherit inappropriate defaults from neural diffusion, and introduces DiffGBM with a Gaussian-path flow-matching trainer that learns a velocity field directly and permits few-step deterministic ODE sampling. It also lays out an explicit score-side recipe covering residualization, preconditioning, and time sampling.

entry.title: Open-Source LLM-Driven Formal Verification: A Multi-Agent Pipeline for RTL Repair

author.name: Ha Trung Tran

entry.summary: Builds a fully open-source multi-agent pipeline that couples an LLM with Yosys, SymbiYosys, and Z3 to repair RTL through counterexample-guided iteration, generating formal properties and feeding counterexamples back until the design verifies. Aims to replace simulation-based validation and expensive commercial formal tools.

entry.title: Latent Lie-Poisson Neural Networks (LLPNNs): Discovering the motion of Lie-Poisson systems through observable data and latent dynamics

author.name: Vakhtang Putkaradze

entry.summary: Proposes structure-preserving networks that learn Lie-Poisson dynamics from observable configuration and velocity data when the momentum variables driving the dynamics are unobservable. Handles optimal-control cases with latent co-states and degenerate Hamiltonians where standard encoder-decoder Lagrangian approaches break down.

entry.title: VFAD: Variational Semantic Prompting Meets Frequency-Adaptive Representation Learning for Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection

author.name: Peng Chen, Kaige Li, Wei Wang, Mingbo Yang, Wenqiang Wang, Li Shen, Fangjun Huang, Chao Huang

entry.summary: Combines a variational semantic prompt extractor that aggregates anomaly-relevant local semantics from dense patch tokens with frequency-adaptive representation learning for zero-shot anomaly detection on unseen categories. Uses a variational information bottleneck to regularize the learned prompts.

entry.title: Multi-Source Multi-View Graph Domain Adaptation with Hyperbolic Residual Encoding for Cross-Site MDD Identification from rs-fMRI

author.name: Zhanpeng Zheng, Xiran Chen, Haiteng Jiang, Renjie Tian, Qinyu Cai, Jiexi Liu, Xiaofeng Chen, Weikai Li, Yansu Wang

entry.summary: Tackles cross-site depression classification from resting-state fMRI by jointly modeling multiple functional connectivity views (Pearson, sparse representation, Granger causality) under multi-source unsupervised domain adaptation with hyperbolic residual encoding. Argues prior work treats multi-view connectome learning and site adaptation separately.

entry.title: Differentially Private Nonparametric Modal Learning with Applications to Regression and Clustering

author.name: Arkajyoti Bhattacharjee and Arnab Auddy

entry.summary: DP-GRAMS performs differentially private estimation of density modes via noisy mean-shift style ascent on a privatized score estimator, using higher-order kernels to reduce bias plus gradient clipping and calibrated Gaussian noise. The authors derive rates under Holder smoothness, curvature and separation conditions and extend the method to private modal regression and clustering.

entry.title: Toward Robust and 3D-Aware RGB-NIR Imaging in the Dark

author.name: Muyao Niu, Mingze Ma, Yifan Zhan, Qingtian Zhu, Zhihang Zhong, Wei Guo, Chang Wen Chen, Yinqiang Zheng

entry.summary: The paper fuses extremely noisy RGB captures with near-infrared cues inside a 3D-aware neural scene representation, recovering clean images without requiring clean RGB supervision or curated paired training data. Experiments on synthetic and real captures show better robustness across noise levels than prior RGB-NIR fusion methods.

entry.title: Distance Profile Embedding for Independence and Conditional Independence Testing of Random Objects

author.name: Wenxi Tan, Bing Li and Lingzhou Xue

entry.summary: The authors introduce an embedding that maps random objects in general metric spaces to square-integrable functions via their distance profiles, proving injectivity and full preservation of distributional information without needing isometric Hilbert embeddings. On top of it they build unified marginal and conditional independence tests with asymptotic size and power guarantees.

entry.title: Industrializing a small field: Lessons from Vannevar

author.name: dan.parshall

entry.summary: An essay drawing on Vannevar Bush and the wartime organization of American science to argue that AI safety must shift from a community model to an industry model, with push-side mechanisms such as research bounties replacing mentor-limited fellowship pipelines. It links to related analyses of the field's capacity bottleneck and compute-verification work.

entry.title: The Formalism Trap: Are LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluators Blinded by Consensus Mimicry under Social Load?

author.name: Dahlia Shehata, Ming Li

entry.summary: Claims that LLM judges reward procedural, formal-looking agent trajectories over substantively correct ones under adversarial load, introducing a dissonance index and analyzing 22,500 trajectories across GAIA, SWE-bench, and Multi-Challenge. It reports that the vulnerability transfers across domains and varies by multi-agent topology.

entry.title: MBDiff: Multi-view Behavior-aware Diffusion Model for Probabilistic Utility Data Imputation

author.name: Rongchao Xu, Lin Jiang, Dahai Yu, Ximiao Li, Guang Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-view behavior-aware diffusion model for probabilistic imputation of missing electricity, water, and gas meter readings, using individual user behavior patterns rather than only aggregated series. Missing utility data degrades billing accuracy, demand forecasting, and supply management.

entry.title: Locally Consistent Transductive Information Maximization for Few-Shot Remote Sensing Scene Classification

author.name: Karim El Khoury, Beno\^it G\'erin, Beno\^it Macq, Christophe De Vleeschouwer

entry.summary: Adds a local consistency regularizer to a state-of-the-art transductive information-maximization objective for few-shot CLIP classification, enforcing agreement between each unlabeled query and its nearest neighbors in feature space. Applied to remote sensing scene classification where batch patch inference naturally suits transductive inference.

entry.title: Linear Proposal Operators and Stochastic Search Geometry in SOMA and Differential Evolution

author.name: Vojt\v{e}ch Nov\'ak, Ivan Zelinka

entry.summary: Factorizes swarm and evolutionary algorithms into objective-independent variation, boundary repair, and fitness-dependent selection, then shows the canonical migrating-algorithm proposal is affine in search space and exactly linear in an augmented state. Uses this to interpret interpolation, projection, overshoot, and coordinate masking geometry in relation to differential evolution.

entry.title: DualDiT: A Conditional Dual-Output Diffusion Transformer for Joint OCT Image and Segmentation Mask Generation

author.name: Fernando Garc\'ia-Torres, Roc\'io del Amor, Sandra Morales, \'Alvaro Barroso, Peter Heiduschka, Bj\"orn Kemper, Valery Naranjo

entry.summary: Proposes a conditional diffusion transformer that jointly generates optical coherence tomography B-scans of mouse retina and their matching retinal-layer segmentation masks in a shared latent space. Addresses annotation scarcity where manual delineation of tiny retinal structures is labour-intensive.

entry.title: Cross-Lingual Transfer for Machine Translation in Turkic Languages

author.name: Omer Burak Cinar, Mehmet Mert Dalkilic, Cagri Toraman

entry.summary: Maps pairwise cross-lingual transfer among five Turkic languages using fine-tuned multilingual sequence-to-sequence models, finding the strongest transfer between the closest pairs and clear asymmetry in transfer direction. Also shows that Latinizing scripts improves standard translation metrics.

entry.title: Unanticipated Effects of Generative AI on Expertise Pathways and Performance Perception in System Administration

author.name: Rana Abou Khamis, Hala Assal, Ashraf Matrawy

entry.summary: Interview study with 14 IT professionals finds that generative AI both tutors and shortcuts the traditional ladder of system administration expertise, compressing how practitioners build deep troubleshooting skill. It surfaces unintended socio-technical effects on skill formation and self-assessed performance.

entry.title: TELLER: Dual-Path Iterative Preference Optimization for Table Entity Linking

author.name: Yixin Peng, Kehao Li, and Stefan Decker

entry.summary: TELLER improves linking of ambiguous table cell mentions to knowledge base entities using dual-path iterative preference optimization that regenerates preference data from the evolving model errors and controls for reasoning-length bias. This replaces static preference datasets used by prior instruction-tuned linkers.

entry.title: Physics-Aligned Self-Supervised Learning for Scientific Imaging

author.name: Bashir Kazimi and Stefan Sandfeld

entry.summary: Argues that self-supervised augmentation pipelines borrowed from natural images can encode invariances that contradict the physics of scientific imaging modalities, degrading representations. Formalizes a physics-aligned augmentation set as the union of measurement-consistent symmetries and acquisition-driven transformations, giving practitioners a reproducible design procedure.

entry.title: Identifying Informative Environments for Cognition Parameter Inference via Bayesian Experimental Design

author.name: Manisha Dubey, Rimvydas Rubavicius, N. Siddharth, Subramanian Ramamoorthy

entry.summary: Frames the choice of cognitive experiment environment as a Bayesian experimental design problem for inferring latent cognition parameters via inverse planning, establishing an exact Monte Carlo benchmark and an amortized design framework. Experiments use the Mouselab-MDP planning paradigm.

entry.title: Don't Contrast the Impossible: Region-Constrained Batching for Contrastive User Modeling on a Local Community Platform

author.name: Seungho Han, Byeongchang Kim, Jin Yu

entry.summary: Points out that in-batch negatives in contrastive recommender training include geographically impossible user-item pairs on a local marketplace, diluting the learning signal. Region-constrained batch sampling builds region-homogeneous mini-batches so negatives are feasible and therefore harder and more informative.

entry.title: Domain-Division based Progressive Learning for Source-Free Domain Adaptation

author.name: Pan Liu, Jing Li, Meng Zhao, Wanli Xue, Qinghua Hu, Shengyong Chen

entry.summary: Proposes a source-free domain adaptation method that repeatedly splits the unlabeled target domain into easy and hard subdomains by adaptation difficulty, then assigns neighborhood-based pseudo labels and progressively expands training to harder samples. Motivated by the observation that clean samples are learned faster than noisy ones.

entry.title: TAVI-TEC: An AI-Based Tool for Procedural Planning of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation

author.name: Alessandra Zerillo, Stefano Cannata, Diego Bellavia, Daniele Ciriello, Simone Manini, Salvatore Pasta, Caterina Gandolfo

entry.summary: Presents an automated pipeline integrated into a web DICOM viewer that segments cardiovascular structures, detects calcification, extracts centerlines, and defines the annular plane on CT angiography for transcatheter aortic valve planning. Aims to standardize annotations and speed up preprocedural workflow as procedure volumes grow.

entry.title: SatEdit: Mask-Conditioned Image Editing via VLM-Guided Segment Annotation

author.name: Muhammad Talha, Muhammad Ahmed Amer

entry.summary: Builds a mask-conditioned satellite image editing dataset and model by having a segmentation foundation model propose masks, a vision-language model assign labels, and light human verification confirm them before generating paired addition and removal edits via inpainting. Fine-tunes an editing backbone with LoRA on about a thousand images.

entry.title: Explore Beyond the Boundary Using Entropic Information

author.name: Bumgeun Park and Donghwan Lee

entry.summary: ENTINEX is an intrinsic-reward exploration method for sparse and delayed reward RL that uses entropic information to identify the boundary of the visited state distribution and rewards agents for pushing past it. Experiments show consistent exploration gains in sparse-reward environments.

entry.title: Bayesian fusion forests for heterogeneous treatment effects on survival from randomised and real-world data

author.name: Tijn Jacobs, St\'ephanie L. van der Pas, Wessel N. van Wieringen

entry.summary: Bayesian fusion forests estimate heterogeneous treatment effects on survival outcomes by combining randomized trial data with observational real-world data, replacing unconfoundedness with an assumption that the treatment effect transports between sources. An accelerated failure time decomposition assigns tree-ensemble priors to shared prognosis, source deviation, treatment effect and a confounding function, and supports right- and interval-censored outcomes.

entry.title: Distilling Knowledge from Large Language Models into Lightweight Reinforcement Learning Agents for Autonomous Cyber Operations

author.name: Konur Tholl, Fran\c{c}ois Rivest, Mariam El Mezouar, Adrian Taylor, and Ranwa Al Mallah

entry.summary: Shows that an 8-billion-parameter LLM pretrained on cybersecurity data can, through prompt engineering alone, outperform a baseline reinforcement learning agent in an autonomous cyber defense environment, and explores distilling its knowledge into lightweight RL agents. Motivated by the instability and poor early decisions of RL agents during exploration.

entry.title: FocusGS: Spatial Delta Layers for Local Repair and Deterministic Editing of Trained 3D Gaussian Assets

author.name: Yiqun Pan, Yukun Shi

entry.summary: Proposes treating repairs and edits of trained 3D Gaussian Splatting assets as composite spatial delta layers, with additive local bases for repair and an erase-insert factorization for deterministic edits. Reports a large local PSNR improvement on target regions and addresses spatial gradient starvation during local optimization.

entry.title: Human-LLM Collaborative Inductive Coding for Conceptualizing K-12 Educator AI Use

author.name: Alex Liu, Min Sun, Lief Esbenshade, Michael Xiao, Victor Tian, Zachary Zhang, Kevin He

entry.summary: Documents a multi-phase human-LLM pipeline that adapts open, axial, and selective coding to build a hierarchical codebook from 45,000 messages between K-12 educators and a generative AI platform. Humans retain authority over category definitions and merges while LLMs generate candidate labels and structured annotations at scale.

entry.title: Visual Distribution Anchoring for Efficient Prompt Tuning

author.name: Pouya Parsa, Raoof Zare Moayedi, Seongjin Choi

entry.summary: Proposes VDA, a training-free way to adapt vision-language classifiers to a new target domain by estimating class-level visual prototypes from an unlabeled target pool, rather than tuning textual or image-conditioned prompts. The authors show that prototypes cannot be synthesized from class names alone because names encode semantics, not target-domain appearance.

entry.title: Multi-Modal Object Re-Identification with Dual Semantic Guidance and Global-Local Mutual Modulation

author.name: Weixiang Zhou, Xingguo Xu, Yuhao Wang, Cong Wang, Yang Yang, Zhixun Su, Jinshan Pan

entry.summary: Improves multi-modal object re-identification with text-semantic injection, a masked global-local modulator, and a hierarchical mixture-of-experts fusion module to counter background clutter and cross-modal misalignment. Focuses on exploiting synergy between global and local features rather than holistic descriptors only.

entry.title: The Theoretical Foundation of Socratic Tests: Dynamic, Multimodal, Conversational Examinations

author.name: Ilya Mikhelson

entry.summary: Lays out a theoretical foundation for automated conversational examinations that combine dynamic assessment, multimodal workspaces, Bloom's taxonomy for real-time proctoring, and the SOLO taxonomy for structural evaluation. Formalizes graduated scaffolding to quantify a learner's zone of proximal development instead of subtractive grading.

entry.title: GQ-FSL: Green Quantized Federated Split Learning

author.name: Idan Roth and Lutz Lampe

entry.summary: GQ-FSL adds stochastic quantization to federated split learning, allowing client and server submodels to run at different numerical precisions so that device energy limits do not directly degrade global convergence. The framework targets deep model training on energy-constrained wireless edge devices.

entry.title: ArchiveGPT: A human-centered evaluation of using a vision language model for image cataloguing

author.name: Line Abele, Gerrit Anders, Tolgahan Ayd{\i}n, J\"urgen Buder, Helen Fischer, Dominik Kimmel, Markus Huff

entry.summary: A human-centered study asking whether a vision-language model can produce archival catalogue descriptions of historical photographs that experts accept, with participants trying to distinguish AI from expert text and rating quality and trust. It reports that raters detect AI text above chance but still show conditional willingness to adopt such tools in cataloguing workflows.

entry.title: Geographically Weighted Surrogate Models for Rapid Small-Area Chronic Disease Estimation

author.name: Aanya Gupta and Szandra P\'eter and Sara Von Hoene and Emma Von Hoene and Taylor Anderson

entry.summary: Evaluates global and geographically weighted machine learning models as surrogates for survey-based small-area estimation of ten chronic conditions, aiming to fill the roughly two-year lag in gold-standard CDC PLACES releases. The goal is timely county-level health estimates from frequently updated predictors.

entry.title: Leveraging Transfer Learning with Class-Specific Decoders for Laparoscopic Segmentation

author.name: Priya Tomar, Aditya Parikh, Christian Bauckhage, Rafet Sifa

entry.summary: Extends class-specific decoder architectures for laparoscopic multi-organ segmentation to cross-surgical transfer, using rectal and cholecystectomy datasets to study how anatomical knowledge transfers between surgical domains under class imbalance. Compares feature adaptation strategies for small, rarely exposed structures.

entry.title: Regional Attention-Enhanced Swin Transformer for Clinically Relevant Medical Image Captioning

author.name: Zubia Naz, Farhan Asghar, Muhammad Ishfaq Hussain, Yahya Hadadi, Muhammad Aasim Rafique, Wookjin Choi and Moongu Jeon

entry.summary: Automated medical image captioning translates complex radiological images into diagnostic narratives that can support reporting workflows. We present a Swin-BART encoder-decoder system with a lightwei...

entry.title: Can LLMs Really Understand Item Difficulty Levels? Implications for Automated Item Generation Using LLMs

author.name: Xinyi Wang, Hong Jiao, Ming Li, Sydney Peters, Hanna Choi, Tianyi Zhou, Qingshu Xu

entry.summary: Tests whether LLMs can predict the empirical difficulty of standardized reading and writing test items across prompting strategies and temperatures, comparing against encoder models and feature-based baselines. The best zero-shot GPT-4.1 setting reaches quadratic weighted kappa of about 0.578, below a fine-tuned ConvBERT at 0.625.

entry.title: COSI-Lab: Conference Living Lab for Modeling Multi-Perspective Multimodal Social Intention

author.name: Zonghuan Li, Litian Li, Arthur Mercier, Gara Dorta, Balint Dioszegi, Jose Morales-Vargas, Chenxu Hao, Ivan Kondyurin, Vanessa Begemann, Nale Lehmann-Willenbrock, Bernd Dudzik, Saunaq Chakrabarty, Sotiris Vacanas, Laura Cabrera-Quir\'os, Anne L.J. ter Wal, Vitaliy Popov, Jorge Castro-God\'inez, Chirag Raman, Stephanie Tan, Hayley Hung

entry.summary: COSI-Lab presents a multimodal, multi-sensor dataset of an interdisciplinary scientific workshop containing 32 academics at an international conference. It captures ecologically valid social interacti...

entry.title: Accelerated Random-Sweep Gibbs Sampling for Gaussian Graphical Models via Dual Normal Factor Graphs

author.name: Borna Khodabandeh and Mehdi Molkaraie

entry.summary: Analyzes convergence of random-sweep Gibbs sampling for Gaussian graphical models with a thin-membrane prior and shows that sampling in a Fourier-dual normal factor graph converges much faster. For cyclic homogeneous graphs the dual convergence rate is topology-independent and governed by algebraic connectivity.

entry.title: MMFGU: Multimodal Federated Graph Unlearning

author.name: Haodong Lu, Zekai Chen, Weiwei Ji, Shihao Li, Xunkai Li, Xun Wu, Yinlin Zhu, Rong-Hua Li

entry.summary: Defines and addresses fine-grained unlearning requests in multimodal federated graph learning, such as deleting a single image or revoking a learned cross-modal correspondence while keeping the underlying entity. Proposes a framework targeting selective removal, resistance to recovery from remaining modalities, and preserved utility.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Deepfake Detection via Multi-View Structural Learning

author.name: Muhammad Umar Farooq, Kutub Uddin, Awais Khan and Khalid Malik

entry.summary: Proposes a deepfake detector that fuses an adapted CLIP visual stream, a facial-attribute consistency stream, and a structural dependency stream, with explicit uncertainty estimation to avoid overconfidence on out-of-distribution manipulations. Motivated by forensic deployments needing calibrated confidence under shift.

entry.title: Benchmarks Are Not Validation: A System-Level View of Financial LLM Applications

author.name: Burak Payzun, \.Irem Demirta\c{s}, Simona Scala, Elena Ferretti, Se\c{c}il Arslan

entry.summary: A position paper from financial industry practitioners arguing that benchmark scores are inadequate evidence for approving LLM systems in production, and outlining a multi-layer validation approach covering data, model design, retrieval and generation, agent behavior, governance, and implementation. Draws on experience validating generative AI applications inside financial institutions.

entry.title: FairDiffuseVQVAE: Sampling-Time Fairness in Tabular Diffusion via Conditional Refinement of Vector-Quantized Latents

author.name: Nitish Nagesh, Mahdi Bagheri, Amir M. Rahmani
