author.name: Wenshuai Yao, Wenyong Zhou, Hanyong Shao, Yizhe Chen, Zhiyuan Ning, Yuannuo Feng, Ru Huang, Kechao Tang

entry.summary: ReTopK accelerates dynamic top-K sparse attention by reusing historical retrieval decisions for similar queries, avoiding the need to score every query against the entire KV cache and thereby removing the selector's linear cost in context length. The method is training-free and preserves most of the exact top-K attention mass.

entry.title: Graph Neural Multilevel Preconditioners for Iterative Solvers

author.name: Zechen Zhang, Rui Peng Li, Yousef Saad

entry.summary: Proposes a graph neural multilevel preconditioner that imposes an algebraic multigrid hierarchy as structural prior while learning the smoothing, restriction, and interpolation operators, aiming at robustness on indefinite and nonsymmetric sparse systems where classical AMG heuristics degrade. It tests how much the AMG-style hierarchy actually helps learned preconditioning.

entry.title: Harness-G: A Graph-Structured Harness for Search Agents

author.name: Yanning Hou, Haoyuan Chen, Sihang Zhou, Xiaoshu Chen, Xirui Liu, Duanyang Yuan, Lingyuan Meng, Quan Liu, Jian Huang

entry.summary: Harness-G questions how retrieval is exposed to RL search agents, documenting retrieval-equivalence collapse in Search-R1 training where rollouts emit different query strings yet converge to overlapping evidence sets, flattening within-group returns. It replaces free-form query generation with a graph-structured retrieval harness at the policy-environment interface.

entry.title: Rethinking LLM-Judged Helpfulness as a Pedagogy Signal: A Pre-Registered Audit Across Tutor Models

author.name: Shuyi Fan, Boyuan Deng, Mengyu Xu, Jiale Liu, Hongyang Zhang, Qiaoxin Yang, Chongyang Gao

entry.summary: A pre-registered audit testing whether a general helpfulness rubric applied by an LLM judge can distinguish tutoring that guides a student from tutoring that simply gives away answers. Claude Opus 4.8 serves as the frozen primary judge with GPT-5.6 Sol as a pre-specified robustness auditor, over roughly 1,179 confirmatory tutor turns with deterministic answer-leakage detectors.

entry.title: DECODE: Tackling Representation and Decision Degradation in Continual AI-Generated Image Detection

author.name: Zihao Cai, Xinghan Li, Ruiyan Yang, Xue Song, Haijun Shan, Jingjing Chen

entry.summary: Shows that continual AI-generated image detection suffers not only from representation drift but also from decision-boundary drift in the classification head, and proposes DECODE to address both. Relevant as detectors must keep pace with a stream of new generative models.

entry.title: Unifying Adversarially Robust Model Experts in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Nguyen Duc Thai, Junhao Dong, Sua Qi Rong, Hua Yu, Yew-Soon Ong

entry.summary: Proposes CARE, a collaborative adversarial fine-tuning framework that trains multiple robust CLIP experts with embedding-alignment knowledge exchange and unifies them, so robustness generalizes across evaluation settings instead of specializing. Targets the deployment fragility of vision-language models under adversarial perturbation.

entry.title: ViewMind3D: Modular View-Aware Inference for Training-Free 3D-QA

author.name: Ping-Kun Chiang, Kun-Ru Wu, Po-han Li, Sandeep Chinchali, Ufuk Topcu, Yu-Chee Tseng

entry.summary: Presents a fully training-free modular framework for 3D question answering from multi-view images, decomposing the task into view selection, language-conditioned grounding, spatial context assembly, and answering without full 3D reconstruction. Avoids costly 3D-specific annotation and fine-tuning.

entry.title: Beyond Frame Selection: Generative Latent Evidence Aggregation for Long-Video Understanding

author.name: Bowen Liu, Shuning Wang, Xinpeng Ding, Zhiheng Wu, Bodong Du, Xiaomeng Li

entry.summary: Argues that selecting relevant frames is insufficient for long-video QA because complementary cues must still be integrated, and introduces a query-conditioned distribution-guided latent evidence aggregation stage between selection and generation. Formalizes a post-selection latent evidence interface.

entry.title: GuideSkill: Evolving Executable LLM Agent Skills for Guideline-Grounded Clinical Reasoning

author.name: Lang Cao, Yuhao Shen, Tianyang Luo, Simo Du, Hao Peng, Yue Guo

entry.summary: GuideSkill compiles clinical practice guideline criteria into executable scoring functions that an LLM consults when proposing a differential diagnosis, rather than merely retrieving guideline text. An evolutionary variant refines and expands the skill library from case-diagnosis pairs, improving macro accuracy across four benchmarks and four backbones.

entry.title: TraceCLIP: Recovering Local Semantics from Patch-to-CLS Contributions

author.name: Xinran Liu, Shouqian Shi, Yutong Chen, Ge Wang, Xin-Wei Yao, Sheng Zhong

entry.summary: TraceCLIP recovers local visual semantics by tracing how individual patch tokens contribute to the CLS representation, rather than reading patch features directly or adding external supervision. This training-free analysis supports dense tasks such as open-vocabulary segmentation and region recognition.

entry.title: Contextualized Counterspeech Can Be More Persuasive Than Generic Counterspeech

author.name: Lorenzo Cima, Alessio Miaschi, Amaury Trujillo, Marco Avenuti, Felice Dell'Orletta, Stefano Cresci

entry.summary: The authors generate counterspeech that is conditioned on conversational context and characteristics of the moderated user, comparing multiple configurations and fine-tuning strategies against generic one-size-fits-all counterspeech. Evaluation combines quantitative indicators with a pre-registered mixed-design crowdsourcing experiment on persuasiveness.

entry.title: AgentGUI: An Interface for Observing and Steering Long-Running AI Agents

author.name: Xuan Zhao, Jiwoong Sohn, Qinyue Zheng, Michael Moor

entry.summary: AgentGUI is a locally hosted interface for observing and steering multiple concurrent long-running agent sessions, offering trajectory visualization, manual and automated steering, and interoperability across open-source and frontier agent frameworks. A controlled user study reports users identify key trace elements about 38 percent faster.

entry.title: SARC-DQ: Runtime Data-Quality Gating for Agentic AI: Silent Evidence Defects, the Incompetence Shield, and Downstream-Only Remediation

author.name: Gaston Besanson

entry.summary: The paper shows that metadata-borne evidence defects such as stale prices or superseded records, which never enter the agent's visible context, are converted into costly wrong actions about sixty percent of the time on a priced replenishment benchmark. Behavioral doubt markers stay at chance and the failure rate is flat across four model tiers spanning roughly fifteen times in inference price, so capability does not buy skepticism.

entry.title: PUDA: An AI-Native Hardware Harness for Self-Driving Laboratories

author.name: Zekun Ren, Hongzhao Tan, Jiaen Yee, Kedar Hippalgaonkar

entry.summary: PUDA is a command-line, headless hardware harness for self-driving laboratories, exposing instruments as discoverable CLIs with JSON protocols and structured, auditable run records designed for LLM agents rather than human GUIs. It aims to make autonomous experimentation deterministic, atomic, and traceable.

entry.title: Efficient Heteroscedastic Bayesian Optimization for Risk-Aware AutoRL

author.name: Mingxuan Che, Tsung-Yuan Tseng, Theresa Eimer, Marius Lindauer, Alexander von Rohr

entry.summary: ERAHBO is a heteroscedastic Bayesian optimization method for automated RL that models both mean and variance of returns as functions of hyperparameters and uses adaptive re-sampling instead of a fixed budget per configuration. It seeks configurations with high average return and low run-to-run variability.

entry.title: BioVLN: A Simulation Platform for Visual Language Navigation in Biomedical Laboratories

author.name: Zhe Liu, Quan Lu, Zhaohui Du, Zhe Wang, Huanbo Jin, Jiaming Gu, Qi Wang, Ting Xiao, Minting Pan, Dongzhan Zhou

entry.summary: BioVLN is a simulation platform for vision-language navigation in biomedical laboratories that models each instrument with a physical body, a clearance region, and a front-side operation area, so agents must approach from the usable side with safe spacing. Existing embodied benchmarks assume household objects and arbitrary nearby goal positions, which is inadequate for lab robots.

entry.title: ECG-InterpBench: Benchmarking the Interpretability of ECG Foundation Models with Matched-Scale Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Yixuan Duan, Wei Qiu

entry.summary: ECG-InterpBench evaluates whether ECG foundation model representations can be faithfully decomposed and clinically interpreted, using capacity-matched sparse autoencoders as standardized probes across six models, five depths, five dictionary widths, and three seeds. The resulting 450-cell grid enables controlled interpretability comparisons rather than only downstream accuracy claims.

entry.title: LoRA Scaffolded Policy Optimization (LSPO): A Sampling-Time Low-Rank Scaffold for Recovering Reinforcement-Learning Gradient on Zero-Reward Cliff Prompts

author.name: Ken Ding

entry.summary: LSPO addresses the RLVR blind spot where all rollouts for a prompt fail, so group-normalized advantages are zero and no gradient flows on the hardest frontier prompts. It detects such cliff prompts, briefly fits a small LoRA adapter on their ground-truth solutions, re-rolls with the scaffolded model, and splices successful completions back with importance-sampling correction.

entry.title: It's All Just Vectorization: einx, a Universal Notation for Tensor Operations

author.name: Florian Fervers, Sebastian Bullinger, Christoph Bodensteiner, Michael Arens

entry.summary: einx proposes a universal notation for tensor operations built on vectorization as a first-class transform, generalizing einsum and einops so that a wide range of array operations can be expressed in one consistent, shape-safe syntax. The aim is to reduce shape bugs and unreadable code in numerical and deep learning programming.

entry.title: Beyond Geometric Complementarity: Coherent Overlap in Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Routing

author.name: Huiyuan Tian, Bonan Xu, Shijian Li

entry.summary: This analysis challenges the geometric-complementarity story for sparse MoE routing, showing across six architectures that co-selected expert subspaces overlap substantially yet actual routes still explain token representations better than matched alternatives. The authors introduce a subspace separation index and use frozen-route interventions and factorial designs to separate route coherence from candidate quality.

entry.title: LEDGERMIND: Provenance-Constrained Multimodal Agentic Reasoning with a Structured Evidence Ledger

author.name: Enjun Du, Hange Zhou, Chenxu Du, Siyi Liu, Zirong Chen, Ziyu Zheng, Yongqi Zhang

entry.summary: LEDGERMIND treats a multimodal agent trajectory as a provenance-constrained state machine, normalizing tool outputs into a structured evidence ledger that downstream reasoning must cite, with entity- and numeric-level grounding checks and typed repair transitions. It moves multimodal VQA evaluation beyond final-answer accuracy toward verifying that answers rest on real evidence.

entry.title: APO: Unsupervised Atomic Policy Optimization for 3D Structure Prediction of Atomic Systems

author.name: Shentong Mo, Yatao Bian

entry.summary: APO performs fully unsupervised alignment for 3D atomic structure prediction by adapting group-relative policy optimization with a dual-reward design, removing the dependence on ground-truth coordinates required by supervised preference methods like FlowDPO. This targets novel crystal phases and de novo proteins where experimental labels do not exist.

entry.title: Foundation-Model Earth Representations Enable Regional-Scale Forest Aboveground Biomass Monitoring Across the Northeastern United States

author.name: Shashika Lamahewage, Chandi Witharana

entry.summary: This study evaluates Google Satellite Embeddings from the AlphaEarth foundation model for estimating forest aboveground biomass across northeastern US temperate forests, fusing the embeddings with airborne LiDAR and field inventories. It tests whether general geospatial foundation representations can substitute for sparse ground and airborne measurements in regional carbon monitoring.

entry.title: WIDE: Boosting Adaptive LLM Inference via Token-level Dynamic Width Pruning

author.name: Haozhe Hu, Hao Wu, Peiran Yin, Chao Han, Yunpu Ma, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: WIDE is an end-to-end differentiable framework for token-level dynamic width pruning that adapts how much computation each token receives during both prefill and decode, rather than making coarse static structural cuts. The goal is to keep hardware-friendly throughput gains while avoiding the accuracy collapse of input-agnostic pruning at high sparsity.

entry.title: Belief Coevolution in a Social Network of Generalist and Specialist Large Language Models

author.name: Germans Savcisens, Samantha Dies, Courtney Maynard, Tina Eliassi-Rad

entry.summary: CoevolveSim runs 1,280 controlled simulations in which networked generalist and specialist LLM agents observe summaries of neighbors' beliefs and revise their own, across four scenarios, two network topologies, and twenty medical statements. It isolates the effects of domain specialization, assigned social role, and network structure on belief diffusion among model populations.

entry.title: A Sparse Glimpse of the Whole: Train-Free Self-Speculative Decoding

author.name: Yuesong Liu, Yuan Zeng, Min Lyu, Ruilin Liu, Yu Guo, Yinlong Xu

entry.summary: Provides a unified efficiency analysis showing that lengthening the speculation horizon can hurt speedup once marginal token acceptance drops below the relative drafting cost, then introduces SparseSpec-L, a training-free self-speculative decoder for long context. Drafts come from the target model itself using a dynamically sparsified and recallable KV cache, recycling per-head attention statistics from full-context verification.

entry.title: ChronoMem: Version Control and Semantic Rollback for Large Language Model Agent Memory

author.name: Yongye Su, Wujiang Xu, Chaoji Zuo, Elisa Bertino

entry.summary: ChronoMem adds a semantic version-control layer to agent memory, committing whole-memory snapshots at each write, maintaining structured version histories, and enabling inspection and rollback after corrections, concept drift, or memory corruption. It is implemented on top of Google's open-source Agent Development Kit.

entry.title: Where and When to Commit: Candidate-Aware Decoding for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Chia-Ming Lee, Ming-Ching Chang, Xin Li, Yu-Lun Liu, Chih-Chung Hsu

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free, candidate-aware early-exit framework for diffusion language models that decides when to stop denoising based on whether the actual output candidates have stabilized rather than on fixed confidence or schedule heuristics. It targets premature termination on long chain-of-thought generations.

entry.title: Using Large Language Models for Idea Generation in Innovation

author.name: Lennart Meincke, Karan Girotra, Gideon Nave, Christian Terwiesch, Karl T. Ulrich

entry.summary: Compares new product ideas from a pre-LLM student design course against GPT-4 zero-shot and few-shot pools, scoring quality with market-research purchase-intent prediction, similarity with text mining, and novelty with human raters. AI-generated ideas outperform human ideas on predicted purchase intent.

entry.title: VAD: Attributing Visual Evidence for Target Reconstruction in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Kangning Zhang, Yixing Li, Shuai Shao, Qingyao Li, Zhengxi Lu, Zhiyuan Yao, Jianghao Lin, Wenxiang Jiao, Yuan Lu, Weiwen Liu, Weinan Zhang, Yong Yu

entry.summary: VAD estimates which parts of a teacher's token-level corrections in multimodal on-policy distillation are actually attributable to visual evidence, by running the same teacher with the relevant evidence present and removed and comparing centered log-probability changes. Distillation is then weighted toward visually grounded corrections rather than linguistic priors or teacher idiosyncrasies.

entry.title: JigShape: Evaluating Visual-Geometric Reasoning in VLMs through Jigsaw Puzzles

author.name: Shawn Li, Wei Yang, Jike Zhong, Jiate Li, Jiawei Yang, You Qin, Ryan Rossi, Franck Dernoncourt, Roger Zimmermann, Yue Wang, Zhengzhong Tu, Vicente Ordonez, Mohit Bansal, Yue Zhao

entry.summary: JigShape benchmarks visual-geometric reasoning with 95K interlocking tab-and-blank jigsaw instances at grid densities from 4x4 to 16x16, where geometric constraints remove the ground-truth ambiguity of rectangular-cut puzzles. Zero-shot frontier models largely perform at chance, with only GPT-5.5 exceeding the random baseline on the easiest grids, while supervised fine-tuning reaches high accuracy.

entry.title: Private Face Recognition Training Dataset Publication via Identity-Decoupled and Geometry-Preserving Face Distillation

author.name: Shuhuan Chen, Xiangyu Zhu, Weisong Zhao, Siran Peng, Tianshuo Zhang, Haoyuan Zhang, Haichao Shi, Xiao-Yu Zhang, Zhen Lei

entry.summary: Addresses the tension in publishing privacy-protected face recognition training data: identity cues needed for supervision are also what make images linkable to real people. The method distills faces by decoupling identity while preserving geometry so that class structure survives for downstream training.

entry.title: One Patch Is Enough: Reinforcement-Optimized Visual Token Grounding for MLLM-Based Scene Text Spotting

author.name: Rui Tang, Wentao Yang, Peirong Zhang, Yongxin Shi, Shun Zhang, Huiguo He, Lianwen Jin

entry.summary: Reformulates MLLM scene text spotting so each text instance is routed through a single anchor visual token, then refined with full-image geometry recovery, with the anchor selected by a reinforcement learning objective over discrete choices. Aims to cut redundancy and localization ambiguity for dense or small text.

entry.title: Think with Extra-Image: A Farmland Segmentation Agent Driven by Spatio-Temporal Information Gain

author.name: Haiyang Wu, Weiliang Mu, Zhuofei Du, Dandan Zhong, Kaijie Shi, Haifeng Li, Chao Tao

entry.summary: Reframes farmland remote sensing segmentation as an agentic decision process that actively acquires extra spatio-temporal imagery when the current image lacks sufficient evidence, motivated by an information bottleneck view. Demonstrates that phenology and spatial context often lie outside the single input image.

entry.title: TARS: Timestep-Aware Data Scaling for 3D-Free Video Re-Shooting

author.name: Jiwen Liu, Shujuan Li, Xiaohan Li, Zijie Meng, Xinyue Liu, Yulong Xu, Yan Zhou, Guoxin Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a 3D-prior-free approach to video re-shooting with text-specified viewpoint changes, based on the finding that camera motion is mostly established during high-noise diffusion timesteps. Uses timestep-aware data scaling to concentrate supervision where camera structure forms.

entry.title: MonoVoc: Decoupling Geometry and Semantics for Lightweight Monocular Open-Vocabulary 3D Gaussians

author.name: Pouya Ardekhani, Zahra Dehghanian, Morteza Abolghasemi, Hamid R. Rabiee

entry.summary: Offers a training-free monocular pipeline that decouples 3D geometric reconstruction from semantic integration to produce compact object-level open-vocabulary Gaussian maps from ordinary video. Avoids multiview capture requirements, per-scene optimization, and dense per-Gaussian language feature storage.

entry.title: Capturing Token Tendencies for Training-Free Token Pruning in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Jie Ma, Zhike Qiu, Jie Gao, Jiayi Ji, Qian Chen, Xiaoshuai Sun, Rongrong Ji

entry.summary: Argues that training-free visual token pruning fails because it uses instantaneous per-layer scores, and instead models the trajectory or momentum of a token's attention importance across layers before irreversible removal. Prevents premature discarding of tokens needed for deep-layer reasoning.

entry.title: Entropy-Smooth Convex Optimization Cannot Be Accelerated

author.name: Jacob M. Aguirre, Dmitrii M. Ostrovskii

entry.summary: Proves an Omega(L/T) lower bound for first-order minimization of functions that are convex and smooth relative to negative entropy on the simplex, showing mirror descent is near optimal and acceleration is impossible in this class. Unlike earlier impossibility results, the hardness does not rely on a pathological prox-function constructed alongside the instance.

entry.title: Value Generalisation 2: The Missing Hole in AIs’ abilities

author.name: Stuart_Armstrong

entry.summary: The second post argues that humans possess a capacity the author calls strong generalisation, and that language models and their derivatives lack it. It uses this hypothesis to explain a cluster of observations: domain experts extract far more useful output from models than novices, models mix impressive competence with odd failures, they demand enormous data and continual retraining, and they saturate benchmarks including long-horizon ones while still feeling short of general intelligence.

entry.title: From Passive Video to Editable Experience: Physically Grounded Experience Synthesis for Embodied Intelligence

author.name: Jia Luo

entry.summary: Pegasus converts human manipulation videos into robot-learnable data by extracting a task graph, transforming it through affordance and constraint graphs into a robot planning graph, and using that to condition robot video generation. It targets the embodiment gap that prevents robots from learning directly from abundant human video.

entry.title: Decoupled Visual Processing: Efficient Multimodal Adaptation via Modality-Specific Transformer Substitution

author.name: Mingkuan Feng, Zhengqi Wen, Jianhua Tao

entry.summary: Decoupled Visual Processing replaces the upper decoder layers of a pretrained LLM with a single lightweight transformer block dedicated to visual tokens, on the premise that visual and textual representation needs diverge in deeper layers. This cuts the cost of visual instruction tuning versus full-parameter fine-tuning.

entry.title: Kalman Meets Curriculum: Efficient Dynamic Prompt Selection for Adaptive RL Finetuning

author.name: Haodong Zhu, Yangyang Ren, Yanjing Li, Sheng Xu, Haiguang Liu, Linlin Yang, Baochang Zhang

entry.summary: KGPS treats prompt difficulty during RL finetuning as a latent state to be tracked with a Kalman filter, so prompt selection adapts to the non-stationary evolution of the policy without the cost of repeatedly evaluating every prompt. It sits between expensive evaluation-based and cheap but stationarity-assuming prediction-based curricula.

entry.title: Beyond Binary Rewards: A Comparative Study of Reward Design for Reinforcement Unlearning

author.name: Efstratios Zaradoukas, Davide Gabrielli, Bardh Prenkaj, Gjergji Kasneci

entry.summary: This study examines how reward shaping affects machine unlearning framed as reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, replacing sparse binary avoid-or-not signals with a decomposed reward that provides denser feedback. The motivation is regulatory pressure to remove specific knowledge from deployed models without full retraining.

entry.title: The Role of Causality in Algorithmic Recourse

author.name: Srikanth Avasarala, Varun Gupta, Shahin Jabbari, Saber Salehkaleybar, Juba Ziani

entry.summary: This paper formalizes algorithmic recourse in a causal performative framework, distinguishing recommendations that genuinely improve an applicant's underlying qualifications from ones that merely game the classifier. It analyzes how recourse-induced behavior degrades predictive accuracy and how policies become ineffective after model retraining.

entry.title: Strategy, Not Payoffs: A Behavioural Embedding of Normal-Form Games

author.name: Joshua Caiata, Sreepriya Pulyassary, Xiang Li, Kate Larson

entry.summary: This work asks whether fine-tuning an LLM on one normal-form game helps or hurts its strategic reasoning in another, and proposes a two-feature behavioural embedding based on Nash equilibrium entropy to predict such transfer. Normal-form games provide clean payoffs and known equilibria for measuring strategic capability shifts.

entry.title: LAST: The Last Query Token Guides Visual Token Pruning for Edge-Cloud Collaborative MLLM Inference

author.name: Feng Yang, Xinrui Ju, Keyang Zhang, Xiandong Meng, Rongqun Lin, Howard Leung, Shiqi Wang, Haoliang Li, Chris Xing Tian

entry.summary: Proposes LAST, a training-free visual token pruning method for edge-cloud MLLM inference that uses the last query token of a compact guidance model to decide token relevance before transmission. Notable because query-aware pruning normally requires internal states of the cloud model that are unavailable at the edge.

entry.title: Beyond Classification: Pathology Foundation Models as Detection Encoders for Mitotic Figures

author.name: Sweta Banerjee, Alireza Teimoury, Nils Porsche, Alexandra K. Stoll, Viktoria Weiss, Niklas Hargarter, Jonas Ammeling, Thomas Conrad, Christoph Stroblberger, Christopher Kaltnecker, Robert Klopfleisch, Christof A. Bertram, Katharina Breininger, Marc Aubreville

entry.summary: Tests whether latent spaces of major pathology foundation models (UNI, Virchow, H-optimus families) are spatially resolved enough to serve as backbones for dense mitotic figure detection, comparing against an end-to-end ResNet50 baseline. Probes a limit of the classification-centric evaluation of pathology foundation models.

entry.title: Landmark shape spaces with induced metrics

author.name: Sarang Joshi, Peter W. Michor, Stefan Sommer

entry.summary: A theoretical geometry paper unifying Kendall landmark shape spaces with Riemannian metrics descending from right-invariant Sobolev metrics on diffeomorphism groups, via a screened elasticity operator. Yields shape spaces where landmarks cannot collide and rigid motion and scale are factored out.

entry.title: Exploring Structures in Physics Problems: Can AI Agents Discover Statistical Mechanical Mappings?

author.name: Wanyu Zhao, Wanbing Zhao

entry.summary: StatMechBench-v0 tests whether LLM agents can recognize that a raw partition function maps onto a known tractable model, covering transfer matrices, gauge-removable disorder, and Pfaffian structure across six Ising-type problems. A propose-verify-revise loop shows numerical feedback helps agents repair code, yet agents often pass numeric checks while misidentifying the underlying structure.

entry.title: Fewer Clarifications, Better Code: Benchmarking Cross-Session Personalized Ambiguity Adaptation in Coding Assistants

author.name: Zijian Xu, Wenshuo Zhang, Zisen Qin, Rui Sheng, Yushi Sun, Huamin Qu, Chuhan Shi

entry.summary: The paper formalizes personalized ambiguity adaptation: given a user's previously resolved coding sessions, an assistant should recognize recurring ambiguity patterns and resolve them without re-asking for clarification. It introduces a cross-session benchmark for this memory-driven behavior in coding assistants.

entry.title: Emergent Sparsity in Frozen Random CNN Feature Extractors for Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Scott M. Norton

entry.summary: Deep RL agents using frozen randomly initialized CNN feature extractors spontaneously develop extreme sparsity in the first fully connected layer, compressing task information into as few as one to three of sixty-four neurons on deterministic Pong. Sparsity scales with task complexity across Pong, Breakout, and Space Invaders and persists under width scaling.

entry.title: Identifying Implicit Bias in LLM-based Chat AI Toward People with Intellectual Disabilities

author.name: Karly V. Coffey, Gloria L. Krahn, John P. Hanley, Jacob E. Neely

entry.summary: Researchers generated 25,000 stories with and without intellectual disability descriptors across five commercial LLMs and analyzed representational differences using an LLM-based coding pipeline. The study measures implicit bias toward people with intellectual disabilities, a group largely absent from mainstream fairness benchmarks.

entry.title: Top-$k$ Pareto Bandits: Hypervolume Regret for Multi-Objective Slate Selection

author.name: Nicolas Gutowski, Fabien Chhel, Alexandre Letard, Sylvain Lamprier

entry.summary: The paper formalizes a multi-objective bandit setting where the learner picks a slate of k arms per round under semi-bandit feedback and aims to approximate the Pareto frontier, measured by dominated hypervolume. It defines an approximate hypervolume regret against the best size-k subset in hindsight using the greedy submodular approximation factor.

entry.title: A Persona-based Rate Action Index

author.name: Hayden Helm, Andrew Dassori

entry.summary: The authors build retrieval-grounded personas for individual FOMC members from about 25,000 document chunks and aggregate persona responses into an index predicting hike/hold/cut decisions. They validate persona likeness through identifiability and detectability tests before using the index for prediction.

entry.title: Physically Real-time Infrared Attack against Optical Flow Estimation Networks

author.name: Shen You, Wei Jiang, Jiarui Liu, Yijian Ye, Qiuzhen Lin, Xiangtao Li, Ka-Chun Wong

entry.summary: The paper demonstrates real-time physical adversarial attacks on optical flow estimation networks using infrared light for stealth, precomputing adversarial examples and displaying them dynamically. Because optical flow feeds downstream autonomous driving and motion detection tasks, the attack raises safety concerns for deployed perception stacks.

entry.title: Progressive Multimodal Alignment for Continual Instruction Tuning

author.name: Duzhen Zhang, Yahan Yu, Qiaoyi Su, Jiahua Dong, Tielin Zhang

entry.summary: Progressive Multimodal Alignment tackles projector-level forgetting in multimodal continual instruction tuning, where shifting visual distributions cause the vision-to-language projector to drift. It detects distribution shifts with a lightweight descriptor and progressively expands projector experts to adapt while preserving prior alignment.

entry.title: Good Rankers, Bad Objectives: Bilinear Contrastive Critics under Expressive Policy Search

author.name: Ayushman Singh, Siddharth Aphale

entry.summary: This paper shows that contrastive critics which rank actions well are still unsafe to maximize: unbounded bilinear scores inflate off-support values through embedding-norm drift, and cosine bounding does not fix the failure. Across four navigation tasks the contrastive critics select off-support actions and are poorly calibrated, while a Bellman-trained TD-Q critic succeeds.

entry.title: Train Small, Deploy Large: Zero-Shot GNN Transfer Through Geometric Renormalization

author.name: Robert Jankowski, Pedro Almagro-Blanco, Mari\'an Bogu\~n\'a, Melanie Weber, M. \'Angeles Serrano

entry.summary: The authors train GNNs on graphs coarse-grained by geometric renormalization and transfer the weights directly to the full-resolution graph without retraining, retaining much of the original predictive performance at greatly reduced training cost. This gives a principled small-to-large deployment protocol for million-node graphs.

entry.title: AutoPref: Automatic Discovery of Task-Specific Preference Objectives for Neural Combinatorial Optimization

author.name: Shengda Gu, Kai Li, Xinyi Ke, Haobo Fu, Yifan Zhang, Jian Cheng

entry.summary: AutoPref uses an LLM to automatically discover preference objectives for neural combinatorial optimization, factorizing the design space into what signal to extract from solution pairs and how to weight pairs within a sampled set. It replaces hand-designed, one-size-fits-all preference losses with task-specific discovered ones.

entry.title: Search Strategies for Optimal Classification and Regression Trees

author.name: Jacobus G. M. van der Linden, Mim van den Bos, Emir Demirovi\'c

entry.summary: The authors build a general algorithmic framework that reproduces and recombines 18 different search strategies for optimal decision trees, enabling a controlled comparison of which components actually drive scalability. The best resulting configuration improves anytime performance over prior state of the art.

entry.title: Why Are GUI Agents Correct but Late? Decode on the Decision-Time Critical Path, Tested with Pre-Compiled Policy Trees

author.name: Zihan Dong, Rui Qian, Qishi Zhan, Dongshen Peng, Kaixin Li, Yu Li

entry.summary: This work diagnoses why GUI and computer-use agents often emit the right action too late, attributing the failure to autoregressive decoding sitting on the decision-time critical path. The proposed fix precomputes bounded conditional policy trees with guards and deadlines during idle screen periods, so a lightweight observer can fire a pre-authorized branch the moment an event occurs.

entry.title: QAdapt: A Noise-Adaptive Neural Pre-Decoding Framework for Quantum Error Correction

author.name: Ran Miao, Rui Luo, Xiaohan Shan, Xiaoming Sun

entry.summary: QAdapt is a neural pre-decoder for surface-code quantum error correction that adapts online to heterogeneous, nonstationary hardware noise and mitigates the simulation-to-hardware distribution shift that degrades fixed decoders. It exploits local spatiotemporal syndrome correlations to reduce classical decoding latency.

entry.title: Nanoparticle Networks for Neuromorphic Computing

author.name: Jonas Mensing, Wilfred G. van der Wiel, Andreas Heuer

entry.summary: Presents a physical neuromorphic substrate of metallic nanoparticles linked by molecular junctions, showing that static control electrodes convert a passive reservoir into a tunable nonlinear dynamical computer. Three design rules are derived, including operating near the cutoff frequency to balance nonlinear tunneling against capacitive memory.

entry.title: Windowed thinning and query complexity for the bouncy particle and Zigzag samplers

author.name: Jianfeng Lu, Yinchen Luo

entry.summary: Analyzes windowed thinning, an exact simulation technique for the bouncy particle sampler and coordinate Zigzag process that uses one gradient per deterministic window to build a tractable local rate envelope. Combining mixing estimates with bounce and flip counts yields explicit gradient-query complexity bounds in dimension and condition number from a cold start.

entry.title: Learning to Trace Seiberg Dualities

author.name: Jonathan J. Heckman, Shani Meynet, Alessandro Mininno, Gary Shiu

entry.summary: Uses machine learning to decide whether two supersymmetric quiver gauge theories are related by Seiberg duality, framed mathematically as finding quiver mutation sequences in the spirit of learning to unknot. The result is both a practical duality-tracing tool and a case study in learning search over discrete mathematical moves.

entry.title: RepBench: Compiling Benchmarks into Capability Representations for Large Language Models

author.name: Yanshi Li, Xueru Bai, Shuman Liu, Long Zhang

entry.summary: RepBench builds a benchmark-grounded data layer for representation engineering, mining 13k benchmark papers into a taxonomy of 182 capability clusters and harvesting 46k audited probe texts across 94 capabilities. Each capability is backed by at least two independent benchmarks to reduce single-source artifacts.

entry.title: VETO: Towards Protecting Images From Frontier AI Editing

author.name: Jonas Grebe, Hossein Shakibania, Tobias Braun, Marcus Rohrbach, Anna Rohrbach

entry.summary: VETO develops protective perturbations against modern frontier image editors such as FLUX.2, whose direct attention from prompt and generation tokens to reference-image tokens defeats defenses built for the semantic bottleneck of legacy diffusion pipelines. The threat model includes extracting identities and objects and recontextualizing them into new scenes.

entry.title: Learning to Understand Body Language from Flight through Robust 3D Avatar Placing

author.name: Dragos Costea, Alina Marcu, Cristina Lazar, Marius Leordeanu

entry.summary: Introduces a dataset that composites metrically correct 3D avatars performing ten communicative intents into real 4K drone footage, enabled by a lightweight geometric world model with provably rigid-invariant anchor placement. Aims to enable long-range human intent perception for aerial robots.

entry.title: Towards Practical Algorithm Selection for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation in Medical Imaging

author.name: Yiheng Xiong, Luisa Gall\'ee, Daniel Santak Wolf, Heiko Hillenhagen, Michael G\"otz

entry.summary: Proposes a label-free criterion for jointly choosing an unsupervised domain adaptation algorithm and its hyperparameters in medical imaging, by scoring candidate models against a two-level agreement reference built without target labels. Tackles the practical blocker that unlabeled deployment domains prevent direct validation.

entry.title: Towards Real-Time PixOOD: Efficient Anomaly Segmentation for Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: Luca de Martino, Federico Aromolo, Federico Nesti, Giorgio Buttazzo

entry.summary: Reformulates the scoring stage of the PixOOD anomaly segmentation method and deploys the full pipeline with TensorRT, reaching 182 FPS on a desktop GPU and 75 FPS on Jetson AGX Orin, roughly 20x and 18x faster than the baseline. Targets safety-critical driving and railway perception on embedded hardware.

entry.title: UniCross: Unified Cross-Skill Dexterous Manipulation Synthesis

author.name: Hui Zhang, Julian Ferchow, Jie Song, Mirko Meboldt

entry.summary: UniCross models grasping, relocation, in-hand rotation, and in-hand translation within one state and action space and a shared objective, instead of using skill-specific formulations. The unified treatment is meant to enable continuous composition of skills for long-horizon dexterous manipulation.

entry.title: DexDirect: Direct Kinesthetic Arm Guidance for Efficient Dexterous Demonstration Collection

author.name: Beom Jun Kim, Shiu-Jen Wang, Jonathan Liu, Alvin Zhu, Quanyou Wang, Hanzhang Fang, Feng Xu, Mingzhang Zhu, Yuchen Cui, Dennis W. Hong

entry.summary: DexDirect collects dexterous manipulation demonstrations by having an operator physically drag a gravity-compensated robot arm by a handle while a single webcam retargets the operator's other hand onto a 16-joint dexterous hand. User studies report roughly 17x and 3x more successful demonstrations than vision-only and pose-tracking teleoperation baselines.

entry.title: TacWAM: Anchor-Guided World Action Model with Mechanics-Aware Tactile Prediction

author.name: Lei Jin, Yiding Ma, Xin Zhang, Chen Gao, Wei Wu, Yong Li

entry.summary: TacWAM adds tactile futures to world action models via an encoder that fuses tactile appearance, dense force fields, and deformation flow into a shared latent prediction space, deliberately preventing tactile prediction from becoming a privileged shortcut for action generation. The aim is better supervision for force, shear, and slip in contact-rich manipulation.

entry.title: Non-partitioned e-detectors for nonparametric sequential change detection

author.name: Aytijhya Saha, Aaditya Ramdas

entry.summary: Develops nonparametric sequential change detectors that aggregate point-null e-processes over candidate changepoints and take an infimum over no-change distributions, without needing a pre-specified partition of the distribution class into pre- and post-change families. The authors characterize which aggregation weights yield average run length versus false alarm probability control and prove first-order asymptotic optimality.

entry.title: How controllers from industrial machinery can coordinate multitask machine learning

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Amazon describes ControlG, an ICML method that handles conflicting objectives in graph self-supervised learning by dedicating capacity to one objective at a time and using a proportional-integral-derivative controller to decide which objective needs attention next. This replaces the usual practice of blending all objectives at every training step.

entry.title: When benchmark inferences do not compose: Projectibility in AI evaluation

author.name: Brett Reynolds

entry.summary: A conceptual paper arguing that AI benchmark claims break down when chained across generalization, capability attribution, transport to new systems, and downstream deployment assumptions. It introduces projectibility as the missing epistemic condition, since individually warranted inference steps do not compose into a warranted chain.

entry.title: Eco3S: Complex Socio-Economic System Simulation via Agent-Based Models

author.name: Shaopeng Wei, Yufei Cheng, Wenxi Sun, Yepeng Ding, Yu Zhao, Gang Kou

entry.summary: Eco3S is an LLM agent-based modeling framework for socio-economic simulation featuring bidirectional agent-environment co-evolution, a structural causal model inspired counterfactual mechanism, and automated simulation workflows for policy analysis. It targets the rigidity and manual overhead of current LLM-based ABM studies.

entry.title: Setoka: A Benchmark for Hierarchical User Understanding in Personalized Agents over Heterogeneous Data

author.name: Lingyang Zeng, Guangze Chen, Kaichen Yu, Zhicheng Pan, Siyang Weng, Zirui Hu, Xiangyun Du, Hailin He, Rong Zhang, Chengcheng Yang, Kai Huang, Xuan Zhou

entry.summary: Setoka is a benchmark for personalized agent memory that goes beyond retrieving explicitly stated facts, defining four levels of user understanding grounded in cognitive and personality psychology over heterogeneous data sources. It tests whether agents can infer abstract personal characteristics rather than just recall conversation content.

entry.title: FinCacheServe: Dependency-Consistent Answer Reuse for Cost-Efficient RAG Serving over Mutable Enterprise Documents

author.name: Lingteng Zeng, Yifan Jin

entry.summary: FinCacheServe caches generated RAG answers as serving objects keyed by enterprise intent and guarded by document versions, evidence fingerprints, tool fingerprints, model identity, and decoding settings, so reuse remains consistent as source documents mutate. On a 2,230-request trace with a 7B model it skips over half of LLM calls with no observed stale outputs.

entry.title: Automorphism-Induced Non-Canonicity in Top-k Explanations of Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Xin Xu, Siru Tao, Kaizhen Tan

entry.summary: The paper shows that permutation-equivariant message passing forces identical attribution scores on automorphic substructures, so any top-k edge report must arbitrarily break ties, making such explanations non-canonical. It gives a parameter-free criterion for when exact-k reports are ill-posed, mechanized in Lean 4.

entry.title: ForgetBench: Benchmarking Forgetting Dynamics of Long-Term Parametric Memory in Language Models

author.name: Ruxi Gu, Zhenliang Zhang, Wei Wang

entry.summary: ForgetBench benchmarks how LLMs forget previously acquired knowledge under repeated continual knowledge editing, using concept-based and scenario-based QA to separate isolated factual retention from contextual usage. It targets temporal dynamics of degradation that static editing evaluations miss.

entry.title: FakeIDet3-DB: Refining Digital Attacks and Patch Extraction for Secure ID Benchmarking

author.name: Mu\~noz-Haro Javier, Teruel Andres, Tolosana Ruben, DeAlcala Daniel, Vera-Rodriguez Ruben, Morales Aythami, Fierrez Julian

entry.summary: FakeIDet3-DB is presented as the first large database of digital manipulations, both classical and generative, applied to real government-issued identity documents, addressing the privacy-driven reliance on synthetic templates that lack authentic security patterns. It also refines patch extraction for benchmarking forensic detectors.

entry.title: SymmGrid: Super-Scaling On-Robot Learning with Parallelized Symmetries and Egocentric-Exocentric Visual Perception

author.name: Gabe Everett, Brice Gunter, Ryan Vander Stelt, Cleiver Ruiz-Martinez, Blake Hull, Juan Rojas

entry.summary: SymmGrid accelerates on-robot reinforcement learning by augmenting trajectories with parallelized group symmetry transformations organized in a symmetry tree, covering both egocentric and exocentric camera setups. Proprioceptive data requires homography-based warping to keep visual scenes consistent with the transformed states.

entry.title: Cost-Sensitive Conformal Prediction and Human-in-the-Loop Abstention for Imbalanced High-Stakes Decision Support: A Multi-Domain Benchmark

author.name: Manpreet Singh, Akshatha Srikantha, Shyamal Lakhanpal

entry.summary: The authors show that standard marginal conformal prediction can badly under-cover rare minority classes (down to fractions of a percent) and benchmark class-conditional conformal prediction plus cost-aware abstention across 15 imbalanced tabular datasets, 7 models, and 3 calibration methods. It matters for deployed high-stakes decision support where the costly errors are exactly the rare ones.

entry.title: DoTime: A Synthetic Benchmark Generator for Interventional and Counterfactual Time Series

author.name: Dennis Thumm, Billy Tim Anthony, Ying Chen

entry.summary: DoTime is an open generator of temporal structural causal models with interventions and counterfactuals, shipped as a Python package with four frozen evaluation suites. It adds continuous-time intervention windows, positivity-guarded counterfactual sampling, and regime-switching processes that generalize interrupted time-series settings.

entry.title: FunL2O: LLM-Guided Feature Function Design for Learning to Optimize

author.name: Bingheng Li, Junyang Cai, Yupeng Zhang, Bistra Dilkina, Jayant Kalagnanam, Dzung T. Phan

entry.summary: FunL2O automates the design of the feature functions that map optimization instances to model inputs, using an LLM in a FunSearch-style evolutionary loop where each proposed program is scored by retraining the downstream learning-to-optimize model. It targets a hand-crafted component that prior L2O pipelines largely ignore.

entry.title: FeatFix: Reuse What You Verify through Local Exact-Feature Correction for Faster Cached Diffusion Inference

author.name: Hanshuai Cui, Zhiqing Tang, Zhi Yao, Qianli Ma, Fanshuai Meng, Weijia Jia

entry.summary: FeatFix observes that training-free diffusion cache accelerators compute exact block features for verification and then throw them away; instead it forwards the exact feature at the verification site to reset local draft residuals and cut downstream error. The result is faster cached diffusion inference with less quality drift.

entry.title: QuantWAMs: Calibrating at the Right Granularity for World Action Models

author.name: Jiacheng Zhou, Jinfan Lv, Ruixuan Li, Longtai Zhang, Yan Wang, Wenqiang Zhang, Lizhe Qi

entry.summary: QuantWAMs is a post-training quantization framework for world action models that jointly predict future observations and actions, arguing that existing PTQ fails because it assumes open-loop objectives and unrepresentative calibration data. It introduces shared-basis outlier calibration across coordinate-compatible modules, co-training-objective saliency, and deployment-matched rollout calibration.

entry.title: Models for minimalist RAG: B1ade 335M Embedding and 1B Parameter Small Language Models

author.name: Shreyas Subramanian, Mecit Gungor, Vikram Elango

entry.summary: B1ade pairs a 335M-parameter embedding model built by parameter-free fusion of five pretrained encoders with a 1B language model trained via GRPO on curated context-question pairs using only answer-similarity rewards. The notable finding is emergent attribution: the small model learns to cite supporting context despite never receiving explicit grounding supervision.

entry.title: LEEPS: Latent-Guided Explore-Exploit Prompt Sampling for Efficient RLVR in Large Language Models

author.name: Shuang Liang, Haoyang Zhou, Yifan Gong, Guowei Wang, Xiting Wang

entry.summary: LEEPS is a pre-rollout prompt selection method for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards that uses latent representations to balance reusing historically informative prompts against exploring new ones. The goal is to avoid wasting rollout budget on prompt groups whose rewards are all identical.

entry.title: Articulated Object Reconstruction from Rest-State Observation

author.name: Daeun Lee, Jaeah Lee, Woosung Kim, Haebeom Jung, Jaesik Park

entry.summary: Proposes reconstructing articulated objects (geometry plus joint kinematics) from a single closed rest-state observation, using an explicit mesh as an intermediate representation to reconcile noisy vision-language and segmentation outputs. Matters for building interactive digital twins where multi-state motion capture is impractical.

entry.title: Beyond Visual Ambiguity: Guiding Robust Monocular Depth Estimation in Challenging Scenarios via Detailed Long Captions

author.name: Junrui Zhang, Jiaqi Li, Yiran Wang, Liao Shen, Zhiguo Cao

entry.summary: Improves monocular depth estimation on non-Lambertian surfaces and adverse weather by conditioning on detailed long textual captions, with finer-grained text feature learning and language guidance during depth decoding. Argues prior language-guided depth methods underused text due to short, coarse inputs.

entry.title: GPT-Red: Automated Red Teaming via Self-Play at Scale

author.name: Eric Wallace, Christopher A. Choquette-Choo, Nikhil Kandpal, Sam Toyer, Dylan Hunn, Stephanie Lin, Yuxin Wen, Xiangyu Qi, Christopher Wolff, Zizhao Wang, Milad Nasr, Sicheng Zhu, Chuan Guo, Juan Felipe Cer\'on Uribe, Kaiwen Wang, Aiden Low, Kai Xiao, Kai Chen

entry.summary: Already covered in Research yesterday, OpenAI describes GPT-Red, an automated red-teaming agent trained by self-play against a population of simultaneously trained defender agents to discover novel prompt injection attacks, and reports using it to adversarially train GPT-5.6. The authors state this is their largest documented LLM safety training run, on a compute scale comparable to some of their biggest RL post-training runs.

entry.title: Partner Capability Estimation for Task-Agnostic Adaptation in Ad-Hoc Teamwork

author.name: Peter Tisnikar, Maja Swieczkowska, Benteng Ma, Gerard Canal, Matteo Leonetti

entry.summary: This paper extends ad-hoc teamwork to multi-task settings where partner capabilities are hidden and human collaborators may act suboptimally, reframing it as joint planning with decentralized execution. The proposed CE-CM method performs approximate Bayesian estimation of partner capability from contextual models to adapt without task-specific training.

entry.title: (EC)2: Event-Centric Explainability for Cybersecurity Through Multi-Agent LLM Investigations

author.name: Neta Kirmayer, David Tayouri, Andr\'es Murillo, Motoyoshi Sekiya, Asaf Shabtai, Rami Puzis

entry.summary: The framework provides detector-agnostic, event-centric explanations for cybersecurity alerts by running a multi-agent LLM investigation that forms and tests hypotheses grounded in verifiable evidence. It targets the gap between feature-level anomaly explanations and the contextual understanding analysts actually need.

entry.title: High-Order Markov Blanket Discovery via a k-Order Relaxation of the Faithfulness Assumption

author.name: Loong Kuan Lee, Ragavi Krishnamoorthy, Nico Piatkowski

entry.summary: The authors propose a k-order relaxation of the faithfulness assumption for Markov blanket discovery, which standard methods violate under higher-order dependencies such as XOR and parity relations or under finite-sample artifacts. The relaxation supports more robust structure learning, causal discovery, and feature selection.

entry.title: ServerlessT2I: Efficient Text-to-Image Workflow Serving on a Serverless Platform

author.name: Xiaoxiao Jiang, Suyi Li, Sheng Yao, Tianyu Feng, Lingyun Yang, Dapeng Nie, Haoran Yang, Wei Wang

entry.summary: ServerlessT2I decomposes text-to-image generation workflows into independently scheduled model functions rather than deploying each workflow as one opaque GPU function. This enables finer-grained scaling, placement, and multi-tenant fairness for intermittently invoked custom pipelines.

entry.title: FedTopo: Relation-Level Topology Sharing for Model-Heterogeneous Federated Learning

author.name: Zhaoyang Ma, Zhihao Wu, Xin Gao, Lipo Wang, Youfang Lin, Jing Wang

entry.summary: FedTopo shares global knowledge in model-heterogeneous federated learning as class relation topology, capturing how classes relate within each client rather than their absolute positions in representation space. This avoids the alignment failures that arise when heterogeneous backbones produce non-comparable embeddings.

entry.title: MMAC: A Massive Multi-dimensional Benchmark for Audio Captioning

author.name: Weijie Wu, Junbo Li, Lin Li, Jun Fang, Qingyang Hong

entry.summary: MMAC is a benchmark of about 5,600 audio clips from over 20 sources that scores free-form audio captions along 15 dimensions across 6 capability categories, checking both whether relevant information is mentioned and whether it is factually consistent. It targets a real gap in audio LLM evaluation, which currently rewards fluency over information coverage and reliability.

entry.title: EvoCause: LLM-Guided Evolution of Causal Graphs for Root Cause Analysis

author.name: Lei Zan, Keli Zhang, Shifeng Xie, Jiale Zheng, Zehao Xiao, Zhiwei Dong, Ke Zhang, Ruichu Cai, Malik Tiomoko, Lujia Pan

entry.summary: EvoCause closes the loop between expert incident diagnoses and learned causal graphs for alarm root-cause analysis by having an LLM propose semantically plausible graph edits that deterministic code then validates. It targets telecom and microservice systems where a static learned graph cannot absorb historical expert labels.

entry.title: S-CEReBrO: Breaking the Memory Barrier in Continuous EEG Monitoring

author.name: Glenn Anta Bucagu, Thorir Mar Ingolfsson, Yawei Li, Luca Benini

entry.summary: S-CEReBrO adapts an EEG foundation model for continuous streaming monitoring by replacing global attention with a windowed alternating attention scheme that keeps the KV cache at constant size regardless of recording length. This removes the memory blow-up that prevents Transformer-based biosignal models from running indefinitely on wearable or clinical monitors.

entry.title: Generalization Bounds on Optimal Control for Transformer Training and Wasserstein Distributional Robustness

author.name: Ka\u{g}an Akman, Naci Saldi, Serdar Y\"uksel

entry.summary: The authors derive finite-sample generalization bounds for Transformers trained via dynamic programming by treating training as a finite-horizon Markovian control problem over measure-valued states, then quantizing the spaces and applying concentration inequalities. They also connect the result to Wasserstein distributional robustness.

entry.title: OneShot: Index-in-Ranking with Neural Scoring for Large-Scale Retrieval

author.name: Ziwei Li, Shuyao Li, Xufeng Cai, Xue Zou, Yiming Ma, Huiting Lu, Wujie Yan, Zhichen Zhao, Yang Lu, Zhe Wang, Rui Luo, Zhengyu Su, Dan Zhang, Ji Liu

entry.summary: OneShot addresses the structural misalignment between ranking objectives and indexing structure in billion-scale retrieval by learning the index jointly within ranking rather than as a separate grouping step, with neural scoring for candidate selection. The target is the first-stage filter in industrial recommender pipelines.

entry.title: Generalization and Trade-off in Adversarial Training: An RKHS Perspective via Kernel Integral Operators

author.name: Yiling Xie, Xiaoming Huo

entry.summary: Analyzes adversarial training in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces via the kernel integral operator, deriving generalization bounds in terms of robustness level, sample size, source smoothness, and spectrum. A matching lower bound on a polynomial-spectrum model shows the optimally balanced rate can be strictly slower than the minimax prediction benchmark, quantifying a robustness-accuracy statistical cost.

entry.title: IFHierBench: Hierarchical Instruction Following for Large Language Models

author.name: Yuetian Mao, Chunyang Chen

entry.summary: IFHierBench tests hierarchical instruction following with 600 prompts whose constraints are scoped to specific sections and nested fields of a layered output, across four constraint-tree depths and 35 constraint types. Existing benchmarks treat constraints as a flat list applied to the whole response.

entry.title: FiRE: Enhancing MLLMs with Fine-Grained Context Learning for Complex Image Retrieval

author.name: Bohan Hou, Haoqiang Lin, Xuemeng Song, Haokun Wen, Meng Liu, Yupeng Hu, Xiangyu Zhao

entry.summary: Builds an automated pipeline for fine-grained multimodal quintuple training data plus a two-stage fine-tuning recipe that turns MLLMs into stronger universal image retrievers for long-text, dialog, and composed image retrieval. Focuses on fine-grained context modeling and disentangled objectives.

entry.title: VisualRouter: Query-Grounded Visual Sampling for Long Video Understanding

author.name: Haiyue Zhang, Yi Bin, Xun Jiang, Zeyu Ma, Duo Peng, Guoqing Wang, Yang Yang, Heng Tao Shen

entry.summary: Proposes a plug-and-play training-free sampler for long video understanding that first classifies whether a query is global or local and then applies a matching frame-sampling strategy. Addresses redundancy and poor temporal coverage in relevance-only sampling.

entry.title: Finding Change in Satellite Archives from Text: How to Combine Before-and-After Images Efficiently

author.name: Simon Roy, Mark Bong, Giovanni Beltrame

entry.summary: Runs a controlled comparison of eight fusion module designs for text-based retrieval of change in bi-temporal satellite image archives, holding the frozen CLIP encoder and training recipe fixed. Because fusion runs per candidate pair at query time, its speed dominates search cost.

entry.title: Three-Photon Bayesian Imaging of Ortho-Positronium

author.name: L. Raczynski, W. Krzemien, A. Coussat, M. Bala, B. C. Hiesmayr, K. Klimaszewski, M. Obara, R. Y. Shopa

entry.summary: Proposes a Bayesian maximum a posteriori algorithm for event-by-event reconstruction of three-photon ortho-positronium annihilations in PET, unifying time-based trilateration with energy-based reconstruction. Could enable positronium imaging biomarkers such as the three-to-two photon yield ratio.

entry.title: Value Generalisation 1: a Research and Deployment Program

author.name: Stuart_Armstrong

entry.summary: The first post in a three-part series proposes a research and deployment program centered on value generalisation, meaning an AI system's ability to correctly extend human values and preferences into situations that were never encountered during training or specification. The author argues this capability gap is why users cannot yet safely hand over credentials, finances, and open-ended authority to an assistant, and floats a commercial vehicle rather than an academic one so that the alignment component is not stripped out and discarded while the capability parts get reused.

entry.title: MultivationBench: A Benchmark for Multimodal Sequential Motivation Reasoning

author.name: Kawai Chung, Chunkit Chan, Yauwai Yim, Yuxuan Liu, Haochen Shi, Weiqi Wang, Qing Zong, Tianshi Zheng, Yixuan Fu, Kai Chung Wong, Hao Liang, Yifan Gao, Xi Yang, Janet Hui-wen Hsiao, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: MultivationBench evaluates whether multimodal LLMs can infer evolving character motivations across story-driven visual narratives, grounding labels in Maslow's hierarchy and Reiss's basic desires. It targets sequential accumulation of motivational evidence rather than static single-image social inference.

entry.title: AlphaSchema: Exploring the Space of Trading Semantics for LLM-Based Alpha Mining

author.name: Jingyang Yi, Jian Yang, Yifei Jin, Yuqi Li, Jian Li

entry.summary: AlphaSchema separates what to search from how to implement in LLM-driven quantitative factor discovery by defining an explicit schema space over event, context, qualities, direction, and output before code generation. This makes exploration in alpha mining controllable rather than implicit in the agent's own decisions.

entry.title: UrbanDS: A Graph-Guided LLM Multi-Agent System for Data-Intensive Urban Tasks

author.name: Zhilun Zhou, Jianghao Yu, Yuming Lin, yongjun yang, Sun Yongquan, Depeng Jin, Yong Li

entry.summary: UrbanDS builds a unified dataset graph over large heterogeneous urban data repositories and uses a graph-guided LLM multi-agent system to discover and combine relevant datasets for data-intensive urban analysis tasks. It targets scenarios where the relevant data is not handed to the agent in advance.

entry.title: AgentMap: Joint Equivalence and Subsumption Discovery for Ontology Matching

author.name: Yiping Song, Jiaoyan Chen, Renate Schmidt, Hui Yang, Wen Zhang

entry.summary: AgentMap unifies equivalence and subsumption discovery into a single hybrid ontology matching task and solves it with an LLM multi-agent pipeline combining semantic retrieval, hierarchical search, and collaborative decisions. It removes the traditional split where systems handle only one correspondence type.

entry.title: Large-Scale ChatBot Validation Through Customer Digital Twin Simulations

author.name: Cristovao Iglesias, Devesh Batra, Alankar Atreya, Stefan Wagner, Robert Hankache, Patrick Sinclair, Giulio Pelosio, Michael McMillan, Greig A. Cowan, Raad Khraishi

entry.summary: An industry team presents synthetic customer agents grounded in real transactional and conversational banking data as digital twins for validating LLM chatbots at scale, plus an evaluation harness. They report high semantic alignment with real customers, low hallucination, and controllable personality trait reproduction.

entry.title: AgentGFM: A Graph Foundation Model with Node-Agent Information-Flow Control

author.name: Jingbo Cui, Jitao Zhao, Di Jin, Dongxiao He

entry.summary: AgentGFM is a graph foundation model in which each node acts as an agent controlling how information flows to it, replacing hand-designed fixed propagation schemes that transfer poorly across graphs. The aim is better cross-domain transfer given that local structural patterns vary between and within graphs.

entry.title: FPSGen: Flexible Point Cloud Scene Generation with BEV-Supported Transport Flows

author.name: Wenzhe He, Meng Wang, JiaWei Qian, Jinfeng Xu, Ying Liu, Ruihui Li

entry.summary: FPSGen generates outdoor LiDAR point cloud scenes by predicting a bird's-eye-view prior and constructing point sources independently of partial scans, avoiding the train-inference mismatch of completion-style methods. This yields denser distant regions and better occluded geometry, and supports generation from layout cues without LiDAR observations.

entry.title: AI as Friction for Reflection Support in Ideation

author.name: Janin Koch, Xiaohan Liao, G\'ery Casiez

entry.summary: This position and design paper argues that generative AI tools for creative ideation should not remove all friction, because the act of accepting, rejecting, and reworking candidate ideas is how designers build the rationale needed to think with and explain their ideas. It proposes deliberate friction to support reflection-in-action, especially in group ideation.

entry.title: SciFigQual-Bench: A Benchmark for Scientific Figure Quality Assessment with Full-Manuscript Context

author.name: Zihan Deng, Chuanzhi Xu, Huiqi Liang, Haoyang Li, Xiaozhen Zhong, Lequan Yu

entry.summary: SciFigQual-Bench evaluates scientific figure quality with full-manuscript context across five dimensions: clarity, layout, caption fit, context relevance, and misleading risk. It goes beyond prior chart-assessment work confined to visual-surface comparisons that cannot verify caption alignment or detect misleading presentation.

entry.title: Anatomy Contextualized Adaption of CT Foundation Models

author.name: Roshan Kenia, Stephanie L McNamara, William Lotter

entry.summary: ACA is a lightweight adapter that takes a frozen CT vision-language foundation model and adds anatomy-level alignment using organ segmentation, while retaining whole-volume global context. It avoids the cost of training fine-grained CT models from scratch, which is the main barrier to anatomy-aware medical foundation models.

entry.title: What Makes Graph Unified? Principles and Generative Sliding-Window Transformer for Graph Foundation Models

author.name: Dongxiao He, Siqi Liu, Jitao Zhao, Yawen Li, Yi Wang, Di Jin

entry.summary: The paper argues that mapping heterogeneous node features into a shared dimension does not actually unify graph domains, and proposes a generative sliding-window Transformer for graph foundation models that addresses feature unification at a principled level. It targets cross-domain generalization for general-purpose graph learning.

entry.title: Multi-channel Uplift Policy Learning

author.name: Changjian Liu, Tianyu Wang, Xiaoxuan Deng, WenTao Zhu, Yuwei Xu, Jungqi Jin, Yong Gao, Chuan Yu, Jian Xu, Bo Zheng

entry.summary: ReAlloc tackles cross-channel marketing budget allocation as a simplex-constrained uplift decision problem, pairing an orthogonal teacher that extracts unbiased local gradients from short-term logs with a student that distills them into a long-horizon marginal field. It reports large-scale online A/B validation on an e-commerce platform.

entry.title: Selecting Open-Weight Language Models for Zero-Shot Intent Classification: A Systematic Evaluation of 41 Models

author.name: Parishruthi Ganesh, Gerry Dozier, Cheryl Seals

entry.summary: A systematic zero-shot evaluation of 41 open-weight models from 15 families spanning 135M to 9B parameters on eight intent-classification datasets, adding calibration, perturbation robustness, and deployment-constraint analysis beyond exact-match accuracy. It provides practitioner guidance for selecting deployable small models for dialogue systems.

entry.title: GyRot: Leveraging Hidden Synergy between Rotation and Fine-grained Group Quantization for Low-bit LLM Inference

author.name: Sangjin Kim, Yuseon Choi, Byeongcheol Kim, Jungjun Oh, Hoi-jun Yoo

entry.summary: GyRot is an algorithm-hardware co-design that reconciles rotation-based outlier suppression with fine-grained group quantization for low-bit LLM inference, introducing coarse rotation with fine grouping and a harmonic-aligned permutation to avoid the usual accuracy or overhead penalty. It also reformulates asymmetric quantization to cut accelerator cost.

entry.title: LightRot: A Light-Weighted Rotation Scheme and Architecture for Accurate Low-Bit Large Language Model Inference

author.name: Sangjin Kim, Yuseon Choi, Jungjun Oh, Byeongcheol Kim, Hoi-Jun Yoo

entry.summary: LightRot proposes grouped local rotation and outlier direction alignment with a hierarchical fast Hadamard transform unit to reduce the energy overhead of rotation operations in low-bit LLM inference, taped out in a 28nm accelerator reaching 27.4 TOPS/W at 4-bit. It is a companion effort to the same group's other rotation-quantization work.

entry.title: Driving up Inference Energy on SNNs: Per-Sample and Universal Sponge Attacks

author.name: Spyridon Raptis, Haralampos-G. Stratigopoulos

entry.summary: Shows that the sparsity advantage of spiking neural networks is also an attack surface: sponge inputs can inflate spike counts and synaptic workload, raising inference energy on neuromorphic hardware while outputs still look correct. The work extends sponge attacks to native event-based binary inputs and studies both per-sample and universal variants.

entry.title: Fully Inductive Cardinality Estimation

author.name: Tim Schwabe, Lukas Ketzer, Maribel Acosta

entry.summary: FICE is presented as the first learned cardinality estimator for SPARQL basic graph patterns that generalizes to entirely unseen knowledge graphs and relations without retraining, using a factor-graph GNN encoder coupled with a second component for estimation. This removes the transductive retraining barrier that has blocked adoption of learned estimators in real triplestores.

entry.title: Graph Neural Network Force Fields for Spin Dynamics in Metallic Magnets

author.name: Ali Rayat, Yunhao Fan, Gia-Wei Chern

entry.summary: Introduces a graph neural network magnetic force field that learns the effective magnetic energy functional of itinerant electron systems directly from electronic-structure calculations, analogous to machine-learned interatomic potentials. This bypasses repeatedly solving the electronic problem during spin dynamics simulations while retaining nonlinear long-range interactions.

entry.title: Benchmarking LLM Competence on Logical Inference over Probability Operators

author.name: Nayera Hasan, Jack Greff, Alvin Grissom II

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark of 14,320 procedurally generated prompts testing whether LLMs can reason validly over gradable epistemic modals such as probably, might, and must, across fifteen inference templates with systematic variation of question form and negation. Procedural generation is used to separate principled symbolic inference from surface pattern matching.

entry.title: AutoSupervision: Closing the Feedback Loop in Scientific Workflows with Grounded Revision Verification

author.name: Haobo Li, Eunseo Jung, Wenxiao Zhao, Feng Liu, Jiong Wang, Kaiyi Xu, Zijie Guo, Zixin Chen, Ben Fei, Fenghua Ling, Lei Bai

entry.summary: AutoSupervision uses transparent peer-review records (reviewer comments, author responses, revised manuscripts) as natural supervision to check whether manuscript revisions actually resolve reviewer concerns with grounded evidence. It targets a missing verification step in AI-assisted scientific workflows.

entry.title: Would You Walk to the Car Wash? Revealing the Salience Bias of Large Language Models in Commonsense Reasoning

author.name: Zheng Wu, Chenhao Xue, Shijie Zheng, Yijie Lu, Cheng Yang, Zhuosheng Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces salience bias, where models fixate on irrelevant explicit details such as numbers and ignore implicit physical or commonsense prerequisites, and builds the SaliTrap benchmark across four trap dimensions. Evaluation of 12 frontier models tests whether the failure reflects missing knowledge or suppression under misleading framing.

entry.title: ReDiPPO: Reference-Guided Value Calibration and Discrepancy-Aware Token Reweighting for Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Zhenrong Zhang, Fei Wu, Jun Du, Jianshu Zhang, Si Wei

entry.summary: ReDiPPO improves PPO for mathematical reasoning by calibrating the critic against a reference and reweighting tokens according to discrepancy signals. The goal is more reliable token-level credit assignment under long horizons and sparse outcome rewards.

entry.title: GLM-RAG: Graph Language Models for Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Maya Arseven, Anette Frank, Beni Egressy, Johann Higl, Moritz Plenz

entry.summary: Introduces a graph language model retriever for knowledge-graph RAG and compares it head-to-head with GNN-based and vector-search retrievers on single-hop and multi-hop questions. The study emphasizes transferability to unseen domains, where fine-tuned graph language models appear favorable.

entry.title: 4DHumanDiff: Direct Text-to-4DGS Generation for Consistent 360-Degree Dynamic Humans

author.name: Renlong Wu, Haoran Chen, Yuxiang Wei, Xiaowei Jin, Wangmeng Zuo, Hui Li

entry.summary: 4DHumanDiff generates dynamic 360-degree human assets directly as 4D Gaussian Splatting representations from text, using a 3D U-Net backbone with temporal attention. This avoids the usual pipeline of synthesizing videos and then fitting a 4D representation, which is costly and view-inconsistent.

entry.title: FootprintNet: State-Transition-Guided Dynamic Footprint Learning for Multi-temporal Remote Sensing Change Detection

author.name: Haotian Zhang, Hao Chen, Han Guo, Zhengxia Zou, Zhenwei Shi

entry.summary: Defines urban building dynamics detection, which recovers the temporal intervals of change rather than a single final change label, and proposes FootprintNet with state-transition guidance for multi-temporal satellite imagery. Enables characterization of recurrent construction and demolition activity.

entry.title: ViP-Rig: Visual-Prompted Controllable Rigging

author.name: Zihan Qin, Mingze Sun, Yifan Mao, Jialei Xu, Jingfeng Guo, Changrong Hu, Wenbo Zhao, Junjun Jiang, Xianming Liu

entry.summary: Presents a visual-prompt-driven rigging framework where user-drawn or edited 2D skeleton and rigidity sketches are injected into frozen pretrained backbones, supporting both prompt-first rigging and iterative result editing. Adds explicit artist control missing from geometry-only automatic rigging.

entry.title: AuricularWorld: Hierarchical Action-Guided World Modeling for Fine-Grained Auricular Structure Segmentation from CT Scans

author.name: Jingwen Yang, Senmao Wang, Luoyao Kang, Runmeng Cui, Keying Zhang, Yunjia Bao, Haifan Gong, Lin Lin, Haiyue Jiang

entry.summary: Applies a world-model-style deterministic recurrent state-space module inside an encoder-decoder to enable iterative anatomical reasoning for fine-grained auricular cartilage segmentation in CT, handling nested and overlapping clinical labels. Moves beyond single-pass feed-forward prediction.

entry.title: Sign Language Question Answering: A New Task, Benchmark, and Baseline for Sign Language Understanding

author.name: Shiwei Gan, Lichen Wang, Xiao Liu, Yafeng Yin, Kuizhuang Liu, Sanglu Lu, Lei Xie

entry.summary: Proposes Sign Language Question Answering, a new task where models must answer arbitrary natural-language questions about sign language videos rather than mapping to fixed glosses or translations, plus a benchmark and baseline. The aim is to test genuine semantic understanding of sign videos instead of memorized sequence mappings.

entry.title: ReGenVC: End-to-End Real-Time Generative Video Coding at Ultra-Low Bitrate

author.name: Zheyuan Zhang, Johnson Wu

entry.summary: ReGenVC compresses talking-head video to roughly 26 kB for a 77-frame clip by transmitting a neurally compressed reference frame plus pose keypoints, then reconstructing with a four-step distilled diffusion transformer in real time. It reports about a tenfold bitrate reduction versus x264/x265 at comparable perceived quality.

entry.title: It's Not Just More Demos: Counterfactual Action Sensitivity Coverage for Data-Efficient Robust Robot Imitation

author.name: Giovanni D'urso, Kaushik Roy, Nicholas Lawrance, Brendan Tidd

entry.summary: CFNBC selects which additional demonstrations to collect for visuomotor policies by generating paired clean and nuisance observations that preserve the expert action and measuring where the policy is most action-sensitive to task-irrelevant visual changes. The goal is targeted robustness repair instead of indiscriminate data scaling.

entry.title: Failure Detection for Surgical Robot Imitation Policies via Flow-Matching World Modeling

author.name: Zhefeng Huang, Yilin Cai, Ankit Patel, Mohammad Hajiha, Brendan Browne, Yue Chen

entry.summary: FoMo-FD detects failures of surgical imitation policies by learning an action-conditioned flow-matching world model of short-horizon visual dynamics and scoring how improbable observed transitions are. It addresses scarce failure data and the tradeoff between missed detections and disruptive false alarms.

entry.title: LabEvolver: Training-Free Experience Evolution for Safe and Grounded Wet-Lab Agents

author.name: Jingya Wang, Yuyang Gao, Liuzhenghao Lv, Yonghong Tian, Yuyang Liu

entry.summary: LabEvolver gives wet-lab agents episodic memory without training, pairing an inner loop for grounded perception, planning, and safety validation with an outer loop that distills completed trajectories into reusable skill, strategy, and safety experience. It reports large reductions in pH-regulation completion time and safety-gate intercepts on real robotic solution preparation, plus gains on ALFWorld over long continual task sequences.

entry.title: RoboBRIDGE: A Modular Framework for Bridging Policies to Robust Real-World Robotic Agents

author.name: Sihyung Yoon, Minjong Yoo, Sanghyun Ahn, Seojeong Choi, Honguk Woo

entry.summary: RoboBRIDGE wraps a pretrained vision-language-action model in an orchestration layer of five modules (monitor, perceptor, planner, and others) to add failure recovery, long-horizon consistency, and robustness to observation, task, and embodiment shifts. The claim is a general recipe for turning an action predictor into a deployable agent without retraining.

entry.title: SemAnCorr: Semantic Anchored Correspondence for Zero-Shot Manipulation Skill Transfer

author.name: Xiaoxiang Dong, William Baron, Hongyi Chen, Uksang Yoo, Jeffrey Ichnowski, Weiming Zhi

entry.summary: SemAnCorr establishes dense correspondence between functionally similar but geometrically different objects by selecting semantically consistent anchor regions through joint pose-correspondence optimization and propagating constraints across the surface with functional maps. It is training-free and aimed at zero-shot manipulation skill transfer.

entry.title: Research directions in condensation: varieties of objectivity

author.name: SamEisenstat

entry.summary: The first installment of a survey of research directions for condensation, a mathematical theory of how descriptions of the world organize into conceptual parts, covering random variable models, latent variable models, and an objectivity theorem. It previews concepts such as almost perfect condensation and algorithmic-information condensation.

entry.title: Position: Evaluation Scores Are Perishable Knowledge Claims

author.name: Sankalp Gilda, Shlok Gilda

entry.summary: This position paper argues that aggregating automated metrics, LLM-judge ratings, human assessments, and benchmark scores by averaging produces trust inflation, where confidence exceeds the weakest underlying signal. It proposes treating evaluation results as epistemic claims with formality, scope, and expiration windows as contamination and distribution shift accumulate.

entry.title: Evidence-Ledger Adjudication for Claim-Evidence Traceability

author.name: Gengyu Chen, Yongjie Yu, Weiling Wang

entry.summary: This work builds an evidence-ledger workflow that pairs each generated claim with an evidence packet, assigns a support relation, and routes unsupported or contradicted claims back to the author. On a 2,335-row blind benchmark assembled from AVeriTeC, CLIMATE-FEVER, and SciFact, the agent ledger reaches about 0.68 relation accuracy versus 0.38 for the best non-agent baseline.

entry.title: Do Methods Support the Claims? Intra-Paper Verification for Peer Review

author.name: Ranjitha Shivaprasad Ballakuraya, Arash Mahyari, Ashok Srinivasan

entry.summary: The paper introduces intra-paper claim verification, checking whether the methods actually deliver the contributions a paper claims, rather than only comparing claims against prior literature. This targets a common human reviewer objection that current automated novelty assessment systems ignore.

entry.title: IFCMemoryBench: Evaluating Long-Term Memory of LLM-Based Agents in BIM Information Retrieval
