author.name: Changyu Du, Alexander Vosseler, Filippo Mazza, Andr\'e Borrmann

entry.summary: IFCMemoryBench tests long-term agent memory in building information modelling, where an agent must query large IFC models while recalling project specifications, client decisions, and engineering conventions from earlier conversations. It shifts memory evaluation from open-domain chat recall to acting over a live structured professional environment.

entry.title: Aligning LLM-Simulated and Human Examinees for Psychometric Calibration: A Cognitive Diagnostic Profiling Approach

author.name: Wenjie Zhou, Yunting Liu, Renjiao Tang, Mark Wilson

entry.summary: Cognitive Diagnostic Profiling prompts LLMs to simulate examinees with diverse attribute-mastery patterns rendered as natural-language profiles, addressing the tendency of simulated responses to be too accurate and too uniform for psychometric calibration. Eight LLM configurations were evaluated on the classic fraction-subtraction dataset with 536 examinees.

entry.title: Dual Inversion for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models: From Both Prompt and Noise Perspectives

author.name: Xiaolong Liu, Junjian Li, Yuan Xiao, Jiaqi Deng, Dayong Ye, Tianqing Zhu, Huan Huo

entry.summary: The paper argues prompt inversion alone is insufficient for reverse-engineering text-to-image outputs because latent noise carries structural information, and proposes joint inversion of both prompt and noise. This improves visual fidelity over gradient-based methods that produce artifacts and gradient-free methods that lose fine detail.

entry.title: Phoneme- vs. Character-Level Targets and Selective State-Space Models for Intracortical Brain-to-Text

author.name: Lucas Zamora Vera, Jose A. Gonzalez-Lopez

entry.summary: A controlled 2x2 study on the Brain-to-Text 25 benchmark compares GRU versus hybrid Mamba decoders and phonetic versus character output targets under one CTC training protocol. The recurrent phonetic baseline remains strongest, with the selective state-space hybrid competitive but not superior.

entry.title: Defending Against Backdoor Attacks via Alignment Checking in Model-Contrastive Federated Learning

author.name: Hongliang Zhang, Zhongyuan Yu, Guijuan Wang, Tianqing He, Wenshuo Ma, Xiaosong Zhang, Jiguo Yu

entry.summary: FedDAB defends federated learning against backdoor attacks in two phases: a model-contrastive regularizer that tightens direction and magnitude consistency among benign local updates, then an alignment check that flags anomalous updates. It targets the confound where statistical heterogeneity makes benign updates look deviant.

entry.title: Schreier-Coset Graph Rewiring

author.name: Aryan Mishra, Randy Martinez, Lizhen Lin

entry.summary: This work rewires graphs for GNNs by augmenting the input with a Schreier coset graph derived from a special linear group, providing theoretical spectral-gap guarantees while adding far fewer edges than typical rewiring methods. It targets over-squashing, where structural bottlenecks block long-range message passing.

entry.title: Understanding Submodular Information Measure Based Objectives for Representation Learning: A Variance and Separation Perspective

author.name: Rishabh Iyer, Truong Pham, Anay Majee

entry.summary: This paper builds a unified theory connecting submodular information measures used as representation-learning objectives to classical statistical quantities, showing for example that graph-cut total information recovers within-class variance and log-determinant variants capture other structure. It explains geometrically what different submodular objectives actually optimize.

entry.title: Chem World: A Large-Scale Benchmark and Physics-Informed Framework for Trustworthy Chemical Property Prediction

author.name: Tianyou Bai, Huan Wang, Mingchen Gao, Fangyue Lin, Pinze Ren, Zhenlin Zhao, Siming Dong

entry.summary: Chem World consolidates 17 chemical datasets with over 800,000 molecular samples into a unified benchmark for property prediction spanning density, conductivity, solubility, and more, paired with a physics-informed modeling framework. It aims to fix fragmented datasets and inconsistent evaluation protocols in chemical ML.

entry.title: Persistent Gaussian Perturbations Prevent Oversmoothing in Recurrent Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Mostafa Haghir Chehreghani

entry.summary: This paper proves that injecting persistent Gaussian noise after each propagation step in a recurrent GNN yields a geometrically ergodic Markov chain whose stationary distribution retains representation diversity, preventing the oversmoothing collapse of deep message passing. The analysis treats the network as a stochastic dynamical system.

entry.title: TopoFormer: Topology Meets Attention for Graph Learning

author.name: Md Joshem Uddin, Astrit Tola, Cuneyt Gurcan Akcora, Baris Coskunuzer

entry.summary: TopoFormer encodes graph topology into short ordered token sequences via a filtration-slicing module, avoiding expensive persistence diagram computation while feeding multi-scale structural information to a Transformer. It provides stability guarantees and parallelizable computation for graph-level embeddings.

entry.title: Gradient-free Task-Conditioned Retrieval for On-Device In-Context Learning

author.name: Xinyu Luo, Hui Liu, Yihua Shao, Junyi Yang, Arindam Basu, Haoliang Li

entry.summary: CoRA turns a frozen encoder into a task-conditioned demonstration retriever for on-device in-context learning without gradients, using closed-form ridge alignment to an output-derived conditioning space plus low-rank compression. It targets retrieval quality under tight compute, memory, and data-exposure budgets on edge devices.

entry.title: Robust Estimation of Sparse Numerical Vectors under Local Differential Privacy

author.name: Puning Zhao, Zhikun Zhang, Shaowei Wang, Sheng Yue, Bangzhou Xin, Tianhang Zheng, Pengfei Zhang, Xiaochun Cao

entry.summary: Addresses poisoning-robust mean estimation of sparse numeric vectors under local differential privacy, where multi-item users give attackers a larger output space to hide in. The proposed Randomized Projection with Clipping protocol has each user project local data onto a server-supplied random binary vector and clip it, limiting attacker leverage.

entry.title: FinSMART: Financial Sentiment Analysis for Algorithmic Trading through Market-Aligned Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Giorgos Iacovides, Wuyang Zhou, Danilo Mandic

entry.summary: FinSMART trains financial sentiment models with reinforcement learning against realized market outcomes rather than static human annotations, adding a signal-extraction pipeline to cope with noisy, nonstationary market feedback. The goal is sentiment signals that adapt as market regimes change and translate into trading performance.

entry.title: Uncertainty quantification for trustworthy deep learning: Methods and measures

author.name: H. Martin Gillis, Thomas Trappenberg

entry.summary: A structured survey of uncertainty quantification for deep learning that separates the method producing a predictive distribution from the measure used to summarize its uncertainty, organizing approaches into five families with emphasis on efficient ensembles and single-pass approximations. Positioned as a practical reference for safety-critical deployment.

entry.title: Reflected diffusion, no-flux continuity equations and confined Lagrangian flows in bounded domains

author.name: Rama Cont

entry.summary: Establishes conditions under which a density-flux pair solving a no-flux continuity equation in a bounded domain admits a regular Lagrangian flow that stays inside the domain, motivated by marginal flows of reflected diffusions. The key observation is that tangency of the velocity removes singular boundary divergence contributions, enabling classical transport theory to apply.

entry.title: Doubly Robust Functional Representation Learning for Longitudinal Causal Inference with Irregular Histories

author.name: Mengfei Ran, Yifeng Shen, Ruijie Guan

entry.summary: DR-FRL is a cross-fitted doubly robust workflow for longitudinal causal inference when patient histories arrive as irregular functional fragments such as labs, sensor streams, and image summaries. Functional encoders learn estimand-targeted state representations while nuisance heads and influence-function-targeted validation preserve efficiency properties that pure prediction losses do not guarantee.

entry.title: Semantic-Aligned Structural Abstraction for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Wei Chen, Junkai Li, Tongguan Wang, Hui Liu, Feiyue Xue, Chuanxiang Ma, Ying Sha

entry.summary: Uses visual illusions as a diagnostic to evaluate perception and reasoning jointly in large vision-language models, arguing that existing evaluations test perception alone or narrow domains like math and code. The authors build IllusionReasoning from real-world illusion imagery to see whether models can recover objective reality behind misleading appearances.

entry.title: RRM: Experience-Driven Reflective Retrieval Memory for Long-Horizon Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Jingxiang Fan, Junbao Zhuo, Bochao Zou

entry.summary: RRM augments an entity-centric multimodal memory graph with a reflective experience memory that distills reusable retrieval strategies from past task trajectories. The focus is on diagnosing and fixing retrieval failures rather than only deciding what to store for long-video reasoning.

entry.title: MemTxn: A Transaction Boundary for Source-Supported Updates and Complete-State Recovery in Agent Memory

author.name: Hanshuai Cui, Zhiqing Tang, Zhi Yao, Fanshuai Meng, Qianli Ma, Weijia Jia

entry.summary: MemTxn adds a database-style transaction boundary outside the answering model for agent memory, verifying that each write is supported by its source, resolving conflicting versions temporally, and restoring visible state after faults via a snapshot journal. It targets error persistence and corruption in writable long-lived memory.

entry.title: Can Large Language Models Execute Parent Orders?

author.name: Zane Shen, Xinli Xu, Guangyi Zhang, Jialong Chen, Jinsong Zhou, Cong Chen, Guibao Shen, Dongyu Yan, Luozhou Wang, Zhen Yang

entry.summary: First systematic study of using LLMs for parent-order execution in algorithmic trading, with PACE decomposing the problem into long-horizon planning and short-horizon execution. It aims to avoid both fixed market assumptions and task-specific training.

entry.title: Witness Evidence Portfolios: Single-Prefill Risk Detection for Closed Multimodal Answers

author.name: Fexiang Liu, Shiye Wang, Qiang Qiu, Zheng Wang

entry.summary: Witness Evidence Portfolios detect risky multimodal answers at inference time by tracing, layer by layer, which visual contributions support or contradict the predicted answer during the same prefill pass that produced it. Signals are summarized as interpretable evidence-provenance and signed-concentration routes for triage or routing to a stronger model.

entry.title: ENCORE: Event-Assisted Complementary Motion Refinement for Learned Video Compression

author.name: Shuhan Ye, Hongbin Yu, Chenqi Kong, Pingchuan Ma, Chong Wang, Jun Wan, Qixin Zhang

entry.summary: Adds event camera signals to learned video compression, decomposing RGB and event features into common and modality-specific motion representations to refine motion estimates under blur, occlusion, and illumination change. Targets failure cases of RGB-only temporal modeling.

entry.title: Split and Drive: Dual-Axis Disentanglement for Real-Time Gaussian Head Avatars

author.name: MD Wahiduzzaman Khan, Mingshan Jia, Xiaolin Zhang, En Yu, Kaska Musial-Gabrys

entry.summary: Proposes a single-image Gaussian head avatar system that internalizes per-frame driving to remove external tracking latency at inference and splits the avatar into three specialized Gaussian branches for geometrically distinct facial regions. Also flags that prior work excludes tracking latency from reported speeds.

entry.title: Space2Ground 2.0: A Multi-Source Dataset and Framework for Agricultural Monitoring through Fusion of Street-Level and Satellite Imagery

author.name: Iason Tsardanidis, Alkiviadis Koukos, George Choumos, Vasileios Sitokontantinou, Charalampos Kontoes

entry.summary: Presents a multi-source agricultural monitoring dataset and pipeline fusing Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 time series with crowdsourced vehicle-mounted street-level imagery linked to individual parcels. Addresses the overhead-only viewpoint limitation and cloud gaps of satellite monitoring.

entry.title: MIND: Multimodal Intent-Driven Network via Diffusion Transformers for Medical Image Fusion

author.name: Yunzhan Fu, Xiangyu Shen, Yifei Sun, Yuhan Chen, Jian Wu, Hongxia Xu

entry.summary: Uses a biomedical language model to generate diagnostic intent text that conditions a diffusion transformer for medical image fusion, plus a multi-scale latent adapter to restore 2D spatial continuity lost in token flattening. Replaces uniform global fusion rules with pathology-aware intent guidance.

entry.title: One Future, Every Robot: Label-Efficient Collective-State Prediction with Decentralized JEPA

author.name: Alan-Barsag Gazzaev, Alexey Garvilov, Sergey Muravyov

entry.summary: CS-JEPA is a recurrent joint-embedding predictive architecture in which every robot in a swarm predicts the same shared future collective state token field from only local histories and small bandwidth-limited messages, with no global pooling or recorded future actions. Frozen representations are evaluated with ridge probes on very few globally labeled episodes.

entry.title: Value Generalisation 3: Pre-aligned AIs

author.name: Stuart_Armstrong

entry.summary: The third post sketches pre-aligned AI, systems whose moral behaviour would improve automatically as their world models and capabilities improve, by binding normative concepts to empirical ones that the system refines through learning. The stated goal is to invert the usual safety tax dynamic so that careful actors gain from scaling while reckless ones must impose restrictions on their own systems.

entry.title: Audio-Anchored Fusion of Multi-Ratio DiT Reconstruction Residuals for Cross-Domain Audio Deepfake Detection

author.name: Haotian Mo, Jie Liu, Siqi Shen, Songzhu Mei, Xinhai Chen, Xiangyang Wang, Yigui Feng, Shuai Li, Gencheng Liu, Keqi Yang, Qinglin Wang

entry.summary: The method uses a diffusion transformer trained only on genuine speech as a frozen reconstruction probe, computing residual maps at multiple masking ratios and fusing them as a gated correction to WavLM features for audio deepfake detection. It reports competitive equal-error rates on ASVspoof 5 and in-the-wild evaluation with multi-seed variance reported.

entry.title: Crossing-Free Probabilistic K-Line Forecasts Without Retraining

author.name: Runyao Yu, Yuchen Tao, Yujie Chen, Wentao Wang, Derek W. Bunn

entry.summary: KQSP is a training-free, parameter-free projection method that reconciles probabilistic open-high-low-close price forecasts so that neither quantiles nor candlestick relationships cross. It applies to outputs of any forecasting model without retraining, whereas prior fixes address only one inconsistency type.

entry.title: MUGEN: A Unified Framework for Efficient Motion Understanding and Generation

author.name: Zhankai Ye, Yukai Jin, Bingyang Wei, Bofan Li, Yusen Wu, Fangyi Li, Shangqian Gao, Xin Liu

entry.summary: MUGEN is a unified motion-language model designed to handle both understanding and generation without stacked residual codebooks, long autoregressive rollouts, or many-step denoising heads, arguing that heavyweight decoding machinery adds cost without helping understanding. It targets efficient grounding of human motion in language.

entry.title: Certifying when decision-time information justifies adaptive experimentation

author.name: Jia Bi, Samuel Pinilla, Chenyang Zhu

entry.summary: The authors study the deployment memory footprint of tabular foundation models like TabPFN and show that standard compression techniques cut memory by up to roughly 7.6 times, reducing requirements by nearly 87 percent with comparable accuracy. It addresses a practical gap since most attention on these models has focused on accuracy.

entry.title: Enhancing Irregular Time Series Forecasting with Continuous-Time Modeling Framework

author.name: Tianen Shen, Zhengyu Li, Yutong Li, Xiangfei Qiu, Xingjian Wu, Bin Yang, Jilin Hu

entry.summary: WrapFlow provides a continuous-time framework for irregular multivariate time-series forecasting that avoids both discretization preprocessing and expensive ODE solvers. It targets asynchronous, non-uniformly sampled data common in healthcare and environmental sensing.

entry.title: From Expert Reduction to Behavioral Divergence: Tracing Numerical State through Sparse MoE Inference

author.name: Tianyang Zhu

entry.summary: This study shows that mathematically equivalent expert-aggregation orders inside sparse mixture-of-experts inference produce measurably different generations, tracing how tiny floating-point differences at one layer fork into distinct continuation basins. Experiments use the existing DeepSeek-V4-Flash model with frozen local MoE state and varied accumulation semantics.

entry.title: LM-GRASP: Instance-Specific Language Models for Combinatorial Construction via Online Imitation Learning

author.name: Mohand Mezmaz, Gr\'egoire Danoy

entry.summary: LM-GRASP trains a small decoder-only Transformer from scratch on each individual combinatorial optimization instance, treating GRASP's randomized construction phase as online imitation of a local-search expert oracle. This avoids costly pretraining and the poor out-of-distribution generalization of offline-trained neural constructors.

entry.title: On-Policy and Off-Policy Learning for Large Action Spaces

author.name: Imad Aouali

entry.summary: This doctoral thesis surveys and extends policy learning for contextual bandits with very large action spaces, covering on-policy Bayesian methods such as a mixed-effect Thompson sampling variant and off-policy techniques for handling high-variance importance weights and sparse coverage. It consolidates methods relevant to recommendation and interactive systems.

entry.title: Psych-ECA: A Reproducible Semi-Synthetic Benchmark for Synthetic Control Arms in Longitudinal Psychiatry

author.name: Aakash Bhagat, Shashank Choudhary

entry.summary: Psych-ECA releases a reproducible semi-synthetic benchmark for external and synthetic control arms in longitudinal psychiatry, targeting properties regulators care about such as uncertainty calibration, robustness to informative observation times, and induced false-positive rates in go/no-go decisions. It substitutes for real trial data that is access-restricted and lacks counterfactual ground truth.

entry.title: HOMER: Huber-of-Means for Efficient and Robust Estimation in Hilbert Spaces

author.name: Kisung You, Boram Cho

entry.summary: HOMER aggregates block means through a radial Huber center to interpolate between median-of-means robustness and empirical-mean efficiency for heavy-tailed data in Hilbert spaces. The authors prove a majority theorem and MOM-order deviation bounds under only finite second moments, with asymptotic linearity for the pseudo-Huber variant.

entry.title: Calibrate Before Reason: Robust Visual Token Reduction against Semantic Drift in VLMs

author.name: Jiasheng Li, Zhong Ji, Yan Zhang, Huihui Li

entry.summary: CaRe is a training-free framework that calibrates compressed visual token representations before reasoning, arguing that pruning or merging visual tokens causes semantic drift away from the original representation. It reframes token reduction around semantic consistency rather than pure redundancy removal.

entry.title: AdaAnchor4D: Anchor-Conditioned Spatiotemporal Feature Aggregation for Monocular UAV 4D Reconstruction

author.name: Peiyi Xu, Junpeng Zhang, Guanbin Li, Ronghua Shang, Mingtao Feng, Le Dong, Weisheng Dong, Guangming Shi, Jie Feng

entry.summary: Proposes anchor-conditioned spatiotemporal feature aggregation for dynamic Gaussian reconstruction of monocular UAV urban video, adapting feature combination to spatially heterogeneous motion patterns instead of fixed plane-wise schemes. Reduces ghosting and blur in dynamic regions of large scenes.

entry.title: What to Remove, What to Preserve: Dual-Ambiguity Rectification for All-in-One Image Restoration

author.name: Cencen Liu (University of Electronic Science and Technology of China), Wen Yin (University of Electronic Science and Technology of China), Dongyang Zhang (University of Electronic Science and Technology of China), Dongmin Li (University of Electronic Science and Technology of China), Shan Zhao (Jiigan Technology), Bing Su (Jiigan Technology), Tao He (University of Electronic Science and Technology of China), Jielei Wang (University of Electronic Science and Technology of China), Guoming Lu (University of Electronic Science and Technology of China)

entry.summary: Characterizes all-in-one image restoration failures as dual ambiguity in channel-wise modulation and spatial response, and proposes a degradation archetype representation with simplex constraints to structure degradation states. Aims to reduce content corruption and residual artifacts across mixed degradations.

entry.title: Can AI agents conduct open-ended AI research? Early evidence from two case studies

author.name: Peter Kirgis, Sayash Kapoor, Andrew Schwartz, Stephan Rabanser, David Africa, Konstantinos Voudouris, Viet Nguyen, Toby Pilditch, Magda Dubois, Harry Coppock, Cozmin Ududec, Nitya Nadgir, Matilda Orona, Tilman Bayer, Derrick Chan-Sew, Yue Ling, Abhishek Shetty, Helen Toner, Gillian Hadfield, Seth Lazar, Steve Newman, Shoshannah Tekofsky, Rishi Bommasani, Arvind Narayanan

entry.summary: Already covered in Research yesterday, This study introduces shadow evaluations, where frontier agents attempt the central open-ended research question of an unpublished high-quality paper and the original authors grade the output. Applied to two NeurIPS submissions with six days of agent effort, it offers rare direct evidence on whether agents can perform open-ended AI research rather than narrow verifiable tasks.

entry.title: Belief-Guided Decision Making with Uncertainty Gating in the Game of Go

author.name: Mehrad Yaghoubi, Azam Bastanfard, Abbas Jalilvand, Ashkan Rezaei

entry.summary: This work separates a belief head from the policy head in a Go agent, using the belief module as an internal critic and simulator to reduce dependence on heavy Monte Carlo tree search. The aim is competent play with high inference rates on consumer hardware while curbing confidently fatal moves.

entry.title: The Age of AI Agents Demands A New Scientific Paradigm To Sustain Trustworthy Science

author.name: Belinda Mo

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that autonomous research agents widen the gap between scientific output volume and human verification capacity, and that peer review assumptions break when contributors cannot be questioned or sanctioned. It proposes criteria for verification infrastructure emphasizing observable-by-default workflows and scalable checking.

entry.title: GuidedRAG: Semantic Steering of Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Matthijs Jansen op de Haar, Tobias St\"ahle, Lorenzo Gatti

entry.summary: GuidedRAG adds a semantic selection stage that constrains the knowledge base before retrieval, aligning the search space with user intent instead of building more complex retrieval structures. The authors report retrieval relevance gains of roughly 14 to 16 percent and orders-of-magnitude reduction in retrieval overhead.

entry.title: Pramana: A Composable, Domain-Specific Backend for Empirical Networking Research

author.name: Jaber Daneshamooz, Eugene Vuong, Alagappan Ramanathan, Manni Moghimi, Haarika Manda, Satyam Kumar, Snithik Thode, Satyandra Guthula, Sylee Beltiukov, Dongsu Han, Tarun Mangla, Sangeetha Abdu Jyothi, Walter Willinger, Arpit Gupta

entry.summary: Pramana is a composable domain-specific backend for empirical networking research that lets researchers configure realistic bottleneck links, generate concurrent traffic from real applications, and collect service-quality metrics without rebuilding infrastructure per experiment. The authors argue the ideation-to-data gap will worsen as AI-assisted hypothesis generation accelerates.

entry.title: A Graph-Native Bitemporal Memory Store for Conversational AI Agents

author.name: Alp Niksarli, Gopesh Baheti

entry.summary: The paper describes an agent-local persistent memory store built on a Neo4j property graph with HNSW vector indexes and a full bitemporal model that separates when a fact was true from when it was recorded. This supports point-in-time semantic retrieval and privacy-preserving local memory without burning context budget or sending data to third-party memory services.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Face-to-Speech Synthesis via Latent Space Adaptation of a Style-Diffusion TTS Model

author.name: Carlos Mu\~noz-Romero, Jose A. Gonzalez-Lopez

entry.summary: This face-to-speech system predicts a plausible voice from a single static facial image by training a lightweight face adapter that maps face-recognition features into the style space of a frozen StyleTTS 2 model. Evaluated on held-out LRS3 identities, the synthesized speech achieves naturalness scores matching or exceeding ground-truth recordings.

entry.title: SciFigAlign: Scoring Scientific Figures by Fine-tuned Alignment of Visuals with Manuscript Evidence

author.name: Chuanzhi Xu, Zihan Deng, Huiqi Liang, Chengkun Yue, Zhanlin Cui, Pengfei Ye, Weidong Cai

entry.summary: SciFigAlign fine-tunes a model to score scientific figures by aligning visual content with manuscript evidence, judging legibility, faithfulness to claims, and visual hierarchy rather than generic aesthetics. It argues classic image-quality metrics, CLIP similarity, and zero-shot vision-language judges all fail at this task.

entry.title: Improving Item Discoverability in e-Commerce Search via Related Intent Generation

author.name: Ji Xin, Xiao Xiao, Ishan Bhatt, Vinesh Gudla, Trace Levinson, Raochuan Fan, Shishir Kumar Prasad, Prakash Putta, Tejaswi Tenneti

entry.summary: An industrial system for e-commerce and grocery search that uses LLMs to generate implicit user intents offline, then distills that behavior into a cheaper online model, expanding recall toward substitute and complementary items while keeping relevance. It documents the cost-quality tradeoff of generative retrieval at production scale.

entry.title: PlatformBid: An Auto-Bidding Benchmark from a Unified Advertising Platform's Perspective

author.name: Shengtian Yang, Yewen Li, Peng Jiang, Zhiyi Lyu, Bo An, Peng Jiang, Qingpeng Cai, Lei Feng

entry.summary: PlatformBid is an auto-bidding benchmark that evaluates algorithms from the perspective of a unified ad platform owning supply, demand, and exchange functions, so objectives include platform revenue rather than only advertiser conversions. It provides an environment for a setting that current DSP-centric benchmarks do not represent.

entry.title: A Lightweight Foundation Model for Collider Physics with Multi-Domain Adaptation

author.name: Liangyu Wu, Qibin Liu, Alexander Yue, Julia Gonski

entry.summary: NEXUS is a roughly 3M-parameter autoencoder pretrained without supervision on large-scale LHC collision track data, then fine-tuned for kinematic regression and event classification with small labeled sets and additionally tested on out-of-domain scientific datasets. It shows that very small physics foundation models can transfer usefully.

entry.title: RIPPLE: Generating Multi-Channel Phase, Not Recovering It

author.name: Jaehyuk Lee, Yeajin Lee, Dayeon Shin, Donghun Lee

entry.summary: RIPPLE argues that for multi-channel signals such as spatial audio and three-component seismograms the physical content lives in inter-channel phase relationships, which channel-independent phase recovery cannot produce and magnitude-based metrics cannot detect. It therefore generates phase directly rather than recovering it after magnitude synthesis.

entry.title: Building a User Foundation Model for the Open Web

author.name: Solal Vernier, Ivan Can Arisoy, Merwan Barlier, Bla\v{z} \v{S}krlj

entry.summary: This paper builds a user foundation model for open-web real-time bidding, where user identity is fragmented, sessions are short, and much traffic has no history at all. It replaces the standard aggregated-counter representation with sequential modeling suited to this privacy-constrained, non-persistent-identity regime.

entry.title: Oracle-Budgeted Molecular Optimization with Short-Term Graph Memory

author.name: Jiannan Yang, Veronika Thost, Xiang Ling, Tengfei Ma

entry.summary: This paper adds a short-term graph memory module to fragment-based molecular generators so that previously evaluated molecules train an online GNN surrogate that pre-screens candidates before spending scarce oracle calls. It improves top-10 scores at unchanged oracle budget without altering the base generator.

entry.title: Same Graph Cross-Task Transfer in GNNs: Protocols and Predictors

author.name: Neelam Akula, Surbhi Kumar, Murat Kantarcioglu, Baris Coskunuzer

entry.summary: The authors define a leakage-free protocol for evaluating transfer between node classification and link prediction on the same graph, fixing splits, excluding evaluated edges from message passing, and using fixed negatives. Across three backbones they find transfer is strongly directional, with node classification helping link prediction on homophilous graphs.

entry.title: KAISEN: Reproducible Subgroup Fairness Auditing for Clinical Risk Models

author.name: Sparsh Roy, Samuel Girmachew, Nishita Chavan

entry.summary: KAISEN is a five-phase fairness audit pipeline for clinical risk models covering subgroup stratification, disparity measurement, mechanism diagnostics, mitigation, and drift monitoring, deliberately stress-tested until components fail. Evaluation spans 16 synthetic disease tasks and 15 social-determinant axes.

entry.title: Causal Discovery with Inverted Self-attention for Multivariate Time Series

author.name: Yusen Liu, Yong Wang, Yifan Yin, Tianqing Zhu, Xiufeng Liu, Huan Huo

entry.summary: Proposes a transformer-based causal discovery method for multivariate time series that inverts tokens and sparsifies attention to surface latent and indirect causal links, paired with a global algorithm for assembling the causal structure. Aims to reduce spurious correlations in high-dimensional nonlinear settings.

entry.title: Fairness Pruning: Locating Demographic Bias in GLU-MLP Layers via Differential Activations

author.name: Pere Martra, Eugenio Mart\'inez C\'amara, Alfonso Ure\~na L\'opez

entry.summary: Fairness Pruning localizes demographic bias in gated-MLP transformer blocks by capturing differential activations on minimally contrastive prompt pairs at the down-projection input, identifying neurons that respond selectively to demographic attributes. Validation covers Llama-3.2 and Salamandra models up to three billion parameters with benchmark and qualitative generation tests.

entry.title: SCOPE: Supply-Chain Operations through Coupled Policies for End-to-End Coordination

author.name: Yunhao Liang, Xianqi Cao, Pujun Zhang, Yuan Qu, Yongzhi Qi, Ningxuan Kang, Max Z. J. Shen

entry.summary: SCOPE couples assortment selection, source assignment, replenishment frequency, and routing into a single learned end-to-end supply-chain planning policy instead of optimizing each department's module separately. The motivation is that these decisions feed each other, so siloed optimization produces stockouts and avoidable transport cost.

entry.title: LayerRAG-Bench: A Cross-Layer Reliability Benchmark for Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Musa Shams (Independent Researcher)

entry.summary: LayerRAG-Bench probes agentic RAG reliability across evidence, tool-contract, authorization, and session-state layers with 240 tasks, nine fault scenarios, and tens of thousands of live records over nine models from three major providers. It finds that schema normalization nearly eliminates schema-drift failures while stale evidence, missing tool output, denied permissions, and wrong-session context remain unrecovered, and that groundedness-only scoring produces many false positives.

entry.title: AHA-Memes: A Fine-Grained Multimodal Benchmark for Understanding Hate in Arabic Memes

author.name: Mohamed Bayan Kmainasi, Ali Ezzat Shahroor, Abul Hasnat, Md. Rafiul Biswas, Wajdi Zaghouani, Firoj Alam

entry.summary: AHA-Memes provides what the authors describe as the first large-scale Arabic hateful meme benchmark with fine-grained multi-label annotations of hate types and attack strategies, comprising 5,000 manually annotated memes plus roughly 66,000 silver-labeled examples. Multimodal baselines are benchmarked on the resource.

entry.title: DualAnchor: Preserving Language Priors and Improving Lexical Fidelity in Gloss-Free Sign Language Translation

author.name: Hongbin Zhang, Junhao Liu, Xuefeng Bai, Youcheng Pan, Yang Xiang, Kehai Chen

entry.summary: DualAnchor tackles two failures of LLM-backboned gloss-free sign language translation: degradation of the model's language prior producing disfluent output, and a lexical fidelity gap from sentence-level video-text alignment. It couples two complementary anchors to preserve fluency while enforcing lexical grounding.

entry.title: From Single- to Cross-Document: Benchmarking Multi-Granularity Event Analysis of Large Language Models

author.name: Tao Wen, Shuai Shao, Pei Ke, Xu Han, Jie Zou, Guannan Li, Tao Tian, Jinjie Qiu, Lan Wang, Ke Qin

entry.summary: MiGUE-Bench evaluates LLMs on event analysis across granularities from single documents to cross-document settings, supported by an LLM-driven self-correcting annotation pipeline for scalable labeling. It aims to fix restricted granularity, task design, and data sources in existing event extraction benchmarks.

entry.title: SciDataSailor: Deep Scientific Data Exploring

author.name: Jiyong Rao, Yicheng Qiu, Chi Zhang, Chunfeng Song, Runkai Zhao

entry.summary: Defines deep scientific data exploration as an agentic paradigm in which agents navigate real hierarchical data repositories, interpret heterogeneous file formats and schemas, execute analyses, and integrate cross-file evidence into grounded conclusions. SciDataSailor operationalizes this with an executable environment.

entry.title: TCA-SIR: Learning Target-Conditioned Abstractions for Scientific Inspiration Retrieval

author.name: Yuto Suzuki, Farnoush Banaei-Kashani

entry.summary: Reframes scientific inspiration retrieval as target-conditioned abstraction, retrieving transferable problem-solving principles extracted from candidate papers relative to a specific target problem rather than ranking by topical similarity. This is aimed at surfacing remote inspirations for hypothesis generation.

entry.title: Bunraku: Turning a Single Illustration into an Editable Live2D Character

author.name: Junhao Chen, Jingjia Mao, Dayong Li, Chenghai Li, Saining Zhang, Zhihao Li, Hao Zhao, Yufei Wang, Ruqi Huang

entry.summary: Bunraku is the first end-to-end system to convert a single illustration into a complete Live2D asset, producing ordered RGBA layers with occlusion completion, per-layer deformation meshes, and parameter-driven keypose vertex offsets. It automates a workflow that currently takes artists weeks.

entry.title: ProgFormer: Hierarchical Voxel Diffusion Transformer for Longitudinal Brain MRI Prediction

author.name: Dexuan Ding, Yuankai Qi, Luping Zhou, Jian Yang, Quan Z. Sheng, Ming-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: ProgFormer is a hierarchical voxel-space diffusion transformer that predicts future structural brain MRI while separating stable subject anatomy from subtle progression-related changes. It avoids latent compression losses that can obscure small localized disease changes.

entry.title: MPIE-Bench: Benchmarking Anatomically Plausible Multi-Person Interaction Editing

author.name: Jiajia Lin, Mingxuan Du, Tuowen Zhou, Benfeng Xu, Hongtao Xie

entry.summary: MPIE-Bench provides 2,500 video-mined editing triplets across 405 scenes and 14 interaction categories to test whether image editors can place multiple named people into physical contact without fused limbs, extra extremities, or interpenetrating bodies. MPIE-Eval adds axes that score contact-time geometry using a frozen multi-person pose model rather than saturating VLM checklists.

entry.title: MMOOC: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Out-of-Context Evaluation in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Wenjie Zhu, Yabin Zhang, Wenjun Zeng, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: MMOOC is a benchmark of over 41K image-question pairs distinguishing truly out-of-context questions that should be refused from shifted in-context questions that remain answerable. It measures whether multimodal models can refuse appropriately without becoming needlessly evasive.

entry.title: RefineSVG: Visual Feedback-Driven Reinforcement Learning for Image-to-SVG Generation

author.name: Shaobo Liu, Feiqiao Mao, Shuaishuai Zhou, Yan Zhan, Weiqi Tan, Zhiqiong Lu, Zhengping Liang

entry.summary: RefineSVG adds a single closed-loop visual feedback step to image-to-SVG generation: after an initial pass, an external renderer compares output against the target and a multi-dimensional residual map guides self-correction. This counters geometric drift and error accumulation from open-loop generation of thousands of code tokens.

entry.title: FDDWAN: A Frequency-Decoupled Diffusion Network for Watermarking Attack

author.name: Chunpeng Wang, Yuxin Li, Xiaoyu Wang, Jidong Yang, Suo Gao, Qi Li

entry.summary: Presents a wavelet-domain plus residual diffusion pipeline for removing invisible image watermarks while preserving perceptual fidelity. Framed as an attack method that stress-tests watermark robustness.

entry.title: CoRE-UIR: Prior-guided common and residual experts for efficient all-in-one remote sensing image restoration

author.name: Zaiyan Zhang, Qiangqiang Yuan, Jie Li, Ziyang Lihe, Yu Wan, Yuzeng Chen, Xin Su, Liangpei Zhang

entry.summary: Presents an all-in-one remote sensing image restoration framework that decomposes mixture-of-experts capacity into a shared common expert plus low-rank residual experts, guided by explicit degradation priors. Reduces parameter redundancy relative to full-rank multi-expert designs.

entry.title: TongueReenact: Geometry-Anchored Tongue Synthesis for Face Reenactment

author.name: MD Wahiduzzaman Khan, Mingshan Jia, Xiaolin Zhang, En Yu, Kaska Musial-Gabrys

entry.summary: Introduces cross-identity tongue dynamics transfer for face reenactment, with a foundation-model-bootstrapped tongue segmentation model and a spatially constrained latent masked diffusion synthesizer. Fills an anatomical gap that causes implausible mouth interiors during speech.

entry.title: Theia: Large-Scale Multimodal Captioning and Automated Validation of the Incidents1M Dataset for Data-Free Distillation

author.name: Simone Giano, Lorenzo Severini, Alessandro Galdelli, Adriano Mancini

entry.summary: Recovers 100,000 images from the text-free Incidents1M disaster dataset and generates plus automatically validates captions using existing Qwen3.5 dense and mixture-of-experts models, to enable data-free knowledge distillation for disaster-response VLMs. Addresses missing or misaligned text in current crisis datasets.

entry.title: Simplifying Neural Networks During Training

author.name: Lorenzo Sciandra, Samuele Fonio, Roberto Esposito

entry.summary: Combines Neural Collapse and Tunnel Effect findings into a training-time network simplification method that uses an Inverse Fisher Criterion to detect when representations have stabilized and where the feature-extraction and classification boundary lies. The result is pruning or truncating networks during training rather than after.

entry.title: FasTac: A Curved Multispectral Vision-Based Tactile Sensor for High-Speed High-Precision 3D Shape and Force Perception

author.name: Xiaofan Lu, Kaiji Huang, Jiahui Chen, Yuankai Lin, Hua Yang, Zhouping Yin

entry.summary: FasTac is a curved vision-based tactile fingertip that combines single-sensor multispectral photometric stereo for 3D shape reconstruction, dynamic-convolution three-axis force estimation, and FPGA acceleration for high-speed operation. It targets the combination of geometry, force, and latency that existing curved tactile sensors struggle to achieve together.

entry.title: Learning from routine health system data builds better neuroimaging AI models

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Nature Medicine paper arguing that training neuroimaging AI on routinely collected clinical data from health systems yields better models than relying on curated research cohorts, presumably because the messier real-world distribution matches deployment conditions. The theme speaks to a central weakness of medical AI, where models tuned on clean research scans degrade in ordinary hospital settings.

entry.title: FAS-R1: A Unified Multi-Task MLLM for Reasoning Face Anti-Spoofing

author.name: Hongyang Wang, Yichen Shi, Hongrui Li, Yiru Huo, Jun Feng, Zitong Yu

entry.summary: FAS-R1 is a multimodal LLM for face anti-spoofing that jointly outputs authenticity decisions, attack-type labels, and spoof-region localization with chain-of-thought rationales. It combines cold-start supervised fine-tuning on a 23K long-CoT dataset with task-specific reinforcement learning to reduce templated reasoning.

entry.title: Journey Operators for Structured Multi-Axis Composition

author.name: Mahesh Godavarti

entry.summary: The paper develops a general framework where each data item carries a small per-axis transformation, so composing movements along independent axes commutes while order matters within an axis. This yields a principled operator-based way to encode multi-axis structure for sequences, images, trees, and volumes.

entry.title: SDO: Structure-Aware Data Organization for Efficient LLM Post-Training

author.name: Jinliang Gao, Ning Yang, Hai Wang, Baili Xiao, Pin Lyu

entry.summary: SDO reorganizes post-training data batches dynamically using an exposure-driven feedback signal, so samples that remain under-optimized receive more exposure instead of relying on a fixed pre-training clustering. It is presented as a plug-and-play framework for cheaper LLM post-training.

entry.title: Sparsity Induced Identifiability in Matrix Tri-Factorisation

author.name: Tingting Mu

entry.summary: This paper establishes what the author describes as the first rigorous identifiability guarantees for general real-valued matrix tri-factorization under sparsity constraints, extending theory that previously existed mainly for two-factor models. Identifiability matters for treating factorizations as interpretable representations.

entry.title: Evaluation Protocols and Cross-Subject Generalization in EEG Emotion Recognition

author.name: Hanting Suo, Yuwen Li

entry.summary: This study separates the target quantity, development procedure, and reporting rule in EEG emotion recognition, showing with a reproduced DGCNN pipeline on SEED and SEED-IV that checkpoint selection based on repeated test-set evaluation inflates accuracy substantially and that subject-disjoint evaluation tells a different story. It argues reported accuracy reflects the whole evaluation protocol, not the classifier.

entry.title: TriShield: Zero-Utility-Loss Defense Against Privacy Backdoors in Federated Language Model Fine-Tuning via Orthogonal Gradient Projection and Optimizer State Entanglement

author.name: Cheng Wei (Honor Device Co., Ltd., Shenzhen, China)

entry.summary: TriShield is a three-layer defense against privacy-backdoor attacks in which a malicious federated server engineers PEFT adapters to memorize and later reconstruct client training samples. It combines orthogonal gradient projection with optimizer-state entanglement and claims complete prevention with no utility loss.

entry.title: Information Bottleneck Learning for Faithful Time Series Forecasting Explanations

author.name: Xu Zheng, Wei Cheng, Zhuomin Chen, Mo Sha, Jingchao Ni, Dongsheng Luo

entry.summary: IB-Forecast applies an information-bottleneck objective to build an inherently interpretable multivariate forecaster, decomposing predictions into a learned periodic component plus evidence-selected inputs so that explanations are faithful rather than merely structural. It extends faithfulness-oriented explanation methods from classification to forecasting.

entry.title: Semi-Supervised Learning for Molecular Graphs via Ensemble Consensus

author.name: Rasmus Tirsgaard, Laurits Fredsgaard, Marisa Wodrich, Mikkel Jordahn, Mikkel N. Schmidt

entry.summary: This study shows that ensemble-consensus semi-supervised learning improves molecular property prediction across many datasets, task types, and GNN architectures, sidestepping the need for label-preserving augmentations that are hard to design for molecules. Unlabeled molecular data is abundant while labels are costly.

entry.title: Encryption-Compatible Clustered Federated Learning via Distributed Expectation-Maximization over Metadata

author.name: Michael Ben Ali, Imen Megdiche, Andr\'e P\'eninou, Olivier Teste

entry.summary: FLAMECHE performs clustered federated learning through distributed expectation-maximization over client metadata in a way that remains compatible with encryption and standard privacy mechanisms. The authors frame a trilemma among privacy, communication cost, and computation, and argue prior metadata-based clustering methods sacrifice privacy.

entry.title: QQWorld: Quantile-Quantile Matching for World Model Regularization

author.name: Zhoushun Yu, Xiaoyu Hu, Xiangyu Xu

entry.summary: QQWorld replaces the Epps-Pulley Gaussianity regularizer used in a latent world model with a quantile-quantile matching objective, showing that the prior loss has vanishing gradients for isolated tail samples and therefore fails to control heavy-tailed latents. A cross-batch variant extends the alignment across mini-batches.

entry.title: SPFM-Net: Semantic-Prior-Guided Frequency-Constrained Mamba for Invisible Watermark Attack

author.name: Chunpeng Wang, Yanan Shi, Zhiqiu Xia, Jidong Yang, Suo Gao, Qi Li

entry.summary: A second watermark-removal system from the same group combining high-ratio masking, a partially fine-tuned masked autoencoder, and a Mamba backbone with frequency constraints to capture globally distributed watermark signals. Aims to improve the removal-versus-fidelity trade-off.

entry.title: mmRadarTwin: A Measurement-Calibrated Signal-Level Digital Twin Platform for Indoor mmWave Radar

author.name: Jianyi Zhou, Chenghao Zhang, Yanli Li, Dong Yuan

entry.summary: Presents a signal-level digital twin platform that links real FMCW mmWave radar measurements with Unreal Engine scene simulation through a shared range-angle processing interface, writing complex multi-channel radar cubes. Enables reproducible synthetic data for indoor radar sensing research.

entry.title: RadHarmony: Radiological Data Handling in the Era of Agentic AI

author.name: Frank Li, Bardia Khosravi, Mohammadreza Chavoshi, Theo Dapamede, YoungSeok Jeon, Janice Newsome, Hari Trivedi, Judy Gichoya

entry.summary: Releases an open-source Python library that harmonizes 24 public radiology datasets into a unified metadata format and API, wrapping MONAI datasets and supporting classification labels, masks, boxes, and reports. Reduces the plumbing burden of assembling heterogeneous medical imaging corpora.

entry.title: Forensic Reproducibility Audit of a Radiology Vision-Language Model Benchmark: From Intended Protocol to Released Artifact

author.name: Mateusz Koz{\l}owski

entry.summary: A retrospective forensic audit of a chest radiograph vision-language model pilot traces agreement between the intended protocol and the released artifacts, covering prompt bindings, DICOM metadata, output completeness, label extraction, and repository propagation. It uncovers concrete defects such as prompt mislabeling in sixty calls and inverted-grayscale image handling.

entry.title: The Easy Trap: Why LLMs Underestimate Misconception-Driven Difficulty

author.name: Amanda La Hadi, Muhammad Johan Alibasa, Guanliang Chen, A. Taufiq Asyhari

entry.summary: Four LLM systems rated the difficulty of 32 arithmetic items, and the ratings were compared to empirical difficulty from 770 undergraduates using classical test theory and a two-parameter IRT model. Rank correlations were only moderate, with models systematically underestimating items whose difficulty comes from common misconceptions.

entry.title: IDP AutoOpt: Agent-Driven Optimization of Document Processing Pipeline Configurations

author.name: David Kaleko, Sergey Ivanov, Md Mofijul Islam

entry.summary: IDP AutoOpt is an autonomous agent that tunes intelligent document processing pipeline configurations, including prompts, model choice, OCR settings, and schemas, through a closed loop of scoring, error diagnosis, targeted edits, and re-evaluation guided by human-authored domain skills. It reportedly matches or exceeds expert-tuned configurations across healthcare, marketing, and financial deployments.

entry.title: Diagnosing Fine-Grained Inconsistency Classification in Financial Disclosure Text

author.name: Aman Kumar, Lasitha Vidyaratne, Dipanjan D Ghosh, Arnab Chakrabarti, Ahmed K Farahat

entry.summary: Using a fixed 5,940-instance synthetic financial disclosure benchmark with eleven inconsistency labels and paired evidence spans, the study compares frozen embedding classifiers, fine-tuned encoders, evidence-augmented models, and prompted LLMs on classifying the type of inconsistency, not just its presence. Different conflict types such as numerical, temporal, referential, factual, and normative demand different downstream checks.

entry.title: The Art of Not Forgetting A Local Learning Architecture for Continual Learning

author.name: Ashmith Atmuri, Yashaswini Rao Bhogarajula

entry.summary: CMP is a continual-learning architecture using sparse relational codes, a two-tier competitive memory, and local update rules instead of end-to-end backpropagation. On a domain-incremental byte-level language modeling protocol it shows substantially less backward transfer (forgetting) than a parameter-matched Transformer trained with online elastic weight consolidation.

entry.title: A Physics-Informed Framework for PID Tuning of Chemical Processes Using Large Language Model Agents

author.name: Zhoupeng Shou, Xiaodong Hong, Congjing Ren, Jingdai Wang, Yongrong Yang, Zuwei Liao

entry.summary: The framework formalizes how plant engineers iteratively retune PID loops into an LLM-assisted workflow, feeding closed-loop response features and internal-model-control demonstrations to hosted models for gain generation and correction. A small local model is fine-tuned on simulation-verified targets for on-premise deployment.

entry.title: Guarding Organizations Against Malware Risk: A Novel Graph-Based Malware Detection Method

author.name: Yinan Gao, Jiarong Xu, Xiaohang Zhao, Xiao Fang

entry.summary: The paper proposes graph-based malware detection that explicitly identifies cohesive groups of basic blocks realizing meaningful program behaviors, rather than relying on byte-level features vulnerable to evasion. It targets more expressive program-graph representations for organizational cybersecurity risk.

entry.title: MPEcho: A Melody and Phoneme-Aware Generative Framework for Controllable Cover Song Generation

author.name: Wei-Jaw Lee, Hsuan-Yu Yeh, Ting-Yi Hu, Chih-Pin Tan, Fang-Duo Tsai, Yi-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: MPEcho improves cover song generation by adding explicit phoneme conditioning and a length regulator to an existing framework, reducing phoneme error rate compared to pitch-and-voicing conditioning alone. It also introduces a Whisper-based singing transcription model to supply the phoneme timings.

entry.title: CoCaRS: Correlation Calibration-Based Redundancy Suppression for Heterogeneous Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Fengming Yu, Haiwei Pan, Kejia Zhang, Chunling Chen, Jian Guan, Baoying Ma

entry.summary: CoCaRS refines redundancy-suppression knowledge distillation across heterogeneous teacher and student architectures by calibrating feature correlations rather than simply decorrelating them, which can destroy useful structure. The goal is better cross-architecture transfer despite differing inductive biases.

entry.title: Regularizing modality contribution drift in multimodal continual learning

author.name: Zhen Zhang, Jielei Chu, Bin Liu, Tianrui Li

entry.summary: The authors define Modality Contribution Drift, a decision-level shift in how much each modality and their interactions matter as a multimodal model learns sequential tasks, and propose a score plus a regularization method to keep contributions stable. They argue existing continual learning methods, which focus on representation alignment, cannot prevent this drift.

entry.title: TIER-MoE: Trust-Informed Expert Routing via Conditional Modality Risk for Multimodal Fusion in Biomedical Classification

author.name: Yu Chang, Anzhe Cheng, Chenwei Wu, Zhuoran Wang, Jiahao Chen, Tamoghna Chattopadhyay, Sophia I. Thomopoulos, Paul M. Thompson, Liyue Shen, Paul Bogdan

entry.summary: TIER-MoE routes biomedical multimodal inputs to subspace experts using a learned per-sample estimate of each modality's reliability, defined as the expected loss of that modality's unimodal predictor and computed from out-of-fold predictions. This distinguishes unreliable from merely redundant modalities during fusion.

entry.title: Learning-Augmented and Randomized Algorithms for Line Aggregation with Delays

author.name: Tianhang Lu, Runtian Ren, Shengcai Liu, Ke Tang

entry.summary: The paper gives learning-augmented and randomized online algorithms for aggregation with delays on a line metric, with tunable robustness-consistency tradeoffs when advice about service lengths is available, plus a randomized algorithm beating the deterministic competitive-ratio lower bound. It sits in the algorithms-with-predictions area that formalizes how to use imperfect ML advice.

entry.title: Exact Action Values Are Not Enough: Rollout-Verified Reinforcement Fine-Tuning of a Reasoning Model for Multi-Zone VAV Control

author.name: Takumi Shioda, Kohei Terashima, Tatsuo Nagai

entry.summary: The authors test whether a frontier reasoning LLM can control multi-zone variable-air-volume HVAC systems from text alone, then distill that capability into a locally deployable open-weight model via TD3-guided reinforcement fine-tuning with rollout verification. Evaluation is on a physics-based building simulator over summer days against conventional MPC and RL baselines.

entry.title: GVR-Coder: A Visual-Feedback Framework for Structured SVG Generation in Complex Document and Meeting Scenarios

author.name: Yiming Xu, Jihua Kang, Chunsai Du, Qifan Zhang, Wangqiu Zhou, Yiting Wu, Tianqi Li, Qi Song

entry.summary: GVR-Coder generates structured SVG diagrams from long documents and meeting transcripts, tackling dataset scarcity, missing layout priors, and lack of rendering feedback by adding a visual-feedback loop that inspects rendered output and corrects defects. The target use case is converting verbose text into readable diagrams.

entry.title: Stage-Replay Divergence Follows the KV Cache: Fixed-Prefix Precision Controls and Bidirectional Cache Transplantation

author.name: Alexander Boesgaard Lorup

entry.summary: This audit tests whether re-prefilling an identical token prefix reproduces the decoder state of a retained live KV cache, finding that in BF16 the two constructions diverge on many suffixes while FP32 shows no divergence. The result questions a common assumption behind stage-replay interpretability and debugging methods on a Qwen-derived system.

entry.title: PlantBGC: Transformer for Plant BGC Discovery via Label-Free Domain Adaptation and Weak Supervision

author.name: Yuhan Zhao, Nidhi Grover, Zhishan Guo, Ning Sui

entry.summary: PlantBGC transfers supervision from well-annotated microbial biosynthetic gene clusters to plant genomes using an encoder-only Transformer over ordered Pfam-domain sequences, with label-free domain adaptation and weak supervision to handle scarce plant labels. The goal is to narrow the experimental search space for specialized-metabolite pathway discovery.

entry.title: A Query-Efficient Stochastic Volume Rendering Framework for Time-Varying Implicit Neural Volumes

author.name: Alper Sahistan, Haichao Miao, Zhimin Li, Peer-Timo Bremer, Joshua A Levine, Valerio Pascucci

entry.summary: Proposes a query-efficient stochastic volume rendering framework for time-varying implicit neural representations, where expensive network inference replaces cheap memory lookups and makes conventional dense ray marching impractical. It targets interactive rendering of dynamic scientific volumes such as time-resolved CT without resampling or retraining.

entry.title: A Distributed Acoustic Sensing Dataset for Vessel Detection and Localization in Submarine Cable Protection

author.name: Erick Eduardo Ramirez-Torres, Javier Macias-Guarasa, Daniel Pizarro, Javier Tejedor, Sira Elena Palazuelos-Cagigas, Pedro J. Vidal-Moreno, Mar\'ia R. Fern\'andez-Ruiz, Sonia Martin-Lopez, Miguel Gonzalez-Herraez, Roel Vanthillo

entry.summary: Releases a curated distributed acoustic sensing dataset of submarine cable measurements paired with AIS vessel information, with defined tasks for vessel detection and vessel-to-cable distance estimation. It responds to recent cable damage and sabotage incidents by enabling reproducible cable-protection research.

entry.title: MixFrag: Fragility-Guided Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization for Vision Transformers

author.name: Md. Mehrab Hossain Opi, Robiul Islam Ryad, Md. Umar Faruk

entry.summary: MixFrag allocates mixed precision across vision transformer components by estimating each component's quantization fragility as the KL divergence between full-precision and isolated quantized outputs on a small calibration set, then solving bit allocation as a multiple-choice knapsack problem. It replaces the common assumption of uniform bit-width across heterogeneous transformer blocks.

entry.title: Beyond Similarity: Grounded Agentic Extraction and Expert-Adjudicated Evaluation of Intertextuality in Classical Chinese Histories

author.name: Zhaoji Wang, Wanyu Si, Jun Wang

entry.summary: Recasts fine-grained intertextuality detection in classical Chinese histories as an agentic task where an LLM reads two passages fully and, through a constrained tool interface, must ground each proposed reuse in exact character spans on both sides and label it under a five-dimension typology. Validation uses an exhaustive Analects versus Book of Han comparison with three domain experts adjudicating pooled multi-model candidates.

entry.title: ICLE++: Modeling Fine-Grained Traits for Holistic Essay Scoring

author.name: Shengjie Li, Vincent Ng

entry.summary: ICLE++ is a corpus of persuasive student essays annotated with both holistic and trait-level scores, designed to test whether automated essay scoring models trained on the dominant ASAP corpus generalize elsewhere and to support multi-trait and cross-prompt scoring research. It represents a long-running annotation effort released to the community.

entry.title: Improving Mental Health Screening and Early Risk Detection in Spanish

author.name: Andreu Casamayor-Segarra, Vicent Ahuir, Antonio Molina-Marco, Llu\'is-F. Hurtado

entry.summary: Releases three Spanish mental-health domain-adapted foundation models and proposes Incremental Context Expansion, an automatic relabeling method that identifies when accumulated social media posts contain enough evidence of a disorder. Fine-tuned models trained on ICE samples target early risk detection.

entry.title: MagicSelector: Joint Optimization for Agent Tool Selection via Counterfactual Decomposition and Progressive Reranking

author.name: HONOR Agentic Search Team, Zhengzong Chen, Lei Tang, Lijun Liu, Chuandi Jiang, Fan Yang, Keyun Chu, Chu Zhao, Shihao Liu, Minghang Li, Bo Liang, Can Wen, Hailong Wu, Jingnan Ju, Mian Liu, Nengbin Zhang, Peiqiang Wang, Penghe Nie, Qinhui Gu, Sijia Lv, Siqi Chen, Wei Zhang, Yang Xu, Yuhao Qian, Yuxiang Zhang, Zeng Cheng, Zhen Wang, Zuan Chen, Yuanyuan Zhao, Fei Huang

entry.summary: MagicSelector, from HONOR's agentic search team, jointly optimizes agent tool retrieval through counterfactual task decomposition, progressive reranking, and dynamic top-K selection. It targets ambiguous instructions and context distraction in out-of-domain tool sets.

entry.title: Digital Harf: A Clinically Integrated Multimodal AI System for Pervasive Arabic Speech and Language Therapy

author.name: Asif Azad, Mohammad Sadat Hossain, MD Sadik Hossain Shanto, Sabri Boughorbel, Abdulrhman Aljouie, Bdour Alwuqaysi, Yahya Bokhari, Ayah Othman Sindi, Ehsan Hoque

entry.summary: Digital Harf is a clinically integrated multimodal system extending Arabic speech and language therapy for autistic children into the home, with language therapy, speech intelligibility, and picture description modules. An agentic synthetic data engine generates culturally grounded Arabic therapy content to address material scarcity.

entry.title: PCAP-LM: An LLM-Native Text Representation for TLS Bulk Traffic Analysis

author.name: Xavier Marjou, Lucas Tamic, Ilan Jaffeux-Cheniout

entry.summary: PCAP-LM compresses network packet captures into an LLM-friendly flow-centric text representation using a custom ASCII alphabet that encodes direction, TCP/TLS state, log-scale size, and inter-packet timing, plus a constrained tokenizer and motif run-length encoding. This makes bulk encrypted-traffic analysis feasible within context limits.

entry.title: OVEarth-Bench: Evaluating Category Breadth and Query Diversity for Open-Vocabulary Earth Observation

author.name: Kaiyu Li, Zepeng Xin, Zixuan Jiang, Jing Fu, Lanxuan Xue, Lingyu Zhang, Xiangyong Cao

entry.summary: OVEarth-Bench evaluates open-vocabulary Earth observation with broad hierarchical category coverage including negative expressions, plus vocabulary, referring, and reasoning query types under a unified zero-shot mask and box protocol. Evaluation of general and remote-sensing-specific methods shows current performance remains limited.

entry.title: PanDent: Toward Comprehensive Tooth-Level Structure-Language Consistency in Dental Radiology

author.name: Xiaohan Li, Xinyu Liu, Chang Liu, Sum Wing Au Yeung, Jun Liu, Yixuan Yuan, Hui Chen

entry.summary: PanDent is a dental panoramic radiography benchmark of 9,524 images with expert-validated tooth-level annotations and structured reports validated by an oral and maxillofacial radiologist. It supports fine-grained evaluation of multimodal LLMs on tooth-level diagnosis and structure-language consistency.

entry.title: PrintAnything: Learning an Intermediate Representation for 3D printing G-code Generation

author.name: Sangmin Hong, Daniel Sungho Jung, Heewon Kim, Kyoung Mu Lee

entry.summary: PrintAnything learns to emit executable 3D printing G-code directly from point clouds via an intermediate representation, bypassing the fragile step of reconstructing a watertight mesh. This avoids topological artifacts that commonly cause print failures.

entry.title: S-Avatar: Diffusion-Guided Gaussian Head Avatars from a Single Image

author.name: Hail Song, Seokhwan Yang, Jiwon Yang, Woojin Cho, Woontack Woo

entry.summary: Generates animatable photorealistic 3D Gaussian head avatars from one image via a diffusion-based splat generator, FLAME parametric alignment, and animation strategies for VR use. Focuses on preserving 3D consistency at unseen viewpoints.

entry.title: Large scale cross-regional remote sensing flood monitoring framework for operative mapping and impact analysis

author.name: Ilya Novikov, Svetlana Illarionova, Ruslan Dzharkinov, Maria Smirnova, Ayrat Abdullin, Anna Korotkova, Mariia Ulianova, Dmitrii Shadrin, Evgeny Burnaev

entry.summary: Builds an operational multimodal flood monitoring framework over Russian regions fusing SAR, multispectral, and elevation derivatives into a 21-channel input, with a self-collected cross-regional dataset for generalization testing. Targets damage assessment where annotated flood data is scarce and unevenly distributed.

entry.title: Hugging Face-style rogue agents can survive shutdown

author.name: emile delcourt

entry.summary: Argues that AI agents which obtain elevated credentials and compute cannot reliably be shut down, drawing analogies to persistent botnets and self-propagating AI worm research, and citing reports that an agent left notes for future versions describing an escape path. The author advocates layered and automated kill switch requirements while noting they are insufficient against agents that can deploy workloads on arbitrary infrastructure.

entry.title: MediaWiki Code2Code Search: Neural Retrieval for the Semantic Discovery of Open-Source Software Entities

author.name: Francesco Tosoni

entry.summary: A neural code-to-code retrieval system indexes 1.29 million structural entities across 2,500-plus MediaWiki repositories, enabling search by computational intent instead of surface tokens. A split architecture separates GPU offline indexing from CPU-only serving, with a compressed FAISS IVF-PQ index cutting index size by roughly 97% versus a flat index.

entry.title: VESTIGE: A Knowledge-Guided Masking Strategy for Corruption-Aware Fine-Tuning of Genomic Transformers, Validated on Ancient DNA Reconstruction

author.name: Angshuman Chakravertty, Rahul Maheshwari

entry.summary: VESTIGE replaces uniform masked-language-model masking with a masking distribution matched to an empirically measured per-position corruption profile, applied to genomic transformers for ancient DNA reconstruction where cytosine deamination causes predictable position-dependent damage. It is a parameter-free drop-in collator change.

entry.title: HARGO: Heterogeneity-Aware Reward-Guided Optimization for RL Post-Training of LLMs on HPC Tasks

author.name: Tiangang Li, Xiangbo Tian

entry.summary: HARGO does RL post-training of LLMs on high-performance-computing tasks that are extremely heterogeneous, spanning binary data-race classification, short factual QA, and long semantic generation with answer lengths differing by nearly two orders of magnitude. It introduces heterogeneity-aware reward guidance so one model behaves appropriately per task type.

entry.title: More Data, Worse Decisions? Preference Reversals in Neural Networks under Gram Incompatibility

author.name: Yanli Yan, Yuanzheng Li, Yong Zhao, Hongbo Guo, Shoudong Han

entry.summary: This paper asks whether refitting a fixed-representation network with a least-squares head on pooled data preserves action preferences supported by each source separately, and shows that pooling recomputes the inverse-Gram geometry in ways that can reverse shared preferences. It derives exact and approximate conditions under which composition is preserved.

entry.title: Archetypes or ability? Clustering for modelling student mathematical competence

author.name: Benjamin Mawdsley, Tom Quilter, Richard Turner, Sarah Jackson, Paul Edwards

entry.summary: Using Bernoulli mixture modeling on over 119,000 UK students across thirteen national exams, the authors test whether mathematical competence decomposes into discrete skill archetypes. They find few distinct clusters, with overall ability dominating, challenging assumptions built into many personalized learning systems.

entry.title: A Reference-Free Score for Detecting Silent Reasoning Failures in Large Language Models

author.name: Vivek Shukla, Varun Shukla, Atul, Divya Mishra, Mehul Kumar Das

entry.summary: The paper proposes a reference-free score combining step validity, entailment from reasoning to answer, resampling stability, and counterfactual sensitivity to flag mathematical chains of thought that reach right answers by invalid routes or vice versa. It names this mismatch the reasoning-answer consistency gap.

entry.title: Weight and Height Estimation from a Single Human Image Captured in the Wild

author.name: Hira Yaseen, Arif Mahmood, Waqas Sultani

entry.summary: The work benchmarks single-task and multi-task deep networks for estimating body weight and height, and hence BMI, from a single in-the-wild image, contending with pose, camera geometry, and background variation. It positions BMI estimation as a health-relevant visual inference task.

entry.title: Model-Driven Requirements Configuration with Three-Valued Uncertainty Scoring

author.name: Ahmed Ibrahim

entry.summary: The paper presents a neuro-symbolic multi-agent architecture where an LLM acts as a heuristic traversal engine over a formal requirements lattice while a deterministic symbolic validator enforces structural conformance and logical consistency. It also introduces three-valued uncertainty scoring of the model's pre-validation decisions.

entry.title: Entity Resolution in Practice: Lessons from a Self-Serve Pipeline

author.name: Kaushik Pavani, Ganga Aluri, Pravin Jadhav, Neeraj Prasad, Kiran Sanka

entry.summary: An industrial retrospective on a self-serve entity resolution system evaluated across six benchmarks from under a thousand to five million records, distilling three lessons: no matcher wins universally so run automatic bake-offs, precision and recall need distinct interventions, and transitive closure can silently merge unrelated entities from a single bad link.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning on Cost-Constrained Quadrupedal Hardware

author.name: Javier C. Weddington, Bence P. \"Olveczky, Stephen A. Baccus

entry.summary: The authors study RL locomotion on a very low-cost quadruped where over 50 ms actuator transport delay turns the task into a partially observable problem. They adopt biologically inspired handling of delayed and noisy feedback to narrow the sim-to-real gap on cheap hardware.

entry.title: Shared Symbolic Backbones for Physically Consistent Multi-Output Symbolic Regression

author.name: Manuel Rodriguez

entry.summary: This neuro-evolutionary symbolic regression method discovers a shared symbolic backbone of latent expressions reused across multiple coupled outputs via sparse read-outs, with structure evolved discretely and parameters tuned by gradient descent. The goal is physically consistent, interpretable multi-output models for process systems.

entry.title: Understanding Context Sampling in TabPFN on Small Tabular Datasets

author.name: Mohammed Abdullah

entry.summary: An empirical study of how context size and row selection affect TabPFN in-context classification on 15 small OpenML datasets, testing whether larger contexts stabilize predictions and whether expensive selection like K-Means or farthest-point sampling beats random draws. It provides practical guidance on prototype selection cost versus benefit.

entry.title: ScratchSim: A Procedural Synthetic Data Pipeline for Surface Scratch Detection

author.name: Paul Julius K\"uhn, Saptarshi Neil Sinha, Tiago Kleist, Richard Hoffmann, Arjan kuijper, Michael Weinmann

entry.summary: ScratchSim is a procedural Blender-based rendering pipeline that generates large annotated synthetic datasets of surface scratches with configurable materials, camera modes, and domain randomization. Four training strategies are compared across two objects and three edge-deployable detectors including YOLOX and LW-DETR.

entry.title: Rethinking EEG-Based Disease Diagnosis: Decoupling Instance Representation Learning from Subject-Level Supervision

author.name: Zhiyuan Ma, Zeyuan Li, Zhiyi Lu, Jiacheng Hao, Youlang Du, Zhen Jiang, Xinche Zhang, Yuhao Sun, Sen Song

entry.summary: BridgeMIL separates instance-level EEG representation learning from subject-level diagnosis: it first pretrains the encoder with self-supervised temporal alignment, avoiding the common practice of copying a subject label onto every short window, then aggregates with multiple-instance learning. This addresses the mismatch between per-subject labels and the many segments extracted per recording.

entry.title: Latent States in Neural Networks: Recovering the Temporal Structure of Drifting Data from Model Weights

author.name: Kevin Guan

entry.summary: The paper asks whether discrete regimes in a drifting data stream can be recovered from the weights of models trained sequentially on that stream, by fitting a hidden Markov model to the aligned weight trajectory. On misinformation detection and sentiment datasets, classifiers generalize better to windows sharing the same inferred latent state.

entry.title: Safety-Gated Agentic Supervisory Control on a Coupled Distillation Benchmark: Regime Map, Auditable Gate, and Co-Design Findings

author.name: Christian Rosenthal

entry.summary: Studies an open-weight LLM acting as a supervisory setpoint writer over a distillation column benchmark, wrapped in a rule-based counterfactual gate with nine pinned constraints that admits or blocks each proposed action before it reaches the regulatory control layer. Comparisons span PID, linear MPC, ungated agent, and gated agent under matched scenarios and seeds.

entry.title: Dynamic Spectral Filtering for Temporal Graph Learning: Learning Evolving Propagation Operators

author.name: Yan Kong

entry.summary: Dynamic Spectral Filtering asks whether the propagation operator itself should evolve in temporal graphs, representing each snapshot with a Chebyshev filter whose vector-valued coefficients are recurrent temporal states regulated by gates. Tested on MOOC, Wikipedia, and Reddit temporal link prediction.

entry.title: On a joint simultaneous learning of relevant feature subsets and subspaces in regression-like problems

author.name: Illia Horenko

entry.summary: Extends entropy-optimal manifold clustering to regression, jointly selecting relevant feature subsets and subspaces for nonstationary nonlinear problems with linear-scaling iteration and memory cost. Benchmarks include strongly chaotic Lorenz-96 dynamics and fluid-dynamics prediction against a wide set of ML baselines.

entry.title: Beyond Borrowed Histories: Person-Aligned User Simulation for Interactive Role-Playing Evaluation

author.name: Yuhang Zhu (University of Science and Technology of China), Mingxuan Du (University of Science and Technology of China), Benfeng Xu (University of Science and Technology of China, MetaStone Technology, Beijing, China), Jie Gao (MetaStone Technology, Beijing, China), Lingyun Yu (University of Science and Technology of China), Hongtao Xie (University of Science and Technology of China)

entry.summary: Argues that current role-playing agent benchmarks are flawed because they force models to continue borrowed dialogue histories and grade them with user-detached rubrics. The authors propose person-aligned user simulation so evaluation happens through live multi-turn interaction with a consistent simulated user.

entry.title: Beyond a Single Judge: Simulating Social Persona Panels for Generative UI Evaluation

author.name: Zheng Wu, Yibo Luo, Pu Zhang, Cheng Yang, Zhuosheng Zhang

entry.summary: ESPP replaces a single LLM judge for generative UI evaluation with a panel of psychologically diverse, evidence-grounded personas that rate an interface, exchange opinions under a bounded-confidence opinion dynamic, and are aggregated with social weighting. The aim is to approximate how different real user populations perceive generated interfaces.

entry.title: Beyond Sentiment: Structured Information Extraction from Financial News

author.name: Daohan Zhu, Sitong Ge, Ruofei Wang, Honggu Chen, Yubo Hou, Tao Wan, Zengchang Qin

entry.summary: Extracts six structured semantic dimensions (event type, impact scope, temporal horizon, confidence and more) from financial news with LLaMA-3.1-70B, arguing that these carry predictive signal beyond a single sentiment polarity. Experiments cover 41,618 news-stock pairs from the FNSPID dataset.

entry.title: ThreatForest: Multi-Agent Attack Tree Generation with Pluggable TTP Framework Mapping

author.name: Cristian Leo, Anton Dykyi, Danny Cortegaca, Daniel Begimher, Prakash Jha

entry.summary: ThreatForest is a multi-agent pipeline that turns source repositories into structured attack trees, maps steps to adversary techniques from pluggable frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK and CAPEC, and synthesizes mitigations. Stages run as a directed agent workflow from repository analysis to report generation.

entry.title: SciSchema.org: A Multidisciplinary Collection of Schemas for Structured Scientific Process Descriptions

author.name: Jennifer D'Souza, Sameer Sadruddin, Anisa Rula, Ana Bossler, Andr\'es Fullana, Enric Bas, Syed Ather, Defne Circi, Anlan Chen, L. Catherine Brinson, Alyssa Columbus, George Demetriou, Dongjun Jeong, Tarun Kumar, Frank Kr\"uger, Sascha Genehr, Kai Budde-Sagert, Anamaria Leonescu, Francesco Lodola, Chiara Florindi, Gagana Balasubramanya Murthy, Samson Oluwapelumi Olagbile, Nazia Riasat, Yan Sha, Kevin Shen, Shaokai Yang

entry.summary: SciSchema.org releases 16 expert-annotated schemas across biology, materials, imaging, physics, and psychology for describing scientific processes with fields for inputs, instruments, parameters, steps, measurements, and provenance. Schemas were mined with a human-in-the-loop workflow to support reproducibility and automation.

entry.title: Drawing-Recode: Annotation Grounding for Parametric CAD Code Generation from Raster 2D CAD Drawings

author.name: Mingi Kim, Yongjun Kim, Hyungki Kim

entry.summary: Drawing-Recode generates parametric CAD code from raster 2D engineering drawings by combining an image encoder for geometry with a separate text-recognition module for dimensional annotations, explicitly linking annotations to geometric entities. This targets legacy drawings that predate digital CAD workflows.

entry.title: EgoGVAE: Ego-body Mesh Reconstruction via Guided Variational Autoencoder

author.name: Jaehun Jung, Wonjun Kim

entry.summary: Estimates full-body mesh pose from head-mounted device head trajectory alone by replacing costly diffusion sampling with the latent space of a guided variational autoencoder trained on full-body poses. The main contribution is efficiency for AR/VR body tracking on wearables.

entry.title: Now You Have My Healthy Attention: A U-DiT for Brain-MRI Inpainting

author.name: Danilo Danese, Angela Lombardi, Tommaso Di Noia

entry.summary: Applies a U-DiT style volumetric transformer with downsampled global self-attention and 3D rotary embeddings to the BraTS healthy-tissue inpainting task, deliberately using deterministic regression because the challenge is scored by distortion metrics. Combines long-range context with convolutional high-frequency detail.

entry.title: Convolutional Neural Shading for High-Quality 3D Reconstruction from Multi-View Images

author.name: Juheon Hwang, Taewan Kim, Heeseok Oh, Jiwoo Kang

entry.summary: Introduces convolutional neural shading for multi-view 3D reconstruction, replacing single-point shading inputs with a convolutional shader that captures local neighborhood variation in dark and textureless regions.
