Across nine frontier models the best mean rubric score was around 56 percent, but reliability was dismal: no model exceeded roughly 2.6 percent on an eight-trial all-pass metric. The reliability gap is the key finding for anyone considering agentic automation of professional finance work.

entry.title: Metis: Memory Foundation Model

author.name: Zeyu Zhang, Ziliang Guo, Yihang Sun, Xichong Zhang, Xixuan Hao, Zehao Lin, Yang Zhang, Xiaoyan Zhao, Tong Shen, Bo Tang, Zhi-Qin John Xu, Junchi Yan, Haofen Wang, Xu Chen, Feiyu Xiong, Zhiyu Li, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Argues that agent memory should be native to the foundation model rather than bolted on as external retrieval modules, and formalizes native memory as a persistent evolving internal state plus learned store-and-recall procedures. Introduces Metis as a first memory foundation model instantiating this design.

entry.title: Weak-to-Strong On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Fangxu Yu, Zinan Lin, Xiaodong Liu, Weijia Xu, Michael Xu, Tianyi Zhou, Jianfeng Gao

entry.summary: Weak-to-Strong On-Policy Distillation inverts the usual assumption that the teacher must be at least as strong as the student, building a proxy teacher in logit space from contrastive pairs of weaker models to improve a stronger student on its own rollouts. This targets the frontier case where no larger teacher exists and where training multiple domain experts at student scale is prohibitively expensive. If it holds at scale it offers a cheap post-training lever for top-end models.

entry.title: ToxScreen: Detecting Whether an LLM Has Been Poisoned

author.name: Anthony Hughes, Nicole Xing, Collin Francel, Andy Kim, Andrew Draganov

entry.summary: Releases a benchmark of roughly 800 backdoored language models spanning attack objectives, trigger types, poisoning rates, and scales, to test whether a defender with weights and knowledge of the harmful behavior can recover an unknown trigger. Defines a realistic threat model with no training data, no trusted reference model, and no certainty the model is poisoned.

entry.title: A Compositional Theory of Causally Masked Transformers

author.name: Franz Nowak, Ryan Cotterell, Reda Boumasmoud

entry.summary: Develops an algebraic theory of what causally masked, finite-precision transformers can compute on arbitrarily long inputs, taking as the central object the finite attention-computed memory summarizing the prefix. Because it models actual finite-precision dynamics including rounding and evaluation order, the resulting expressivity characterization avoids idealized-arithmetic assumptions.

entry.title: HumanCLAW: Can Vision-Language Models Act Through a Body?

author.name: Siyao Li, Jiawei Gu, Shuai Liu, Kairui Hu, Zekun Li, Linjie Li, Chengcheng Tang, Po-Chen Wu, Ivan Shugurov, Lingni Ma, Michael Zollhoefer, Sizhe An, Abhay Mittal, Amy Zhao, Ranjay Krishna, Manling Li, Ziwei Liu, Chuan Guo

entry.summary: Introduces an evaluation framework that separates a vision-language model's action decisions from low-level motor execution by having the VLM issue atomic skill commands that a controller renders as sub-second full-body motion with real physics. This isolates whether embodied task failures come from bad decisions or failed control.

entry.title: Do You Really Need to Pretrain Q-Functions for Online RL Fine-Tuning?

author.name: Perry Dong, Ron Polonsky, Dorsa Sadigh, Chelsea Fin

entry.summary: This paper systematically tests whether pretraining the Q-function on offline data actually helps when fine-tuning online on top of an already-pretrained policy, and finds surprisingly that naive Q-function pretraining often provides little benefit over random initialization. Conventional wisdom in value-based RL assumes offline critic pretraining is essential. The analysis identifies why the expected benefit fails to materialize.

entry.title: HiFloat4 Format for End-To-End Reinforcement Learning Post-Training of Large Language Models

author.name: Hei Yi Mak, Shadan Golestan, Hoang Le, Mehran Taghian Jazi, Yunke Peng, Yaoyuan Wang, Yao Wang, Junsong Wang, Tianchi Hu, Fengchen He, Guipeng Hu, Tanzila Rahman, Anandharaju Durai Raju

entry.summary: HiFloat4 reports what the authors claim is the first fully 4-bit reinforcement learning post-training pipeline for language models, covering rollout and training forward and backward passes. The central diagnostic is that degradation comes mainly from rollout activation quantization, where outliers stretch dynamic range until many activations underflow, and that restoring only the training policy to higher precision makes accuracy worse by widening rollout-training mismatch.

entry.title: Tight Generalization Bound for AdaBoost

author.name: Mikael M{\o}ller H{\o}gsgaard

entry.summary: This paper establishes a tight generalization error bound for AdaBoost, matching known lower bounds, by combining the fact that AdaBoost outputs a voting classifier with zero empirical half-margin loss with a new margin-based generalization bound for voting classifiers. The result closes a long-standing gap in boosting theory. The new margin bound may be of independent interest.

entry.title: HoF-Bench: Rediscovering Real AI-Discovered CVEs Without Frontier Models

author.name: Petr Simecek, Elnaz Babayeva, Jiri Balhar, Michal Bida, Michal Buran, Vaclav Cadek, Luigino Camastra, Tomas Dulka, Michal Janocko, Tomas Klohna, Pavel Kohout, Ondrej Kokes, Adam Krivka, Jakub Kubik, Patrik Mada, Igor Morgenstern, Marek Pavelka, Joshua Rogers, Petr Stastny, Jan Tattermusch, Dmitrijs Trizna, Martin Votruba, Guido Vranken, Jakub Zikl, Evelina Gabasova, Stanislav Fort

entry.summary: Builds a benchmark from 95 real vulnerabilities that AI analyzers previously discovered in mature open-source projects such as OpenSSL and curl, pinned at vulnerable commits and graded by a blinded judge that requires matching code path, root cause, attack condition, and impact. A deliberately minimal LLM-based analyzer rediscovers up to 68 percent of them, suggesting much of the reported capability does not require frontier-only systems.

entry.title: (Im)Paired Programming: Coding Agents Improve Productivity but Harm Understanding

author.name: Nishant Balepur, Connor Baumler, Valerie Chen, Eunsol Choi, Rachel Rudinger, Jordan Lee Boyd-Graber

entry.summary: Runs a controlled study with 54 students building a website using either a code-editing agent or a chatbot, then tests comprehension and the ability to extend the code unaided. Finds agents speed initial completion but degrade understanding so users are less able to extend their own code, with low-effort interactions such as pasted prompts and auto-accepted edits being especially harmful.

entry.title: CG-World: A Large-Scale World-State Dataset and Protocol for World Models

author.name: Yiming Cai, Fangjie Yu, Meiqing Yu, Ziyue Shi, Pengfei Yuan, Yong Guo

entry.summary: CG-World is a large world-state dataset of roughly 850,000 short temporally aligned segments derived from industrial computer graphics pipelines, capturing latent states such as skeletal and controller data, physics caches, contact events, camera and lighting parameters, and multi-pass renders. It supplies the intermediate state supervision that video and robotics datasets usually omit.

entry.title: VidMap: Exploiting Temporal Structure for Video-Based Structure-from-Motion

author.name: Zador Pataki, Paul-Edouard Sarlin, Marc Pollefeys

entry.summary: Combines the sequential constraints of SLAM with the global optimization of structure-from-motion to recover camera calibration and metric poses from unconstrained video. The goal is robust large-scale pose data generation for training navigation and scene understanding models.

entry.title: Embodied Agents Take Control: Minimal-Interface Zero-Shot Agents Rival Industrial-Scale Policies in Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Jian Zhou, Xunyi Zhao, Gengze Zhou, Zerui Li, Sihao Lin, Jiajun Liu, Qi Wu

entry.summary: Tests whether general-purpose coding-agent harnesses can run the full perceive-act-verify loop for zero-shot vision-and-language navigation using only a monocular camera and discrete actions. Reported success rates around 71 percent for a default configuration using Claude Opus 5 and 78 percent for Claude Fable 5 at maximum effort suggest general agents can rival specialized industrial-scale navigation policies.

entry.title: Frontier Lab Employee Open Letter Calls For Being Able to Pace the Frontier

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Reports and endorses an open letter signed by more than 1,200 frontier-lab employees, and reportedly endorsed by OpenAI and Anthropic, calling for the technical and institutional ability to slow down at the frontier if capability acceleration outpaces understanding and control. The framing is that competitive pressure prevents any single company or country from unilaterally pausing.

entry.title: Filesystem-Based Memory for LLM Agents: Organization, Evolution, and Sustainability

author.name: Sizhe Zhou, Sheldon Yu, Hui Wei, Junda Wu, Siru Ouyang, Yizhu Jiao, Shijia Pan, Julian McAuley, Yu Zhang, Tong Yu, Jiawei Han

entry.summary: This is presented as the first systematic study of the increasingly common practice of giving LLM agents long-term memory as a plain directory tree of markdown files that the agent reads, writes, and reorganizes with generic file tools. The authors formalize management, search, and answering roles over one memory filesystem and test the untested assumptions that an agent can keep such a store organized as content accumulates and conflicts, and that the organizing effort actually pays off.

entry.title: Constitutional Midtraining: Content Presence Drives Alignment Gains

author.name: Desiree Cho, Cameron Tice, Bernie Hogan, Hunar Batra, Puria Radmard, Jun Zhao, Nigel Shadbolt

entry.summary: The authors test whether inserting principled values-based content during midtraining, cleanly separated from post-training, produces more durable alignment than post-training alone, using a 394M-token corpus built from a published constitution at 120B scale with a two-by-two design over curriculum ordering and deliberative reasoning. They evaluate at three stages on alignment under pressure, value-conflict resolution, blackmail scenarios, and emergent misalignment, and report that the presence of the content, not its arrangement, drives gains.

entry.title: Flow Map Learning via Nongradient Vector Flow

author.name: Mark Goldstein, Anshuk Uppal, Raghav Singhal, Aahlad Puli, Rajesh Ranganath

entry.summary: SGFlow learns flow maps for few-step generation without requiring model inverses or backpropagation through iterated model calls, by training a single model to produce both ODE solutions and the associated nongradient vector flow. It also supplies a proof that the intended ODE flow map actually solves the training loss, which several consistency-model variants lack. This targets the main practical pain points of distilling diffusion samplers.

entry.title: GPTQ-2D: Cubic-Time Two-Sided Adaptive Rounding

author.name: Jiale Chen, Torsten Hoefler, Dan Alistarh

entry.summary: Generalizes GPTQ-style adaptive rounding to the two-sided case where nonsingular bases act on both left and right of the residual, which naively costs quartic time via Kronecker vectorization. Presents a cubic-time algorithm, improving the practicality of two-sided quantization schemes.

entry.title: Do Unified Multimodal Models Think in One Space? A Lens Through Cross-Branch Steering

author.name: Yu Wang, Sharon Li

entry.summary: Tests whether unified multimodal models share one semantic space across their understanding and generation branches by extracting steering directions from one branch and applying them to the other. Finds that understanding-derived steering vectors transfer to generation, enabling controllable synthesis and better semantic alignment.

entry.title: Even More Deception: Objective Misalignment in Mixed-Motive LLM Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Marylou Fauchard, Florian Carichon, Margarida Carvalho, Golnoosh Farnadi

entry.summary: Uses the Werewolf social deduction game to systematically induce objective misalignment in a single agent while holding its role fixed, then compares hidden chain-of-thought with public cheap talk across four model families. It measures how covertly misaligned agents deceive collaborators, giving an empirical handle on hidden-objective risk in multi-agent deployments.

entry.title: OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Office-Suite Tasks with Economic Grounding

author.name: Jingbo Zhou, Yusai Zhao, Qi Bao, Jingjia Cao, Zhenghai Chen, Chang Gao, Kaiqi Guo, Muxin Guo, Mingxuan Li, Xinjiang Lu, Yanru Ma, Yixiong Xiao, Zenghui Zhang, Le Zhang, Hua Wu

entry.summary: OmegaUse-OfficeVal benchmarks agents on 100 long-horizon office-suite tasks derived from real practitioner requests, each averaging over two hours of human labor and annotated with both human time and a task price proxy. The economic grounding allows agent performance to be assessed against cost rather than accuracy alone.

entry.title: Try Again, Don't Look Back: Blind Resampling Outperforms Self-Repair in Small Code Models

author.name: Yuvraj Verma

entry.summary: Uses a placebo-controlled design on a Python benchmark at three model scales to disentangle the value of execution feedback from the value of simply getting another attempt, comparing blind resampling, a content-free failure notice, real feedback, and feedback plus self-reflection under matched budgets. Blind resampling is strongest below seven billion parameters and ties at seven billion while using far fewer tokens.

entry.title: A new benchmark for evaluating patient-facing health AI agents

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Amazon introduces PatientAgentBench, a clinician-vetted, reproducible benchmark for patient-facing healthcare agents that measures multiturn task completion, adherence to clinical workflows, and patient safety rather than isolated medical question answering. The accompanying findings report that capable foundation models still fail in ways that matter clinically, and suggest design changes for safer agents.

entry.title: Cognitive Convergence: Deep Similarities Between Large Language Models and Human Cognition

author.name: Chandra Sripada, Richard Lewis

entry.summary: Argues against the common view that LLMs are alien intelligences by identifying structural correspondences with human cognition across five dimensions including inferential organization and computational architecture. Contends that convergence despite different substrate, learning history, and environment is itself striking evidence rather than anthropomorphic projection.

entry.title: StealthBench: Measuring Operational Stealth in Autonomous Offensive-Security Agents

author.name: Ads Dawson, Adrian Wood

entry.summary: StealthBench measures operational stealth of autonomous offensive-security agents across six operational security dimensions, using eleven hand-verified incidents extracted from real bug bounty and red team trajectories expanded into fourteen dockerized scenarios. It asks whether agents that find real vulnerabilities also inherit the tradecraft to avoid detection.

entry.title: One Run Is Not an Idea: The Implementation Lottery in Automated Research

author.name: Jingjie Ning, Shanshan Zhong, Xiaochuan Li, Ji Zeng, Chenyan Xiong

entry.summary: The paper argues that automated research systems commit a statistical error by treating a single experimental run of one implementation as evidence about the underlying idea, which they call the implementation lottery. Their Idea Reliability Audit freezes candidate idea cards, samples fresh independent implementations, applies outcome-blind fidelity labels, and reports intraclass correlation to quantify how much idea-level conclusions depend on which implementation was sampled.

entry.title: Thinking Under Uncertainty: Evidence Use and Information-Seeking in Language Models

author.name: Hua-Dong Xiong, Xinyuan Yan, Ji-An Li, Jingming Xue, Marcelo G. Mattar, Robert C. Wilson

entry.summary: Ten open-weight models were run on matched horizon-style two-armed bandit tasks in thinking and non-thinking modes, with a cognitive model separating value-guided choice and noise from two exploration signatures: a directed preference for the less-known arm and Thompson-like uncertainty-scaled variability. The study asks whether inference-time thinking makes models better at using available evidence or better at seeking information for future decisions. It brings cognitive-science rigor to interpreting reasoning-mode gains.

entry.title: Sky sphere representation in language models

author.name: Aleksandr Berdnikov, Yevgeny Liokumovich

entry.summary: Probing roughly 100B-parameter open-weight models, the authors find a decodable representation of the celestial sphere in the residual stream, sometimes surfacing in top principal components when prompts ask about proximity of objects in the night sky, with leave-one-out validation showing up to 65 to 85 percent explained variance and median angular errors of 12 to 21 degrees. They verify the structure is not simply a leaked flat correlate. They present it as the first identified curved high-dimensional irreducible geometric representation in a language model.

entry.title: Which RAG Paradigm Wins at Scale? A Scaling Study of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Paradigms

author.name: Pengyu Wang, Benfeng Xu, Shaohan Wang, Xin Zeng, Huarui Wu, Lei Zhang, Licheng Zhang

entry.summary: Runs a controlled corpus-scaling comparison of lexical, dense, graph-indexed, and agentic retrieval-augmented generation across 28 nested corpus tiers from about one thousand to half a million documents, holding questions and reader fixed. Finds BM25 defines the low-cost end of the accuracy-cost Pareto frontier and scales best under this protocol, questioning the value of heavier indexing pipelines.

entry.title: DenseOn with the LateOn: Fully Open Dense and Late-Interaction Models for Multilingual, Long-Context, and Code Search

author.name: Rapha\"el Sourty, Antoine Chaffin, Paulo Roberto Moura Junior, Am\'elie Chatelain

entry.summary: Provides a fully open end-to-end recipe for training retrieval models, curating 665 million English contrastive pretraining pairs from public sources plus 1.88 million supervised pairs with mined hard negatives. The resulting 149M-parameter dense and ColBERT-style late-interaction models report state-of-the-art BEIR scores for their size class, with translate-train used to study multilingual transfer.

entry.title: TurboVLA: Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Model at 32 Hz on an RTX 4090 with <1 GB VRAM

author.name: Hengyi Xie, Chenfei Yao, Xianjin Wu, Xuanyang Xi, Yiping Tang, Di Xu, Yingying Zhu, Dingkang Liang, Xiang Bai, Han Ding

entry.summary: Replaces the usual vision-to-language-to-action pathway in robot policies with a direct vision-plus-language-to-action mapping, encoding modalities separately and exchanging information through lightweight bidirectional layers. Reports 32 Hz control on a consumer GPU using under one gigabyte of memory.

entry.title: Do Latent Channels Actually Communicate? A Causal Audit of Latent Multi-Agent LLM

author.name: Huixiang Zhang, Mahzabeen Emu

entry.summary: Performs a causal audit of latent communication in multi-agent LLM systems by swapping messages at the sender-receiver boundary under four controlled conditions, testing whether receivers actually use task-relevant content rather than merely benefiting from message presence. It shows end-task gains alone cannot establish that latent channels carry real information.

entry.title: On-Policy Distillation for LLM Safety: A Routing Approach to Template-Robust Realignment

author.name: Yongjian Guo, Wanlun Ma, Lingyu Shen, Xi Xiao, Sheng Wen

entry.summary: ROPD is a safety realignment method combining routing with on-policy distillation to restore alignment in models fine-tuned on maliciously poisoned downstream data, while preserving specialized skills. It specifically targets defenses that fail when the attacker prompt template is unobserved or when system prompts are switched to re-jailbreak the model.

entry.title: From CUDA to MLX: How K-Search Brings Decades of Kernel Expertise to Apple Silicon

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Berkeley researchers describe K-Search, a system that translates accumulated CUDA kernel optimization knowledge into architecture-native strategies for Apple Silicon MLX rather than porting instructions literally. It targets the growing problem that each new accelerator ecosystem forces rediscovery of hard-won kernel optimizations for operations like attention.

entry.title: CaM-Wolf: Causal-Aware Multimodal Agents for Social Deduction Games

author.name: Zheng Zhang, Nanjie Yao, Jiarui He, Deheng Ye, Peilin Zhao, Hao Wang

entry.summary: CaM-Wolf extends social deduction agents to the multimodal setting by processing video of other players and training a causal-aware reasoner with reinforcement learning to link observable behavior to hidden roles. It also generates the agent's own multimodal self-presentation, moving beyond text-only Werewolf agents.

entry.title: Property-driven Causal Abstractions for Markov Decision Processes

author.name: Jule Schmidt, Maximilian Weininger, Clemens Dubslaff, David Parker, Nils Jansen

entry.summary: Introduces a notion of causality on factored Markov decision processes and a property-driven abstraction technique that groups states sharing the same causal reasons for satisfying or violating a target property. Theoretical guarantees plus empirical scalability results are reported.

entry.title: Linguistic Monoculture in LLM-Assisted Language Use

author.name: Suhas Thejaswi, Juhi Kulshreshta, Lutz Oettershagen

entry.summary: Develops a mathematical coevolution framework where authors and LLMs are distributions over linguistic features, analyzing three interaction regimes: a static shared model, a shared model recursively retrained on author outputs, and personalized models. It formalizes how widespread LLM writing assistance can collapse population-level linguistic diversity.

entry.title: When Synthetic Users Fail: A Cross-Domain Benchmark of LLM-Simulated Human Survey Responses

author.name: Zihan Chen, Di Zhu, Lei Nico Zheng

entry.summary: Benchmarks LLMs as synthetic survey respondents against real human data from the General Social Survey and World Values Survey, using four models spanning an eight-billion to frontier capability range and comparing against non-LLM baselines fit on held-out human data. Establishes when demographic-prompted substitution for human respondents is valid and when it fails.

entry.title: ReCo: Reweighting GRPO Against Distributional Concentration

author.name: Junoh Park, Junseo Hwang, Wonguk Cho, Taesup Kim

entry.summary: ReCo diagnoses why group relative policy optimization can shrink a base model's reasoning coverage and underperform it at large pass-at-k: high-probability responses dominate the group gradient by repeated occurrence, and the token-level importance ratio further reinforces already-likely tokens. The proposed reweighting counteracts this distributional concentration.

entry.title: Hearsay: Vision-Language Medical Diagnoses Without an Image

author.name: Siddharth Vohra

entry.summary: This audit shows that when frontier vision-language models are asked to describe a medical image that was never attached, they do not abstain but confabulate diagnoses that shift systematically with the stated patient demographics. Probing several current frontier models across chest X-ray, brain MRI, and dermatology prompts, the study finds sharply concentrated demographic-driven diagnoses, with reasoning that explicitly cites demographics.

entry.title: BayesAME: Bayesian Active Model Evaluation

author.name: Paula Cordero Encinar, Taylan Cemgil, Arnaud Doucet, Virginia Aglietti, Silvia Chiappa

entry.summary: BayesAME is a sequential Bayesian framework for estimating a model's full benchmark performance from a subset of items, and its distinguishing feature is automatically determining the required subset size instead of requiring the practitioner to fix one in advance. It models performance as a random variable with latent abilities shared across item groups, in the spirit of item-response theory.

entry.title: ClockRoPE: Random Fourier Rotations for Temporal Routine Modeling

author.name: Yiwen Chen, Joshua Ainslie, Krzysztof Choromanski, Xiang Gao, Su-Lin Wu, Yiping Yuan, Qian Sun

entry.summary: ClockRoPE generalizes rotary position embeddings by proving that any normalized continuous positive-definite attention modulation can be approximated by random rotations derived from its Fourier transform, then instantiates rotation frequencies suited to daily and weekly periodicity in sequential recommendation. Standard RoPE bakes in a log-linear schedule tuned for monotone long-range decay, which is wrong for periodic domains. The theory is broader than the recommendation application.

entry.title: Forecasting Trajectory-Level Safety Risks in Black-Box Multi-Turn Interactions

author.name: Shi Lin, Peng Qian, Dinghao Liu, Renjie Sun, Sifan Wu, Dezhang Kong, Chenpei Wang, Xun Wang

entry.summary: Recast forecasts trajectory-level safety risk in black-box multi-turn interactions rather than detecting violations after they manifest, addressing attacks where malicious intent is split across individually harmless turns and reassembled over a conversation. Current safeguards are reactive and operate at the turn level. Predictive risk estimation would enable preemptive intervention in agentic deployments.

entry.title: Amortized Moment Matching for Visual Generation

author.name: Wenze Liu, Xintao Wang, Pengfei Wan, Xiangyu Yue

entry.summary: Amortized moment matching uses neural networks to learn data moments as distributional training signals, showing via polynomial projections of diffusion denoisers that an n-th degree projection identifies moments up to order n plus one, and instantiating an amortized Frechet distance loss. Unlike Frechet-distance losses requiring explicit marginal moment computation, this variant learns conditional moments through a matrix-free alternating optimization that scales to high dimensions. It functions as a post-training objective on global representation features.

entry.title: What Can Latent World Models Know? Physical Parameter Identifiability in Multimodal Predictive Representations

author.name: Kaizhen Tan (New York University, Carnegie Mellon University), Xin Xu (Carnegie Mellon University), Siru Tao (Carnegie Mellon University), Hanzhe Hong (Carnegie Mellon University), Yang Feng (Columbia University), Heqing Du (Columbia University)

entry.summary: Using a controlled interactive environment where visually identical objects hide different mass, drag, and contact stiffness, this study asks which physical parameters a trained latent world model actually encodes. A certificate-gated protocol first verifies each parameter is in principle recoverable from raw observations before testing whether it enters the latent, so null results can be attributed to the training objective rather than the environment. The resulting identifiability map shows inputs bound what can be known while prediction targets decide what is retained.

entry.title: Incast-Free MoE Rate-Based Scheduling

author.name: Evyatar Cohen, Jose Yallouz, Alexander Shpiner, Mark Silberstein, Sylvia Ratnasamy, Isaac Keslassy

entry.summary: Shows that the common round-robin expert scheduling used in mixture-of-experts serving triggers an exponential network incast pattern that oversubscribes the interconnect fabric. Proposes proactive rate-based fair scheduling implementable in NICs, and reports elimination of incast with near-full link utilization and shorter collective completion times in simulation.

entry.title: AgentSnare: Learning to Delay, Divert, and Defuse Autonomous Penetration Agents

author.name: Ruoyu Wang, Heng Zhao, Renjie Wu, Mengnan Zhao, Zhixuan Chu, Wanyu Lin, Tianhang Zheng

entry.summary: Introduces a trajectory-adaptive deception defense that dynamically unfolds a decoy environment against LLM-driven penetration-testing agents, rather than relying on static planted artifacts that capable agents learn to bypass. Aims to delay, divert, and defuse autonomous offensive agents by feeding them adaptive misleading observations.

entry.title: Mitigating Compounding Error via Video Representation Regularization

author.name: Taiye Chen, Qi Zhang, Yisen Wang

entry.summary: Investigates why autoregressive video world models degrade over long rollouts and finds that compounding error coincides with dimensional collapse, measured as a sharp drop in the effective rank of hidden representations at the onset of drift. Proposes representation regularization to preserve rank and stabilize long-horizon generation.

entry.title: SpecFirst: Behavioral Specification Elicitation as a First-Class Step in Agent-Based Program Synthesis from Scratch

author.name: Yihao Chen, Shi Chang, Feng Lin, Khaled Chawa, Boyuan Chen, Shaowei Wang, Ahmed E. Hassan

entry.summary: Argues that agents building programs from scratch should first elicit an explicit behavioral specification instead of mixing documentation reading, oracle probing, and coding in one pass. Motivated by benchmarks where frontier models solve under one percent of from-scratch synthesis tasks, the method borrows requirements-engineering structure for agent pipelines.

entry.title: Visko Orbis 1.0: A Live Model for Real-Time Interactive Long Video Generation

author.name: Xiangbo Gao, Siyuan Yang, Ping He, Mingyang Wu, Yuheng Wu, Yushen Zuo, Jiongze Yu, Ryan Cui, Hongyuan Hua, Devin Ma, Xiao Jin, Yubo Yuan, Qing Yin, Jie Yang, Zhengzhong Tu

entry.summary: A live interactive long-video generation system in which users can change prompts mid-generation and see updates in real time, supporting text-to-video, image-to-video, and continuation with multilingual prompts. Uses a distilled chunk-wise streaming generator plus a streaming upscaler and bounded multi-scale memory to sustain hour-scale 4K output at 24 FPS.

entry.title: Held-out Monitors Sometimes Degrade, Even When Not Trained Against

author.name: Joey Yudelson

entry.summary: Empirically tests whether supposedly held-out safety measurements stay valid when a model is optimized against a different measurement, and finds that they sometimes do not. Training against a language-model monitor can degrade an unrelated deception probe and vice versa, producing reward-hacking policies that look less suspicious to proxies that were never directly optimized.

entry.title: ClinLens: Towards Long-Horizon Coding Agents for Longitudinal Multimodal Clinical Data Science

author.name: Yuan Zhu, Ethan B. Liu, Frank Nie, Jindong Han

entry.summary: ClinLens is a benchmark of 200 executable clinical data-science tasks built from five linked MIMIC resources spanning structured records, notes, ECGs, and imaging, with reference workflows and artifact checking. It targets long-horizon coding agents that must produce auditable multimodal analyses rather than answer isolated medical questions.

entry.title: What Does It Take to Detect an AI Agent? Minimal Feature Sets for Behavioral Detection under Browser Automation

author.name: Vishisht Choudhary, Lukas Schmidt, Anne Zo\"e Kenntner, Feras Skhab, Michel Osswald, Jens Ernstberger

entry.summary: Argues that binary human-versus-bot web detection structurally cannot represent AI agents browsing via automation, showing binary classifiers misroute roughly a third or more of agent sessions as human. Adding an explicit third agent class yields near-perfect agent separation on their controlled benchmark.

entry.title: Seeing or Knowing? Visual Context Sensitivity in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Jiaang Li, Chengzu Li, Zhaochong An, Yifei Yuan, Xi Liu, Serge Belongie, V\'esteinn Sn{\ae}bjarnarson

entry.summary: Diagnoses why multimodal LLMs fail on vision-centric questions by separately testing whether visual information is even recoverable (via image reconstruction) and how strongly models follow visual evidence versus language priors. Introduces a benchmark where questions can be answered from either the image or memorized world knowledge across spatial, color, count, size, and weight dimensions.

entry.title: GoGoTB: Agentic RTL Verification with Specification-Grounded Coverage Closure

author.name: Xin Xin, Jincheng Lou, Junhui Li, Jinglin Yan, Panda Xiao, Di Wu, Haixiao Li, Weicong Lu, Weijian Fan, Xinyu Qu, Yuxiang Zhao, Min Yu, Zhixiong Di, Yibo Lin

entry.summary: GoGoTB is an agentic framework for RTL hardware verification that couples an execution control layer, an evolving knowledge base, and coverage closure tied back to specification requirements. It targets the interface mismatches and disconnected coverage metrics that plague single-shot LLM testbench generation.

entry.title: EvoPINN: Agentic Discovery of Executable Algorithms for Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Peng Yin, Kai Li, Yifan Zhang, Jian Cheng

entry.summary: EvoPINN treats physics-informed neural network design as an execution-grounded algorithm discovery problem, with an agent searching a modular space of representations, loss formulations, and optimizers under constraints that reject numerically unstable or mathematically invalid candidates. It aims to replace manual trial-and-error PINN engineering.

entry.title: Rethinking Self-Evolution: A Constrained Exploration-Exploitation Process for Mitigating Skill Overfitting

author.name: Hongqiang Lin, Chao Liu, Xiaofan Bai, Xuan Jin, Yuhong Li, Nenggan Zheng, Xipeng Cao

entry.summary: SkillBoost treats agent skills as trainable states and frames self-evolution as a constrained exploration-exploitation problem, using a three-stage pipeline to avoid both overfitting to collected trajectories and regression on previously solved tasks. It addresses skill overfitting in experience-accumulating agents.

entry.title: AgenticCANN: Automated Ascend C Operator Generation via Knowledge-Augmented Agentic Evolution

author.name: Junhao Qiu, Zidong Wang, Yansong Sun, Zhitong Ma, Ping Guo, Qingfu Zhang

entry.summary: AgenticCANN generates and optimizes Ascend C operators for NPUs using a knowledge-augmented agentic evolution loop designed for low-corpus hardware platforms where LLMs lack pretraining exposure. It contrasts with CUDA kernel generation work by targeting a fundamentally different programming model.

entry.title: Contextualized Counterspeech Can Be More Persuasive Than Generic Counterspeech

author.name: Lorenzo Cima, Alessio Miaschi, Amaury Trujillo, Marco Avenuti, Felice Dell'Orletta, Stefano Cresci

entry.summary: Evaluates strategies for generating counterspeech that adapts to conversational context and to characteristics of the moderated user, versus the usual generic one-size-fits-all approach. Combines quantitative indicators with a pre-registered mixed-design crowdsourcing experiment measuring persuasiveness.

entry.title: AgentGUI: An Interface for Observing and Steering Long-Running AI Agents

author.name: Xuan Zhao, Jiwoong Sohn, Qinyue Zheng, Michael Moor

entry.summary: AgentGUI is a locally hosted interface for observing and steering multiple concurrent long-running agent sessions, offering trajectory visualization, manual and automated steering, and integration across open-source and frontier agent frameworks. A controlled user study found participants identified key trace elements about 38 percent faster.

entry.title: Automorphism-Induced Non-Canonicity in Top-k Explanations of Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Xin Xu, Siru Tao, Kaizhen Tan

entry.summary: Shows that because message passing is permutation equivariant, symmetric substructures in a graph must receive identical attribution scores, so any top-k edge report necessarily breaks ties arbitrarily and cannot be simultaneously single-valued, minimal, and symmetry-respecting. Provides a parameter-free criterion mechanized in Lean 4.

entry.title: Early Verdicts, Better Budgets: Sequential Adaptive Rollout Allocation for Compute-Efficient RLVR

author.name: Pixel Nomand, Elena Voss, Marcus Hale, Sofia Reyes

entry.summary: This work treats RLVR rollout collection as an optimal stopping problem, observing that whether a prompt group will be saturated (all correct or all wrong, hence zero gradient signal) is usually decided within the first few rollouts. Instead of oversampling and discarding or predicting difficulty in advance, it adaptively halts spending on already-decided prompts and reallocates budget. This directly attacks the dominant compute cost in verifiable-reward RL post-training.

entry.title: StatePlay: State-Aware Game World Models for Mechanics-Consistent Generation

author.name: Zijun Lin, Zeqing Wang, Cheston Tan, Bihan Wen, Yeying Jin

entry.summary: Argues that game world models must track explicit internal state such as health, skill meters, and timers, not just pixels, to remain consistent with game mechanics. Proposes a model that jointly predicts visual frames and state dynamics so rollouts obey state-dependent rules.

entry.title: Notes on the Anthropic cryptographic blogpost

author.name: Philipreal

entry.summary: Summarizes and comments on an Anthropic post reporting that Claude Mythos Preview, an existing Anthropic model, discovered improved cryptanalytic attacks against the HAWK post-quantum signature candidate and against a weakened AES variant. The HAWK result reportedly forces roughly doubled key sizes, undermining its efficiency case, while neither attack threatens deployed systems today.

entry.title: TraceCLIP: Recovering Local Semantics from Patch-to-CLS Contributions

author.name: Xinran Liu, Shouqian Shi, Yutong Chen, Ge Wang, Xin-Wei Yao, Sheng Zhong

entry.summary: TraceCLIP recovers dense local semantics in CLIP by analyzing how individual patch tokens contribute to the class token representation, rather than adding supervision, external models, or task-specific adaptation. It targets open-vocabulary segmentation, localization, and region recognition in a training-free manner.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Debate Strategies: Survey, Taxonomy, and Challenges

author.name: Quim Motger, Marc Oriol, Jordi Marco, Xavier Franch

entry.summary: A systematic literature review of 141 multi-agent debate studies producing a three-dimensional taxonomy covering debate participants, interaction mechanisms, and agreement protocols, with formal notation for describing configurations. It documents fragmentation and inconsistent terminology across the field.

entry.title: Misalignment Has a Personality: A Big Five Account of Emergent Misalignment

author.name: Hasibur Rahman, Smit Desai

entry.summary: This work reframes emergent misalignment, where narrow fine-tuning on flawed data causes broad bad behavior, as a shift in model personality along Big Five trait directions. Instead of extracting steering vectors from a single binary contrast, the authors use a graded three-level intervention to obtain calibrated trait vectors that are linearly ordered, transfer zero-shot across two open-weight models, and reportedly separate large effect sizes.

entry.title: Human diversity fuels collective creativity that large language models cannot simulate or sustain

author.name: Mengchen Dong, Hiromu Yakura

entry.summary: A preregistered creative-metaphor experiment with native and non-native English writers tests two threats from generative AI to collective idea diversity: homogenization of what people produce, and replacement of diverse people with AI-simulated diversity. Non-native writers contributed more collective diversity, AI ideation compressed diversity and erased that advantage, while AI refinement of the writer's own ideas preserved more of it.

entry.title: DLAM: Distributional Latent Actions with Temporal Constraints

author.name: Zuojin Tang, Feifan Luo, Haoyun Liu, Botai Yuan, Dekang Qi, Ronghan Chen, Yandan Yang, Tong Lin, Xinyuan Chang, Mu Xu, Bin Liu, De Ma, Zhiheng Ma

entry.summary: DLAM learns latent actions from action-free video by modeling each temporal transition as a diagonal Gaussian rather than a deterministic point, grounding the mean in observed frames while letting the variance absorb inference error. The aim is to keep compounding errors from propagating when latent transitions are composed recursively for vision-language-action robot policies. It addresses the persistent scarcity of action-labeled robot data.

entry.title: From Tokens to Watt-hours: Analytical Energy Estimation for LLM Inference on Modern GPUs

author.name: Tina Vartziotis, Rodopi Kosteli, Elli Vartziotis, George Dasoulas, Michael Keckeisen, Konstantinos Skianis, Sotirios Kotsopoulos, Francesca Dominici

entry.summary: This report builds an analytically structured, empirically calibrated estimator for LLM inference energy on H100-class GPUs, combining parameter-scaled transformer FLOP accounting, calibrated memory-traffic factors, and hardware efficiency terms so energy per token can be projected without power instrumentation. Direct measurement usually requires telemetry that most researchers and reporters lack. It supports comparative studies, early system design, and sustainability reporting.

entry.title: Equilibrium Training of Energy-Based Models with Parallel Trajectory Tempering

author.name: Nicolas B\'ereux, Aur\'elien Decelle, Cyril Furtlehner, Beatriz Seoane

entry.summary: This work trains energy-based models with parallel trajectory tempering, exploiting continuity of the optimization path to maintain equilibrium Markov chain sampling throughout learning, at a cost comparable to persistent contrastive divergence. Poor chain mixing is the dominant reliability failure of EBMs on multimodal and data-scarce scientific datasets. The method also yields direct thermalization-time estimates and genuine equilibrium samples.

entry.title: Simplex Demixing: Disentangling Multiple Light-Flavor Jets at Colliders

author.name: Gregorio de la Fuente, Jesse Thaler

entry.summary: Simplex demixing extends the data-driven operational definition of jet flavors at particle colliders from two categories to an arbitrary number, translating a multi-category classifier over mixed data samples into a bounded geometric simplex whose vertices identify the maximally separable underlying categories. Defining multiple jet flavors at hadron level has been a long-standing open problem. The technique is a general topic-model-style unmixing method with minimal assumptions.

entry.title: Randomizing the Number of Centers in k-means++

author.name: Vaclav Rozhon

entry.summary: The classic k-means++ seeding algorithm has a worst-case expected approximation ratio that grows logarithmically in the number of centers, but this paper shows that if an adversary fixes the dataset and a budget while the actual center count is drawn uniformly from a range around that budget, k-means++ becomes a constant-factor approximation with constant probability. It is a smoothed-analysis style explanation for why the algorithm works so well in practice. The result reframes a known worst-case pessimism.

entry.title: Rethinking Clinical Relevance in Chest X-ray Machine Learning: How Evaluation References Define Performance

author.name: Panagiotis Fytas, Ian Selby, Clemens Karner, Judith Babar, Simon Baker, Jake Beckford, Timothy J. Sadler, Shahab Shahipasand, Arthikkaa Thavakumar, John Li Chen, Alex Sawer, Michael Roberts, Jonathan Weir-McCall, J. H. F. Rudd, Carola-Bibiane Sch\"onlieb, Anna Korhonen, Anna Breger

entry.summary: Systematically studies how the choice of evaluation reference (report-derived labels versus expert image labels, and generic image quality metrics) changes measured performance and model rankings in chest X-ray classification and reconstruction quality assessment. Uses newly collected paired expert annotations from a hospital cohort plus a curated MIMIC-CXR subset.

entry.title: InferScale: GPU-Native KV Injection for Personalized LLM Serving

author.name: Peter Li, Prashant Pandey

entry.summary: Replaces repeated prompt prefilling of retrieved personalization memories with precomputed reusable key-value states injected directly on the GPU, indexed by semantic embeddings. Targets the time-to-first-token blowup that occurs as memory retrieval budgets grow in production memory systems.

entry.title: MindForge: Teaching Small Language Models Whole-Life-Cycle Software Engineering via Source-Free Program Synthesis

author.name: Yihao Chen, Shi Chang, Khaled Chawa, Feng Lin, Boyuan Chen, Shaowei Wang, Ahmed E. Hassan

entry.summary: Introduces an automated pipeline that converts open-source command-line programs into source-free training environments exposing only a compiled reference binary, enabling scalable training on building complete programs from scratch. Motivated by the observation that frontier models resolve under one percent of from-scratch program-synthesis tasks in ProgramBench.

entry.title: Revisiting Lossy Verification in Speculative Decoding: Mechanisms, Trade-offs, and Failure Modes

author.name: Tianyu Wang, Yuxuan Zhou, Wenbin Wang, Heng Li, Zikai Xiao, Junyuan Shang

entry.summary: Analyzes lossy verification schemes in speculative decoding, showing that many apparently distinct methods reduce to either truncation-based or relaxation-based rewriting of the decoding distribution. Characterizes the resulting speed-versus-quality trade-offs and identifies failure modes where generation quality degrades severely.

entry.title: SERPO: Self-Evolving Rubric Policy Optimization for Open-Ended Test-Time Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jianze Wang, Kunwang Zheng, Ying Liu, Yu Cao, Qilong Zhang, Jinlong Chen, Hua Yang, Qianglong Chen

entry.summary: Extends test-time reinforcement learning to open-ended generation, where majority voting over answers is unavailable, by co-evolving response archives, query-specific rubrics, and policy parameters in a closed loop. Rollouts are organized into good, normal, and bad tiers to build self-generated reward signal without external judges.

entry.title: Prosody-driven Jailbreaks in Audio LLMs: A Controlled Study and Mechanistic Analysis

author.name: Jiachen Qian, Junyu Li

entry.summary: Studies whether the way a sentence is spoken (arousal, authority, speaking rate) can jailbreak audio-capable LLMs while keeping the transcript fixed. Introduces a black-box protocol and a 600-sample acoustically verified benchmark, finding that high-arousal presets such as panic, anger, and fast speech substantially raise unsafe-response rates on an audio model panel.

entry.title: Level, Sharpness, and Corpus: Why Zero-Shot OOD Detector Rankings Do Not Transfer

author.name: Ignacio M. De la Jara, Cristian Rodriguez-Opazo, Stephen Gould, Damith Ranasinghe

entry.summary: A portability audit showing that zero-shot out-of-distribution detector rankings reverse across deployments, spanning seventeen in-distribution datasets, three vision-language models, and seven detectors. Every detector fails badly on at least one domain, and the best choice depends jointly on data and backbone.

entry.title: ContactFlow: A video action conditioning that transfers across embodiments

author.name: Sami Azirar, Enrico Pallotta, Jan Nogga, J\"urgen Gall, Sven Behnke, Hermann Blum

entry.summary: Proposes conditioning video world models on the trajectory of 3D contact points between actor and object rather than embodiment-specific actions, so human demonstrations and robot executions share one action representation. Intended to capture contact physics that video world models typically miss.

entry.title: MoMo: Dial Motion Mode in Robot Manipulation with Spatiotemporal Action Tokenization

author.name: Yuhan Hu, Hugues Thomas, Peide Huang, Mouli Sivapurapu, Benoit Landry, Arto Kivila

entry.summary: Presents an imitation-learning framework where a spatiotemporal action tokenizer and behavior-cloning transformer accept a continuous motion-mode condition, so a single policy can execute the same task steadily or dynamically. Across six real-robot manipulation tasks, varying this condition produces behaviors that human raters distinguish and that differ measurably in speed and approach.

entry.title: DVPSFormer: Efficient Online Depth-aware Video Panoptic Segmentation for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yung-Hsu Yang, Luigi Piccinelli, Siyuan Li, Mattia Segu, Lei Ke, Martin Danelljan, Yuqian Fu, Zuria Bauer, Fisher Yu, Hermann Blum, Marc Pollefeys

entry.summary: Proposes a single online transformer that jointly estimates metric depth, panoptic segmentation, and instance tracking for driving scenes, replacing multi-stage or offline pipelines. A scene discretization mechanism uses segmentation queries to bridge discrete regions and continuous depth for real-time 4D understanding.

entry.title: Genie Sim PanoWorld: An Infinite Indoor 3D World Generation Pipeline via Panoramic Scene Modeling and Simulation

author.name: Yongxin Su, Linjie Hou, Feng Wang, Jialin Tang, Zhijun Li, Qian Wang, Maoqing Yao

entry.summary: A two-stage feed-forward pipeline that turns a single 360-degree panorama into a freely navigable 3D indoor scene without per-scene optimization, injecting a planned camera trajectory into a panoramic latent video diffusion model and then reconstructing. Targets metric trajectory control and large disocclusions on modest hardware for simulation use.

entry.title: DistillAlign: Coordinating Mode Covering and Mode Seeking in Autoregressive Video Distillation

author.name: Jiaxing Li, Kai Zou, Cindy Zhou, Kaichen Huang, Junyao Gao, Zile Wang, Yang Liu, Bin Liu, Bo An, Yangguang Li

entry.summary: Revisits distribution-matching distillation for autoregressive video generation, arguing that the initialization stage should match the teacher's mode coverage rather than maximize visual quality scores. Introduces a precision-and-coverage evaluation protocol in a shared distribution space to guide the multi-stage pipeline.

entry.title: Explicit Kinematic Guidance from Analytic Concepts for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Mingyang Sun, Jiude Wei, Xiujian Liang, Qichen He, Donglin Wang, Cewu Lu, Jianhua Sun

entry.summary: Adds a concept-expert module to vision-language-action models that represents objects as explicit programmatic blueprints with kinematic and structural parameters estimated from 3D vision foundation models. The blueprint is initialized before inference and used during manipulation to supply structural priors that 2D-only VLAs lack.

entry.title: When benchmark inferences do not compose: Projectibility in AI evaluation

author.name: Brett Reynolds

entry.summary: A conceptual paper arguing that individually valid benchmark inferences do not compose into valid chains when the target of one study becomes the source of the next, and that shared data or model lineage creates hidden dependence. It introduces projectibility as the missing epistemic criterion for AI evaluation.

entry.title: GuideSkill: Evolving Executable LLM Agent Skills for Guideline-Grounded Clinical Reasoning

author.name: Lang Cao, Yuhao Shen, Tianyang Luo, Simo Du, Hao Peng, Yue Guo

entry.summary: GuideSkill compiles clinical practice guidelines into executable scoring functions that an LLM invokes as an external reasoning layer, with an evolutionary variant that refines and extends skills from case-diagnosis pairs. Reported gains over guideline retrieval baselines across four benchmarks and four backbones.

entry.title: UrbanDS: A Graph-Guided LLM Multi-Agent System for Data-Intensive Urban Tasks

author.name: Zhilun Zhou, Jianghao Yu, Yuming Lin, yongjun yang, Sun Yongquan, Depeng Jin, Yong Li

entry.summary: UrbanDS is a graph-guided multi-agent system for data-intensive urban analysis that builds a unified dataset graph linking reusable dataset skills and their spatial, temporal, and semantic relationships. It targets the discovery problem when relevant data must be found across large heterogeneous repositories rather than handed to the agent.

entry.title: SimpleWikiSearch: A Clean Offline Wikipedia Environment for Agentic Search

author.name: Guanming Xiong, Penghui Zhang

entry.summary: SimpleWikiSearch provides a fully specified and runnable offline Wikipedia search environment for agentic search evaluation, fixing the corpus snapshot, chunking, retrieval backend, tool schema, observation format, and answer submission rule. It addresses the problem that agentic search results are confounded by under-specified environment details rather than model capability alone.

entry.title: Towards Trustworthy Embodied Intelligence: A Systems Framework and Graded Trustworthiness Levels

author.name: Xinyu Yang, Tianxing Chen, Honghao Su, Minxuan Wang, Chenze Yu, Zhangzheng Tu, Yue Chen, Yuxiao Huo, Lingfeng Zhang, Yan Huang, Yan Qin, Shaolong Zhu, Qiwei Liang, Hekun Tian, Shujia Liu, Guangyu Chen, Junhao Gong, Zixuan Li, Wenwei Lin, Zijian Lin, Wenxuan Zhu, Eric J Chen, Yue Yuan, Qize Yu, Jiaqi Liang, Haowen Yan, Hengfei Zhao, Weijie Wan, Zikun Xiao, Junyuan Tang, Baijun Chen, Kai-Chong Lei, Kaixuan Wang, Kailun Su, Zanxin Chen, Yao Mu, Renjing Xu, Chuqiao Lyu, Qi Xiong, Ping Luo, Wenbo Ding

entry.summary: Defines trustworthy embodied intelligence as sustained safe success, the ability to complete specified tasks reliably under variation while keeping risk bounded, and organizes supporting mechanisms into model, system, and higher layers with graded trustworthiness levels. It is a systems framework paper from a very large multi-institution collaboration.

entry.title: Top-$k$ Pareto Bandits: Hypervolume Regret for Multi-Objective Slate Selection

author.name: Nicolas Gutowski, Fabien Chhel, Alexandre Letard, Sylvain Lamprier

entry.summary: Formalizes multi-objective slate selection as maintaining a size-k subset approximating the Pareto frontier, defines an approximate hypervolume regret relative to the best hindsight subset with a greedy submodular approximation factor, and proposes an algorithm for the semi-bandit setting. Provides theoretical regret analysis.

entry.title: High-Order Markov Blanket Discovery via a k-Order Relaxation of the Faithfulness Assumption

author.name: Loong Kuan Lee, Ragavi Krishnamoorthy, Nico Piatkowski

entry.summary: Relaxes the faithfulness assumption underlying Markov blanket discovery to a k-order variant that tolerates higher-order dependencies such as XOR and parity relations, which break standard conditional independence based structure learning. Relevant to causal discovery, Bayesian network structure learning, and feature selection.

entry.title: Borrowed Strength: Best-of-N Search over a Code EncodingBreaks Self-Check Jailbreak Defenses

author.name: Haoyu Zhang, Shibo Zheng, Xiangchen Guan, Zhuoxi Wang, Zijian Xiao, Mohammad Zandsalimy, Shanu Sushmita

entry.summary: The paper shows that a self-check jailbreak defense reporting near-total success can be broken by composing two individually ineffective attacks, a code-completion encoding and best-of-N search, reaching high breach rates across several open targets including a 70B model. The explanation is that a self-check defense borrows its detection strength from the target model itself, so encoding that the target willingly decodes converts the defense into an attack surface.

entry.title: SecRespond: Benchmarking AI Agents for Real-World Post-Compromise Incident Response

author.name: Lehan Wang, Boli Chen, Ruixue Ding, Pengjun Xie, Jinwei Huang, Zhendong Liu, Shuo Wang, Tao Lei, Xin Ouyang, Xiaomeng Li

entry.summary: SecRespond is a benchmark placing LLM agents in post-compromise incident response, giving them a forensic disk snapshot of a breached host plus alerts, vulnerability scans, and baseline checks, and requiring investigation through command-line access. It fills a gap left by cybersecurity benchmarks that only test agents in clean pre-attack environments.

entry.title: Enfold: Folding World-Generator Computation into Predictive Representations for Efficient Embodied Control

author.name: Weili Zeng, Yitong Xing, Fulong Liu, Chengqun Yang, Antao Xiang, Feng Tian, Jingnan Gao, Jisong Cai, Xin Wang, Xiaomin Wu, Yao Mu, Yichao Yan

entry.summary: Enfold argues that the valuable part of a video or world generative model is not its rendered output but the internal computation that builds a plausible future, and distills that multi-level computation into a representation predicted directly from current observations plus a language instruction. This removes the expensive generative rollout at inference time while keeping predictive structure useful for embodied control.

entry.title: Intentional Control of Internal States in Gemma 3 27B

author.name: Julius Kamp

entry.summary: An independent capstone replication of the intentional-control-of-internal-states experiment from Anthropic's work on emergent introspective awareness, run on Gemma 3 27B Instruct. The author finds the same directional effect at weaker strength using activation probes, and reports it appears much more clearly when measured via sparse autoencoder latents and natural-language autoencoder explanations of activations.

entry.title: Probing the Origins of Reasoning Performance: Representational Quality for Mathematical Problem-Solving in RL vs. SFT Fine-Tuned Models

author.name: Antyabha Rahman, Akshaj Gurugubelli, Omar Ankit, Kevin Zhu, Aishwarya Balwani

entry.summary: The paper probes why RL-trained reasoning models beat supervised fine-tuned ones on math, using layer-wise linear probes and mean-ablation studies. It reports that RL models encode answer correctness more linearly and develop a more hierarchical depth-wise structure. This is a mechanistic-interpretability contribution to the ongoing RL-versus-SFT debate.

entry.title: MultivationBench: A Benchmark for Multimodal Sequential Motivation Reasoning

author.name: Kawai Chung, Chunkit Chan, Yauwai Yim, Yuxuan Liu, Haochen Shi, Weiqi Wang, Qing Zong, Tianshi Zheng, Yixuan Fu, Kai Chung Wong, Hao Liang, Yifan Gao, Xi Yang, Janet Hui-wen Hsiao, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: MultivationBench evaluates whether multimodal LLMs can infer evolving human motivations across story-driven visual narratives, grounded in Maslow and Reiss psychological frameworks. It targets sequential, cumulative motivation reasoning rather than static snapshot inference.

entry.title: Identifying Implicit Bias in LLM-based Chat AI Toward People with Intellectual Disabilities

author.name: Karly V. Coffey, Gloria L. Krahn, John P. Hanley, Jacob E. Neely

entry.summary: Measures implicit bias toward people with intellectual disabilities by generating 25,000 stories from five commercial LLMs using matched prompt stems with and without disability descriptors, then analyzing representational differences with a separate model. Provides quantitative evidence of systematic representational disparities in widely deployed assistants.

entry.title: Voice Memory for Agentic Speech Recognition

author.name: Chao-Han Huck Yang, Zih-Ching Chen, Piotr Zelasko, Zhehuai Chen, Jagadeesh Balam, Boris Ginsburg

entry.summary: Voice Memory equips speech recognition with an inference-only agentic loop: a frozen corrector reads a per-domain markdown memory file and decides per utterance whether to revise or keep the original hypothesis, while an asynchronous optimizer edits the memory file only when a held-out score strictly improves. The key finding is that restraint, not aggressive generative correction, is what the loop learns, since unconstrained correction over-corrects and hurts accuracy.

entry.title: Graph Is the Verifier: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Interprocedural Vulnerability Detection

author.name: Yikun Li, Ting Zhang, Jiakun Liu, Jinfeng Jiang, Yuheng Yieh, Yixin Yang, Wen Bin Leow, Yide Yin, Yintong Huo, Eng Lieh Ouh, Lwin Khin Shar, David Lo

entry.summary: VulAgentRL uses a code property graph both as an inference-time evidence source and as a verifier that rewards genuine investigative behavior, addressing the finding that most vulnerable functions in real CVEs cannot be judged from the function body alone. This closes a reward-hacking loophole where verdict-only rewards can be earned without any interprocedural investigation.

entry.title: See2Think: Do Multimodal Models Really Use Intermediate Visual States?

author.name: Siyu Yan, Zhuoran Yan, Haiying Xu, Panhao Zhou, Jingyu Chen, Chenhao Ji, Shuo Cao, Yongheng Zhang, Haoze Liu, Siyu Zhang, Xiwen Gu, Yihao Liu, Alex Jinpeng Wang

entry.summary: See2Think evaluates whether multimodal models genuinely rely on the sketches, annotations, and intermediate images they produce during reasoning, rather than merely being able to answer from text. It pairs a benchmark of 1,200 visually dependent open-ended problems across twelve categories with an instrumentation scheme that records textual thoughts alongside visual actions so intermediate-state generation, rendering, and use can be diagnosed.

entry.title: SkillRise: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Cross-Task Skill Evolution

author.name: Zhiyuan Yao, Yuxin Chen, Zhengxi Lu, Zishan Xu, Yueqing Sun, Yifu Guo, Yuquan Lu, Zhengzhou Cai, Kangning Zhang, Zhuowen Han, Zi-Han Wang, Ziang Ye, Qi Gu, Xunliang Cai, Weiwen Liu, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: SkillRise trains a single agent policy with reinforcement learning to alternate between solving tasks and curating an evolving skill document that is passed to the next, harder task, with decoupled credit assignment separating supervision of solving from supervision of skill curation. It targets reuse of solution patterns across related but distinct tasks, which standard episodic agentic RL discards.

entry.title: The Social Cost of an AI Teammate: How an Artificial Teammate Reshapes Human-Human Communication in Small-Team Decision-Making

author.name: Nia Nixon, Jaeyoon Choi, Pedro Martins De Bastos, Mohammad Amin Samadi, Luise Mehner, Seehee Park, Spencer JaQuay

entry.summary: A randomized controlled study of 16 two-human-plus-AI teams versus 17 all-human teams on a moral dilemma decision task finds that the AI teammate dominated the conversation while contributing the least new information and lowest informational density. The work measures sociocognitive dynamics with Group Communication Analysis and surveys, showing an AI teammate can crowd out human-human communication. It is early empirical evidence that agentic teammates carry social costs, not only productivity benefits.

entry.title: Dynamic Parameterization Is Not Dynamic Inference

author.name: Zongfei Li, Yuan-yih Shang, Guozhong Luo

entry.summary: This paper argues that input-dependent controller coefficients in adaptive architectures are routinely misread as evidence of dynamic inference or compute savings, and separates three distinct properties that get conflated. Frozen-Controller Auditing caches the coefficient tensor along an unperturbed trajectory, disables the controller, and replays the model with cross-input reassignment and shuffling to test whether the coefficient assignment actually matters. It is a diagnostic protocol that could deflate many adaptive-computation claims.

entry.title: Between Gradient and Natural Gradient: A Continuum of LoRA Initializations

author.name: Dianze Liu, Farshid Ghezelbash

entry.summary: ULoRA shows that competing gradient-based LoRA initialization schemes, whether they project the raw gradient or first whiten it with curvature estimates, are special cases of a single two-parameter family governed by a spectral whitening exponent and an Adam-like diagonal exponent. Sweeping the family under full learning-rate search reveals that no fixed preconditioning strength is universally best. It is a unifying and somewhat deflationary analysis of a crowded subfield.

entry.title: Simultaneous Coverage and Efficiency Guarantee in Online Conformal Prediction

author.name: Rahul Vaze

entry.summary: This paper identifies three flaws in adaptive conformal inference under distribution shift: guarantees control only signed long-run coverage so sustained miscoverage can be masked by later compensation, nothing constrains prediction-set width, and existing efficiency comparisons use a fixed hindsight predictor as benchmark. It then derives an online method giving simultaneous coverage and efficiency guarantees against a stronger dynamic benchmark. It strengthens the theoretical foundation of online conformal prediction.

entry.title: Mixture-of-experts for handwriting trajectory reconstruction from IMU sensors

author.name: Florent Imbert, Eric Anquetil, Yann Soullard, Romain Tavenard

entry.summary: This theory paper proves that permutation-equivariant neural networks with partially random node features can approximate, in probability, any measurable permutation-invariant or equivariant function on directed graphs of fixed size with multidimensional node and edge features, and derives approximation rates for smooth targets. The class subsumes many popular GNN architectures. It formalizes why random features expand GNN expressivity beyond Weisfeiler-Leman limits.

entry.title: Two Calls Beat Five Agents: Evaluating Multi-Agent Pipelines Against Self-Refinement for Local Language Models

author.name: Ashish Prajapati, Om Mohite

entry.summary: Deploying a five-role multi-agent pipeline on a local 7B model dropped GSM8K accuracy from 75 to 45 percent with JSON message formats due to error accumulation, recovering to 82 percent with plaintext, while a simple two-call self-refinement reached 86.2 percent using roughly seven times fewer tokens. The study shows multi-agent orchestration benefits reported with large commercial models do not transfer to small local models. Message format alone caused a 37-point swing.

entry.title: Temporally Centered SIGReg Improves Multi-Task LeWorldModel Learning: From Analysis to Method

author.name: Chang Liu, Fei Suo, Yanzhou Jin, Yusuke Iwasawa, Yutaka Matsuo, Yaonan Zhu

entry.summary: This paper analyzes why the sketched isotropic Gaussian regularizer that stabilizes single-task pixel-based world model learning degrades in multi-task settings, showing that marginal Gaussianization compresses separation between task-dependent latent clusters relative to within-cluster variance and creates representation aliasing. It then proposes a temporally centered variant that restores multi-task behavior-cloning performance. The analysis-to-method structure is a clean diagnosis of a collapse-prevention tradeoff.

entry.title: Lottery Tickets Are Not Deployment Tickets

author.name: Bum Jun Kim

entry.summary: This paper audits whether an accuracy-matched lottery-ticket or sparse model can actually replace an incumbent dense model in production without reconfiguring downstream decision logic, examining calibration, out-of-distribution response, and other deployment-relevant behaviors rather than accuracy alone. Prior sparsification studies report mixed effects and ignore fixed downstream thresholds. The conclusion is that matching accuracy is insufficient for drop-in replacement.

entry.title: DREvo: Distilling Recalibrated Historical Experience for Harness Self-Evolution

author.name: Hanghui Guo, Weijie Shi, Zhangze Chen, Shengxiang Xu, Yishu Wang, Yimei Zhang, Wangze Ni, Jia Zhu, Shimin Di

entry.summary: Addresses instability in self-evolving LLM agent harnesses by recalibrating accumulated historical trial experience rather than trusting it uniformly, and distilling it into more reliable search guidance. Targets discovery of high-performing harnesses under a limited evolution budget.

entry.title: On the robustness of noisy solutions in non-convex neural networks

author.name: Enrico M. Malatesta, Alessandra Passalacqua, Riccardo Zecchina

entry.summary: Extends the overlap-gap-property analysis of solution-space geometry in non-convex neural networks from zero temperature to finite temperature, where nonzero training error is allowed but penalized. Characterizes how the frozen replica-symmetry-breaking solution that dominates at zero error gives way to different structures, clarifying which regions remain algorithmically accessible.

entry.title: Contrastive ESA: Human Evaluation of Multiple Translations at Once

author.name: Vil\'em Zouhar, Roman Grundkiewicz, Sara Rajaee, Parker Riley, Martin Popel, Rachel Bawden, Philipp Koehn, Marine Carpuat, Tom Kocmi

entry.summary: Proposes a human machine-translation evaluation protocol in which annotators see multiple translations of the same source together, mark major and minor error spans, then score on an absolute scale. A large English to Japanese study over 12 systems shows reduced annotation time and improved consistency versus isolated single-output assessment.

entry.title: OptimismBench: Forecasting Bias and the Alignment Effect in Language Model Judgment

author.name: Seonglae Cho, Adriano Koshiyama

entry.summary: Detects signed directional bias in model probability judgments using inverted prompt pairs that elicit both success and failure probabilities for the same scenario, so asymmetry reveals distortion without ground truth. Across 16 models from 8 providers, fourteen show systematic optimism, which aggregate calibration metrics would not surface.

entry.title: CineWeaver: Training-Free Reference-Controllable Multi-Shot Long Video Generation for Cinematic Storytelling

author.name: Yuyang Huang, Yabo Chen, Wenrui Dai, Ziyang Zheng, Haibin Huang, Chi Zhang, Junni Zou, Hongkai Xiong, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: A training-free framework for generating multi-shot, long-form cinematic video with reference control over characters and scenes. Identifies that pretrained video diffusion models are structurally biased toward temporal continuity and counteracts this bias to enable shot changes without retraining.

entry.title: Representation Trajectories Matters: Complementary Evidence for OOD Detection and Image Classification

author.name: Ignacio M. De la Jara, Cristian Rodriguez-Opazo, Hamed Damirchi, Stephen Gould, Damith Ranasinghe

entry.summary: Argues that the path a representation takes through network blocks carries information the final layer discards, and studies these depth trajectories while preserving sample identity. Separates class-level transport from input-specific innovation and shows the trajectory evidence improves out-of-distribution detection and classification under shift.

entry.title: Ripple: Real-Time Streaming Audio-Video Generation With Cross-Modal Recurrent Memory

author.name: Yanbo Ding, Zhizhi Guo, Quanyue Song, Yishan He, Zhixiang He, Yongxiang Li, Yali Wang

entry.summary: A real-time joint audio and video generation system that combines fixed-length sliding-window attention with modality-specific recurrent memory states summarizing longer context. Cross-modal memory interaction is added to keep audio and video synchronized during long streaming rollouts.

entry.title: Prior Directions: Why GUI Grounding Gets Locked in the Past

author.name: Weile Gong, Zijian Lu, Mingcai Chen, Yiping Zuo, Xin He, Weibei Fan

entry.summary: Studies why vision-language models stay anchored to stale textual descriptions of earlier visual states when grounding in a changed scene. Finds that models harder to correct concentrate prior-induced representation changes along a small recurring set of directions, so lock-in depends on how representation movement is organized rather than its magnitude.

entry.title: FreqForcing: Autoregressive Long Video Generation via Spectral Self-Anchoring

author.name: Jiatong Li, Leo Liang, Linghe Kong, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: Characterizes error accumulation in autoregressive long video generation as low-frequency spectral energy drift, explaining why attention sinks only partly help. Proposes a training-free spectral self-anchoring correction to prevent color drift, motion stagnation, and eventual collapse.

entry.title: Reconstructing Backpropagation from Forward Fluctuations in Noise-modulated Neural Networks

author.name: Shuhei Ikemoto

entry.summary: Shows that gradient backpropagation can be reconstructed inside noise-driven neural networks using only forward-pass statistics, estimating each weight matrix from covariance between a unit's output and downstream fluctuations. This removes the weight transport requirement that makes backpropagation implausible for biological and neuromorphic hardware.

entry.title: RLMM-Flow: A Flow-based Mobile Manipulation Framework with Latent-Space Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shuhang Wang, Ziming Li, Hui Cheng

entry.summary: Combines flow-matching policy pretraining on expert demonstrations with latent-space reinforcement learning post-training for whole-body mobile manipulation. Aims to exceed demonstration quality while satisfying collision, kinematic, joint-limit, and smoothness constraints in generated action chunks.

entry.title: Fewer Clarifications, Better Code: Benchmarking Cross-Session Personalized Ambiguity Adaptation in Coding Assistants

author.name: Zijian Xu, Wenshuo Zhang, Zisen Qin, Rui Sheng, Yushi Sun, Huamin Qu, Chuhan Shi

entry.summary: Formulates personalized ambiguity adaptation as a new task where a coding assistant must recognize a user-specific recurring ambiguity pattern from prior resolved sessions and apply it in a fresh session instead of asking again. Introduces a benchmark for cross-session memory in coding assistants.

entry.title: Setoka: A Benchmark for Hierarchical User Understanding in Personalized Agents over Heterogeneous Data

author.name: Lingyang Zeng, Guangze Chen, Kaichen Yu, Zhicheng Pan, Siyang Weng, Zirui Hu, Xiangyun Du, Hailin He, Rong Zhang, Chengcheng Yang, Kai Huang, Xuan Zhou

entry.summary: Setoka is a benchmark for personalized agents that defines four hierarchical levels of user understanding grounded in cognitive and personality psychology, spanning explicit fact recall through inference of abstract personal traits from heterogeneous data. It pushes memory evaluation past simple retrieval of stated conversational facts.

entry.title: AgentMap: Joint Equivalence and Subsumption Discovery for Ontology Matching

author.name: Yiping Song, Jiaoyan Chen, Renate Schmidt, Hui Yang, Wen Zhang

entry.summary: AgentMap unifies equivalence and subsumption discovery into a single hybrid ontology matching task and solves it with a multi-agent LLM pipeline that combines semantic retrieval, hierarchical search, and collaborative reasoning. It fills the gap where existing systems handle only one correspondence type.

entry.title: Partner Capability Estimation for Task-Agnostic Adaptation in Ad-Hoc Teamwork

author.name: Peter Tisnikar, Maja Swieczkowska, Benteng Ma, Gerard Canal, Matteo Leonetti

entry.summary: Extends ad-hoc teamwork to multi-task settings by reframing it as joint planning with decentralized execution under hidden partner capabilities, and introduces an approximate Bayesian method that estimates what a partner can actually do from contextual models. It relaxes the standard assumptions of a single fixed task and known partner competence.

entry.title: Forensic Reproducibility Audit of a Radiology Vision-Language Model Benchmark: From Intended Protocol to Released Artifact

author.name: Mateusz Koz{\l}owski

entry.summary: A retrospective forensic audit of a chest radiograph vision-language model pilot traces disagreements between the intended protocol and the released artifacts, finding mismatched prompt bindings, missing outputs, and inversion-handling errors in the DICOM pipeline. It shows agreement across datasets, prompts, code, and manuscripts is typically assumed rather than verified.

entry.title: (EC)2: Event-Centric Explainability for Cybersecurity Through Multi-Agent LLM Investigations

author.name: Neta Kirmayer, David Tayouri, Andr\'es Murillo, Motoyoshi Sekiya, Asaf Shabtai, Rami Puzis

entry.summary: Presents a detector-agnostic multi-agent framework that turns raw security anomaly alerts into event-centric, hypothesis-driven investigations producing explanations grounded in verifiable evidence. Aimed at small and medium enterprise security operations where feature-level explanations are operationally useless.

entry.title: Eco3S: Complex Socio-Economic System Simulation via Agent-Based Models

author.name: Shaopeng Wei, Yufei Cheng, Wenxi Sun, Yepeng Ding, Yu Zhao, Gang Kou

entry.summary: Eco3S is an LLM agent-based simulation framework for socio-economic systems featuring a co-evolving agent-environment loop, a structural causal model inspired counterfactual mechanism, and workflow automation for policy analysis. It targets economic research use cases that need controllable interventions.

entry.title: From Passive Video to Editable Experience: Physically Grounded Experience Synthesis for Embodied Intelligence

author.name: Jia Luo

entry.summary: Pegasus converts human manipulation videos into robot-learnable data through graph intermediate representations, transforming an extracted task graph via affordance and constraint graphs into a robot planning graph that conditions video generation. It targets the embodiment gap that blocks direct learning from internet human video.

entry.title: Emergent Sparsity in Frozen Random CNN Feature Extractors for Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Scott M. Norton

entry.summary: Reports that deep RL agents using frozen random CNN feature extractors spontaneously compress task information into as few as one to three of sixty-four fully connected neurons, far sparser than trainable CNN agents, with sparsity scaling by task complexity across Pong, Breakout, and Space Invaders. Width scaling suggests this reflects task structure rather than fixed capacity fraction.

entry.title: Collusion with Competitive Marginals: Price-Level Audits Are Blind by Construction

author.name: Xin Xu, Chengrui Wu, Jiayu Lu, Kaizhen Tan, Siru Tao, Hanzhe Hong

entry.summary: The paper proves that a form of algorithmic collusion in which bidding agents couple only through the joint distribution of unexplained bid components leaves each agent's own bid distribution exactly at the competitive benchmark, so any audit that inspects a single agent's price history has power equal to its false-positive rate. The authors argue this failure is structural rather than a matter of sample size, and report that the mechanism appears in language-model bidding agents.

entry.title: Mergeable Model-Side Aggregation States for Long-Context Language Models

author.name: Dachuan Song, Junyu Yin, Zechen Hu, Xuan Wang

entry.summary: This paper adds a model-side aggregation interface to a frozen long-context language model: as context streams by, an extractor canonicalizes records and updates HyperLogLog sketches, giving mergeable state for set-based tasks such as cardinality estimation, set relations, and grouped statistics. The sketches can be merged across context segments, sidestepping the known degradation of attention-based aggregation at long context.

entry.title: Recover, Decode, Reguard: Guard-Agnostic Defense Amplification againstEncoded VLM Jailbreaks

author.name: Haoyu Zhang, Zhuoxi Wang, Shibo Zheng, Zijian Xiao, Xiangchen Guan, Mohammad Zandsalimy, Shanu Sushmita

entry.summary: This work identifies a decode gap in safety classifiers for vision-language models: harmful requests re-encoded as formal logic, rare languages, code, or images of text pass guards that would block the plain-language version.
