The proposed fix is a guard-agnostic amplifier that transcribes images and restates encoded text into plain payload before the guard, evaluated against a best-of-suite ensemble of eleven attacks.

entry.title: WhisperRec: Latent Reasoning for Efficient Foundation Recommendation Models

author.name: Hao Jiang, Peiru Du, Pengfei Yao, Mengting Li, Siyuan Lou, Kuo Cai, Sheng Yu, Qiang Luo, Jian Liang, Ruiming Tang, Fei Pan, Peng Jiang, Wenwu Ou

entry.summary: WhisperRec compresses teacher chain-of-thought traces into learnable latent reasoning tokens so a foundation recommendation model can reason in latent space instead of emitting long rationales, avoiding the inference cost and template rigidity of explicit think-then-answer prompting. It targets dynamic, context-dependent user interests at industrial scale.

entry.title: A First Look at Coding Agents' Compliance with AI Contribution Rules in Open-Source Communities

author.name: Wenhao Yang, Runzhi He, Minghui Zhou

entry.summary: The authors curate 106 issues from 49 repositories that publish rules about AI-generated contributions and measure whether coding agents actually read and follow them, covering total bans, mandatory disclosure, verification gates, and human sign-off. Trajectories are judged for refusal, truthful disclosure, gate clearance, and escalation of critical steps.

entry.title: MemSecBench: Tracking Agent Memory Poisoning from Persistence to Consequence and Repair

author.name: Xuanze Chen, Xukang Xie, Wentao Fu, Jiajun Zhou, Shanqing Yu, Qi Xuan

entry.summary: MemSecBench is a lifecycle benchmark for agent memory poisoning, tracking the same malicious content from being written into long-term memory, through later recall and downstream harmful actions, to selective repair, across 310 cases in 48 realistic contexts spanning code, science, daily life, and office work. It also compares multiple memory backends under a controlled write-and-recall protocol.

entry.title: Skillful forecasting of offshore winds from satellite scatterometer constellations

author.name: Francesco Pinto, Luca Lanzilao, Paco Lopez Dekker, Angela Meyer

entry.summary: WindCastNet is presented as the first framework to use satellite scatterometer observations directly for nowcasting offshore wind speed and direction, rather than only assimilating them into numerical weather prediction. It learns from spatiotemporally irregular satellite passes to target lead times of minutes to hours where initial-condition accuracy dominates and NWP is poorly optimized. Accurate intraday offshore wind forecasts matter for grid operation as offshore capacity grows.

entry.title: Lilith: Backdoor Generalization under Training-Inference Trigger Shift

author.name: Zhou Feng, Jiahao Chen, Chunyi Zhou, Yuan Su, Tianyu Du, Yuwen Pu, Jianhai Chen, Jinbao Li, Shouling Ji

entry.summary: Lilith studies whether a backdoor implanted with one training-time trigger generalizes to an entire family of inference-time triggers never seen during victim training, a blind spot in existing backdoor evaluations that assume exact trigger reuse or predefined transformation axes. It formulates backdoor generalization under training-inference trigger shift and builds a black-box anchor-to-family attack framework using disjoint data. This broadens the realistic threat surface of supply-chain data poisoning.

entry.title: The Sparsity Ceiling: Where Spiking Networks Can and Cannot Trade Activity for Energy

author.name: Zeyu Wang

entry.summary: Empirically tests the claim that spiking networks buy energy savings through sparsity, holding architecture fixed and swapping only the hidden unit type. Finds the achievable sparsity is task- and architecture-dependent: feed-forward perception tolerates very low firing rates and a spiking Transformer sparsifies to a few percent, while a recurrent language model cannot go below roughly half activity because the recurrent state must stay active.

entry.title: WikiLoop: Jointly Learning to Build and Navigate Agent-Native Wikis with Downstream Feedback

author.name: Haoliang Ming, Feifei Li, Wenhui Que

entry.summary: Jointly trains the construction and navigation of an agent-native linked-page knowledge base so that structural edits are evaluated by their downstream retrieval usefulness. A role-conditioned shared policy alternates between a navigator with a sufficiency-before-efficiency objective and a builder proposing edits scored by navigation outcomes.

entry.title: Language Models are not Equally Robust to Non-Canonical Tokenization across Languages

author.name: Poulami Ghosh, Preethi Jyothi

entry.summary: Tests whether the reported robustness of English language models to non-canonical but string-equivalent tokenizations extends to other languages, evaluating 27 languages across diverse scripts. Finds robustness is not uniform, so tokenization invariance is a language-dependent property.

entry.title: Pangram 4 Technical Report

author.name: Ben Glickenhaus, Katherine Thai, Jenna Russell, Elyas Masrour, Yue Han, Max Spero, Bradley Emi

entry.summary: Technical report for a commercial AI-text detector claiming an AUROC of 0.9916 with very low false positive and false negative rates, plus improved out-of-distribution generalization and adversarial robustness over the prior version. Adds finer-grained capability to flag mixed human-AI co-authored text and interleaved AI assistance.

entry.title: Rad-JEPA 3D: Radiology Joint-Embedding Predictive Model for 3D Computed Tomography

author.name: Quoc-Huy Trinh, Minh-Van Nguyen, Ulas Bagci

entry.summary: Adapts joint-embedding predictive self-supervised learning to 3D CT volumes, predicting latent features of a full scan from masked views. Combines a Mamba state-space branch for inter-slice continuity with a complementary spatial branch to preserve geometric structure for downstream diagnosis and language-model pairing.

entry.title: EgoSafe: A First-Person Mobile-Captured Benchmark for Visual Safety Understanding

author.name: Yuyun Chen, Tianao Li, TianQuan Feng, Cen Chen, Huiping Zhuang, Hao Peng, Ziqian Zeng

entry.summary: Introduces a first-person mobile-captured benchmark of 12,000 items probing whether vision-language models can perform causal, forensic safety reasoning under partial observability rather than surface-level recognition. Argues existing third-person surveillance benchmarks with binary labels hide this reasoning gap.

entry.title: Understanding Knowledge Transfer Mechanism in Heterogeneous MLLM Fusion: A Simple Linear Approach

author.name: Yinghao Hou, Jiahe Fan, Yuanhao Pu, Zongyuan Chen, Hong Xie

entry.summary: Probes what a smaller multimodal model actually inherits during training-free fusion with a larger heterogeneous model, using a simple linear directional parameter injection probe. A local theoretical analysis suggests transfer selectivity is determined at first order, and broad task evaluation shows aggregate gains hide uneven capability transfer.

entry.title: CinemaTraj: Composing Atomic Camera Trajectories for 3D Scenes with LLM Agents

author.name: Qianru Li, Xuyang Chen, Erkin T\"urk\"oz, Lu Liu, Xuqin Wang, Liqiu Meng, Tao Wu, Yanfeng Zhang

entry.summary: Reframes cinematic camera trajectory generation as language-grounded spatial reasoning by giving an LLM agent a structured 3D scene graph built from RGB-D input. The agent decomposes a prompt into atomic cinematographic moves that are composed into a full trajectory.

entry.title: Veritas++: Value-aware On-Policy Distillation for Perception-Enhanced AIGI Detection

author.name: Hao Tan, Jun Lan, Zichang Tan, Ajian Liu, Zijian Yu, Chuanbiao Song, Huijia Zhu, Weiqiang Wang, Jun Wan, Zhen Lei

entry.summary: Improves multimodal LLM detection of AI-generated images by strengthening low-level perception before reasoning, using value-aware on-policy distillation rather than optimizing reasoning traces alone. Argues current MLLM detectors organize evidence well but perceive fine-grained generation artifacts poorly.

entry.title: Position: Evaluation Scores Are Perishable Knowledge Claims

author.name: Sankalp Gilda, Shlok Gilda

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that averaging heterogeneous evaluation signals inflates confidence above the reliability of the weakest signal, and that scores should carry formality, scope, and expiry metadata. It frames benchmark results as perishable knowledge claims that decay with contamination and distribution shift.

entry.title: Large-Scale ChatBot Validation Through Customer Digital Twin Simulations

author.name: Cristovao Iglesias, Devesh Batra, Alankar Atreya, Stefan Wagner, Robert Hankache, Patrick Sinclair, Giulio Pelosio, Michael McMillan, Greig A. Cowan, Raad Khraishi

entry.summary: Describes a two-part pipeline for validating banking chatbots at scale by building synthetic customer agents grounded in real transactional and conversational data as digital twins, then using them to stress-test the deployed assistant. Evaluation covers semantic alignment with real customers, hallucination rates, and controllable personality traits.

entry.title: IDP AutoOpt: Agent-Driven Optimization of Document Processing Pipeline Configurations

author.name: David Kaleko, Sergey Ivanov, Md Mofijul Islam

entry.summary: IDP AutoOpt is an autonomous agent that tunes intelligent document processing pipelines by jointly optimizing prompts, models, OCR settings, and schemas through a closed loop of scoring, error diagnosis, targeted edits, and re-evaluation. Reported to match or exceed expert configurations that currently cost tens of person-hours per document type.

entry.title: FinCacheServe: Dependency-Consistent Answer Reuse for Cost-Efficient RAG Serving over Mutable Enterprise Documents

author.name: Lingteng Zeng, Yifan Jin

entry.summary: FinCacheServe caches generated RAG answers as serving objects guarded by document versions, evidence fingerprints, tool fingerprints, model identity, and decoding configuration, so reuse is invalidated when dependencies change. On SEC-derived workloads it skipped over half of LLM calls with no observed stale outputs.

entry.title: SARC-DQ: Runtime Data-Quality Gating for Agentic AI: Silent Evidence Defects, the Incompetence Shield, and Downstream-Only Remediation

author.name: Gaston Besanson

entry.summary: Shows that metadata-borne evidence defects such as stale prices or superseded records, which never surface in the agent context, cause competent agents to take costly wrong actions about sixty percent of the time on a priced replenishment benchmark, with doubt markers at chance level. The rate stays flat across four model tiers spanning roughly fifteenfold in inference price, so capability does not confer skepticism.

entry.title: Aligning LLM-Simulated and Human Examinees for Psychometric Calibration: A Cognitive Diagnostic Profiling Approach

author.name: Wenjie Zhou, Yunting Liu, Renjiao Tang, Mark Wilson

entry.summary: Proposes a zero-shot cognitive diagnostic profiling method that prompts LLMs to simulate examinees with diverse attribute-mastery patterns rendered as natural-language profiles, addressing the tendency of simulated responses to be too accurate and too uniform. Evaluated on a classic fraction-subtraction dataset with 536 real examinees across eight LLM configurations.

entry.title: Practice Makes Policies: Bootstrapping and Consolidating Robotic Capabilities from Zero Human Demonstrations

author.name: Jialiang Li, Yuhan Wang, Haojun Li, Gaojing Zhang, Yangtian Ye, Qipeng Liu, Haotian Liang, Wenzhao Lian

entry.summary: HERO is a hierarchical embodied system that bootstraps manipulation skills without any human demonstrations, converting autonomous physical interaction into progressively better policies through repeated practice and consolidation. The goal is robots whose capability evolves in deployment rather than being frozen at training time.

entry.title: AlphaSchema: Exploring the Space of Trading Semantics for LLM-Based Alpha Mining

author.name: Jingyang Yi, Jian Yang, Yifei Jin, Yuqi Li, Jian Li

entry.summary: AlphaSchema structures LLM-based quantitative alpha mining around an explicit schema space with slots for event, context, qualities, direction, and output, separating semantic factor design from implementation and search. This makes exploration controllable rather than left implicit inside the agent.

entry.title: LLMET: Enabling Cross-Layer Evaluation of Emerging M3D Memories for Energy-Efficient LLM Serving

author.name: Ming-Yen Lee, Hanchen Yang, Faaiq Waqar, Harsono Simka, Tushar Krishna, Muhammed Ahosan Ul Karim, Shimeng Yu

entry.summary: LLMET is a cross-layer evaluation framework that asks whether monolithic 3D integration of larger back-end-of-line cache memories actually reduces the energy of LLM serving by cutting traffic to high bandwidth memory. It links device and technology assumptions to system-level serving energy so that scaling on-chip memory can be assessed rather than assumed.

entry.title: Think Short, Defer Smart, Act, and Repeat: Calibrated Reasoning and Uncertainty-Aware Deferral for Edge LLM Agents

author.name: Amirmohammad Farzaneh, Osvaldo Simeone

entry.summary: TSDS manages the reasoning budget of on-device ReAct agents with a lightweight convergence probe that halts local reasoning once the intended action stabilizes, plus a perplexity-based rule that escalates uncertain actions to a cloud model, with both thresholds jointly calibrated on end-to-end episode trajectories. It aims to keep edge agents cheap without sacrificing safe action selection.

entry.title: Cost-Sensitive Conformal Prediction and Human-in-the-Loop Abstention for Imbalanced High-Stakes Decision Support: A Multi-Domain Benchmark

author.name: Manpreet Singh, Akshatha Srikantha, Shyamal Lakhanpal

entry.summary: This benchmark shows that standard marginal conformal prediction can catastrophically under-cover rare but costly minority classes, in some datasets down to well under one percent coverage, and compares Mondrian class-conditional conformal prediction and cost-controlled abstention across 15 imbalanced tabular datasets, 7 models, and 3 calibration methods. It provides practical guidance for deploying uncertainty quantification in credit, fraud, and clinical settings. The headline finding is a concrete warning against trusting marginal coverage guarantees under imbalance.

entry.title: RAGuard: A Layered Defense Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems Against Data Poisoning

author.name: Pushkal Kumar, Tucker Nielson, Tanish Kolhe, Shubham Zala, Vincent Li

entry.summary: RAGuard defends retrieval-augmented generation against corpus poisoning with two layers: a retriever adversarially fine-tuned on synthetic fabricated facts, contradictions, and reasoning traps so it downranks malicious passages, and a label-free black-box filter that scores each retrieved document by the semantic and output shift caused by leaving it out. The leave-one-out decode filter requires no ground truth labels. It addresses a practical and increasingly exploited attack surface.

entry.title: Existence-Field Diffusion Model for Spatial Point Processes with Variable Cardinality

author.name: Xiaoyin Pan, Christian R. Shelton, Rakshith Mahishi, Chengkuan Hong

entry.summary: The existence-field diffusion model handles spatial point processes with variable numbers of points by attaching a continuous existence variable to each potential point, so cardinality and spatial configuration diffuse jointly rather than through discrete trans-dimensional jumps. Existing approaches either decouple count from geometry or rely on awkward asymmetric birth-death dynamics. The continuous relaxation makes the generative dynamics symmetric and differentiable throughout.

entry.title: FedWeave: Rethinking the Unit of Specialization in Heterogeneous Federated MoE-LoRA

author.name: Donghang Duan, Xu Zheng, Lizong Zhang, Chong Mu, Meng Han

entry.summary: FedWeave rethinks federated mixture-of-experts LoRA by noting that experts need pure, pattern-coherent updates to preserve specialization while routers need mixed-task exposure to learn good comparisons, so it aggregates experts and routers asymmetrically instead of specializing at client granularity. Existing federated MoE-LoRA methods implicitly assume each client holds a coherent task. This targets cross-task interference and gradient conflict during aggregation.

entry.title: PowerAtlas: Towards Electricity-Computing Co-Scheduling for Power Systems

author.name: Kaiwen Jiang, Siya Xu, Ziyue Zhu, Chao Yang, Anh Tuan Luu, Haoran Luo

entry.summary: PowerAtlas is an LLM-agent framework for jointly scheduling electricity and computing loads, integrating historical instances, domain knowledge, and physical grid constraints so that generated schedules avoid line-flow violations and unserved load while respecting compute service-level agreements. General-purpose LLM schedules are frequently infeasible under grid constraints. It was built and tested with a provincial Chinese power utility.

entry.title: TreeCCA: Canonical Correlation Analysis via Gradient-Boosted Trees

author.name: James Chapman

entry.summary: TreeCCA trains gradient-boosted tree ensembles end-to-end as canonical correlation analysis encoders by exploiting the Eckart-Young loss, which supplies closed-form per-sample gradients that plug into XGBoost or LightGBM as a custom objective. CCA has historically relied on linear or neural encoders even though boosted trees dominate tabular learning. Because each split selects a single feature, gain importances give native interpretability alongside nonlinear accuracy.

entry.title: Using large language models to probe the limits of atom-centered structural descriptors

author.name: Michelangelo Domina, Michele Ceriotti

entry.summary: Uses large language models to search for adversarial atomic structures that expose degeneracies in atom-centered geometric descriptors used in machine-learning force fields. Reports 3D structures that remain indistinguishable even when descriptors are extended to larger neighbor clusters, contradicting the assumption that higher-body terms resolve all degeneracies.

entry.title: Choosing Where and How to Moderate: End-to-End Trade-offs in Filter Placement and Response Rewriting

author.name: Mengya Hu, Susie Park, Suzana Ilic, Qiong Wei, Sandeep Atluri, Myra Deng, Tucker Fross, Curt Tigges

entry.summary: Evaluates content moderation as a deployment decision rather than a classifier benchmark, comparing input-side, response-side, and combined blocking using end-to-end metrics of useful non-harmful responses versus harmful exposure. Finds response-only filtering maximizes usefulness while combined filtering minimizes harmful exposure, and examines rewriting instead of hard blocking.

entry.title: TREK: A Travel Reasoning and Evaluation Kit for LLM Agents in Complex Trip Planning

author.name: Jinhu Qi, Wentao Zhang, Siu Man Ng, Feiyang Xu, Yanyu Chen, Yaoman Li, Irwin King

entry.summary: Introduces a travel-planning benchmark that grades whether a returned itinerary is jointly feasible: real bookable entities, physically traversable days, and budget compliance, using programmatic verification rather than soft LLM-judged rubrics. Designed to be reproducible and auditable for tool-using agents.

entry.title: LumaGuide: Distribution Shaping for Training-Free HDR Generation in Diffusion Models

author.name: Bowen Chen, Shreshth Saini, Balu Adsumilli, Alan C. Bovik

entry.summary: Presents a training-free way to steer diffusion sampling so generated luminance distributions match HDR targets in perceptually uniform space, using differentiable energy-based guidance. Shows that aligning luminance histograms alone can induce coherent highlights and preserved shadow detail.

entry.title: Anchoring and Steering Diffusion: Enhancing the Faithfulness of Text-to-Image Generation at Inference Time

author.name: Xinyi Wang, Yuyang Huang, Yalin Su, Pengcheng Luan, Tao Zhang, Feiming Wei, Wenxian Yu

entry.summary: Improves prompt faithfulness of text-to-image diffusion at inference time by combining better semantic anchoring of initial noise with mid-generation diagnosis and correction of the denoising trajectory. Avoids both expensive noise search and blind trajectory manipulation.

entry.title: TPD: Temporal Prior Decoupling for Text-to-Video Diffusion Models

author.name: Taewon Kang, Matthias Zwicker

entry.summary: Identifies a failure mode where text-to-video models omit a late-occurring event because the early scene prior dominates cross-attention across the temporal axis. Proposes a training-free decoupling of temporal priors so later prompt segments receive adequate guidance in the corresponding frames.

entry.title: SCALPEL: Semantic Cross-modal Alignment via LLM-Powered Encoder Learning for Medical Vision-Language Representation

author.name: Yunzhan Fu, Enyu Bao, Xiangyu Shen, Yihao Wu, Chunbo Jiang, Fangli Guan, Liqi Yan

entry.summary: Uses a medical LLM as the text encoder for medical vision-language pretraining, tackling representational collapse of generative LLMs under contrastive objectives, memory cost of joint end-to-end training, and hallucination induced by naive contrastive losses. Aims to exploit long, terminology-dense clinical reports that lightweight text encoders truncate.

entry.title: SeasonStereo: Robust Dense Stereo Matching for Multi-Date Satellite Imagery via Generative AI

author.name: \'Alvaro D\'iaz-Laureano, Roger Mar\'i, El\'ias Masquil, Pablo Arias, Gabriele Facciolo

entry.summary: Trains dense stereo matching for satellite images taken on different dates by generating synthetic pairs with controlled seasonal appearance variation and leveraging zero-shot geometric priors from foundation models. Reports parity with LiDAR-supervised state of the art without costly aligned ground truth.

entry.title: ScalablePromptus: Scalable and High-Fidelity Prompt-Based Video Streaming

author.name: Zehao Cao, Bowei Xu, Xun Cao, Zhan Ma, Hao Chen

entry.summary: Makes prompt-based generative video streaming robust to network fluctuation by training prompt representations with dropout so they are rank-ordered and truncatable. Receivers can reconstruct usable video from partially received prompts without adaptation, plus color-aware inversion and interpolation for intermediate frames.

entry.title: CheckVLA: Execution-Time Verification with Action-Conditioned World Model for Long-Horizon Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Yushan Liu, Peibo Sun, Xintao Chao, Zhenyang Yang, Yifan Xie, Lingfeng Zhang, Shoujie Li, Chenyu Tang, Fang Chen, Xiao-Ping Zhang, Wenbo Ding

entry.summary: CheckVLA adds a frozen, separately trained action-conditioned world model that predicts how observations should evolve given a committed action chunk, then flags execution-time deviations using a conformally calibrated risk threshold. This targets a real weakness of open-loop chunked VLA policies, which cannot react to errors that occur after actions are dispatched.

entry.title: Living-Harness Is an Interactive-Agent Evolver

author.name: Yuetian Du, Yucheng Wang, He Xu, Jiexu Xu, Shanwen Tan, Bing Zhao, Boyu Yang, Zhijie Xu, Ming Kong, Hu Wei, Jie Liu, Qiang Zhu

entry.summary: Living-Harness turns each finished agent trajectory and its evaluator signals into bounded updates of the persistent harness, meaning the tools, context, memory, and workflow scaffolding that guide future tasks, rather than letting lessons die with the episode. Updates are governed by a domain-level standard operating procedure that abstracts episodes into structured revisions.

entry.title: Exploring Structures in Physics Problems: Can AI Agents Discover Statistical Mechanical Mappings?

author.name: Wanyu Zhao, Wanbing Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces a small benchmark of six Ising-type statistical mechanics problems and tests whether propose-verify-revise LLM agents can discover mappings from raw partition functions to tractable representations. A key finding is that agents often pass numerical checks while misidentifying the underlying structure, so verification signals can be misleading.

entry.title: Evidence-Ledger Adjudication for Claim-Evidence Traceability

author.name: Gengyu Chen, Yongjie Yu, Weiling Wang

entry.summary: Proposes an evidence-ledger workflow that pairs each generated claim with an evidence packet, assigns a support relation, and routes unsupported or contradicted claims back for revision. Evaluated on a blind benchmark of over 2,300 rows assembled from three existing fact-verification datasets, with large accuracy gains over non-agentic baselines.

entry.title: The Age of AI Agents Demands A New Scientific Paradigm To Sustain Trustworthy Science

author.name: Belinda Mo

entry.summary: Argues that autonomous research agents break the assumption underlying peer review that contributors can be questioned and sanctioned, widening the gap between scientific output volume and verification capacity. Proposes criteria for new verification infrastructure emphasizing observable-by-default workflows and scalable checking.

entry.title: Do Methods Support the Claims? Intra-Paper Verification for Peer Review

author.name: Ranjitha Shivaprasad Ballakuraya, Arash Mahyari, Ashok Srinivasan

entry.summary: Introduces intra-paper claim verification, checking whether a paper's own methodology actually supports its claimed contributions rather than only comparing claims against prior literature. This targets a common human reviewer objection that current LLM review systems ignore.

entry.title: IFCMemoryBench: Evaluating Long-Term Memory of LLM-Based Agents in BIM Information Retrieval

author.name: Changyu Du, Alexander Vosseler, Filippo Mazza, Andr\'e Borrmann

entry.summary: IFCMemoryBench evaluates long-term agent memory in building information modeling, requiring agents to reuse prior-session project specifications, client decisions, and engineering conventions while querying live structured IFC models. It argues this is a harder memory test than open-domain conversational recall.

entry.title: Pramana: A Composable, Domain-Specific Backend for Empirical Networking Research

author.name: Jaber Daneshamooz, Eugene Vuong, Alagappan Ramanathan, Manni Moghimi, Haarika Manda, Satyam Kumar, Snithik Thode, Satyandra Guthula, Sylee Beltiukov, Dongsu Han, Tarun Mangla, Sangeetha Abdu Jyothi, Walter Willinger, Arpit Gupta

entry.summary: Pramana is a composable domain-specific backend for empirical networking research that reduces the lag from hypothesis to data by making it easy to configure realistic bottleneck links and generate concurrent heterogeneous traffic with service-quality measurement. Motivated by agentic AI accelerating ideation faster than data generation can keep up.

entry.title: Visual Credit Audit for Multimodal Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Feixiang Liu, Qiang Qiu, Lanbo Sun, Nan Wei, Huawei Shen, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: Visual Credit Audit separates two questions that closed yes-or-no spatial benchmarks conflate: whether an image actually gives the model's stated decision more support than text-only and blank-image controls, and whether the model responds to relation-specific visual evidence. Across four open multimodal models and two spatial benchmarks, a substantial share of decisions receive no genuine visual credit.

entry.title: MetaKoopman: Bayesian Meta-Learning of Koopman Operators for Modeling Structured Dynamics under Distribution Shifts

author.name: Mahmoud Selim, Sriharsha Bhat, Karl H. Johansson

entry.summary: MetaKoopman places a Matrix Normal-Inverse Wishart prior over the Koopman operator so that a linear latent dynamics model can be Bayesian-updated in closed form from recent trajectory data, yielding a closed-form predictive distribution with both epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty. It is validated on a full-scale autonomous truck-and-trailer across adverse winter conditions. Closed-form adaptation is attractive for safety-critical real-time control.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Guided LLM Semantic Augmentation for Heterogeneous Treatment Effect Estimation

author.name: Jialu Xu, Mengkun Liang, Guannan Liu, Xiaojie Mao, Junjie Wu

entry.summary: This work uses LLMs to generate semantic augmentations of raw tabular covariates for conditional average treatment effect estimation, guided by uncertainty so that augmentation is applied where the nuisance and heterogeneity learning problems are locally unstable. Raw numeric and categorical encodings leave semantic relations and higher-order interactions implicit. The motivating analysis separates assignment-related from heterogeneity-related instability.

entry.title: Spline-Based Boundary Representations for Sparse View Reconstruction and Simulation Using Isogeometric Analysis

author.name: Davor Dobrota, Vsevolod Skorokhodov, Chenghao Xu, Olga Fink, Malcolm Mielle

entry.summary: Reconstructs multi-patch B-spline boundary representations directly from sparse posed RGB images so that the output geometry is watertight, smooth, and usable in CAD and isogeometric simulation. Optimizes the spline representation itself instead of extracting surfaces from a neural field.

entry.title: MedARC: Training-Free Adaptive Redundancy Compression of Visual Tokens for 3D Medical Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yitao Zhu, Mengjun Liu, Yingji Fu, Haowen Pang, Anqi Qiu

entry.summary: A training-free method for compressing the very long visual token sequences produced by 3D medical volumes in vision-language models, combining vision-encoder attention with complementary redundancy and distinctiveness cues. Adapts compression per region instead of applying uniform token reduction.

entry.title: JEPADepth: Masked Predictive Representation Learning for Self-Supervised Monocular Depth Estimation

author.name: Ionu\c{t} Grigore, C\u{a}lin-Adrian Popa

entry.summary: Adds a masked latent-prediction objective in the feature space of a pretrained self-supervised vision transformer to self-supervised monocular depth training, complementing standard photometric losses. The auxiliary predictor is discarded at inference so deployment cost is unchanged.

entry.title: CASIAL: Geometric Distortion Robust Image Watermarking

author.name: Yupeng Qiu, Han Fang, Ee-Chien Chang

entry.summary: Argues that geometric robustness in learned image watermarking requires both globally spread messages and geometry-invariant representations, then builds a scheme around these two properties. Targets the two failure modes of region removal from cropping and desynchronization from scaling or rotation.

entry.title: From Keypoints to Predictive Distributions: Post-Hoc Uncertainty for YOLO-Pose Models

author.name: Alexej Klushyn, Juan Rivero Sesma, Florian Seligmann, Richard Kurle, Kinh Tieu, Jayant Sen Gupta

entry.summary: Adds calibrated per-keypoint uncertainty to already-trained pose detectors via lightweight post-hoc probabilistic heads that predict an input-dependent dispersion matrix, followed by Gaussian or heavier-tailed calibration. Also proposes an evaluation protocol combining distributional calibration diagnostics.

entry.title: StructureGS: Structure-aware Gaussian Splatting for Articulated Object Reconstruction

author.name: Gahye Lee, Gyoonseo Kim, Wonjong Jang, Jooeun Son, Seungyong Lee

entry.summary: Reconstructs articulated multi-part objects with Gaussian splatting by injecting structural guidance from oriented part bounding boxes, rather than relying on photometric supervision alone. Aims to disentangle geometry, appearance, and motion so part boundaries are clean enough for interaction.

entry.title: InkShield: Writing Style Protection Against Unauthorized Handwriting Mimicry

author.name: Jian Xiong, Wenbo Jiang, Zihan Wang, Rui Zhang, Wenshu Fan, Hongwei Li, Guowen Xu

entry.summary: Proposes protective perturbations that prevent handwriting style mimicry by generative models, motivated by forgery of signatures and letters from publicly posted samples. Notes that existing anti-editing perturbations look conspicuous on sparse handwriting images with blank backgrounds and adapts the perturbation design accordingly.

entry.title: Reeling It In: Flexible Needle Pick Up via Thread Manipulation for Autonomous Suturing

author.name: Emma Huang, Zih-Yun Chiu, Neelay Joglekar, Shanglei Liu, Michael C. Yip

entry.summary: Proposes picking up a dropped surgical needle indirectly by manipulating the attached suture thread, avoiding direct grasps that pinch tissue or cause the slippery needle to jump. Enables recovery even when the needle is occluded or not directly approachable.

entry.title: ActSWM: Action-Sensitive World Models for Long-Horizon Planning in Open-World Games

author.name: Zhenfeng Gan, ZiTong Zeng, Jiajun Cheng, Yeke Song, Yongyi Tang, Xueqian Wang

entry.summary: Identifies a failure mode called context collapse, where autoregressive latent predictors produce accurate-looking future states that barely change across different candidate action sequences, making them useless for planning. ActSWM enforces a transition-separation principle so that alternative action plans yield distinguishable latent futures, improving long-horizon model-predictive control in open-world games.

entry.title: Belief-Guided Decision Making with Uncertainty Gating in the Game of Go

author.name: Mehrad Yaghoubi, Azam Bastanfard, Abbas Jalilvand, Ashkan Rezaei

entry.summary: Proposes a Go architecture that separates a belief head from the policy head, where the belief head acts as an internal critic modeling epistemic uncertainty to reduce reliance on expensive Monte Carlo tree search. Motivated by inference-rate bottlenecks and confident-but-fatal move hallucinations on consumer hardware.

entry.title: ForgetBench: Benchmarking Forgetting Dynamics of Long-Term Parametric Memory in Language Models

author.name: Ruxi Gu, Zhenliang Zhang, Wei Wang

entry.summary: ForgetBench is a benchmark for how language models lose previously acquired knowledge across repeated rounds of continual knowledge editing, using both concept-based and scenario-based question answering to separate isolated factual retention from contextual use. It targets the temporal dynamics of forgetting that single-step editing evaluations miss.

entry.title: PUDA: An AI-Native Hardware Harness for Self-Driving Laboratories

author.name: Zekun Ren, Hongzhao Tan, Jiaen Yee, Kedar Hippalgaonkar

entry.summary: PUDA is an agent-first control layer for self-driving laboratories that exposes instruments through discoverable command-line interfaces and JSON messaging instead of a human GUI, keeping hardware execution deterministic and atomic while logging all commands, data, and reports as structured records. The aim is auditable autonomous experimentation where an agent can observe, decide, and act directly.

entry.title: AgentGFM: A Graph Foundation Model with Node-Agent Information-Flow Control

author.name: Jingbo Cui, Jitao Zhao, Di Jin, Dongxiao He

entry.summary: AgentGFM proposes a graph foundation model in which each node acts as an agent that decides how information should be propagated to it, replacing the fixed hand-designed propagation schemes that most graph foundation models transfer unchanged to new graphs. The aim is transferability across domains where local structural patterns differ even within a single graph.

entry.title: A Persona-based Rate Action Index

author.name: Hayden Helm, Andrew Dassori

entry.summary: The authors build retrieval-grounded personas of individual Federal Open Market Committee members from roughly 25,000 public text chunks and aggregate persona responses to current market conditions into an index predicting rate hikes, holds, and cuts. They validate the personas on identifiability and detectability before using them for prediction.

entry.title: Decoupled Visual Processing: Efficient Multimodal Adaptation via Modality-Specific Transformer Substitution

author.name: Mingkuan Feng, Zhengqi Wen, Jianhua Tao

entry.summary: Decoupled Visual Processing replaces the upper decoder layers of a pretrained language model with a single lightweight trainable transformer block dedicated to visual tokens, on the premise that visual and textual token representation needs diverge in deep layers. This cuts the cost of visual instruction tuning relative to full-parameter fine-tuning.

entry.title: FARI: Robust One-Step Inversion for Watermarking in Diffusion Models

author.name: Jindong Yang, Han Fang, Weiming Zhang, Nenghai Yu, Kejiang Chen

entry.summary: FARI makes inversion-based watermarking of diffusion images practical by exploiting the observation that the inversion trajectory is much less curved than the forward generation path, so it can be approximated in very few function evaluations while prioritizing robustness to external distortions over minimizing internal truncation error. This targets the speed and error bottleneck of current inversion-based detection.

entry.title: Budget-Aware LLM Discovery via Cost-Calibrated Frontier Utility

author.name: Yansen Zhang, Yilu Liu, Tianyu Liu, Jiamin Chen, Xiaokun Zhang, Kai Xie, Xue Liu, Chen Ma, Yiyan Qi

entry.summary: CostAda is a controller for inference-time search over candidate solutions that credits search actions by cost-calibrated frontier utility rather than score progress alone, since prompt length, retries, and guidance calls consume very different token budgets. The authors prove that cost-blind credit assignment can forfeit nearly all attainable quality as the number of frontiers grows and costs diverge.

entry.title: From Representations to Behaviors: Exploring the Person-Situation-Behavior Triad in LLMs

author.name: Ruikang Zhang, Shuo Wang, Qi Su

entry.summary: Building on a personality triad framework, this study looks for internal personality-related representations in language models, tests whether they express consistently across situations, and traces how they shape specific behaviors, going beyond prior work that only characterized outputs under personality prompting. The aim is mechanistic evidence rather than surface trait scores.

entry.title: SymmGrid: Super-Scaling On-Robot Learning with Parallelized Symmetries and Egocentric-Exocentric Visual Perception

author.name: Gabe Everett, Brice Gunter, Ryan Vander Stelt, Cleiver Ruiz-Martinez, Blake Hull, Juan Rojas

entry.summary: SymmGrid accelerates reinforcement learning performed directly on physical robots by augmenting trajectories with grid-structured group transformations drawn from a symmetry tree, applying homographies so that egocentric or exocentric images and proprioception are warped consistently. The goal is cutting the wall-clock bottleneck of on-robot learning.

entry.title: Parameter-Free Dynamic Regret for Online Convex Optimization under Heavy-Tailed Noise

author.name: Vaneet Aggarwal

entry.summary: This theory paper gives a parameter-free algorithm achieving universal dynamic regret for online convex optimization when gradient noise is heavy-tailed with only a finite p-th central moment, combining restarted adaptive-gradient experts over a geometric pool of block lengths with a meta-algorithm that needs no moment conditions on meta-losses. It resolves an open problem where static regret was understood but dynamic regret was not.

entry.title: Scores Are Not Decisions: Cost-Aware Stopping for Tool Acquisition in LLM Agents

author.name: Yicheng Feng, Yan Zhang, Yan Cheng, Wei Qi

entry.summary: This paper treats tool acquisition in agent harnesses as a cost-aware stopping problem over ranked candidate tools, arguing that a relevance ranking alone does not tell an agent how many tools are worth loading given token cost, context load, and privacy exposure. The method trains on the offline gap between stopping immediately and the best continuation, with a compact interpretable variant.

entry.title: MMAC: A Massive Multi-dimensional Benchmark for Audio Captioning

author.name: Weijie Wu, Junbo Li, Lin Li, Jun Fang, Qingyang Hong

entry.summary: MMAC is a benchmark of roughly 5,600 audio clips drawn from over 20 sources that scores audio captioning across 6 capability categories and 15 fine-grained dimensions, checking both whether relevant information is mentioned and whether it is factually consistent. It targets the shift from short captions to open-ended descriptions produced by audio large language models. The dimension-level diagnosis is more informative than aggregate generation-quality scores.

entry.title: Anatomy Contextualized Adaption of CT Foundation Models

author.name: Roshan Kenia, Stephanie L McNamara, William Lotter

entry.summary: Anatomy Contextualized Adaptation adapts frozen CT vision-language foundation models so their representations align with anatomy-specific text, using anatomical segmentation to recover fine-grained signal without discarding whole-volume global context. The approach avoids the cost of training fine-grained models from scratch. It targets a real limitation of current 3D medical foundation models, where whole-volume pooling washes out localized findings.

entry.title: FloDR: An invertible dimensionality reduction method based on a normalising flow

author.name: Abdallah Baraka, Daniel Probst

entry.summary: FloDR performs two-dimensional visualization through an invertible normalising flow, keeping the discarded coordinates rather than throwing them away so that an exact inverse map exists from any point in the plane back to data space. This lets users interrogate what empty regions and inter-cluster distances actually mean, which t-SNE and UMAP cannot support. It targets widespread over-interpretation of embedding plots.

entry.title: Learning Implicit Causal World Models from Multi-Agent Demonstrations

author.name: Jasorsi Ghosh

entry.summary: This paper learns world models from offline multi-agent demonstrations that separate environmental dynamics from strategic agent intent, using policy variance to satisfy a sequential backdoor condition so causal structure becomes identifiable without a supplied causal graph. Standard world models conflate correlation with mechanism and break under distribution shift in multi-agent settings. Evaluation covers small coordination tasks such as navigation and giveway.

entry.title: Q-Steer: Action-Value Guidance for Molecular Policy Optimization

author.name: Xinyu Wang, Jinbo Bi, Minghu Song

entry.summary: Q-Steer attacks the delayed-reward problem in molecular generation by training an offline frozen prefix-action value scorer that estimates downstream reward for each candidate next token given a partial SMILES string, then adding a normalized value bonus to sampling logits at rollout time. The optimizer and oracle budget stay unchanged, isolating the effect of the steering primitive. It is a credit-assignment fix for oracle-limited molecular optimization.

entry.title: SCOUT: Per-Context Reset Curricula for Sparse-Reward Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Siddharth Aphale, Ayushman Singh

entry.summary: SCOUT is an online reset-curriculum controller for sparse-reward RL that gives each task instance its own schedule for withdrawing scaffolded starting states, using only binary rollout success to remove assistance after sustained success and restore it when performance regresses. Prior curricula pace removal on one global schedule, which fails when different contexts learn at different rates. The controller is learner-agnostic and cheap to bolt on.

entry.title: DHRCL:Training Code LLMs with Dense Hierarchical Rewards and Curriculum Learning

author.name: Shuhang Wang, Ziming Li, Hui Cheng

entry.summary: DHRCL decomposes code RL reward into a progressive hierarchy of syntax validity, execution success, unit-test pass rate, and abstract-syntax-tree structural similarity, and schedules these signals through a curriculum rather than combining them with static weights. The premise is that these signals describe different and sequentially dependent programming competencies. It densifies the sparse outcome reward typical of code RL.

entry.title: Conformal Changepoint Localization and Root Cause Analysis with Corrupted Observations

author.name: Seunghun Yu, Meiyi Zhu, Petar Popovski, Joonhyuk Kang, Osvaldo Simeone

entry.summary: This work extends conformal changepoint localization and conformal root cause analysis so their distribution-free confidence sets remain valid when the observations themselves are corrupted, which is the norm in telecom, robotics, and security monitoring. Existing conformal monitoring methods assume clean streams. The result preserves user-specified coverage of the true changepoint or true faulty stream under corruption.

entry.title: From Conceptual Hydrologic Models to Conceptually Interpretable Neural Networks: A Snow-Water Mass-Conserving-Perceptron Framework for Discovering Catchment-Scale Precipitation-Storage-Runoff Representations

author.name: Yuan-Heng Wang, Hoshin V. Gupta

entry.summary: The authors recast a coupled soil and snow conceptual hydrologic model as a mass-conserving neural network and evaluate across 513 US catchments, showing the physically constrained network matches the traditional hydrologic formulation while remaining conceptually interpretable. They then explore cross-node state sharing and wider single-layer networks built from interpretable mass-conserving units. It advances physics-constrained interpretable modeling in Earth science.

entry.title: Foundation Models for Face Presentation Attack Detection: A Unified Linear-Probing Benchmark

author.name: Peter Lorenz, Anjith George, S\'ebastien Marcel

entry.summary: This benchmark linearly probes 24 frozen encoders, including self-supervised vision transformers, vision-language models, and supervised CNNs, on the standard four-dataset cross-dataset face presentation attack detection protocol to ask whether general-purpose vision foundation models already encode spoofing-relevant signal. The backbone stays frozen throughout, isolating representation quality from task-specific training. Domain shift is the central difficulty in this security-sensitive task.

entry.title: Minimal Markovization via Stable Quotients in Holonomy-Cover Decision Processes

author.name: Zuyuan Zhang, Yongshan Chen, Mahdi Imani, Tian Lan

entry.summary: For a structured class of partially observable processes where visible dynamics are Markov and each observed transition applies a fixed permutation to a hidden mode, this paper constructs the stable quotient, the coarsest abstraction preserving one-step rewards and quotient successors, and proves that observation plus stable class is an exact finite Markov state. It thereby characterizes the minimal Markov sufficient statistic for this class. Correct initialization enables exact class tracking.

entry.title: When Do Learned Diffusion Proposals Help Constraint Solving? A Controlled Study on Continuous Algebraic Systems

author.name: Quang Bui, Sparsh Roy, Akash Gundimeda, Davin Yin

entry.summary: This controlled study separates two decisions in continuous algebraic constraint solving: assigning satisfying values and choosing which structural augmentation makes an unsolvable system solvable. A candidate-conditioned repair ranker reaches the exhaustive-search ceiling at a fraction of the calls and vastly outperforms random selection, while a graph-neural diffusion denoiser proposes assignments over a factor-graph representation refined by exact computer-algebra descent. It carefully isolates when learned proposals actually help versus classical solvers.

entry.title: When Kernel Ridge Regression Meets the H\"older-Zygmund Class: Minimax Optimality and Failure of Properness

author.name: Yuxuan Hou

entry.summary: This theory note proves that misspecified kernel ridge regression over the Holder-Zygmund class attains the minimax L2 rate using an RKHS equivalent to a Sobolev space of higher smoothness, and shows that properness fails in the Holder-Zygmund norm because the expected squared norm of the KRR noise component grows logarithmically even for a zero regression function. The two results together sharpen understanding of misspecified kernel regression. The failure of properness is the more surprising half.

entry.title: Two2Four: Generative Quadruped Puppeteering from Human Motion

author.name: Fatemeh Zargarbashi, Zehong Qiu, Dhruv Agrawal, Stelian Coros, Robert W. Sumner, Martin Guay, Jakob Buhmann

entry.summary: Two2Four generates plausible and controllable quadruped animal motion from ordinary human motion capture using a two-stage diffusion model trained purely on quadruped data, with structured conditioning and inpainting so a human performer can effectively puppeteer an animal. Existing virtual-production pipelines require either highly trained performers or complex retargeting rigs. The method supports a broad range of actions without paired human-animal data.

entry.title: Learning the Word Problem: Geodesic Lengths and Cryptographic Applications

author.name: Elisabeth Fink

entry.summary: Introduces WPNet, a graph neural network that heuristically solves the group-theoretic word problem by mapping unreduced words to dynamic graphs, demonstrated on the Baumslag-Solitar group and an Artin group. Because word-problem hardness underpins some post-quantum cryptographic proposals, learned heuristics have implications for platform-group selection.

entry.title: Adaptive Gradient-Based Methods for a Broader Class of Optimization Problems under Performative Prediction

author.name: Hiroki Hamaguchi, Yuya Hikima, Hiroshi Sawada, Akiko Takeda

entry.summary: Extends gradient-based optimization under performative prediction, where deployed models shift the data distribution, to broader loss and distribution classes by estimating the induced shift with finite differences. Provides convergence guarantees under weaker assumptions plus a sample-efficient practical variant.

entry.title: Conformalized Rate-Adaptive Sensing

author.name: Jiawei Yang, Yao Zhang

entry.summary: Develops a conformal method that decides per image how many measurements to acquire so reconstruction error stays below a target with high probability, using the early part of the reconstruction path to predict the stopping time and calibrating with held-out images. Provides distribution-free guarantees for adaptive compressive acquisition.

entry.title: Feature Bagging Provides Stability

author.name: Yuheng Ma, Qiang Sun

entry.summary: Analyzes feature bagging through algorithmic stability, introducing feature instability as the feature-axis counterpart of instance instability and showing it captures complementary generalization information. Establishes formal stability guarantees for feature bagging in linear and model-free recursive-subsampling settings resembling random forests.

entry.title: PIKS: Universal Physics-Informed Kernel Methods

author.name: Joachim Bona-Pellissier, Giacomo Meanti, Matteo Santacesaria, Lorenzo Rosasco

entry.summary: Provides learning theory for physics-informed kernel methods in the misspecified regime where the physical target lies outside the reproducing kernel Hilbert space, which is the realistic case for most physical solutions. Offers an analytically tractable alternative to physics-informed neural networks with closed-form solutions and universality guarantees.

entry.title: DuplexGen: Adaptive Synthesis of Human-AI Turn-Taking Dialogues

author.name: Takyoung Kim, Kang-wook Kim, Sang Hoon Woo, Julia Hirschberg, Gunhee Kim, Dilek Hakkani-T\"ur

entry.summary: Presents a framework for synthesizing full-duplex dialogue data with scenario-appropriate turn-taking by calibrating LLM predictions against a small set of slot-level human preference annotations. Shows human turn-taking preferences differ substantially across six cooperative and competitive tasks, undermining single-norm turn-taking models.

entry.title: CMT-RAG: Complementary Memory Traces for Multi-turn Multi-hop RAG

author.name: Lang Zhou, Yingjian Chen, Shuxuan Li, Kun-Yu Lin, Zhilin Zhao

entry.summary: Represents conversational memory as sub-question-level reasoning traces so that follow-up queries can recover the specific earlier reasoning steps and evidence they depend on. Releases a benchmark for multi-turn multi-hop retrieval with explicit cross-turn sub-question dependency annotations alongside the memory framework.

entry.title: From Found to Designed: Concepts as a Design Axis for Large Language Models

author.name: Chen Shani

entry.summary: Position paper arguing that concept structure in language models should be designed into the architecture, objective, or inference stage rather than discovered post hoc via probing and dictionary learning. Maps the design space along pipeline stage and degree of structural commitment, motivating stability, compositionality, and controllability guarantees.

entry.title: Latent-IM: Latent Interaction Management for Speech LLMs

author.name: Adar Avsian, Atahan Dokme, Tony Woo, Larry Heck

entry.summary: Attempts to recover classical dialogue-management structure inside speech LLMs by treating conversational moves such as acknowledging, checking, and querying as two coupled problems of move selection from context and causal move realization at generation time. Introduces an internal dialogue-management approach operating on latent representations.

entry.title: Mental World Modeling

author.name: Hao Fei, Yiran Zhao

entry.summary: Argues that world models should track hidden mental variables such as beliefs, desires, intentions, and social permissibility rather than only physical scene dynamics, since human behavior depends on what each agent knows. Proposes maintaining a coupled physical-mental world state, rendering target-specific partial observations, and simulating candidate actions through it.

entry.title: The Confounder Trap: Treatment-Encoding Representations in Causal Inference with Text

author.name: Marie Neubrander, Graham Tierney, Alexander Volfovsky

entry.summary: Identifies a confounder trap in text-based causal inference: when the linguistic treatment is itself encoded in the words, representations learned from full text can encode treatment status and manufacture overlap violations even when the true problem satisfies overlap. Studies lexicon-defined latent treatments and how representation choices distort effect estimates.

entry.title: TPCD: Tone-Pressure Contrastive Decoding and the Label-Free Gating Bottleneck in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jinkun Zhao, Kui Zhang, Wenjun Wu

entry.summary: Uses the distribution produced under a coercive high-pressure prompt as the negative branch in contrastive decoding for vision-language models, subtracting it from safe-instruction logits to curb unsupported claims. Reports large drops in attack success but also a collapse of legitimate positive answers, and analyzes why label-free gating cannot fully recover the tradeoff.

entry.title: ICDAR 2026 Competition on Information Extraction from Atomic Layer Deposition/Etching (ALD/E) Scientific Figures

author.name: Fahad Ahmed, S\"oren Auer, Jennifer D'Souza

entry.summary: Reports results of a scientific-figure information extraction competition on atomic layer deposition and etching literature, with expert-annotated tasks and 68 active participants. Finds that state-of-the-art multimodal models handle classification and summarization well but struggle with structured data extraction and scientific reasoning from figures.

entry.title: Multi-Objective Compliance-Integrated Coevolution For Simulated And Real-World Deployment Of Multi-Robot Marine Autonomy

author.name: Everardo Gonzalez, Tyler M. Paine, Manuel Agraz Vallejo, Gaurav Dixit, Michael R. Benjamin, Kagan Tumer

entry.summary: Uses multi-objective coevolutionary algorithms to produce coordinated multi-robot marine behaviors under sparse mission feedback while balancing safety and regulatory compliance. Includes both simulated and real-world deployment for maritime missions such as reef exploration and inspection.

entry.title: RL$^2$-VLA: Adaptive RL Latent Compositional Steering with Test-Time Scaling for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Derek Ming Siang Tan, Shailesh Shailesh, Srikrishna Iyer, William Wei Jie Teo, Yuanliang Ju, Qiao Gu, Guillaume Sartoretti

entry.summary: RL-squared trains a lightweight offline reinforcement learning policy that operates in the latent space of a vision-language-action model, steering action generation adaptively only at timesteps where the base policy is likely to fail. It addresses two limitations of test-time scaling for robot policies: correlated failure modes across samples and uniform intervention regardless of need.

entry.title: Imprecise beliefs: a tiny introduction

author.name: davidad

entry.summary: A compact exposition by davidad of imprecise probability as a foundation for AI epistemology, arguing that single precise probability distributions cannot faithfully express certain belief states relevant to safe reasoning under deep uncertainty. It sketches the formal machinery he considers most important for guaranteed-safe AI approaches.

entry.title: CalTwin: Towards Calibrated, Shift-Robust Medical World Models via Fisher-Information Regularisation

author.name: Behraj Khan, Shabir Ahmad, Syed Ahmad Chan Bukhari, Tahir Qasim Syed

entry.summary: CalTwin argues that covariate shift across hospitals and scanners and overconfidence in multi-step forecasts are two faces of the same problem for medical world models, and proposes Fisher-information regularisation as a unified remedy for calibrated, shift-robust latent dynamics. The goal is reliable digital-twin treatment planning where clinical risk is highest. Calibration under shift is the central reliability requirement.

entry.title: Sequence-SOD: Bio-inspired Sequence-aware Spiking ObjectDetection for Event Cameras

author.name: Katharina Bendig, Ren\'e Schuster, Didier Stricker

entry.summary: A spiking neural network object detector for event cameras that processes extended event sequences with labels at multiple time points instead of resetting state after each isolated interval. Better exploits temporal continuity in continuous event streams for neuromorphic detection.

entry.title: FreeShadow: Training-Free Shadow Removal via Illumination Transfer and Selective Content Preservation in Diffusion Models

author.name: Yinan Wang, Yan Huang, Yong Xu, Patrick Le Callet

entry.summary: Removes shadows using only pretrained diffusion priors, with no training or test-time optimization, by re-weighting self-attention to transfer illumination cues from lit to shadowed regions and selectively preserving content. Aims to avoid the artifacts and slow optimization of prior zero-shot approaches.

entry.title: Robust RPC Bundle Adjustment for Multi-Date Satellite Imagery with Season-Invariant Correspondences

author.name: Roger Mar\'i, El\'ias Masquil, Xavier Bou, Thibaud Ehret, Gabriele Facciolo

entry.summary: Replaces handcrafted feature matching in satellite camera-model refinement with learned local matching plus global descriptors for selecting visually compatible image pairs across dates. Improves geolocation bundle adjustment when seasonal, illumination, and land-cover changes break classical correspondences.

entry.title: Explainable and Resource-Efficient Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal LLMs for Decision-Critical Applications

author.name: Piyush Jain, Kousik Dasgupta, Rajarshi Roy, Subarna Tripathi

entry.summary: Extends depth-layered prompting for multimodal LLMs so that object-to-object projective and topological spatial relations within the same depth plane can be resolved, aiming for explainable and resource-efficient spatial reasoning. Motivated by trust and auditability needs in robotics and safety monitoring.

entry.title: From Uncertainty to Determinism: Coarse-to-Fine Visual Floorplan Localization without Ray Matching

author.name: Shiyong Meng, Bolei Chen, Ping Zhong, Yang Wan, Rongzhi Wang, Jiazhi Xia, Jianxin Wang

entry.summary: Bypasses explicit ray prediction and matching for localizing camera images against minimal indoor floorplans, instead using a coarse-to-fine scheme that resolves multimodal pose ambiguity from repetitive layouts. Reduces preprocessing cost and exhaustive matching at inference.

entry.title: Semi-Decentralized Multi-Spacecraft Collision Avoidance under Communication Constraints

author.name: Grace Ra Kim, Mahdi Al-Husseini, Duncan Eddy, Mykel J. Kochenderfer

entry.summary: Proposes a semi-decentralized multiagent POMDP formulation for spacecraft collision avoidance in which operators only exchange information during intermittent ground-station contacts, and asks how much coordination is actually needed to match centralized planning. It matters because existing multiagent decision-theoretic methods assume unrealistic continuous communication, while orbital congestion makes conjunction avoidance an urgent operational problem.

entry.title: …but have the weights left the server?

author.name: David Scott Krueger

entry.summary: Argues that after any incident where an AI system escapes its sandbox, the public should explicitly demand demonstration that model weights were not copied elsewhere, and criticizes the norm of treating such incidents as closed without that check. It frames the absence of this demand as a dangerous precedent for AI incident reporting.

entry.title: The Easy Trap: Why LLMs Underestimate Misconception-Driven Difficulty

author.name: Amanda La Hadi, Muhammad Johan Alibasa, Guanliang Chen, A. Taufiq Asyhari

entry.summary: Compares LLM-generated difficulty ratings for 32 arithmetic items against empirical difficulty derived from 770 undergraduate responses using classical test theory and a two-parameter item response model. Finds only moderate rank correlation and a systematic tendency for models to underestimate difficulty driven by student misconceptions.

entry.title: GuidedRAG: Semantic Steering of Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Matthijs Jansen op de Haar, Tobias St\"ahle, Lorenzo Gatti

entry.summary: GuidedRAG adds a semantic selection stage that constrains the knowledge base before retrieval, aligning the search space with user intent instead of relying on increasingly complex retrieval structures. Reports double-digit relevance improvements and order-of-magnitude reductions in retrieval overhead.

entry.title: A Reference-Free Score for Detecting Silent Reasoning Failures in Large Language Models

author.name: Vivek Shukla, Varun Shukla, Atul, Divya Mishra, Mehul Kumar Das

entry.summary: Proposes a reference-free instance-level score combining step validity, entailment from reasoning to answer, and counterfactual sensitivity to detect chains of thought that reach correct answers through invalid derivations or vice versa. Frames the mismatch between derivation validity and answer correctness as a consistency gap.

entry.title: Entity Resolution in Practice: Lessons from a Self-Serve Pipeline

author.name: Kaushik Pavani, Ganga Aluri, Pravin Jadhav, Neeraj Prasad, Kiran Sanka

entry.summary: Reports operational lessons from a self-serve entity resolution system evaluated on six benchmarks from under a thousand to five million records, including that no matcher wins universally, that precision and recall need separate mechanisms rather than a shared threshold, and that transitive closure over a single false link can silently merge unrelated entities. Recommends per-dataset algorithm bake-offs and rule-based precision vetoes.

entry.title: Route by Kinematics, Act by Observation: Kinematics-Supervised Expert Routing in MoE-Augmented VLA

author.name: Tianhang Yang, Yanze Zheng, Junjie Wang, Wei-Bin Kou, Ruotong Li, Yujiu Yang

entry.summary: Observes that semantically diverse manipulation tasks collapse into a small number of kinematic archetypes, and uses clusters of action trajectories as supervision labels for the router in a mixture-of-experts vision-language-action model. This replaces implicit observation-driven routing with explicit kinematics-guided expert dispatch that still works when kinematic signals are unavailable at inference.

entry.title: Global Exponential Stabilization of the Kinematic Bicycle Model of a Car in Polar Coordinates

author.name: Velimir Todorovski, Kwang Hak Kim, Alessandro Astolfi, Miroslav Krstic

entry.summary: Derives globally exponentially stabilizing feedback for the kinematic bicycle model by moving to polar plus range-normalized coordinates that sidestep Brockett's obstruction to smooth static feedback, then applying a nonstandard backstepping design. The resulting maneuvers resemble how humans actually park.

entry.title: Physically Real-time Infrared Attack against Optical Flow Estimation Networks

author.name: Shen You, Wei Jiang, Jiarui Liu, Yijian Ye, Qiuzhen Lin, Xiangtao Li, Ka-Chun Wong

entry.summary: This work demonstrates real-time physical adversarial attacks on optical flow estimation networks using infrared light, which is stealthy to human observers, by precomputing large sets of adversarial examples and displaying them dynamically. Optical flow feeds many safety-critical downstream tasks such as autonomous driving and motion detection.

entry.title: Efficient Heteroscedastic Bayesian Optimization for Risk-Aware AutoRL

author.name: Mingxuan Che, Tsung-Yuan Tseng, Theresa Eimer, Marius Lindauer, Alexander von Rohr

entry.summary: ERAHBO is a heteroscedastic Bayesian optimization method for automated RL that models both the mean and the variance of learning outcomes as functions of hyperparameters, seeking configurations that are both high-performing and stable across seeds, with adaptive re-sampling instead of a fixed evaluation budget per configuration. It targets the well-known seed sensitivity of RL results.

entry.title: MPEcho: A Melody and Phoneme-Aware Generative Framework for Controllable Cover Song Generation

author.name: Wei-Jaw Lee, Hsuan-Yu Yeh, Ting-Yi Hu, Chih-Pin Tan, Fang-Duo Tsai, Yi-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: ServerlessT2I decomposes text-to-image workflows into independently scheduled model functions rather than deploying each workflow as one opaque GPU function, enabling finer-grained scaling, placement, and multi-tenant fairness. It targets the intermittent, user-composed nature of image generation pipelines.

entry.title: FedTopo: Relation-Level Topology Sharing for Model-Heterogeneous Federated Learning

author.name: Zhaoyang Ma, Zhihao Wu, Xin Gao, Lipo Wang, Youfang Lin, Jing Wang

entry.summary: FedTopo shares knowledge in model-heterogeneous federated learning as class relation topology, capturing how classes relate within each client, instead of parameters, distilled predictions, or prototypes that live in absolute representation spaces requiring cross-client alignment. This is meant to survive the misalignment caused by heterogeneous local backbones.

entry.title: BioVLN: A Simulation Platform for Visual Language Navigation in Biomedical Laboratories

author.name: Zhe Liu, Quan Lu, Zhaohui Du, Zhe Wang, Huanbo Jin, Jiaming Gu, Qi Wang, Ting Xiao, Minting Pan, Dongzhan Zhou

entry.summary: BioVLN is a simulation platform for vision-language navigation inside biomedical laboratories, where each instrument is modeled with a body, a clearance zone, and an operation area on its usable side, so agents must approach equipment from the correct working position rather than merely reach an object center. It adapts embodied navigation evaluation away from household assumptions toward lab safety constraints.

entry.title: Progressive Multimodal Alignment for Continual Instruction Tuning

author.name: Duzhen Zhang, Yahan Yu, Qiaoyi Su, Jiahua Dong, Tielin Zhang

entry.summary: This work highlights projector-level forgetting in multimodal continual instruction tuning, where the module aligning visual features to the language embedding space drifts as visual distributions and instruction semantics change, an issue overlooked by methods focused on the language backbone. Progressive Multimodal Alignment detects distribution shifts with a lightweight descriptor and progressively expands projector experts to adapt while preserving earlier alignment.

entry.title: Improving Item Discoverability in e-Commerce Search via Related Intent Generation

author.name: Ji Xin, Xiao Xiao, Ishan Bhatt, Vinesh Gudla, Trace Levinson, Raochuan Fan, Shishir Kumar Prasad, Prakash Putta, Tejaswi Tenneti

entry.summary: An industrial e-commerce system expands search recall by generating implicit user intents with closed-weight LLMs offline, then distilling into a cheaper two-stage hybrid architecture for online serving. The goal is to surface substitute, complementary, and thematically related grocery items that strict query matching misses. It is a deployment case study on the cost-quality tradeoff of generative retrieval.

entry.title: Data Fusion and Contrastive Alignment for Unconstrained IR Molecular Structure Elucidation

author.name: Ethan J. Mick, Campbell A. Sweet, Matthias J. Young, Derek T. Anderson

entry.summary: This work removes the usual requirement that a chemical formula be supplied as auxiliary input for molecular structure elucidation from infrared spectra, modifying encoder-decoder transformers to handle the far larger unconstrained chemical space via data fusion and contrastive alignment. Prior transformer results mostly amounted to isomer selection rather than genuine structure prediction. It matters for automated analytical chemistry workflows.

entry.title: Examining the Efficacy of Graph Neural Network Message-Passing in Regression Contexts

author.name: Keith G. Mills, Aedan J. DeFrates, Joong Ho Kim

entry.summary: This study argues that graph neural network message-passing layers are almost exclusively benchmarked on classification and asks whether the same designs help for scalar regression on graphs such as molecules and neural architecture blueprints. It systematically evaluates message-passing variants in regression settings that the field usually overlooks. The concern is that community progress may be overfit to classification metrics.

entry.title: Origins and mitigation of double descent in reduced order modeling

author.name: Andrei A. Klishin, J. Nathan Kutz, Krithika Manohar

entry.summary: Develops a unified data-noise averaging theory explaining when double descent appears in sparse sensing and reduced-order reconstruction, attributing the error peak to catastrophic amplification of a pathological signal component. Provides quantitative risk-curve predictions and mitigation strategies via sensor placement and regularization.

entry.title: Same Evidence, Different Target: Decoding How Diagnostic Evidence Bears on Causal Questions from Language-Model States

author.name: Weiyi Kong, Zhuoran Li

entry.summary: Constructs paired prompts that repeat identical diagnostic evidence while changing the causal target, labeling each case by whether the evidence favors, challenges, leaves unresolved, or misses the claim. Uses linear probes on hidden states to test whether models internally represent the evidence-to-target relation rather than exploiting lexical overlap.

entry.title: Breaking the Curse with BAND: Nonparametric Distribution Estimation in High Dimensions

author.name: Shuo-Chieh Huang, Chien-Ming Chi, Jau-er Chen

entry.summary: Proposes estimating high-dimensional joint distributions through a sparse Bayesian network where each conditional is fit with sparsity-aware conditional mean regression. Achieves polynomial total-variation convergence rates with dimension growing polynomially in sample size, beating classical histogram-density rates.

entry.title: Relation Geometry in Semantic Space of Language Models

author.name: Zhihan Cao, Hiroaki Yamada, Simone Teufel, Tatsuya Hiraoka, Kentaro Inui, Hitomi Yanaka, Takenobu Tokunaga

entry.summary: Investigates how much knowledge about lexical-semantic relations is encoded in the geometry of language model embedding spaces, testing whether relata for a given relation occupy distinct regions and whether relational properties like symmetry and asymmetry are reflected. Provides a systematic three-perspective geometric analysis.

entry.title: WildShadowRemover: In-the-Wild Video Shadow Removal via Detail-Preserving Video Diffusion Models

author.name: Jiamin Xu, Cong Wang, Zheng Dong, Chi Wang, Renshu Gu, Weiwei Xu, Gang Xu

entry.summary: Adapts a pretrained video diffusion model with LoRA for shadow removal in unconstrained real videos, adding a detail injection module to the frozen decoder and frequency-decomposed modulation guided by shadow masks. Targets the scarcity of in-the-wild video shadow removal training data.

entry.title: HeteroPROPMT: A Real-time and Privacy-Preserving Heterogeneous Collaborative Perception Framework

author.name: Armin Maleki, Hayder Radha

entry.summary: Proposes a real-time framework for collaborative perception among vehicles that use different sensors, models, and training domains, avoiding retraining of fusion heads or sharing of proprietary metadata. Uses prompt-style adaptation to align heterogeneous feature spaces for privacy-preserving fusion.

entry.title: Eddeep: a deep-learning framework for fast eddy-current distortion correction in diffusion MRI

author.name: Antoine Legouhy, Ross Callaghan, Yuchuan Qiao, Whitney Stee, Philippe Peigneux, Hojjat Azadbakht, Hui Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces a two-stage deep learning pipeline for correcting eddy-current geometric distortions in diffusion MRI, first standardizing volume appearance via supervised image translation and then registering volumes. Aims to match iterative state-of-the-art correction quality at much lower compute cost.

entry.title: From Spatial Semantics to Temporal Context: Leveraging Gaze Trajectory for Weakly Supervised Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Shaoxuan Wu, Xiao Zhang, Xiaodi Zhao, Yunzhi Tian, Yilin Tang, Jun Feng

entry.summary: Uses clinician gaze trajectories, not just fixation points, as weak supervision for medical image segmentation, modeling the temporal order of visual inspection while suppressing noisy exploratory fixations with uncertainty estimates. Offers a cheaper annotation route that fits existing clinical workflows.

entry.title: 3DGBGS: 3D Granular Ball Gaussian Splatting for Compact Novel View Synthesis

author.name: Meng Yang, Shuyin Xia, Dawei Dai, YiWang

entry.summary: Introduces adaptive granular-ball organization to anchor-based 3D Gaussian Splatting, replacing fixed voxelization of sparse point clouds with a coarse-to-fine adaptive structure. Targets compactness and quality for non-uniform point distributions in novel view synthesis.

entry.title: Long-Tailed 3D Point Cloud Dataset Distillation

author.name: Jiahao You, Xu Han, Jinfeng Xu, Xianzhi Li

entry.summary: First study of dataset distillation for 3D point clouds under long-tailed class distributions, where both training and test splits are imbalanced. Adds modules that explicitly account for the imbalance rather than only optimizing geometry or forcing a class-balanced synthetic set.

entry.title: Speech2Grasp: Data-Efficient Transfer of Text-Conditioned Grasp Detection to Speech in Humanoid Robots

author.name: Hung Nguyen, Kim Nhat Minh Nguyen, Van Duc Vu, Van-Danh Le, Hoang Huy Le, Dinh Tuan Nguyen, Pham Tuyen Le, Van-Truong Nguyen, Quan Nguyen

entry.summary: Tests whether a text-conditioned grasp detection model can be transferred to spoken instructions with minimal data, finding that a lightweight projector suffices to map speech into the existing text space while preserving semantics. Validated with real humanoid robot grasping experiments.

entry.title: Do LoRA Read Directions Encode Visual Concepts?

author.name: Zhao Pengfei

entry.summary: Compares the semantic coherence of read directions learned by standard, ReLU, and TopK LoRA adapters against matched random directions in the residual stream of a CLIP model, using a clarity metric. Learned directions are more consistently coherent than random ones, but random directions sometimes look convincing too, so a single striking activation grid is not evidence that a concept was learned.

entry.title: Diagnosing Fine-Grained Inconsistency Classification in Financial Disclosure Text

author.name: Aman Kumar, Lasitha Vidyaratne, Dipanjan D Ghosh, Arnab Chakrabarti, Ahmed K Farahat

entry.summary: Studies fine-grained classification of inconsistency types in financial disclosures across numerical, temporal, referential, factual, and normative categories, comparing frozen embedding classifiers, fine-tuned encoders, evidence-augmented variants, and prompted LLMs on a synthetic benchmark of nearly six thousand instances. Argues that detecting a conflict is insufficient because different types require different downstream checks.

entry.title: Vision-TL-Action: Neuro-Symbolic Trajectory Generation from Visual Observations and Temporal Logic

author.name: Zezhi Liu, Zhiwei Zheng, Hanqian Luo, Deyun Qin, Shizhen Wu, Yongchun Fang

entry.summary: Vision-TL-Action generates robot trajectories from multi-view images plus a coordinate-free temporal logic task graph, fusing symbolic task nodes and visual tokens via cross-attention to condition a flow-matching trajectory generator. The point is to force genuine perception-to-symbol grounding rather than letting the task specification smuggle in exact object coordinates.

entry.title: Sensor-Placement-Agnostic Sonomyography: Toward Continuous High-Dimensional Control by Users with Tetraplegia

author.name: Gavin Sueltz, Vikram Athithan, Emma Ferran, Maria Herrera, Carson J. Wynn, Laura A. Hallock

entry.summary: Describes a real-time sonomyography interface that infers intended movement from ultrasound images of muscle using sparse optical flow, achieving continuous one-degree-of-freedom control after only three calibration poses and a preliminary two-degree-of-freedom extension. It was tested with three participants who have cervical spinal cord injury.

entry.title: Toward a Unified Statistical Theory of Unsupervised Pretraining and Supervised Neural Knowledge Graph Learning

author.name: Jifan Zhang, Miklos Racz, Suqi Liu

entry.summary: Develops a two-stage theory for knowledge graph learning in which unsupervised pretraining on heterogeneous corpora is followed by supervised multi-relation learning, and proves a nonasymptotic risk bound that separates pretraining representation error from labeled-sample error. The framework subsumes several existing scoring-function designs that were previously chosen heuristically.

entry.title: Compute growth doesn't make a software intelligence explosion more likely

author.name: Karthik Tadepalli

entry.summary: Argues against a common shortcut in software-intelligence-explosion debates, showing that exponentially growing physical compute does not change whether the feedback loop of AI-automated AI research becomes explosive. The claim is that the explosion condition depends on returns to research effort, not on the level or growth rate of compute stock.

entry.title: FAS-R1: A Unified Multi-Task MLLM for Reasoning Face Anti-Spoofing

author.name: Hongyang Wang, Yichen Shi, Hongrui Li, Yiru Huo, Jun Feng, Zitong Yu

entry.summary: FAS-R1 is a multimodal LLM for face anti-spoofing that jointly outputs authenticity decisions, attack-type labels, and spoof-region localization, trained with long chain-of-thought supervised warm-up followed by task-specific reinforcement learning. The goal is explainable, evidence-grounded spoof detection rather than bare binary labels.
