Convergence theory, iteration bounds, and complexity estimates are provided along with experiments.

entry.title: ARC’s research agenda: solid mathematics, an unclear safety case

author.name: Ondřej_Kubů

entry.summary: A mathematician entering AI safety begins a series critiquing theory-first safety organizations, starting with an assessment that ARC's heuristic-argument agenda is mathematically solid but does not clearly connect to a safety case. It mainly links to a longer external writeup.

entry.title: Localized Anomaly Detection via Differentiable D-vine Copulas

author.name: Nicholas Andrea Pearson, Francesca Zanello, Davide Russo, Luca Bortolussi, Francesca Cairoli

entry.summary: Replaces the greedy sequential family selection used to fit D-vine copulas with a differentiable formulation that considers configurations jointly, avoiding early commitment to locally optimal pair-copula choices. Applied to localized anomaly detection in multivariate data.

entry.title: JKO-RAG: Distributional Retrieval as Wasserstein Free-Energy Gradient Flow

author.name: Levi Segal, Murari Ambati

entry.summary: JKO-RAG reframes retrieval reranking as minimizing a free-energy functional balancing relevance, entropy and redundancy under Wasserstein-2 gradient flow, using an embedding-geometry ground metric. A linear-response analysis argues why optimal-transport geometry beats KL-style selection for choosing passage sets rather than ranked lists.

entry.title: VAD to the Bone: Ultra-Tiny Speech Activity Detection for Edge Deployment

author.name: Stephen Bauer, Sheila Seidel, Shanza Iftikhar, Scott Veidenheimer, Gorkem Ulkar

entry.summary: kiloVAD is an ultra-small voice activity detector using only standard Mel features and causal convolutions so it runs on commodity embedded hardware, trained with structured pruning, self-distillation and angle-based quantization-aware training. It reports competitive causal per-frame accuracy with about two thousand parameters.

entry.title: Can Deep Generative Models Reproduce Non-Stationary Gaussian Random Fields?

author.name: Daniel Kua, Yan Song

entry.summary: This benchmarking study asks whether flow matching, DDPM, score-based SDE and VAE models can recover the true mean and covariance structure of a known non-stationary Gaussian random field, with oracle and stationary controls as references. It provides diagnostic metrics for spatial generative modeling where ground truth is normally unavailable.

entry.title: Quasi-SVD: Learning a Lie-constrained matrix factorisation for real-time imaging

author.name: Christopher Hahne

entry.summary: Quasi-SVD replaces sequential singular value decomposition with a fully parallel, differentiable factorization that enforces exact orthogonality on only one Lie-parameterized factor and uses soft constraints for the rest. The asymmetric design targets real-time GPU matrix factorization in clinical imaging pipelines.

entry.title: TimeCapsule: Generative Hallucination as a Method for Historical Sensemaking

author.name: Hayk Grigorian, Hamed Yaghoobian

entry.summary: TimeCapsule is a 1.2B-parameter language model trained only on Victorian-era texts to serve as an epistemologically isolated generative archive, avoiding the contemporary concept contamination of standard LLMs. It reduces perplexity on held-out Victorian prose relative to a GPT-2 baseline and produces period-plausible analogies for modern concepts.

entry.title: Room-Mediated Co-occurrence for Zero-Shot Object-Centric Semantic Navigation via Frontier Scoring

author.name: Adam Scicluna, Gavin Paul, Alen Alempijevic

entry.summary: A training-free object-goal navigation pipeline that routes object-to-object relationships through a compact set of room categories, converting CLIP similarities into room probability vectors and propagating scores over a map with fast marching to rank exploration frontiers. It gives interpretable semantic priors without any training.

entry.title: GrocLM: Grocery Category Recommendation in E-Commerce with Large Language Models

author.name: Yuan Zhong, Chuanwei Ruan, Moein Hasani, Tejaswi Tenneti, Haixun Wang, Fenglong Ma

entry.summary: A production-deployed fine-tuned language model for grocery category recommendation that uses two-stage LoRA training to encode cyclical repurchase patterns into weights, plus trie-based constrained decoding to keep outputs within a valid taxonomy. Reports real-world e-commerce deployment.

entry.title: MusiChat: Vibe Composing for Music Creation

author.name: Callie C. Liao, Duoduo Liao, Ellie L. Zhang

entry.summary: A conversational music creation system that supports iterative refinement of existing compositions rather than regeneration from scratch, using a hierarchical framework that separates lyric-aligned structure generation from expressive surface realization. Enables structure-preserving stylistic edits through dialogue.

entry.title: Quotient Dynamics, Effective Curvature, and Implicit Bias in Positive Quadratic Networks

author.name: Pengcheng Cheng

entry.summary: Analyzes gradient dynamics of positive quadratic networks by identifying the factorization quotient space with the manifold of low-rank PSD matrices, showing factor gradient flow projects exactly onto Riemannian flow and deriving effective curvature and implicit bias results. Contributes to theory of implicit regularization in overparameterized factorized models.

entry.title: Distributing Security Controls Through Harness Engineering

author.name: William Robert Gore

entry.summary: Tests whether off-the-shelf security controls can be layered onto commercial AI coding agents through a custom harness, comparing four configurations across a 23-test suite and avoiding vendor lock-in. Relevant to enterprises where security concerns block agentic coding rollout.

entry.title: dtControl2+$\varepsilon$: Trading Optimality for Explainability in MDPs via Decision Trees

author.name: Tereza Kinsk\'a, Jan K\v{r}et\'insk\'y, Tobias Meggendorfer, Sabine Rieder, Maximilian Weininger

entry.summary: Extends a state-of-the-art decision-tree controller representation tool so that users can trade a bounded amount of optimality for a much smaller, more human-comprehensible tree, with guarantees on the resulting policy quality in Markov decision processes. Useful for explainable and certifiable controller deployment.

entry.title: CARE-MH: Towards Unified, Reproducible, and Comparable Evaluation of Mental Health LLMs

author.name: Asher Sprigler, Yixue Zhao, Yi Ding

entry.summary: CARE-MH provides a unified framework for reproducing and comparing mental health LLM benchmarks, finding that reproducibility depends heavily on model output stability and that cross-benchmark disagreement mostly traces to inconsistent metric definitions rather than genuine capability differences. Calls for standardized evaluation configurations and shared metric specifications.

entry.title: Reading Without a Reader: Large Language Models Collapse Reading and Writing into a Single Entangled Code

author.name: Diego Salda\~na Ulloa

entry.summary: Compares input embedding and output unembedding matrices across nine model families using similarity measures calibrated against independent-initialization floors and weight-tied ceilings, arguing decoder-only models collapse reading and writing into one entangled code unlike the doubly dissociable human systems. Offers a cognitive-neuroscience framing of a structural property of transformers.

entry.title: HVM-GraphRAG: Holistic-View Multimodal Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Complex Document

author.name: Xin He, Yili Wang, Wenqi Fan, Qing Li, Qinggang Zhang, Yi Chang, Xin Wang

entry.summary: HVM-GraphRAG constructs a multimodal document graph under a holistic view to reduce noisy and conflicting updates, building reliable indices between concept nodes and supporting multimodal chunks, then searching to avoid expensive traversal. Targets question answering requiring evidence scattered across distant regions and modalities of complex documents.

entry.title: GraphRareBench: An Auditable Graph-Evidence Benchmark for Phenotype-Driven Rare-Disease Diagnosis

author.name: Guiling Guo, Jia Yang, Jiahao Xu, Shuyuan Zheng, Zhonghai Sun, Qiyuan Li

entry.summary: GraphRareBench is a provenance-preserving rare-disease diagnosis benchmark with over 2,300 ontology-derived cases and 18,000 target-confounder pairs, exposing graph-defined hard confounders and source-linked evidence rather than only reporting the rank of the correct disease. It compares supervised rankers against tool-using agents on a gene-disjoint test split.

entry.title: Spectral Truncation in Synthetic Control

author.name: Mojtaba Eslami

entry.summary: Analyzes synthetic control estimators that match treated units in coordinates from the leading temporal singular vectors of the donor panel, plus a hybrid weighting retained and discarded directions. Proves the family collapses to standard synthetic control at full rank and characterizes underdetermination and bias mapping.

entry.title: Multi-Scale Structural Features for Continual, Comprehensible Visual Recognition in a Developmental Learning Framework

author.name: Zeki Doruk Erden

entry.summary: Improves a gradient-free developmental learning framework that builds a discrete topological model of inputs through local variation and selection, replacing a low-expressivity visual feature representation with multi-scale structural features. The framework offers continual learning without replay buffers or task boundaries.

entry.title: Contrastive Representation Learning of Longitudinal Disease Trajectories on Temporal Graphs

author.name: Bastian Pfeifer

entry.summary: Models longitudinal patient data as temporal graphs where nodes are observations over time and edges capture temporal continuity and trajectory similarity, then learns embeddings with contrastive graph neural networks guided by structure-aware random walks. The embeddings support clustering of patients with similar disease progression.

entry.title: Shared Voxel-Map-Based Cooperative Indoor UAV Guidance with a Multi-Agent Soft Actor-Critic Controller

author.name: Thomas Hickling, Dylan Wynne, Yu Su, Nabil Aouf

entry.summary: This work combines a shared voxel occupancy map fused from multiple drones with a multi-agent soft actor-critic controller that acts on ego-aligned bird's-eye-view crops. The integrate-in-world, act-in-ego design supports centralized training with decentralized execution for indoor multi-UAV navigation.

entry.title: FinAbstain: Uncertainty-Calibrated Multimodal RAG for Selective Financial Forecasting

author.name: Dorothy Torres, Wei Cheng, Henan Huang

entry.summary: FinAbstain is an uncertainty-calibrated multimodal RAG framework for financial forecasting that enforces point-in-time retrieval and aggregates agent assessments with contradiction and consistency signals to decide when to abstain. It targets confident model outputs generated from sparse, stale or conflicting evidence.

entry.title: Physics-Informed CNN-LSTM for Street-Scale Urban Flood Prediction: Reconciling Aggregate Accuracy and Street-Level Plausibility

author.name: Luc DCosta, Yidi Wang, Jonathan L. Goodall, Rohan Chandra

entry.summary: A CNN-LSTM urban flood surrogate is trained with three differentiable physics penalties, discouraging water flowing uphill, enforcing local mass conservation with rainfall-adaptive thresholds, and penalizing false alarms using topographic wetness. The goal is street-level physical plausibility rather than only good aggregate error metrics.

entry.title: Zhinv: Real-time hub-height wind field reconstruction using only local sparse observations

author.name: Zongwei Zhang, Chin Chun Ooi, Lianlei Lin, Sheng Gao, Tiantian He, Yew Soon Ong, Junkai Wang, Hangyi Yu, Jiaqi Zhang, Hanqing Zhao, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: Zhinv reconstructs continuous hub-height wind fields directly from sparse, irregular local observations, validated in Northeast China, Europe and Southeast Asia. Fine-grained regional wind knowledge supports wind power regulation, resource assessment and low-altitude environmental perception.

entry.title: TWICE: Two-Clock, Two-Window Learning for Long-Horizon Conversion Prediction in Online Advertising

author.name: Kaiyuan Li, Kun Wang, Zhongbo Wang, Teng Sha, Ming Yan, Yanhua Cheng, Xialong Liu

entry.summary: TWICE handles long-horizon conversion prediction in advertising, where clicks are observed on one clock but conversions mature over a much longer window with delay composition biased by historical click cohorts. It factorizes long-horizon CVR into target-window components to reconcile timely partial supervision with delayed labels.

entry.title: PIcsC: Partitioning-Induced Covariate Shift Correction

author.name: Behraj Khan, Behroz Mirza, Syed Ahmad Chan Bukhari, Tahir Qasim Syed

entry.summary: PIcsC uses a Fisher Information Matrix approximation of divergence between data partitions and a reference distribution as a regularizer, correcting covariate shift that biases model selection in cross-validation, lifelong learning and federated settings. One formulation covers both centrally partitioned and inherently distributed data.

entry.title: MorphUNet: Alpha-Controlled Biometric Transport for Diffusion-Based Face Morphing Attacks

author.name: Taimoor Rizwan, Sara Atito, Zhenhua Feng, Muhammad Awais, Josef Kittler

entry.summary: MorphUNet builds diffusion-based face morphs by treating two-parent generation as alpha-controlled biometric transport, keeping each parent's ArcFace identity evidence in separate token banks routed through parent-separated dual cross-attention inside the denoising network. The goal is to produce morphs that verify against multiple identities, exposing weaknesses in border-control face verification.

entry.title: OpenPVMapper: A Multi-source, Nationwide Database of Rooftop Photovoltaic Systems in France

author.name: Gabiel Kasmi

entry.summary: OpenPVMapper assembles a nationwide installation-level database of over a million rooftop photovoltaic systems in France by reconciling deep-learning detections on aerial imagery with OpenStreetMap and probabilistic building-level detections. It fills a gap where public registries only record installations above a capacity threshold.

entry.title: CD-RMOT-Bench: Benchmarking the Cross-Domain Referring Multi-Object Tracking

author.name: Xiangqun Zhang, Likai Wang, Zekun Qian, Ruize Han, Wei Feng

entry.summary: Introduces cross-domain referring multi-object tracking, where a language-conditioned tracker trained on a labeled source domain must follow natural-language expressions under unseen visual conditions, together with the CD-RMOT-Bench benchmark. It probes robustness of language-guided tracking to domain shift.

entry.title: Towards Reliable Stain Transfer: An Iterative Data-Model Co-Optimization Framework Based on Multimodal Expert-Guided Assessment

author.name: Siyuan Xu, Yan Wang, Haofei Song, Lili Gao, Jiansheng Wang, Qing Zhang, Dan Huang, Boxiang Yun, Hongkai Xiong, Qingli Li

entry.summary: DMCoStain iteratively co-refines training data and model capability for virtual immunohistochemistry staining from hematoxylin-and-eosin images, using multimodal expert-guided assessment to handle pixel-unaligned supervision across heterogeneous biomarkers. It targets both staining accuracy and interpretability.

entry.title: Group Equivariant Diffusion for Anomaly Detection in Computational Cytology

author.name: Swarnadip Chatterjee, Ssharvien Kumar Sivakumar, Anirban Mukhopadhyay

entry.summary: Proposes a group-equivariant diffusion model for unsupervised anomaly detection in cytology whole-slide images, exploiting the fact that rotating or flipping a single-cell patch should not change its diagnostic class or its anomaly score. Standard diffusion models produce transformation-dependent reconstructions that destabilize scoring.

entry.title: Beyond Facial Consistency: Personalized Person Image Generation with Holistic Identity Preservation

author.name: Yuxuan Xiao, Shanshan Zhang, Jian Yang, Shengcai Liao

entry.summary: Addresses the trade-off in personalized person image generation between facial fidelity and overall appearance consistency using a dual-branch baseline plus Dynamic Balancing Scaling, a fine-tuning strategy that coordinates the contributions of the global-appearance and local-face branches. It targets holistic rather than face-only identity preservation.

entry.title: Adversarial Deepfake Generation and an Investigation of Purification-Based Adversarial Detection

author.name: Junghyun Kim, Seunghyun Kim, Jiyoung Woo

entry.summary: A shared-task entry that generates identity-preserving deepfakes evading twelve detectors simultaneously via multi-model projected gradient descent with compression and transformation robustness, achieving 90 percent evasion against organizer detectors. It also builds an ensemble detector combining vision foundation model features, reaching high accuracy on baseline sets.

entry.title: On the Use of Synthetic Data for Threshold Calibration in Face Recognition: Performance and Security Implications for Border Control Systems

author.name: Arto Apila

entry.summary: Investigates whether synthetic face data can be used to calibrate verification thresholds for the European Entry/Exit System at the very low false-match rates required by border control, given legal and privacy constraints on real data. It analyzes how well synthetic score distributions align with operational ones and the resulting security implications.

entry.title: Motion Generation With Environmental Constraints

author.name: El\H{o}d P\'all, Oliver Brock

entry.summary: This work argues that robots should deliberately use contact with the environment to simplify motion planning rather than always avoiding collisions, calling the idea Environmental Constraint Exploitation. It integrates the idea into sampling-based planners such as RRT and shows reduced planning complexity and improved execution robustness in a real-world task.

entry.title: Atmospheric Diffusion-Guided Spatio-Temporal Transformer for Nuclear Radiation Forecasting

author.name: Tengfei Lyu, Jindong Han, Hao Liu

entry.summary: A spatio-temporal transformer guided by atmospheric diffusion physics for forecasting environmental radiation levels across thousands of monitoring stations. Addresses non-stationary station time series driven by decay, weather variability, and human interventions.

entry.title: Dual-Domain Manifold Modeling for Hyperspectral Image Fusion

author.name: Chengxin Xie, Qiya Song, Yangbangyan Jiang, Renwei Dian, Xudong Kang

entry.summary: A dual-domain framework for hyperspectral image fusion that adds explicit geometric constraints in the spatial domain to counter low-frequency bias and exploits local manifold structure induced by spectral similarity in the spectral domain. Targets simultaneous spectral richness and spatial fidelity.

entry.title: Loss Invariance Determines What Concept Layers Encode: Volume Grounding in Echocardiography

author.name: Hyunkyung Han, Min Jung Kim

entry.summary: Examines whether concept bottleneck models genuinely ground their intermediate variables, using left-ventricular volumes as concepts for ejection fraction estimation from echocardiography video. Shows that what a concept layer actually encodes depends on which transformations the training loss is invariant to, so accurate downstream prediction does not imply valid concepts.

entry.title: A Cost-Effective Multimodal LLM Reasoning Framework for Question Answering over Irregular Clinical Time Series

author.name: Frank Nie, Ethan B Liu, Yuan Zhu, Wei Fan, Jindong Han

entry.summary: ClinPRISM is a cost-conscious multimodal LLM framework for question answering over irregular clinical time series, using an irregularity-aware multi-scale encoder plus a temporal evidence distiller to compress sparse asynchronous observations before reasoning. Targets the mismatch between general time-series LLMs and real clinical sampling patterns.

entry.title: Large Language Model for Operations Research Formulation Selection in Multi-Warehouse Inventory Allocation

author.name: Jintao Xu, Yingzheng Ma, Jiong Dong, Yongzhi Qi, Jianshen Zhang

entry.summary: Frames multi-warehouse inventory allocation as instance-wise selection among a library of solver-executable mixed-integer formulations, training a language-model selector with solver feedback to match each instance regime to the right formulation. Applies LLMs to formulation choice rather than to generating optimization code from scratch.

entry.title: From Naive RAG to Deep Agentic Retrieval: An Evolving Context Engineering Pipeline for Regulatory Compliance

author.name: Mishca de Costa, Muhammad Saleh Anwar, Dave Mercier, Issam Hammad

entry.summary: Traces the production evolution of a regulatory-compliance retrieval pipeline at a large power utility from naive RAG through hybrid retrieval with reranking to agentic function calling and finally a deep multi-agent architecture with code-based tool synthesis and explicit planning, documenting the failure modes that forced each transition. A rare longitudinal industrial account of context engineering at scale.

entry.title: When Thinking Before Retrieval Hurts: TraceBound Diagnostics for Adaptive Knowledge-Graph Retrieval

author.name: Partha Sarathi Purkayastha (ETH Z\"urich)

entry.summary: Introduces a diagnostic protocol that adds pre-retrieval query profiles and post-failure trace hints to an adaptive knowledge-graph retriever, and reports that this extra conditioning improves inspectability but consistently degrades retrieval quality with open-weight controllers. A useful negative result on when reasoning before retrieval hurts.

entry.title: Dual-Level Atomic and Coordination Geometry Learning for Crystal Property Prediction Using Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Sanjay Chakraborty

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-scale graph network for crystal property prediction that explicitly models coordination polyhedra alongside atoms and bonds through three coupled graphs, arguing that many material properties are governed by these structural units rather than atoms alone. Extends the standard atom-level message-passing paradigm.

entry.title: MedJudgeRAG: Option-Wise Evidence Judgment with Dynamic Knowledge Graphs for Medical MCQA

author.name: Seongwon Seo, Seung Hwan Cho, Young-Min Kim

entry.summary: MedJudgeRAG builds a dynamic knowledge graph from retrieved documents, issues a per-option evidence verdict for medical multiple-choice questions, and selects a knowledge-utilization strategy accordingly, trained by supervised fine-tuning on teacher-generated structured reasoning traces. Addresses the failure of vanilla RAG when retrieved documents are irrelevant or misleading.

entry.title: REPREC: Representation Driven Parameter-Efficient Recommendation System

author.name: Harshini Kavuru, Dwipam Katariya, Giri Iyengar, Pranab Mohanty, Kalanand Mishra, Kalanand Mishra

entry.summary: REPREC makes LLM-based sequential recommendation cheaper by aligning a single fixed-size user embedding from a frozen sequential encoder into the language model's space, avoiding LLM fine-tuning, extra modules, distillation, or long item-level history conditioning. Prioritizes deployment cost in industrial recommendation.

entry.title: MARS: Multi-Agent Re-ranking for Repeat-Order Food Delivery Recommendation

author.name: Jiahao Tian, Zhenkai Wang

entry.summary: A modular multi-agent reranking framework for repeat-order food delivery recommendation that predicts cuisine then ranks vendors, combining graph-based global preference signals, peer evidence and contextual filtering with pretrained LLM reasoning. Serves as a controlled test of how much strong backbones alone contribute inside a structured pipeline.

entry.title: DRIFT: Direct-Recursive Intervention-Conditioned Forecasting of ICU Physiological Trajectories

author.name: Weixin Liu, Juming Xiong, Congning Ni, Yanfan Zhu, Xingtao Lin, Bradley A. Malin, Zhijun Yin

entry.summary: DRIFT is a hybrid forecasting framework for ICU vital signs and labs that combines a direct multi-horizon predictor with a recursive treatment-conditioned corrector, so that planned interventions such as vasopressors actually influence the forecast. It is validated on two large public critical-care cohorts (MIMIC-IV and eICU-CRD) across 8-, 24- and 48-hour horizons.

entry.title: Sharpness-aware Model Merging with Salience Recovery for LLM-based Cross-Domain Sequential Recommendation

author.name: Huwei Ji, Jiajie Su, Yuyuan Li, Xiaohua Feng, Chaochao Chen

entry.summary: SharpRec merges domain-specific LLM adapters for cross-domain sequential recommendation using sharpness-aware objectives plus recovery of salient parameters, diagnosing knowledge conflict and multi-domain saturation as parameter misalignment and statistical homogenization. It targets scalable multi-domain recommendation without overlapping users.

entry.title: A Cross-lingual Comparison of Human and Classification Model Entrainment Behavior in Code-switched Speech Settings

author.name: Debasmita Bhattacharya, Siying Ding, Alayna Nguyen, Julia Hirschberg

entry.summary: This cross-lingual study examines conversational entrainment in Mandarin-, Hindi- and Spanish-English code-switched speech, finding lexical entrainment generalizes while acoustic-prosodic and code-switching style entrainment vary by language pair. It then shows classifiers detect entrainment but rely on features different from those most salient in human behavior.

entry.title: Interpretable Column Annotation with LLM-Symbolized Decision Process Materialization

author.name: Mengqi Wang (UNSW Sydney), Jianwei Wang (UNSW Sydney), Qing Liu (Data61, CSIRO), Xiwei Xu (Data61, CSIRO), Zhenchang Xing (Data61, CSIRO), Michael Bain (UNSW Sydney), Liming Zhu (Data61, CSIRO), Wenjie Zhang (UNSW Sydney)

entry.summary: SymCA makes table column type and property annotation interpretable by having an LLM materialize a global-to-local symbolic decision process over a label-space skeleton rather than mapping learned embeddings straight to categories. The goal is both better accuracy through label semantics and auditable decisions.

entry.title: Instruction-Tuned Models Locally Reuse Human Syntax More Than Humans Do

author.name: Zandi Eberstadt

entry.summary: By substituting model generations for one speaker's turns in existing human dialogues, this study measures turn-adjacent reuse of grammar rules across sixteen open-weight Llama and Gemma models from 1B to 70B at nearly two thousand matched positions. Instruction-tuned models are found to locally mirror human syntax more strongly than humans mirror each other.

entry.title: Decentralized Scalable Exploration via Emergent Adaptive L\'evy Walks on Minimal-Sensing Platforms

author.name: Wai Lun Leong, Teo Swee Huat Rodney

entry.summary: Proposes a lightweight sensor-driven Levy walk controller for sub-50-gram nano-drones with sparse range sensing, where each robot samples its own Levy exponent to diversify search without any inter-robot communication. The approach yields decentralized, scalable exploration on extremely constrained hardware.

entry.title: DynaBridge: Dynamic Summary-Guided Cross-Task Multimodal Fusion for DASS-Structured Mental Health Assessment

author.name: Shiyu Teng, Haichen Yu, Jiaqing Liu, Hao Sun, Yu Song, Shurong Chai, Ruibo Hou, Lanfen Lin, Yen-Wei Chen

entry.summary: DynaBridge fuses acoustic, visual and text cues with frozen-LLM-generated summaries to predict DASS-21 item-level ordinal distributions rather than only coarse depression, anxiety and stress labels. The design respects the psychometric item-to-subscale structure of the questionnaire instead of treating labels as flat targets.

entry.title: Semantic Space Search Trajectory Networks

author.name: Julian Agudelo, Alberto Tonda, Gabriela Ochoa, Vincent Guigue, Cristina Manfredotti, Evelyne Lutton

entry.summary: This work extends Search Trajectory Networks, a graph tool for visualizing optimizer behavior, from raw parameter space to semantic space defined by a model's predictions on a fixed sample set. Because any predictor reduces to a semantic vector, learning dynamics of otherwise incomparable algorithm families become directly comparable.

entry.title: When Does Deep Representation Learning Help Single-Cell Clustering? A Sensitivity-Aware Diagnostic Benchmark for Biomedical AI Pipelines

author.name: Nguyen Thanh Phong, Truong Viet Vu, Nguyen Ha Thu, Tran An Ky, Tran Hoang Thong, Le Pham Thuy Hien, Nguyen Thai Anh

entry.summary: A diagnostic benchmark of nine single-cell clustering pipelines across ten real datasets asks when an extra deep representation learning stage actually beats classical PCA pipelines. The framing is a practical engineering decision about whether the compute and tuning cost is justified.

entry.title: Mind the Missing Split: Resolving Feature Heterogeneity in Swarm Learning with Random Forests

author.name: Mohammad Tajabadi, Dominik Heider

entry.summary: In decentralized swarm learning, sites often have only partially overlapping feature sets, which makes pooled random forest inference ill-defined when a tree traversal hits a split on a locally missing feature. This paper diagnoses that failure mode and proposes resolutions for feature-heterogeneous collaborative tree ensembles.

entry.title: Optimization with Dynamic Constraint Learning (DCL)

author.name: Ezgi Oztekin, Figen Oztoprak, S. Ilker Birbil

entry.summary: Dynamic Constraint Learning handles constrained optimization when constraint functions are unknown and cannot be queried during solving, by fitting local surrogates from nearby data at each iteration and solving subproblems inside a data-supported trust region. It matches global constraint-learning quality with simpler models and smaller subproblems.

entry.title: A Generalized Tangent Approximation based Variational Inference Framework for Strongly Super-Gaussian Likelihoods

author.name: Somjit Roy, Pritam Dey, Debdeep Pati, Bani K. Mallick

entry.summary: The paper generalizes tangent-transformation variational inference beyond logistic regression to the broad class of strongly super-Gaussian likelihoods, giving structured, geometry-exploiting variational updates instead of black-box stochastic optimization. It targets scalable Bayesian computation with theoretical guarantees.

entry.title: Language as a Material Interface for Creative LLM Interaction

author.name: Jon McCormack, Tace McNamara, Chen Wang, Maria Teresa Llano

entry.summary: An HCI study exploring how creative practitioners engage with an LLM when language is treated as a malleable material rather than a directive prompt, using a tangible device called the Memetic Mixer over a two-week ecological deployment with four practitioners. It identifies distinct modes of associative, symbolic and temporally extended language use that current chat interfaces do not support.

entry.title: Diff-ID: Identity Consistent Facial Image Generation and Morphing via Diffusion Models

author.name: Taimoor Rizwan, Sara Atito, Muhammad Awais, Zhenhua Feng, Josef Kittler

entry.summary: Diff-ID is a diffusion framework for identity-consistent face generation and morphing, combining ArcFace identity and CLIP appearance embeddings through dual cross-attention and trained on a purpose-built 210K synthetic caption-augmented face dataset. It targets biometric and security-relevant applications where identity drift is unacceptable.

entry.title: MEDit-Bench: A Dataset for Evaluating Message-Driven Narrative Video Editing

author.name: Katsuya Ogata, Zongshang Pang, Mayu Otani, Yuta Nakashima

entry.summary: MEDit-Bench pairs long-form videos with multiple editing messages and multiple professionally produced edits per message, showing that editorial intent substantially changes which shots are selected from identical footage. It proposes temporal alignment metrics and shows existing summarization-style saliency assumptions fail to capture this diversity.

entry.title: Hyperspectral Intrinsic Decomposition: Joint Recovery of Reflectance and Photometric Components for Non-Lambertian Scenes

author.name: Hao Ye, Zhan Shi, Chenglong Huang, Tao Lv, Mingjie Ji, Qiu Shen, Xun Cao

entry.summary: Revisits the dichromatic reflection model to develop a unified hyperspectral intrinsic decomposition method that jointly recovers reflectance and photometric components for non-Lambertian scenes without auxiliary inputs. It moves beyond the Lambertian and simplified-specularity assumptions of prior work.

entry.title: Gaussian Volumetric Representation for Efficient Shear-Warp Visualization

author.name: Mayuri Mathur (Indraprastha Institute of Information Technology Delhi), Ojaswa Sharma (Indraprastha Institute of Information Technology Delhi)

entry.summary: Proposes a Gaussian-based volumetric representation for medical volume rendering, optimized with Monte Carlo volumetric estimation so training can use a sparse voxel subset while remaining consistent with the dense objective, plus curriculum-based slice sampling. It targets fast, faithful visualization of large medical volumes.

entry.title: HOME: Robust Hough-space Matching Method for Structured and Textureless Videos

author.name: Masaki Satoh

entry.summary: HOME is a training-free feature matching front-end that maps images into Hough space so global linear structures become stable local extrema used for matching, targeting structured or textureless environments where point features like ORB fail. It is designed to be ultra-lightweight for real-time edge robotics.

entry.title: RDVSv2: A Large-scale Benchmark for RGB-D Video Salient Object Detection

author.name: Tianyu Li, Jiahao He, Keren Fu, Qijun Zhao

entry.summary: RDVSv2 is a large-scale RGB-D video salient object detection benchmark with 249 sequences and over 29,000 densely annotated frames, using stereoscopic online videos for geometry-consistent depth and eye-tracking-guided mask annotation. A strong baseline is also provided.

entry.title: ANFI: Rethinking Neighbor Feature Interaction in Person Re-ID

author.name: Xulin Li, Yan Lu, Bin Liu, Jiaze Li, Qinhong Yang, Tao Gong, Qi Chu, Nenghai Yu

entry.summary: ANFI improves person re-identification by modeling the negative effects of unreliable neighbors rather than assuming affinity-based neighbor selection is trustworthy, allowing samples to stay discriminative under noisy neighborhoods. It analyzes neighbor-based interaction under differing reliability regimes.

entry.title: Bi-Level Collaborative Learning for Few-Shot Scribble-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Xiang-Xiang Su, Yufan Ye, Yihang Zheng, Min Gan, Guang-Yong Chen

entry.summary: A bi-level framework for medical image segmentation under the combined constraints of sparse scribble annotations and very few annotated samples, where an upper-level learnable superpixel model supplies region-structural priors and pseudo-labels to a lower-level segmenter. It targets both region completeness and boundary precision.

entry.title: A Unified Benchmark and Modality-Adaptive Network for Day-and-Night Drone-View Geo-Localization

author.name: Songtianhao Xu, Zhongwei Chen, Zhao-Xu Yang, Weifeng Wang

entry.summary: Introduces IRCHN, a drone-view geo-localization benchmark with geographically aligned visible drone, infrared drone, and satellite imagery from the same locations, enabling unified evaluation across day and night rather than cross-dataset transfer. A modality-adaptive network baseline is provided.

entry.title: GeoMFD: Continual Drone-View Geo-Localization with Geometry-Aware Adapter and Margin-Field Distillation

author.name: Zhongwei Chen, Hai-jun Rong, Tao Zhang, Xianfeng Nie, Xiangbao Zhang, Guoqi Li, Zhao-Xu Yang

entry.summary: Formalizes continual drone-view geo-localization, where a single model must adapt to sequentially encountered environments without maintaining separate models or distorting previously learned cross-view embedding geometry. GeoMFD combines a geometry-aware adapter with margin-field distillation to limit forgetting.

entry.title: Freq-RemoteVAR: Next-Frequency Autoregressive Modeling for Remote Sensing Change Detection

author.name: Luqi Gong, Rui Xu, Yue Chen, Chao Li, Jingqi Hong, Xuefeng Zhao

entry.summary: Freq-RemoteVAR recasts bi-temporal remote sensing change detection as autoregressive generation in the frequency domain, predicting change masks progressively from coarse to fine frequency bands using a frequency-aware mask tokenization. This replaces the usual one-shot dense prediction paradigm.

entry.title: Beyond Static Costs: Learning-Dynamics Aware Loss Functions for Long-Tailed Classification

author.name: Varad Shinde, Nikhil Kumar Shrey, Magesh Rajasekaran, Md Saiful Islam Sajol, Harshil Bhargava, Subhajit Sidanta, Supratik Mukhopadhyay, Yimin Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes a Learning-Dynamics Aware Loss for long-tailed classification that reweights classes based on how effectively the network is actually learning each class over training, rather than on static class frequencies. It targets tail-class underperformance in domains like rare species and defect detection.

entry.title: SAFAARI: Schema-Aware Framework for Accelerated Advertiser Response Intelligence

author.name: Bhanu Teja Rangaraju, Chandan Kumar

entry.summary: A multi-agent framework for enterprise natural-language-to-SQL that separates content, metadata, and orchestration agents to attack the schema-linking bottleneck, plus a composite evaluation metric that penalizes inconsistent results. Targets advertiser support chatbots without predefined API endpoints.

entry.title: Joint Text-Audio Alignment for EEG-to-Text Decoding in Chinese Speech Production and Perception

author.name: Tian Zheng, Xurong Xie, Xinxin Zhu, Xiaolan Peng, Feng Tian

entry.summary: Proposes joint text-semantic and audio-acoustic supervision for decoding Chinese sentences from scalp EEG during speech production and perception, targeting the huge character output space and low signal-to-noise ratio. Aims at non-invasive communication for people with severe speech impairments.

entry.title: Domain-Prior-Regularized Graph Modeling for Anomaly Detection in Cyber-Physical Systems

author.name: Youngseok Hwang, Joonsung Kwon, Geonwoo Lee, Hyunwoo Park

entry.summary: DPR-GM improves graph-based anomaly detection on industrial sensor time series by using a language model to extract directed physical couplings from system design documentation, regularizing the learned graph toward domain priors. Aimed at small cyber-physical systems where data scarcity makes learned topologies unstable.

entry.title: Neural Network Learning of One-Bit Protocols for Qubit Measurement Simulation

author.name: Josep Escrig, Mani Zartab, Giulio Gasbarri, Estel Ferrer, Ramon Mu\~noz-Tapia, Gael Sent\'is

entry.summary: Uses neural network optimization to search for one-bit classical protocols that approximate qubit prepare-and-measure statistics, showing that although two bits are needed in general, single-bit strategies achieve high average fidelity for structured measurement families such as symmetric uniformly weighted sets. Machine learning is used as a discovery tool in quantum communication complexity.

entry.title: Three Sides of Retrieval: Factorial Evidence for Document-Side, Query-Side, and Answer-Side Complementarity in RAG

author.name: Ng S. T. Chong

entry.summary: Introduces table-of-contents guided page retrieval that infers document headings from visual formatting without extra model calls, embeds them as a parallel index, and returns whole page sections, then tests document-side, query-side, and answer-side interventions factorially over 1,280 conditions on enterprise documents. Reports significant answer-quality gains and complementarity across the three intervention sides.

entry.title: DDSNet: Dual-domain Symmetry-aware Network for PCSEL Property Prediction

author.name: Cen Chen, Haitao Huang, Jiazhi Mao, Feifan Xu, Zhe Zhuang, Yuxiang Ren

entry.summary: DDSNet is a neural surrogate for photonic crystal surface-emitting laser property prediction that explicitly incorporates spectral components and structural asymmetry of unit-cell dielectric patterns, features that coupled-wave theory identifies as governing device physics. Enables faster design-space screening than direct physical computation.

entry.title: DisasterTD: Disaster Toponym Disambiguation Using Multimodal LLMs and Cross-View Geolocalization

author.name: Wenping Yin, Ziqi Liu, Naixia Mou, Weijia Li, Danfeng Hong, Hao Li

entry.summary: DisasterTD disambiguates vague place names in disaster-related social media imagery by combining multimodal LLM extraction of candidate toponyms with cross-view matching between ground photos, remote sensing imagery, and other geospatial sources. Supports faster situational awareness in emergency response.

entry.title: From Dyad to Triad: Eliciting XAI Requirements in Stroke Rehabilitation

author.name: Param Rajpura, Yogesh Kumar Meena

entry.summary: Develops a video-based scaffolding protocol for eliciting explainable-AI requirements from stroke survivors, including participants with moderate-to-severe aphasia, and their caregivers who lack prior frameworks for reasoning about transparency. Pilots four scaffolding approaches with three survivors and three caregivers.

entry.title: SpectONet: A Physics-Guided Spectral Deep Operator Network for Euler-Bernoulli Beam Dynamics

author.name: Shivani Saini, Ramesh Kumar Vats, Arup Kumar Sahoo

entry.summary: SpectONet augments DeepONet with physics-informed constraints and Chebyshev-Gauss-Lobatto spectral sensor placement to solve Euler-Bernoulli beam vibration problems. Concentrating sensors near boundaries improves representation of boundary-sensitive structural responses with few branch inputs.

entry.title: Improving Rare Medication Recommendation with Counterfactual Data Augmentation and Large Language Models

author.name: Shinhwan Kang, Soo Yong Lee, Jaewon Kim, Kijung Shin, Buru Chang

entry.summary: GenRxR uses large language models to generate counterfactual patient records and to reason about co-prescribed drugs, specifically to improve recommendation of rarely prescribed medications where existing systems underperform. It addresses both data scarcity and neglect of co-recommendation structure.

entry.title: SpeechLLM Meets Federated Learning for End-to-End ASR: English and Italian Case Studies

author.name: Mohamed Nabih Ali, Daniele Falavigna, Alessio Brutti

entry.summary: This paper presents the first systematic study of federated training for speech-LLM based end-to-end ASR, designing a communication-efficient optimization strategy for high-dimensional speech-LLM parameters and evaluating on English and Italian. It shows stable federated fine-tuning is feasible for privacy-sensitive speech data.

entry.title: Right-sizing Recommendations (RSR): Cloud Workload Conformal Prediction for Virtual Machines in Data Center Operations

author.name: Mehryar Majd, Feng Cheng, Ali Pahlevan

entry.summary: Applies conformal prediction to forecast virtual machine resource utilization intervals so cloud operators can right-size instances under uncertain and fluctuating demand. Frames VM sizing as an interval-prediction problem with calibrated coverage guarantees.

entry.title: AI Deployment and Cyber Governance Failures in Public-Sector Organizations: A Typological Analysis

author.name: Md Salahuddin, James Rooney, Fida Hasan

entry.summary: Proposes a seven-domain typology of ten mechanisms by which AI adoption produces cybersecurity governance failure in government organizations, and tests whether existing governance instruments address those AI-specific causes. Argues prior literature treats AI risk, public-sector governance, and framework adequacy as separate streams.

entry.title: Engine-Equal, Human-Unequal: A Reproducible Outcome Skew in Engine-Assessed Equal Chess Positions

author.name: Jesung Park

entry.summary: Using millions of online human games, the study shows that chess openings a strong engine rates as dead equal still produce reproducible, direction-stable win-rate skews for humans, replicating across player sets, time periods, rating bands, and an out-of-sample month. It documents a systematic gap between engine-optimal evaluation and human playability.

entry.title: Cognivia: A Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Copilot for Evidence-Based Mental Healthcare

author.name: Qi Chen, Siria Xiyueyao Luo, Jian Wang, Yuan Shi, Haocong Rao, Xuejiao Zhao

entry.summary: Cognivia is a CBT copilot that identifies cognitive distortions and generates rational responses grounded in authoritative therapy protocols, with annotation schemes designed to reduce sycophantic replies. Aimed at scaling evidence-based mental health support given therapist shortages.

entry.title: Runtime Uncertainty Monitoring for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems Using Bayesian Networks

author.name: Bart Custers, Koorosh Aslansefat

entry.summary: Proposes runtime uncertainty monitoring for LLM multi-agent workflows in actuarial risk modelling, propagating token-level log-probabilities through a Bayesian network that captures inter-agent dependencies. Targets a regulated, high-stakes decision-support setting where silent errors carry compliance risk.

entry.title: Verification Without Distrust: Reframing User-Side Oversight as Routine Epistemic Governance in Everyday Human-Chatbot Interaction

author.name: Aung Pyae

entry.summary: A mixed-methods survey of 153 frequent chatbot users finds no detectable relationship between trust and output verification, challenging the standard assumption that better-calibrated trust reduces checking behavior, and distinguishes evaluative from interventionist oversight. Reframes user-side verification as routine epistemic governance instead of distrust.

entry.title: Authoring Agent Skills: A Software-Engineering Approach

author.name: Giuseppe Destefanis

entry.summary: A short conceptual note arguing that agent skills, the reusable on-demand procedural bundles specified in Anthropic's open Agent Skills format and used by Claude Code, should be engineered like software artifacts with single responsibility, interface separation, low coupling and token budget discipline. It substitutes behavioral evaluation for deterministic testing.

entry.title: Balanced Soft mixture-of-expert model for Glaucoma Detection

author.name: Sai Venkatesh Chilukoti, Krishna Rauniyar, Min Shi, Xiali Hei

entry.summary: Applies a balanced soft mixture-of-experts architecture to multi-modal glaucoma detection, combining imaging modalities to learn richer representations for earlier diagnosis. Emphasizes expert-balancing to avoid collapse in the routing.

entry.title: A Machine-Learning-Based Gas Lift Optimization Workflow for Unconventional Fields

author.name: Sha (Sasha), Miao, Alexandra Vendetti, Logan Smart, Gunta Chomchalerm, Yang Chen, Christopher Frazier, Dustin Haralson, Jeremy Sorenson, Xiao Ma, Huafei Sun, Aaron Shinn, Haining Zheng, Xiao-Hui Wu, Peng Xu

entry.summary: An automated machine learning workflow forecasts gas lift performance curves from historical production time series without downhole gauges or multi-rate well tests, then uses Bayesian optimization to set injection rates under facility capacity constraints. A pilot on 30 wells achieved over five percent average production uplift and the system was scaled to more than 200 wells.

entry.title: Depression Markers in Speech: An Approach based on Tract Variables Dynamics

author.name: Sahar Altalhi, Tanaya Guha, Alessandro Vinciarelli

entry.summary: This study extracts depression biomarkers from the nonlinear dynamics of vocal tract variables, characterizing predictability, complexity and randomness through Lyapunov exponents, correlation dimension and sample entropy. Experiments use a public corpus of 64 clinically diagnosed depressed and 54 control speakers.

entry.title: Neurai-VN Benchmark: Standardized Machine Learning Models for Multimodal Digital Phenotyping in Mental Health Classification

author.name: Quoc-Cuong Pham, Hoang-Thuy-Duong Vu, Thi-Thanh-Huong Ha, Huy-Hieu Pham

entry.summary: The Neurai-VN benchmark standardizes preprocessing and evaluation for multimodal digital phenotyping from smartphones and wearables, based on two weeks of data from 100 Vietnamese adults. It defines four clinically relevant binary classification tasks with subject-wise cross-validation and baseline linear, tree and neural models.

entry.title: AMRD: Adaptive Multi-Teacher Relational Distillation for Lightweight Speech Emotion Recognition

author.name: Yuqi Li, Yi-Cheng Lin, Xianglong Wang, Kuo Yang, Xiaoqin Feng, Yixuan Wang, Huiran Duan, Yingli Tian

entry.summary: AMRD compresses large self-supervised speech models into lightweight on-device emotion recognizers using multiple teachers, weighting teachers per batch via a one-class SVM on their logit similarity structure and adding a relational distillation loss over sample similarity matrices. It targets edge deployment where full models are too costly.

entry.title: OrthKD: Extracting Generalized Clinical Knowledge from Heterogeneous Teachers for Lightweight Deployment

author.name: Yi Xu, Cheng Chen, Mufan Cao

entry.summary: OrthKD compresses diabetic retinopathy screening models by transferring full supervision only from the reliable CNN teacher, using feature-only distillation from a weaker Transformer teacher, and enforcing orthogonality so the weak teacher's misleading logits do not corrupt the student. It targets accurate, edge-efficient screening under domain shift.

entry.title: Prototype Adaptation for Zero-Shot sEMG Movement Classification

author.name: Rui Liu, Benjamin Paassen

entry.summary: Two prototype-network methods, Compositional Prototype Interpolation and Synthetic Adaptation for Prototypes, enable zero-shot recognition of combined and unseen hand movements from surface EMG after training only on basic movements. This avoids collecting and retraining on data for every possible movement combination in prosthesis control.

entry.title: MOSAIC-FL, a micro-service based privacy-preserving framework with application to genomics

author.name: Paul Largillier, Karl Paygambar, C\'edric Gouy-Pailler, Vincent Meyer, Mallek Mziou, Oana Stan

entry.summary: MOSAIC-FL is a microservice-based federated learning framework combining gRPC communication, a finite-state-machine orchestration layer for synchronization and threat detection, and threshold homomorphic encryption for blind secure aggregation. It is demonstrated on privacy-sensitive genomics workloads.

entry.title: WALoMA: A Multitask Wireless Foundation Model via Adaptive Low-Rank Masked Autoencoders

author.name: Madi Makin, Asmaa Abdallah, Abdulkadir Celik, Ahmed M. Eltawil

entry.summary: WALoMA is a masked-autoencoder foundation model for 6G physical-layer tasks that treats channel state information as a universal modality and uses adaptive low-rank components to learn transferable representations from unlabeled channel data. It targets multi-task reuse where labeled wireless datasets are scarce.

entry.title: Variance-Reduced Conditional Gradient Methods under Markovian Sampling for Nonconvex Composite Optimization

author.name: Zhaojun Peng

entry.summary: The paper develops a projection-free momentum conditional-gradient method with coupled multilevel Monte Carlo variance reduction for nonconvex composite optimization when gradient samples arrive along a single Markov chain trajectory. It provides Frank-Wolfe gap convergence guarantees with explicit mixing-time dependence.

entry.title: Multi-Objective Structured Pruning of LLMs for Latency and Model Size Optimization

author.name: Muhammad Junaid Ali, Smail Niar, El-Ghazali Talbi

entry.summary: This paper applies multi-objective search to structured pruning of LLMs, jointly selecting layers, attention heads and MLP widths to trade off latency against model size for embedded and edge deployment. It argues exhaustive exploration of the joint design space is infeasible and prone to unstable configurations.

entry.title: Fourier Feature Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Elasto-Plastic Analysis of Geomaterials with a Non-Associative Mohr-Coulomb Model

author.name: Apisit Robjanghvad, Sompote Youwai

entry.summary: Applies Fourier feature encodings to physics-informed neural networks to overcome spectral bias when solving non-associative Mohr-Coulomb elasto-plastic problems, where sharp stress gradients at elastic-plastic boundaries defeat standard PINNs. The aim is a mesh-free alternative to costly incremental finite element analysis.

entry.title: Steeringless Drifting: Differential-Torque Control of a Four-Wheel Independently Driven Vehicle

author.name: Sheng Zhao, Zexin Wu, Dongyang Zhou, Bolin Zhao, Xiaodong Wu

entry.summary: Develops drift control for a four-wheel independently driven vehicle without mechanical steering, generating yaw moment purely through differential wheel torques, with a double-track model, drift equilibrium computation, and a closed-loop controller validated in simulation and on a 1:10-scale car. It explores handling-limit control for emerging chassis architectures.

entry.title: Tripody: An Overconstrained 3-SPR-like Parallel Robot for High-Reach Construction Tasks

author.name: Julien Kindle, Jakub Raczy, Riccardo Balbi, Andrea Alessandretti, Cesar Cadena, Marco Hutter

entry.summary: A multi-agent deep RL framework for cooperative UAV navigation that stacks several mechanisms: novelty and memory driven escape from local optima, tiered behavior cloning from a demonstration buffer, curriculum-based safety scheduling, and structure-aware generalization across scenarios. It targets sparse rewards and uneven learning among agents.

entry.title: TRWH: A Text-Driven Random Walk Heterogeneous GNN for Semantic-Aware Sparse Recommendation

author.name: He Ma, Chen Liu

entry.summary: Combines LLM-generated textual user and item profiles with heterogeneous graph neural networks and random-walk augmentation to improve recommendation quality in sparse interaction settings. Fuses classical embedding methods with language-model profiling before graph propagation.

entry.title: Matrix-Free Photoacoustic Image Reconstruction via Sensor-Token Self-Attention

author.name: Mary John, Shibili Said, Imad Barhumi, Sherzod Turaev, Mohamed Yahia

entry.summary: Presents a transformer that treats each ultrasound sensor time series as a token and reconstructs photoacoustic images directly from raw measurements, avoiding the system matrix at inference for faster reconstruction. Aimed at real-time clinical imaging under sparse-view sampling.

entry.title: Untrusted Authors, Trusted Answers: A Calculus of Fidelity-Graded Translations

author.name: Christoph Kirsch

entry.summary: Develops a compositional calculus for reasoning about programs via chains of translations between languages, where each hop carries a checkable contract covering assurance class, direction of approximation, preserved observables, and cost, and route trust is the meet of hop contracts. Argues witness-carrying answers can be trusted even from untrusted translators.

entry.title: VLD-RAG: Agentic Vision-Language Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Long, Visually-Rich Multi-Page Documents

author.name: Seonok Kim

entry.summary: VLD-RAG is an agentic multimodal retrieval-augmented generation framework for long, visually rich documents, building a page-preserving index with parsed text, page metadata, and dense visual embeddings, then combining sparse and dense retrieval for cross-page reasoning. Targets questions whose evidence spans tables, charts, and figures on multiple pages.

entry.title: Selective Impairment of Motor Recovery from Typing Errors in Parkinson's Disease: A Survival Analysis

author.name: Navin Bondade

entry.summary: Uses backspace events in a public keystroke dataset as natural error-correction episodes and finds that Parkinson's severity is unrelated to pre-error typing instability but strongly related to how long it takes to restore normal typing rhythm afterward, modeled as a survival outcome. Suggests passive typing data can dissociate error monitoring from motor restart.

entry.title: Image Quality Dependent Degradation for AI Systems

author.name: Yannick Kees, Elena Hoemann, Frank K\"oster, Sven Hallerbach

entry.summary: The paper studies how perception network performance degrades as input image quality falls, distinguishing error types by safety criticality such as missed pedestrians versus false detections. It aims to support trustworthiness assessment for automated driving perception stacks.

entry.title: Knowledge-Guided Multimodal Reasoning over Interacting Streams for Video-Level Ambivalence and Hesitancy Recognition

author.name: Podakanti Satyajith Chary, Barath Parthiban, Pranesh Velmurugan, Adeeba Khan, Nagarajan Ganapathy

entry.summary: PRISM-AH models ambivalence and hesitancy in video as cross-modal conflict unfolding over time, aligning frozen vision, audio and text encoders into short windows and scoring dissonance plus next-window prediction surprise. The targeted affective states matter for predicting health behavior change abandonment.

entry.title: Contextual Deconvolution for Variance-Stable Demand Sensing: Kernel-Modulated Operators in Promotional Retail

author.name: Mohammad Forouhesh

entry.summary: Contextual Deconvolution treats retail demand sensing as convex decomposition, using a kernel-modulated banded operator to separate transient promotion shocks from a smooth baseline, with hierarchical pooling for catalog-scale deployment. The operator reduces to the identity when promotional response is impulsive, so gains appear only where genuine multi-day carryover exists.

entry.title: SourceMinds at CheckThat! 2026: NLI-Grounded Citation Auditing in a Multi-Agent Pipeline for Full Fact-Checking Article Generation

author.name: Farhan Sharukh Hasan, Anirban Saha Anik, Eric Liu, Xiaoying Song, Mohotarema Rashid, Lingzi Hong

entry.summary: A shared-task system for generating full fact-checking articles, combining dense retrieval, structured planning, gated self-critique, and a natural-language-inference-based citation auditor that repairs missing citations and strips unsupported ones. It illustrates how entailment checking can be used as an automated grounding control in multi-agent generation pipelines.

entry.title: Sense it with your eyes: Sensation Generation and Understanding for Advertisements

author.name: Aysan Aghazadeh, Sina Malakouti, Adriana Kovashka

entry.summary: Introduces the first study of sensory advertising for AI, with a Sensory Ad dataset, a sensation classification benchmark for LLMs and multimodal models, an automated metric aligned with human judgments, and a generation task for images that evoke specific senses. It probes whether models understand how visuals evoke touch, taste, or smell.

entry.title: Leak-Free Cross-Validated Stacking with Per-Architecture Calibration for Sand-Boil Segmentation in Earthen Levees

author.name: Padam Jung Thapa, Anav Katwal, Ayon Dey, Abdullah Bin Naeem, Steve Sloan, Kendall Niles, Md Tamjidul Hoque

entry.summary: Presents a levee sand-boil segmentation framework that closes two leakage loopholes common in scarce-data medical-style pipelines: tuning ensemble weights on test images, and training on synthetic images derived from held-out photographs. Every synthetic image is traced to its real parent so leakage can be filtered per fold.

entry.title: Towards Faithful Sentimental Image Captioning via Evidence-Aware Multi-Agent Reasoning

author.name: Tiecheng Cai, Zexian Yang, Chao Chen, Shanshan Lin, Xiangwen Liao

entry.summary: SEA-Cap generates sentiment-laden image captions grounded in verifiable object-level affective evidence, orchestrating a generator, hallucination checker, and arbitrator in an iterative multi-agent loop. It targets the trade-off between emotional expressiveness and visual faithfulness.

entry.title: FLASH: Efficient Impact Fall Detection with Unified Hypergraph State-Space Model

author.name: Tresor Y. Koffi, Youssef Mourchid, Yohan Dupuis

entry.summary: FLASH detects fall impact moments by combining single-matrix hypergraph representations of multi-joint coordination with Mamba selective state-space temporal modeling and adaptive feedback, avoiding the quadratic cost of transformer temporal models. It argues pairwise joint graphs miss the coordinated multi-joint patterns characteristic of impacts.

entry.title: Motion-Acceleration Calibration and Compensation in IMUs without External Equipment for Attitude Estimation Filters

author.name: Fabian Arzberger, Andreas N\"uchter

entry.summary: Presents an IMU calibration and compensation method that uses gyroscope data to estimate and remove motion-induced accelerations without external calibration equipment, improving attitude estimation filters such as Madgwick and Mahony. It reduces long-term drift around the gravity vector for sensors mounted far from the platform base.

entry.title: LaughBench

author.name: Taylor G. Lunt

entry.summary: Introduces an informal benchmark testing whether models can produce novel jokes that actually make a human laugh, with results showing current frontier models only occasionally elicit a smile and never laughter. The author argues laughter-generating humor is a strong general intelligence signal because it requires modeling another mind's assumptions and violating them precisely.

entry.title: On the Use of LLMs for Specialised Terminology: A Good Alternative to Corpora?

author.name: Joachim Minder (ALTAE), Guillaume Wisniewski (LLF - UMR7110), Natalie K\"ubler (ALTAE)

entry.summary: Evaluates whether four proprietary LLMs can substitute for specialized corpora when translators seek English-to-French technical term equivalents in earth science and NLP domains, comparing two prompting strategies over eighty terms per domain. Focuses on the practical workflow of specialized translation.

entry.title: Balancing multiscale similarity and cartographic constraints: A similarity-driven optimization framework for line generalization

author.name: Pengbo Li, Haowen Yan, Xiaomin Lu, Binbin Lin

entry.summary: Frames automated cartographic generalization as a constrained multiscale similarity optimization problem, unifying similarity evaluation, cartographic constraints, and parameter tuning that are normally handled as separate stages. Uses spatial similarity between original and generalized representations as the optimization objective for adaptive, interpretable control across map scales.

entry.title: Re-thinking Mammography Transfer Learning: The Dataset-Informed Transfer Learning (DITL) Framework for Breast Cancer Screening and Lesion Diagnosis

author.name: Adarsh Bhandary Panambur, Siming Bayer, Andreas Maier

entry.summary: DITL is a transfer-learning framework for mammography that weights samples by dataset-derived difficulty signals and adds neighborhood-based triplet supervision, targeting both small curated sets and population-scale screening cohorts. It aims to make transfer learning sensitive to dataset-specific characteristics rather than applying generic fine-tuning.

entry.title: FunnelAL: Retrieve-then-Rank Active Learning for Single-Class Discovery

author.name: Reihaneh Rostami (RAIC Labs), Brian Goodwin (RAIC Labs)

entry.summary: FunnelAL adapts the cascaded retrieve-then-rank funnel architecture from industrial recommenders to active learning for single-class discovery, starting from one positive and one negative example. It separates efficient candidate retrieval from fine-grained discrimination of visually confusable negatives.

entry.title: Evaluation of Adversarial Robustness in Arabic Language Models

author.name: Anwar Alajmi, Ayed Salman, Imtiaz Ahmad

entry.summary: The study probes five Arabic language models with adversarial perturbations at multiple granularities and finds that adding diacritics is particularly effective at degrading accuracy, then tests adversarial training as a defense. It quantifies robustness gaps specific to Arabic morphology and orthography.

entry.title: Beyond Memory: A Templated Substrate for Heterogeneous Collaborative Knowledge Work with LLM Agents

author.name: Priscila Saboia Moreira, Christopher R. Sweet

entry.summary: Proposes a reusable template that places an LLM-maintained interlinked wiki between raw project artifacts and coding agents, so that dead ends, walked-back claims, and decisions persist across sessions. Aimed at making collaborative knowledge work compound rather than restart with each new agent session.

entry.title: HOBA: Hierarchical On-Policy Bidding Agents for Adaptive Online Advertising

author.name: Ji Wu, Yunshan Peng, Wentao Bai, Yunke Bai, Wenzheng Shu, Jinan Pang, Yanxiang Zeng, Xialong Liu

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.24779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Online advertising bidding systems typically deploy multiple offline-trained expert models (e.g., PID controllers, model predictive control, offline RL...

entry.title: How Often Should a Recommender Call an LLM? Value-Weighted Routing, Monitoring, and Seasonal Robustness

author.name: Bhavtosh Rath

entry.summary: Studies how often a recommender should escalate from a cheap heuristic to an expensive LLM, arguing that routing should weigh business value of errors and not just estimated difficulty. Evaluates a value-weighted threshold router against difficulty-only and random baselines in a fully synthetic retail simulation, with monitoring and seasonal robustness stages.

entry.title: How Small Can You Go? A Controlled Study of LoRA Rank, Target Modules, and Quantization Trade-offs for Text-to-SQL on a 60M-Parameter Model

author.name: Mahendra Singh Rathor, Anagheem Azzam

entry.summary: A controlled single-variable study of LoRA rank, adapted module choice, and numeric precision on a 60M-parameter T5-small doing single-table text-to-SQL, reporting accuracy alongside memory and latency costs. Provides a fully reproducible cost curve for extreme low-budget adaptation.

entry.title: Multi-Sensor Alignment for Weather Simulations

author.name: Samsad Alam, Devyani Lambhate, Aditya Mohan, Vishal Kumar, Vaibhav Katewa

entry.summary: Proposes two alignment methods so that simulated adverse weather (fog intensity, rain and snow particle placement) matches real conditions consistently across different autonomous-vehicle sensors, validated with statistical and geometric tests. Shows misaligned simulations distort 3D detection evaluation.

entry.title: AIriskEval-edu Demo: Auditing of Pedagogical Risks in Educational Explanations

author.name: Javier Irigoyen, Roberto Daza, Francisco Jurado, Julian Fierrez, Ruben Tolosana, Alvaro Ortigosa, Miguel Lopez-Duran, Aythami Morales

entry.summary: A demo platform that audits instructional explanations across five pedagogical risk dimensions with binary verdicts, confidence scores, rationales, and evidence spans, combining an external frontier model API with a locally fine-tuned small evaluator. Note that the frontier model used, GPT-5.5, has been generally available since April 2026, so this is application of an existing model.

entry.title: Nudging Sustainable Choices through LLM-Generated Recommendation Explanations

author.name: Haya Halimeh, Dietmar Jannach, Oliver M\"uller

entry.summary: Tests whether generatively produced, nudge-theory-framed sustainability explanations in recommender interfaces shift user choices, validated by human evaluation and model-based audits and then measured in randomized experiments. Explores explanations as behavioral interventions rather than just transparency devices.

entry.title: Toward Standardized Cross-Vendor Agent Tool Trust Management in Autonomous Networks

author.name: Ravi Kant Sharma, Ashutosh Uttam, Ajay Kumar

entry.summary: Proposes a telecom network management information model for agent tool trust, with a trust state machine, damped cascade propagation, cross-vendor trust notifications over existing management interfaces, and retroactive impact assessment. Motivated by highly autonomous networks where agents from one vendor keep invoking a compromised tool from another.

entry.title: DocAnnot -- Accelerating the Creation of Key Information Extraction Datasets with GenAI-Powered Auto-annotation

author.name: Siddartha Reddy, Harikrishnan P M, Goutham Vignesh, Varun V, Vishal Vaddina

entry.summary: DocAnnot auto-annotates key information extraction datasets by combining a vision-language model for value extraction, OCR for text boxes, and a spatially informed contextual matching algorithm to associate labels with values, reporting F1 around 0.68 and 0.85 on two receipt benchmarks. Reduces manual document-annotation effort.

entry.title: Game AI Not Fun? A Scoping Review and Meta-Analysis on the Differences in Enjoyment between Human and Computer Opponents

author.name: Ray Ito

entry.summary: A scoping review of 20 studies and three-level meta-analysis of nine finds a statistically significant medium-to-large reduction in player enjoyment when opponents are believed to be computer-controlled rather than human. Suggests perceived artificiality itself, not just skill level, shapes the player experience.

entry.title: Patterns of Learner-AI Interaction and Academic Performance in an Object-Oriented Programming Course

author.name: Marina Lepp

entry.summary: Surveys 210 first-year undergraduates on their self-directed use of generative AI in an object-oriented programming course and relates usage patterns to grades, perceived difficulty, understanding, and trust. Contributes empirical evidence to the contested question of whether AI assistance helps or hinders programming learning.

entry.title: AI-Assisted Knowledge Access for Legacy Enterprise Asset Management in Energy Operations: A Practical Retrieval System

author.name: Dave Mercier, Mishca de Costa, Muhammad Anwar, Mark Randall, Issam Hammad

entry.summary: Describes a deployed retrieval assistant that improves knowledge access over legacy enterprise asset management systems across vendor documentation, database schema questions, and interface how-to queries, combining intent understanding, query rewriting, hybrid retrieval, and deterministic hallucination checks. Presents an improvement layer rather than platform replacement.

entry.title: Decoding Error-Related Potentials under Multisensory Feedback with Varying Congruency

author.name: Yixin Liu, Kang Yin, Hye-Bin Shin, Seong-Whan Lee

entry.summary: Studies decoding of error-related brain potentials when feedback arrives through visual, auditory, and tactile channels with controlled congruency, using a multi-branch EEG network with auxiliary supervision to improve robustness where incongruent feedback degrades accuracy. Relevant to error-aware human-machine interfaces.

entry.title: Two Views, One Voice: Evidence-Grounded Conversational Music Recommendation

author.name: Sungwook Yoo, Sewook Yoo

entry.summary: Describes a third-place competition solution that decouples retrieval from response generation for conversational music recommendation, combining hybrid lexical-dense candidate pools, fine-tuned adapters on an 8B model, gradient-boosted calibration, and evidence-grounded response generation. Illustrates practical architecture choices for grounded conversational recommenders.

entry.title: Using Data-Derived Priors to Guide CNN Architecture Design for NIR Chemometrics

author.name: D\'ario Passos

entry.summary: Across 25 near-infrared spectroscopy regression tasks, this work computes dataset descriptors such as size, spectral spacing, entropy, intrinsic rank and wavelet structure, then relates them to near-optimal CNN hyperparameters found by Bayesian optimization. The goal is data-derived priors that replace generic architecture rules in chemometrics.

entry.title: Generator-Aligned Representation Interfaces for Diagnostic Soft Equivariance

author.name: Weitao Li, Gong Cheng

entry.summary: The paper proposes exposing transformation generators to a generic sequence backbone through aligned canonical and generator-induced views, achieving approximate (soft) equivariance without specialized equivariant operators. It formalizes a probe-specific soft-equivariance residual to separate representation consistency from task robustness and exact equivariance.

entry.title: Gradient-Based Latent Decomposition Reveals Mechanisms of Feature Degradation in Weakly Supervised Mammography

author.name: Vinceline Bertrand, Ionut Cardei

entry.summary: This study decomposes the latent space of hierarchical VAEs into a task-aligned component and an orthogonal residual to explain why coarse lesion features survive reconstruction while fine malignancy cues degrade in weakly supervised mammography. Only a small fraction of latent magnitude is found to align with the supervised direction.

entry.title: Deep Label-Wise Attentive Temporal Convolutional Networks Improve Medical Coding

author.name: Muhammed Yavuz Nuzumlal{\i}, Alexander Fabbri, Irene Li, Dragomir Radev

entry.summary: The paper models automated medical coding as extreme multi-label classification using a multi-layer temporal convolutional encoder followed by label-wise attention, so each code attends to the relevant parts of long clinical notes. It reports improvements over prior neural coding baselines.

entry.title: SciClaimSeekers at CheckThat! 2026: Retrieving Scientific Sources for Social Media Claims with LLM Reranking

author.name: Mohotarema Rashid, Nansu Baniya, Anirban Saha Anik, Xiaoying Song, Lingzi Hong

entry.summary: A retrieval system for linking social media scientific claims to their original scholarly sources, fusing BM25 with multilingual E5 dense retrieval via reciprocal rank fusion and reranking with a mid-size instruction-tuned Qwen model. It reports roughly 64 percent MRR@5, a large gain over BM25 alone, without any fine-tuning.

entry.title: Track-Leakage-Free Hold-Out Self-Validation for Photogrammetric Reconstruction: Protocol, Sensitivity, and Limits

author.name: Behnam Asadi

entry.summary: Proposes a hold-out validation protocol for photogrammetric 3D reconstruction that prevents track-level leakage, so held-out images are only localised against points supported by retained views, yielding a self-assessed reliability score without external ground truth. Sensitivity analysis characterises where the confidence estimate holds and where it fails.

entry.title: LGFNet: A CTC-Guided Local-Global Fusion Framework for Single-Channel Sleep Staging

author.name: Chongjian Wang, Zhenghang Hou, Junjie Gao, Xiaofang Zhong, Shiyuan Han, Tong Zhang

entry.summary: LGFNet performs single-channel sleep staging with a local-global fusion encoder plus joint CTC-attention training to handle long-range dependencies, ambiguous N1 transitions, and distribution shift across subjects and montages. It targets wearable, low-latency deployment.

entry.title: ObliCity: A Benchmark and Baseline for Roof-to-Ground Projection Displacement Correction

author.name: Kai Li, Yupeng Deng, Ligao Deng, Zhihao Xi, Chenhao Wang, Jierui Zhang, Yingrui Ji, Yu Meng, Xiangyu Zhao

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.25210v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Oblique-view urban remote sensing imagery inevitably exhibits geometric projection displacements between building roofs and footprints, leading to sign...

entry.title: Human-in-the-Loop Signature Bootstrapping for UAV Hyperspectral PFM-1 Mine Detection

author.name: Sagar Lekhak, Prasanna Reddy Pulakurthi, Emmett J. Ientilucci

entry.summary: Compares classical hyperspectral target detectors for UAV-based landmine screening using ground-measured, in-scene, and human-in-the-loop bootstrapped spectral signatures, reporting operationally meaningful metrics such as target-discovery curves and candidate-review counts rather than only AUC. It highlights how many false alarms operators must inspect.

entry.title: DensFiLM: Density-Conditioned Video Saliency for Crowd Scenes

author.name: Anis Ur Rahman

entry.summary: DensFiLM conditions a video saliency model on crowd density using a lightweight feature-wise linear modulation layer inserted at the bottleneck of a Video Swin Transformer, so the decoder can switch between individual-tracking and collective-motion attention regimes. The module adds only about 100K parameters.

entry.title: Safety-Aware Cascaded Inference for Crop Damage Assessment with Controlled Error Trade-offs

author.name: Jos\'e Thi\'ery Messigb\'ed\'e Hagbe, Gani Kawsar Gounou, Songbian Karim Zim\'e

entry.summary: CascadeCropNet is a two-stage classifier for smallholder crop damage assessment in picture-based insurance, calibrated so that damage recall stays above 95 percent by escalating uncertain cases from a lightweight triage model to an expert model. It operationalizes the asymmetric cost of missed payouts versus unnecessary review.

entry.title: A systematic evaluation of machine learning classifiers for event-by-event background rejection in LAFOV PET scanners

author.name: Konrad Klimaszewski, Micha{\l} Obara, Mateusz Bala, Beatrix C. Hiesmayr, Lech Raczy\'nski, Roman Y. Shopa, Wojciech Zdeb, Wojciech Krzemien

entry.summary: Systematically compares gradient-boosted trees and neural classifiers for event-by-event rejection of accidental and scattered coincidences in long-axial-field-of-view PET, applied as a pre-reconstruction filter using Monte Carlo simulations of a commercial scanner with realistic phantoms. It shifts machine learning from post-processing to raw-event classification.

entry.title: A Functional Approach to Curve Alignment and Shape Analysis

author.name: Issam-Ali Moindji\'e, C\'edric Beaulac, Marie-H\'el\`ene Descary

entry.summary: A functional-data-analysis framework for statistical shape analysis that treats object contours as continuous curves and jointly models deformation variables such as scaling, translation, rotation and reparametrization rather than discretizing them away. It aims to preserve geometric structure and dependencies between deformations and shape.

entry.title: When Does Legacy Data Start to Help? Emergent Transfer in Cross-Configuration Robot Learning

author.name: Tao Wang, Hudson Hou, Yingdong Hu, Yufeng Liu, Qinghai Li, Yingjie Jiang, Yingzhi Wang, Cheng Ma, Richard Wang, Yang Gao

entry.summary: arXiv:2607.25593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Robotic hardware evolves over time, but demonstration data is often tied to a specific sensor and actuator configuration. This raises a practical and u...

entry.title: A GAN-Based Framework for Robust Data Synthesis in Satellite Internet Observations

author.name: Xiang Shi, Peng Hu

entry.summary: Proposes a GAN-based framework to synthesize high-fidelity measurements directly from incomplete low-Earth-orbit satellite Internet observation data, with a characterization of representative missingness patterns. Motivated by dataset scarcity for 6G-era non-terrestrial networks.

entry.title: A Riemannian View on Active Subspaces

author.name: Zachary Grey

entry.summary: The paper extends active-subspace dimension reduction from Euclidean domains to functions defined on Riemannian manifolds using parallel transport, and contrasts this intrinsic formulation with extrinsic embedding-based gradient averaging. It shows the two agree only to second order within small geodesic balls.
